About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) Fellowship brings together top researchers and domain experts to collaborate on high-impact work that are shaping the future of AI. As an HFC Fellow, you’ll apply your academic and professional expertise to help design, evaluate, and interpret advanced generative AI systems—while gaining exposure to cutting-edge research and working alongside an interdisciplinary network of leading thinkers.

What You'll Do

  • Collaborative Work: Get invited to engage in high-impact projects with our partnered AI labs and platforms. Design complex, domain-specific problems and datasets to rigorously evaluate AI models, and provide expert insights that enhance their accuracy, reasoning, and overall performance. 
  • Join the HFC Community: Beyond the work, you’ll become part of a supportive, interdisciplinary network of innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI across domains.
  • Contribute to Research Publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition.

Who Should Apply

  • Professional and Academic Background: 5+ years of software engineering or related technical experience, or equivalent domain expertise through academic work (e.g. PhD, postdoctoral research, or faculty experience in Computer Science or related field).
  • Skills: Demonstrated coding proficiency and analytical abilities, with deep expertise in one or more of the following programming languages: Python, Java, Rust, Swift, JavaScript, or C++.
  • Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion in applied AI research and a commitment to collaboration.

Why Join the HFC?

  • Professional Development: High-impact experts expand their influence through review projects, advisory roles, and research—while deepening their AI expertise, strengthening analytical and problem-solving skills, and engaging with pioneering AI applications in science and technology.
  • Join a Top-Tier Network: Collaborate with a global network of academics and experts to advance responsible AI through impactful, flexible research and training. 80% of our members come from leading institutions.
  • Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule, with flexible 10–40 hour weeks that fit around your life and other commitments.
  • Competitive Pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and are depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to; projects, scope, skillset, and location. 

Application Process

  1. Apply: We review applications on a rolling basis.
  2. Interview: Candidates will meet with the HFC team to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI.
  3. Join the Collective: Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship.

Scale AI is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Team Lead for our ARC (Architecture, Reliability, & Compute) team supporting our dynamic Public Sector Engineering team. As the lead of this team, you will define how the company ships software, establishing the patterns for deploying into complex government and high-security environments, rather than just running Terraform scripts. You will build and maintain internal CLIs/tools that standardize testing, deployment, environment management and are tools that engineering relies on to prevent downstream breakages. You will execute on automated deployment efforts to pay down tech debt, creating fully functional staging/testing environments, and defining the company's standard for safe deployments. As Team Lead, you will provide mentorship for the rest of the team and manage their performance while also guiding the technical direction of the team.

You will:

  • Design and implement secure scalable backend systems for Public Sector customers, leveraging Scale's modern and cloud-native AI infrastructure.
  • Provide mentorship to and manage the performance of the other team members
  • Own services or systems and define their long-term health goals, while also improving the health of surrounding components.
  • Re-architect the stack to run in compliant or restrictive environments. This requires designing swappable components (auth, storage, logging) to meet government/security mandates without breaking the product.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define and execute the vision for backend solutions, ensuring they meet the unique needs of government agencies operating in secure environments.
  • Participate actively in customer engagements, working closely with stakeholders to understand requirements and deliver innovative solutions.
  • Contribute to the platform roadmap and product strategy for Scale AI's Public Sector business, playing a key role in shaping the future direction of our offerings.

Must have:

  • At least an active secret clearance. This is a requirement and candidates will not be considered who do not hold at least a secret clearance

Ideally you'd have:

  • Full Stack Development: Proficiency in both front-end and back-end development, including experience with modern web development frameworks, programming languages, and databases. Experience with developing & delivering software to air-gapped & isolated environments is a plus.
  • Cloud-Native Technologies: Understanding of containerization (e.g., Docker) and container orchestration (e.g., Kubernetes) is desired. Familiarity with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and experience in developing and deploying applications in a cloud-native environment. 
  • Security Focused: Experience with Federal Compliance frameworks, and requirements(e.g, Cloud SRG, FedRAMP, STIG Benchmarks, etc). Experience developing software & technical solutions that meet strict security & regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Problem Solving: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to understand complex challenges and devise effective solutions. Ability to think critically, identify root causes, and propose innovative approaches to overcome technical obstacles.
  • Collaboration and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and customers. Ability to clearly articulate technical concepts to non-technical audiences and foster a collaborative work environment.
  • Adaptability and Learning Agility: Willingness to embrace new technologies, learn new skills, and adapt to evolving project requirements. Ability to quickly grasp and apply new concepts and stay up-to-date with emerging trends in software engineering.
  • Must be able to support work 3 days a week from the DC, SF, NYC, or STL office.

Scale's LLM post-training platform team builds our internal distributed framework for large language model training. The platform powers MLEs, researchers, data scientists, and operators for fast and automatic training and evaluation of LLMs. It also serves as the underlying training framework for the data quality evaluation pipeline.

Scale is uniquely positioned at the heart of the field of AI as an indispensable provider of training and evaluation data and end-to-end solutions for the ML lifecycle. You will work closely with Scale’s ML teams and researchers to build the foundation platform which supports all our ML research and development works. You will be building and optimizing the platform to enable our next generation LLM training, inference and data curation.

If you are excited about shaping the future AI via fundamental innovations, we would love to hear from you!

You will:

  • Build, profile and optimize our training and inference framework.
  • Collaborate with ML and research teams to accelerate their research and development, and enable them to develop the next generation of models and data curation.
  • Research and integrate state-of-the-art technologies to optimize our ML system.

Ideally you’d have:

  • Passionate about system optimization
  • Experience with multi-node LLM training and inference
  • Experience with developing large-scale distributed ML systems
  • Experience with post-training methods like RLHF/RLVR and related algorithms like PPO/GRPO etc.
  • Strong software engineering skills, proficient in frameworks and tools such as CUDA, Pytorch, transformers, flash attention, etc. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills to operate in a cross functional team environment.

Nice to haves:

  • Demonstrated expertise in post-training methods and/or next generation use cases for large language models including instruction tuning, RLHF, tool use, reasoning, agents, and multimodal, etc.

Scale's Public Sector customer base is growing rapidly, and you will ensure that these customers become passionate, lifelong Scale partners. In this role, you will lead technical delivery for one of Scale's most consequential Public Sector programs, building AI-enabled planning and decision-support capability for major Department of War commands. Partnering with the program's Delivery Lead, you own the technical shape of what we ship: how Scale's products come together, where we extend them, and what we build from scratch. You will also lead a team of Technical Program Managers, coaching them through ambiguous problems and multiplying what the group can take on.

 

You will:

  • Lead and mentor a team of Technical Program Managers who own the program's key technical delivery areas, allocating scope, raising the technical bar, and unblocking them as they interface directly with stakeholders and end users
  • Own the technical shape of what we deliver: whether we are combining Scale's products in the right way, extending them in the right way for this program, and being deliberate about what genuinely warrants a bespoke build
  • Plan and sequence releases alongside engineering, anticipating technical risk early and putting engineering trade-offs in terms stakeholders can decide on
  • Serve as the senior technical voice to program stakeholders and users, translating operational needs into delivery decisions the team can execute against
  • Drive innovation and transformation by diving deep into technical and operational challenges, solving undefined problems, and delivering impactful solutions for Public Sector customers
  • Leverage technical concepts, tools, and expertise to create solutions from scratch or drastically improve existing solutions
  • Use data, analytics, and technical expertise to align internal resources and create tools that directly add value to customers in the public sector space
  • Transition AI/ML technologies and processes into working Public Sector products / solutions even when requirements are undefined or ambiguous
  • Partner with engineering, operations, and other public sector teams to build and deliver AI systems tailored to unique government use cases in the computer vision and generative AI domains
  • Set the technical direction for a cross-functional team of engineers, operations, and delivery staff to exceed the customer's AI/ML objectives
  • Manage the long-term health of the customer base by identifying and preempting areas of risk or concern
  • Build with an eye toward reuse, identifying where program work can generalize into durable capability and surfacing it to Product, while holding the line on the program's technical delivery goals
  • Address engineering problems alongside the product development teams

 

Must Haves:

  • An active TS/SCI clearance
  • 7+ years of experience succeeding in stakeholder management or customer-facing role
  • Experience leading or mentoring other program managers, engineers, or technical staff
  • Demonstrated ownership of the technical delivery of a complex, multi-workstream program with senior government or enterprise stakeholders
  • Technical background (education or professional experience with CS, Economics, Statistics, Engineering)
  • Deep understanding of ML operations process
  • Working knowledge of software delivery pipelines and DevOps principles
  • A track record of structured, analytics-driven problem-solving
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Willingness to travel: 25–50% (typically 1–2 weeks per month on-site with CONUS and OCONUS customers)

We have a diverse team with a variety of skill sets, many have:

  • 10+ years of professional experience, often in a customer-facing technical program management role in industry or government.
  • Experience in a Department of War or Intelligence Community operational environment, or supporting a combatant command
  • Experience delivering a technical platform or product that other teams build on top of, with a feel for the integration, versioning, and support burden that creates
  • Enough hands-on fluency with Python, SQL, and modern AI/ML tooling to interrogate data and prototypes directly, rather than relying on an engineer to answer every question

Role summary

Scale’s Operations Planning Team sits at the intersection of Engagement Management (EM), GenAI Delivery, GTM, and Growth Ops. The Planning TPM reduces friction between customer requirements and delivery by centralizing planning, standardizing reporting, and driving consistent process execution across accounts. As a TPM on Planning you will own program-level planning and systems workstreams that translate demand into reliable production plans, validate staffing, and ensure opportunities move through ingest accurately. This role combines program management, operational rigor, analytics literacy, and strong stakeholder management, with the goal of making account planning predictable, auditable and scalable.

This is a role designed to build deep account knowledge: each Planning TPM will ultimately be assigned to support 1–2 priority accounts to develop the context and relationships required to drive lasting operational improvements and more accurate planning and forecasting.

 

What you’ll own (key responsibilities)

Demand Forecasting

  • Ensure project-level customer demand is captured accurately, consistently and at the right level of granularity.
  • Own day-to-day monitoring and execution of Production Plan and Opportunity Forecast; act quickly on demand changes.
  • Partner with Supply Ops to review the Production Plan weekly (PP, TCD, historical productive hours) and drive forecasting accuracy and adjustments.
  • Surface forecast risks and coordinate tactical interventions through the Ops Planning leads.

Staffing & Resource Planning

  • Create/validate staffing requests and communicate staffing changes to Delivery teams, STOs and EMs.
  • Monitor account-level FTE budgets and employee spend; contribute to cost/benefit analysis of staffing vs. revenue.
  • Stress-test staffing scenarios to provide early warnings on headcount risks and to inform hiring / reallocation decisions.
  • Validate staffing tracking accuracy weekly; identify and correct discrepancies in project-level staffing data.

Opportunity Forecast & Ingest

  • Ensure all revenue-generating opportunities are correctly logged in Opportunity Ingest (Linear) and that scoping is consistent.
  • Act as the owner for opportunities as they move through the ingest workflow — expedite translation of demand signals into the forecast (Airtable / PP / OF).
  • Run weekly checks to confirm Opportunity Forecast accuracy, and coordinate tactical scoping fixes when needed.

Account Intelligence & Systems Enablement

  • Actively participate in core account meetings (ops, finance, GTM, delivery) as the Ops demand operational lead.
  • Design, build and maintain scalable planning tools and account-level reporting artifacts (ramp planning sheets, account dashboards, account playbooks).
  • Standardize and centralize information flow across customer ops pillars (demand forecasting, staffing, opportunity ingest).
  • Drive systems enablement, process documentation (SOPs), and handoffs that reduce manual work and increase reliability.

Scale's Red Team and Safety function stress-tests the most capable AI models in the world, and shapes how labs, governments, and enterprises deploy them. We are hiring a Technical Program Manager to own day-to-day partnerships with frontier model developers. This is a hands-on role for someone who is technically curious, comfortable with researchers, and operationally rigorous. You will partner closely with research, operations, and go-to-market. 

The team

Red Team and Safety is a nimble function that stress-tests frontier AI. We partner with major model developers to generate adversarial data, run evaluations, and publish benchmarks across jailbreaks, prompt injection, agentic misuse, LLM-based cyber security, CBRN, political bias, and self-harm. Our work shapes how leading labs train their models and how governments and enterprises deploy them.

 

You will:

  • Own a portfolio of frontier-lab partnerships day-to-day. Run customer conversations, scope new engagements, and grow accounts from one-off projects into ongoing scope.
  • Act as a credible subject-matter expert in customer conversations; explain adversarial methodology, vulnerability taxonomies, benchmark findings, and what they imply commercially, in language that lands with technical buyers.
  • Partner with Enterprise and Public Sector account teams to qualify and close opportunities where safety, red teaming, or LLM-based cyber security are part of the deal.
  • Coordinate delivery with research and operations leads. Make sure scope, capacity, and timelines line up before we commit, and unblock the team as engagements run.
  • Contribute to public benchmark launches. Help shape the framing, the rollout, and the narrative we take to customers and the field.
  • Feed signal back into the roadmap. Surface what customers are asking for, what is breaking, and what we should build next.

 

Ideally, you would have:

  • Working fluency in model behavior, adversarial ML, and AI safety, enough to hold a substantive conversation with researchers and ML engineers.
  • Experience managing technical accounts or partnerships, ideally with frontier AI labs, large enterprises, or federal agencies.
  • Genuine interest in AI safety, evidenced in prior work, writing, or research.
  • Strong written and verbal communication and the ability to translate between research and commercial audiences.
  • Operational rigor; you scope carefully, track commitments, and keep complex engagements moving.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action.

 

Nice to haves:

  • 2+ years of relevant experience.
  • Hands-on red teaming, penetration testing, or adversarial ML experience.
  • Background at a frontier AI lab, AI policy organization, or national security agency.
  • Experience contributing to public benchmarks, evaluations, or research publications.
  • Advanced degree in a relevant technical field.

  • Use proprietary software to provide labels, annotations, recordings, and inputs on projects involving multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, speech samples, and auditory elements in various languages.

  • Work with technical staff to improve annotation tools for efficient audio workflows.

  • Demonstrated ability to transcribe audio with high accuracy across accents and varying audio quality.

  • Strong comprehension skills and the ability to make independent judgments on ambiguous or varied audio material, including noisy or accented speech.

In this role, you will leverage your expertise in fields such as graphic design, brand and visual design, product or UI/UX design, web design, game design, and illustration to support the training of Grok.   • Ability to evaluate design quality even outside your primary specialty, and to say clearly what works, what does not, and why.
  • Fluency in English, with excellent written communication for critiques, annotations, and design rationale.
  • High attention to detail and comfort working from evolving instructions in a fast-paced evaluation setting.
  • Comfort creating high-quality reference examples, not only scoring existing ones.

  • Working knowledge of modern design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, or equivalent; frontend or game-engine familiarity is a plus but not required.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to design evaluation tasks, rubrics, and examples that test and strengthen Grok’s behavior and personality in the humanities.

  • Habitual reliance on primary sources, with skill at weighing them against secondary literature.
  • Ability to steel-man opposing views and separate settled knowledge from interpretation or speculation.
  • Excellent analytical writing in English: clear, precise, and calibrated to the strength of the evidence.
  • Comfort working from evolving instructions to produce annotations, critiques, and reference answers at a consistently high standard.

  • Range across more than one listed field, or across historically and culturally distinct canons within a field.
  • Familiarity with evaluating AI or LLM outputs, building benchmarks, or creating training data.

  • Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to noise and industrial conditions.

By building forms, platforms, railings, and related structures, SpaceXAI carpenters support the full construction team’s needs across civil, concrete, plumbing, electrical, and related disciplines.

As a Construction Carpenter, you will layout, cut, assemble, and turn over the temporary and permanent structures that keep the Memphis/Southaven supercomputer campus moving: concrete formwork, work platforms, stairs and railings, blocking, embeds, protection, and related wood and light-gauge work. This is a build job, not a facilities-maintenance job — you build what the next trade needs, then move with the work. This position is based in Southaven, MS / Memphis, TN.

This is an hourly position with overtime.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build, set, and strip concrete formwork, bulkheads, blockouts, embeds, and related forming for foundations, pads, walls, piers, and equipment bases in support of civil and concrete work.
  • Construct work platforms, stairs, ladders, railings, toe boards, and access structures so civil, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and related crews can work safely at height and around equipment.
  • Frame, hang, and finish wood and light-gauge structures, including blocking, backing, partitions, door and window bucks, and equipment pads per issued-for-construction drawings.

  • Operate hand and power tools (saws, drills, nailers, lasers, levels); climb structures; stage, protect, and store materials.
  • Coordinate with civil, concrete, plumbing, electrical, and other trades so forms, openings, embeds, and platforms land correctly for the next install.
  • Support punch-list closeout and turnover with engineers, contractors, and vendors.

  • Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).

You are the commercial owner for your book of business: strategy, relationships, pipeline, and revenue.
You will work as a trusted advisor to brand marketers and their agency partners, building consultative, insight-led programs that put X at the center of both brand and performance plans. You will work as a peer with the Agency Development and X Cross Functional Teams — close partnership, distinct ownership. This role reports to the Head of Global Brands, APAC.

  • Partner with agencies without outsourcing the sale. You own the client outcome even when the buy sits with a holding company or local shop.
  • Bring market fluency. Know how decisions get made in Singapore, Jakarta, Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, Manila, Kuala Lumpur, Mumbai, and Delhi — and adjust the motion accordingly.
  • Partner tightly with Agency Development, Client Solutions, Marketing, Content Parternships and regional market teams to remove friction and create incremental revenue.
  • Stay fluent in the evolving social and digital landscape, X product developments, and competitor activity so you can lead the conversation — not follow it.
  • Represent X at client meetings, industry events, and in-market reviews across SEA and India.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Driven, commercially hungry, and comfortable being measured on revenue. Hunter mentality is non-negotiable.

  • Willingness to travel approximately 30% of the time across Southeast Asia and India.

  • Prior platform, publisher, social, ad tech, or martech sales experience.
  • Fluency across brand and performance buying.
  • Additional SEA or Hindi language capability.
  • Experience with joint business plans, annual commitments, or multi-market brand coordination.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a Construction Rigger to support the buildout of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this hands-on role, you will plan and execute lifts, land mechanical equipment, and keep construction moving on our next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with mechanical, structural, electrical, and operations teams to rig, signal, and set loads from construction through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Plan and execute lifts using mobile and tower cranes (as signal person), forklifts, gantries, tuggers, chain falls, come-alongs, and other hoisting equipment.
  • Inspect, select, and install slings, shackles, spreader bars, below-the-hook devices, and other rigging hardware; confirm working load limits, hitch type, and sling angles before a pick.
  • Keep damaged, unlabeled, or out-of-date gear out of service and maintain an orderly rigging crib and laydown yard.
  • Signal crane and forklift operators and run the lift team communication for the duration of the pick, including exclusion zones.
  • Crib, block, roll, and land pumps, cooling towers, air handlers, skids, pipe racks, modules, and other mechanical gear.
  • Assist with simple lift sketches, load paths, and field changes; flag drawing or lift-plan conflicts before the pick starts.
  • Stage, move, and inventory rigging gear and construction materials; fetch and return tools and keep consumables stocked.
  • Open and close work areas: protection, debris removal, scrap segregation, and end-of-shift reset so the next crew can start immediately.
  • Follow LOTO, PPE, lift-permit, and site rules; do not start a lift without authorization and a clear exclusion zone.
  • Report damaged gear, unsafe conditions, and near misses immediately.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Develop, maintain, and communicate construction schedules that the field, subcontractors, and leadership can actually use. You will build CPM baselines, update them from real progress, flag risk early, and explain schedule impact of changes, delays, and recovery plans. This is not a data-entry role. You need enough means-and-methods knowledge to challenge a sequence that will not work in the field.

Superintendents run the work; project managers own cost and contracts; the scheduler is the person who can tell you what is actually driving the end date, what slips if a trade is late, and whether a recovery plan is real.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build baseline CPM schedules from drawings, specs, estimates, bid packages, and construction sequences (WBS, activity coding, logic, calendars, and constraints used sparingly and correctly).
  • Maintain the live schedule: collect progress from superintendents, project managers, and trades; update percent complete, remaining duration, and logic; publish a clean current-period update on a set cadence (typically weekly look-aheads and monthly official updates).
  • Own the critical path. Identify near-critical work, float erosion, and out-of-sequence progress. Tell the team why the end date moved, not just that it did.
  • Produce three-week (or similar) look-aheads that match the master schedule and what the field can actually crew.
  • Analyze schedule impact of RFIs, change orders, design late-outs, access constraints, long-lead procurement, weather, and labor shortages. Prepare time-impact analyses (TIA) and what-if, recovery, and acceleration scenarios.
  • Coordinate with project managers, superintendents, estimators, procurement, design, owners/CMs, and subcontractors so the schedule reflects committed dates, not wishful ones.
  • Resource-load and, where required, cost-load the schedule. Flag crew stacking, craft shortages, and unrealistic production rates.
  • Prepare narratives, variance reports, S-curves, histograms, and executive summaries for internal reviews and owner/CM submittals.
  • Support claims and delay documentation with contemporaneous records (as-planned vs. as-built, fragnets, delay categorization) when needed.
  • Enforce schedule standards: naming, coding, update process, backup, and version control so the file remains auditable.
  • Facilitate or support pull-planning / Last Planner sessions and convert those commitments into logic in the CPM model.
  • Visit the site regularly. A scheduler who never walks the job will be wrong.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 4+ years of construction scheduling on active projects (GC, CM, owner’s project controls, or specialty contractor).
  • 4+ years of experience using Smartsheet, MS Project, or similar and comfortability with multiple calendars, relationship types, filters, layouts, global vs. project data, and schedule quality checks (open ends, negative float, SS/FF overuse, constraints). 
  • 4+ years of experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics).

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s in construction management, civil engineering, or a related field — or equivalent field experience.
  • PSP (AACE), PMI-SP, PMP, CCM, or similar credential.
  • Experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics).
  • Forensic delay analysis, time-impact analysis, and claims support.
  • Cost/resource loading, earned value, and integration with cost systems.
  • Last Planner / pull planning; BIM 4D (Navisworks, Synchro) is a plus.
  • Additional tools as applicable: Power BI, Smartsheet, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud. 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours as needed, including the current 6-day / 12-hour construction cadence.
  • Must be comfortable working in a fully onsite environment.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join the power generation engineering team to design, commission, and maintain plant control systems. As a Controls Engineer, you will own BOP PLC/HMI and the control-room SCADA picture that brings generation and balance-of-plant into one operating view — Solar, 6000, and BOP on a single set of screens. You will work from control philosophy through commissioning and ongoing reliability, hands-on at the panel and in the control room. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Own BOP PLC and HMI design, programming, and commissioning for power generation balance-of-plant systems (fuel gas, water, compressed/instrument air, HVAC, cooling, electrical auxiliaries, and related process/utility systems) 
  • Design and maintain the plant SCADA architecture so operators have one operating picture in the control room integrating Solar, 6000, and BOP — graphics, alarms, historian, and situational awareness on a single platform 
  • Develop control philosophy, control narratives, I/O lists, network drawings, cause-and-effect diagrams, and HMI/SCADA standards for reuse across the facility 
  • Specify PLC, HMI, SCADA, remote I/O, industrial networking, and interface hardware; define data exchange with OEM turbine/generation controllers (Solar and 6000) and with electrical protection, metering, and plant systems 
  • Program, test, and troubleshoot PLC logic and HMI applications (IEC 61131 — ladder, function block, structured text as applicable) 
  • Integrate OEM packages and third-party systems into plant SCADA using industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, IEC 61850, and others as required) so Solar, 6000, and BOP operate as one system 
  • Commission controls: I/O checkout, loop checks, functional testing, HMI validation, alarm rationalization, and start-up support; stay hands-on with technicians and operators 
  • Support day-to-day operations: troubleshooting, sequence issues, bad actors, and control changes under MOPs/MOC 
  • Maintain configuration management for PLC/HMI/SCADA programs, as-left files, firmware, and network documentation 
  • Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, fluids, protection, and operations so controls scope is fully integrated through construction, commissioning, and turnover 
  • Apply relevant standards for industrial control systems and electrical work (NFPA 70 / 70E, IEC 61131, and site cybersecurity/ICS practices such as NERC CIP where applicable) 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, controls engineering, computer engineering, or another engineering discipline 
  • 3+ years of experience in PLC, HMI, and/or SCADA engineering (design, programming, or commissioning) on industrial or power generation systems 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

  • 5+ years in a controls role at a power plant, independent power producer, OEM, EPC, or heavy industrial facility 
  • Hands-on BOP PLC/HMI experience on gas turbine or similar generation projects 
  • Experience building a unified control-room SCADA/HMI that aggregates multiple OEM controllers (e.g. Solar, 6000, or equivalent turbine packages) with plant BOP 
  • Familiarity with major platforms (e.g. Ignition, Allen-Bradley/Rockwell, Siemens, Emerson, GE, SEL) and industrial networking (IT/OT) 
  • Experience with IEC 61131 programming and protocols such as Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, and IEC 61850 
  • Experience across the project lifecycle: design, programming, construction support, commissioning, and operations 
  • Experience with alarm management, historian, and control-room graphics that operators actually use 
  • Working knowledge of how BOP controls interface with electrical power systems (switchgear, protection, metering) without owning relay settings 
  • Experience managing OEM and contractor interfaces on multi-discipline power or capital projects 
  • Professional Engineering license, or actively working toward one 
  • Ability to support technicians in the field and to remain effective during outages, start-up, and event investigations 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in the plant and control room, including during outages and commissioning 
  • Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support power generation operations 
  • Must be able to work on-site in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other SpaceX facilities

  • Provide controls support for process-critical campus systems, including cooling plants, liquid-cooling loops, electrical distribution, and fire / emergency shutdown (ESOP); protect plant stability during recovery

  • Experience with electrical control panel building and wiring; sensors and instrumentation (temperature, flow, pressure, leak detection, proximity, encoders, IO-Link)
  • Experience with SCADA systems (Ignition preferred), actuators, VFDs, interlocks, and industrial networks
  • Experience in data centers, power generation, semiconductor, or other high-reliability industrial environments
  • Excellent documentation and communication skills; familiarity with CMMS or work-ticket systems
  • Creative problem-solver with a high sense of urgency, able to work independently or as part of a team in a fast-paced environment

  • Must be willing to travel to other locations
  • Ability to work onsite in the Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS area
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted
  • Must be able to walk and stand for long periods of time, and to climb ladders, bend, stoop, and work in tight spaces

ABOUT THE ROLE:

SpaceXAI’s legal team plays a critical role, working closely with finance, tax, accounting, operations and engineering, to achieve our mission. This role is for someone passionate about working at the intersection of AI and law.

As a Corporate Counsel, you will support and lead mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, partnerships and other strategic transactions. You’ll also handle corporate governance and subsidiary management and provide counsel to multiple internal clients on a wide variety of complex legal and business issues.

This role is full time, five days a week, on-site and based in either Palo Alto, CA, Washington D.C., Austin, TX, or New York, NY.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead and support mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, partnerships and other strategic transactions from start to finish, including diligence, deal structuring, drafting, negotiating, executing and integrating
  • Partner closely with corporate development, finance and operation teams to execute a smooth and efficient deal process
  • Drive post-closing integration
  • Build processes, templates, and playbooks for mergers and acquisitions and strategic transactions 
  • Advise on corporate governance, including subsidiary board matters and consents 
  • Oversee subsidiary maintenance, including formations, dissolutions, and compliance across US and international entities 
  • Provide counsel on general corporate matters
  • Willingness to roll up sleeves and possess a can-do attitude

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • J.D. from an accredited law school
  • 6+ years in Corporate or M&A at a top-tier law firm or in-house company
  • Expertise in complex corporate structures and transactions, including diligence, structuring and negotiation
  • Experience representing mature private and public companies
  • Flexible team player, able to adapt to rapid developments and diverse projects in a fast paced organization working with novel legal issues

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be admitted to the bar, in good standing, in at least one U.S. State
  • This position is office-based, on-site, five days a week - remote work not considered
  • Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$220,000 - $260,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at xAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Imagine Product team is redefining AI-driven media experiences for Grok users worldwide. In this role, you’ll build the communications system that meets creators where they are: public proof of what Grok Imagine can do, programs that show creators how it makes them faster, more cost-efficient, or more ambitious, and a community that runs from individual makers to production houses. The job is to move the brand from talking about itself to making other people talk about it — through proof, craft, and community. If you’re a hands-on communicator who can turn product capability into credible stories, repeat advocates, and a feedback loop back into the product, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own creator and community communications strategy for Grok Imagine — plan and execute outreach that turns product capability into visible proof, creator adoption, and durable brand affinity.
  • Build and ship product-showcase content across owned channels.
  • Design and run influencer programs as two distinct motions: awareness partners who put Grok Imagine in front of volume, and craft partners.
  • Build relationships with production houses, studios, and in-house creative teams. Get Grok Imagine into real editorial and post-production pipelines, and run a two-way channel so professional workflow feedback reaches the product.
  • Manage external production when in-house capacity is not enough — bidding, contracts, workflow, and quality control — in close partnership with creative leads who set the taste bar for anything that ships under Grok’s name.
  • Track how competing AI media products talk to creators and professionals. Build the measurement that shows which communications work actually drives adoption, and that can support investment in the work.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Proven experience leading communications, creator partnerships, or community programs for a consumer or creator-facing product, including shipped showcases, tutorials, case studies, or creator programs that moved people from curiosity to practice.
  • Hands-on operator: you can write a brief, run outreach, ship a content calendar, manage a vendor, and stand up a curation and rights-clearance pipeline without a large team underneath you.
  • Experience working with creators, influencers, or professional media practitioners, and judgment about which voices confer reach versus which confer credibility.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; you can be precise with internal partners and compelling with external audiences.
  • Strong editorial judgment and a clear standard for what can go out under the brand.
  • Comfort operating in a small, high-velocity team alongside product, research, design, and engineering.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Background in AI-driven media, generative tools, or adjacent creative software.
  • Experience running both broad-reach influencer programs and credibility-building partnerships with working professionals.
  • Familiarity with production, post-production, or studio workflows — and how new tools actually enter them.
  • Experience managing agencies or production vendors end to end.
  • Analytics-informed content practice: using performance data to set cadence, format mix, and spend.
  • Demonstrated taste in visual and motion media, and a point of view on what makes generative work look professional rather than novel.
  • Prior work moving a product’s public perception from novelty to working tool.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$140,000 - $196,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at xAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Facilities Operations Technician at SpaceXAI, you'll dive in, operating and maintaining the critical facility systems that power our supercomputing data centers. Working hands-on with MEP systems, you’ll tackle maintenance, operations, and repairs, ensuring peak performance and reliability. Expect to troubleshoot complex issues, streamline processes, and collaborate with teams to keep our infrastructure running smoothly, directly supporting SpaceXAI's mission to accelerate human scientific discovery through AI. 

This role includes the following positions, each with increasing responsibility:

  • Facilities Operations Technician: Independently operate and maintain critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in supercomputing data centers, ensuring high reliability and performance through hands-on maintenance, troubleshooting, and process optimization.

  • Sr Facilities Operations Technician: Perform advanced maintenance and troubleshooting of critical data center systems like HVAC, power, and environmental controls, while mentoring junior technicians to ensure operational reliability.

  • Facilities Operations Lead: Oversee the maintenance and optimization of critical data center infrastructure, including power, cooling, and environmental systems, while leading a team of technicians to ensure operational reliability and efficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Responsible for MEP Infrastructure site safety and environmental compliance, ensuring the sites align with all local and regional health and safety requirements.
  • Provide operational expertise for Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) systems at the datacenter facility. The systems and equipment can include pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, CRAH units, wiring, lighting systems, generators, motors, water supply, UPS and switchgear, etc.
  • Routinely inspect all areas to ensure performance measures are being maintained and proactively self-report the problems of facilities.
  • Experience with writing and executing MOPs, SOPs, EOPs.
  • Perform daily inspections of critical systems.
  • Identify and maintain spare parts inventory to minimize downtime.
  • Coordinate and supervise scheduled system shutdowns.
  • Develop and implement energy monitoring metrics.
  • Support commissioning efforts by witnessing equipment startup, assisting with functional testing, and monitoring construction progress.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Electrical or 2+ years of hands-on operations/facilities work experience in lieu of degree (data center experience preferred).
  • Knowledge of mechanical or electrical engineering principles and systems (both would be a huge plus).
  • Experience and knowledge of all critical systems documentation including Plans, Procedures, and Operations Manuals.
  • Experience and knowledge of Building and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems and Operations.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience with PLC-based control systems and/or with Building Management Systems (Client).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and technical writing skills in English.
  • Physical Requirements:
    • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
    • Ability to utilize hand tools and power tools as needed.
    • Work is often performed in tight quarters, and physical dexterity is necessary to perform job functions.
    • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs. unassisted.
    • Comfortable working at elevated heights (up to 100 feet) with appropriate safety gear.
    • Comfortable working in extreme outdoor environments—heat, cold, rain, etc.
    • Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.
  • Available to work flexible shifts providing 24x7 coverage as needed, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment and annual post-employment background checks.
  • Willing to travel as needed (up to 10%).
  • Valid driver’s license.

As a Construction Electrician, you will install and terminate new electrical infrastructure: conduit, cable tray, underground duct bank, cable, wire, and 480 V building and feeder work. This is a build job, not an operating-plant job — pull, land, and energize new equipment from drawings, then turn it over.   • Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).

  • Working knowledge of NFPA 70E and lockout/tagout (LOTO).
  • Ability to lift 50+ lbs, work at heights and in confined spaces, and work outdoors in all weather.

  • Ensure the reliability and maintainability of new and modified installations.

  • Work with the Space Force to acquire building permits when appropriate, and ensure all certificates and final inspections have been obtained prior to project close out

  • Experience with AutoCAD, Revit, or similar design software

  • Experience using precision measuring instruments
  • Ability to produce drawings for welders and machine shop fabrication in AutoCAD
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work in a team environment
  • Experience operating boom lifts, man lifts, fork lifts and cranes
  • Proficient skill level using Microsoft Office suite  

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Ability to travel to other SpaceXAI project sites to support work.   
  • Occasionally exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments- heat, cold, rain

  • Must be available to work extended hours and weekends
  • A valid driver’s license

ABOUT THE ROLE:
The fire protection technician keeps facility fire and life safety systems working: fire suppression, sprinklers, fire alarm and detection, extinguishers, and related life safety equipment. This is a field role. You inspect, test, troubleshoot, and support the installation and commissioning of systems that protect people and high-density computing. GPU racks and industrial processes can and do catch fire. 

You will work with facilities, contractors, and the local fire marshal. You are not the design engineer of record. You are the technician who ensures the as-built system is installed, tested, and kept in service.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Inspect, test, and maintain fire and life safety systems (sprinklers, suppression, alarms, detection, extinguishers) and close out deficiencies
  • Support installation, upgrades, and commissioning of fire protection systems: walkdowns, device checkout, punch lists, functional tests, and turnover
  • Verify that installed systems stay in working order and that impairments are logged, mitigated, and restored
  • Work with facilities teams, fire contractors, and the authority having jurisdiction (fire marshal) on inspections, permits, impairments, and certifications
  • Read drawings, submittals, and test reports well enough to follow a job in the field and flag what does not match
  • Keep inspection, test, and corrective-action records so audits and AHJ visits have a clean paper trail
  • Respond to impairments, leaks, trouble signals, and after-hours issues as the site requires

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 2+ years installing, inspecting, testing, and/or servicing fire protection systems (sprinkler, fire alarm, and/or special suppression)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Working knowledge of NFPA standards and basic building/fire code requirements for systems you work on (for example NFPA 13, 25, 72)
  • NICET certification in Inspection and Testing, Water-Based Systems, Fire Alarm, or Special Hazards
  • Hands-on time with ESFR, fire pumps, preaction, clean agent, or other industrial / warehouse / data-center suppression
  • OEM or vendor experience (Simplex, Siemens, Notifier, Viking, Reliable, or similar)
  • Construction or commissioning experience on active jobsites
  • OSHA 10/30 or equivalent site-safety training

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours as needed, including the current 6-day / 12-hour construction cadence
  • Willing to travel to site for the shift (this is a travel-to-site technician role, not a design-office role)

SpaceXAI  ·  X Money

Soho, London  ·  Full-time  ·  On-site 5 days  ·  Competitive base + equity

X Money is live in the US. The UK financial crime programme is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA. This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end — AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm. You will still work the hard cases. It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with “strategy” in the title.

If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat.

Why this seat is interesting

  • You write the UK programme while it is still being built. The standards you put in place are the ones the team — and the FCA — will actually use.
  • Payments financial crime at consumer scale, not a private-banking book of 400 names. You sit with Product and Engineering, not three layers from the customer journey.
  • Small team. Direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer. Scope is large; process theatre is not.
  • The measure of the job is a programme that still works a year later. The role sits next to MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity. If you want to be the named specialist in the room, this is how you get there.

What you will own

  • Design and run the UK financial crime programme: policy, procedures, CDD/EDD, risk rating, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, SAR handling, escalation, QA, and training.
  • Turn MLR 2017, POCA, the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, JMLSG, the FCA Financial Crime Guide, SYSC 6.3, and payments/EMI expectations into something operations and product can run.

  • Report on quality, residual risk, throughput, and control health. Prepare the programme for internal audit, skilled-person reviews, and FCA scrutiny.
  • Build the operating model as the team grows. Hire, coach, and set the standard. Support MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties as the UK permissions model requires.

Who this is for

  • 8+ years of hands-on financial crime in a regulated UK firm (bank, EMI, PI, payments, or e-money), including substantial KYC/CDD/EDD.
  • You know the UK regime well enough to argue a point — MLR 2017, JMLSG, POCA, UK sanctions, FCA expectations — and how it lands in a payments product.

  • You have led people or a workstream. You can defend a risk decision and explain it to the Product without jargon.

  • Stand: up to 6 hours per day.

You will work closely with mechanical, welding, structural, electrical, and operations teams to fit, hang, and test pipe from construction through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Open and close work areas: protection, debris removal, scrap segregation, and end-of-shift reset so the next crew can start immediately.
  • Follow LOTO, PPE, and permit rules; do not work on live systems without authorization.
  • Report damaged material, unsafe conditions, and drawing conflicts immediately.
  • Support punch-list work and cleanup through system turnover.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years installing large industrial or commercial piping OR completion of a recognized pipefitter apprenticeship, OR equivalent military experience.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience fitting and installing welded, flanged, grooved, and/or threaded pipe, including hangers and supports.
  • Willingness to work at heights, outdoors, and on a changing data center construction site.
  • Ability to use pipefitting hand tools, power tools, bevelers, and material-handling equipment safely.
  • Strong safety mindset and willingness to follow site procedures, including LOTO and permits.
  • Willingness to work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical construction windows.
  • Prior experience on data center, industrial, or heavy-civil construction sites.
  • Experience on large-bore welded industrial piping (carbon and/or stainless) and equipment connections (pumps, air handlers, cooling towers, skids).
  • Ability to read isometric, spool, and P&ID drawings.
  • UA, NCCER, or equivalent pipefitter credential.
  • OSHA 10 or equivalent training.
  • Familiarity with hot-work, hydrotest, and flange-management practices.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI data center construction sites and remain onsite during peak construction phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders, lift and position moderate loads, stand and walk for a full shift, and wear PPE for extended periods, with or without reasonable accommodation.

We are seeking an Industrial Welder to support the buildout of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this hands-on role, you will fit and weld large industrial piping and structural steel to ASME Section IX and keep construction moving on our next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with mechanical, structural, electrical, and operations teams to weld pipe, supports, and structures from construction through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Fit, tack, and weld large-bore industrial piping and/or structural steel (pipe racks, platforms, supports, skids, and related assemblies) per drawings and ASME Section IX welding procedure specifications (WPS).
  • Lay out, cut, bevel, grind, and align joints; check fit-up, root opening, and reinforcement before and after the weld.
  • Read isometric, spool, and structural drawings; work to weld maps, heat numbers, and rod-control / continuity requirements where used.
  • Support hanging of strut, supports, hangers, and structural members; assist with equipment set and bolt-up as needed to complete the weld package.
  • Stage, move, and inventory pipe, fittings, structural members, filler metal, and tools; keep laydown yards and work areas orderly.
  • Open and close work areas: protection, fire watch and hot-work permits, debris removal, scrap segregation, and end-of-shift reset so the next crew can start immediately.
  • Follow LOTO, PPE, hot-work, and site rules; do not weld on live or unpurged systems without authorization.
  • Report damaged material, rejected welds, unsafe conditions, and drawing conflicts immediately.
  • Support punch-list, repair, and NDE hold-point work through system turnover.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Journey-level industrial construction welding experience: 3+ years welding large industrial piping and/or structural steel, completion of a recognized welding apprenticeship, or equivalent military experience.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Hands-on experience with GTAW (TIG) on stainless steel and/or SMAW (stick) on carbon steel.
  • Qualified to ASME Section IX, or ability to pass a pre-employment weld test to ASME Section IX in the process(es) and position(s) used on site.
  • Willingness to work at heights, outdoors, and on a changing data center construction site.
  • Ability to use welding machines, torches, grinders, and related hand and power tools safely.
  • Strong safety mindset and willingness to follow site procedures, including hot-work permits and LOTO.
  • Prior experience on data center, industrial, or heavy-civil construction sites.
  • Experience welding large-bore process, mechanical, or utility piping and heavy structural members.
  • Current ASME Section IX qualification (e.g. 6G) in GTAW on stainless and/or SMAW on carbon.
  • Proficiency in both TIG-on-stainless and stick-on-carbon; FCAW a plus.
  • AWS D1.1 structural welding qualification or equivalent.
  • OSHA 10 or equivalent training.
  • Ability to read isometric, spool, and structural drawings.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI data center construction sites and remain onsite during peak construction phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders, lift and position moderate loads, stand and walk for a full shift, and wear PPE (including welding PPE) for extended periods, with or without reasonable accommodation.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a skilled Iron Worker to support the buildout of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers and AI supercomputing campuses. In this hands-on role, you will erect structural steel, miscellaneous metals, and equipment supports that form the backbone of our next-generation supercomputer halls, cooling plants, substations, and site infrastructure.

You will work closely with civil, mechanical, electrical, and operations teams to install the steel that carries buildings, pipe racks, cable tray, busway, cooling equipment, and access systems from foundations through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Erect structural steel for supercomputer halls, mechanical plants, substations, cooling yards, and site buildings, including columns, beams, bracing, joists, and metal deck.
  • Install miscellaneous metals: stairs, ladders, platforms, catwalks, grating, handrail, embeds, and equipment frames that support construction, operations, and maintenance access.
  • Fabricate and install pipe racks, aerial galleries, mezzanines, and support steel for chilled-water piping, cable tray, busway, and liquid-cooling distribution serving AI compute halls.
  • Rig, hoist, and set structural members and heavy equipment-support steel using cranes, come-alongs, chain falls, and approved lifting gear; act as rigger or signal person when qualified.
  • Bolt, torque, weld, and plumb connections to drawings, AISC and AWS standards, and inspection requirements; install high-strength bolts and close connection punch lists.
  • Read structural drawings, erection plans, and shop drawings; lay out from control, check elevations and plumb, and report conflicts before steel goes up.
  • Coordinate with civil, mechanical, and electrical crews so embeds, penetrations, and support steel land correctly for cooling towers, generators, transformers, pumps, CDUs, and IT equipment.
  • Follow fall protection, crane, rigging, hot-work, LOTO, PPE, and permit rules; keep a safe work area at height and around live construction and energized yards.
  • Support inspection, punch-list, and turnover work through building and yard completion.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of ironworking experience on commercial, industrial, or heavy-civil structural steel, or equivalent military structural or rigging experience.
  • Ability to read structural and erection drawings and work to AISC connection details.
  • Hands-on proficiency with structural bolt-up, cutting, and safe use of aerial lifts, ladders, and material-handling equipment.
  • Willingness to work at heights, outdoors, and on a changing construction site.
  • Strong safety mindset with current OSHA 10 or equivalent training.
  • Willingness to work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical construction windows.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Journey-level ironworker experience (union or non-union) and/or completion of an ironworker apprenticeship.
  • AWS D1.1 structural welding certification.
  • Qualified rigger and/or signal person; NCCCO or equivalent crane, rigger, or signal certification.
  • OSHA 30 and/or fall-protection competent person.
  • Prior experience on hyperscale data center, power plant, industrial, or other mission-critical steel.
  • Experience with pipe rack, equipment support steel, and miscellaneous metals in addition to building steel.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite during peak construction phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders and structural steel, lift moderate to heavy loads, stand and walk for a full shift, and wear PPE for extended periods.
  • Ability to work at elevation in varying weather, around cranes and heavy equipment, and in active construction yards.

This is a full-time position, onsite with occasional on-call or after-hours support.

  • Monitor and maintain IT systems, including performing patch management, updates, and basic server administration.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

$68,400 - $102,600 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

  • Proficiency with electrical test equipment (multimeter, megger, torque wrench).

  • Own the storage fleet as a power plant, not as an accessory: architecture, sizing, controls, safety case, and grid-forming behavior that lets the campus ride through compute step loads and generation contingencies.

  • Own the OEM relationship: technical requirements, factory testing, performance guarantees, and degradation and augmentation planning.
  • Direct Design, Commissioning, Ops/Build, Network, Civil, and Program Manager seats on Battery Storage as those seats fill.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for a Manager of Engineering to own the design, build-out, commissioning, and continuous improvement of automation, controls, and electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility in Southaven. This plant is critical infrastructure for SpaceX’s AI supercomputers: it must deliver high-reliability power and supporting utilities at scale, with the uptime and response expected of a mission-critical compute campus. 

If it has a gas or steam turbine control system, a switchgear lineup, a plant electrical distribution network, a SCADA/DCS point, a control loop, or a supporting utility/process system (water, wastewater, fuel gas, HVAC, cooling) that must run reliably, this team designs it, specifies it, commissions it, and keeps it running. As a Manager, you will lead a team of engineers in a high-reliability, fast-paced environment. This is a hands-on technical leadership role — you will review P&IDs, challenge control philosophies, dive into DCS/PLC architecture, electrical protection schemes, and commissioning details, not just manage a roadmap. You will scale both the team and the systems as generation capacity and AI compute load grow. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Own automation, controls, and electrical scope for power generation assets (gas turbine simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam turbine systems) and plant electrical systems, including DCS/SCADA architecture, PLC systems, turbine control interfaces, switchgear, protection and metering, plant distribution, instrumentation, and control networks — from control philosophy through commissioning and reliability, in compliance with NFPA 70/70B/70E, NESC, and IEEE standards. 
  • Lead controls scope for mechanical and electrical balance-of-plant and supporting utilities, including fuel gas, HVAC, fire protection, compressed air, cooling water, raw water intake, demineralization, wastewater treatment, and industrial gas systems that keep the plant and downstream compute campus online. 
  • Build, mentor, and manage a team of automation and controls engineers and technicians; scale the team with power generation capacity growth and AI supercomputer demand. 
  • Review and approve control philosophy documents, I/O lists, control narratives, single-line diagrams, electrical/pneumatic schematics, cause-and-effect diagrams, and control panel designs; drive standardized DCS/PLC/SCADA architecture, cybersecurity posture, documentation, and engineering practices across the Southaven facilities. 
  • Interface with internal engineering, construction, OEMs (turbine, HRSG, BOP, and electrical equipment vendors), and contractors; develop SOWs, negotiate, and manage contractor work to keep controls and electrical scope integrated and on schedule. 
  • Own field commissioning for automation, controls, and electrical systems (loop checks, functional testing, protection testing, start-up, and hand-off) and drive root-cause investigations and reliability improvements on operating assets. 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, or related engineering field. 
  • 8+ years of experience in automation and controls engineering, with direct experience on industrial power generation projects (gas turbine, combined cycle, or steam systems preferred) or large-scale critical power infrastructure. 
  • 3+ years of experience directly managing or leading a team of engineers (and preferably technicians). 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES: 

  • Hands-on experience with DCS, PLC, HMI, and SCADA platforms used in power generation or heavy industry (e.g., Emerson, ABB, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, SEL, Ignition), including IEC 61131 programming, industrial networking (IT/OT), and protocols such as Modbus and DNP3. 
  • Direct experience with gas turbine or combined-cycle plant controls (turbine control systems, HRSG controls, plant-wide DCS integration, and BOP), plus water treatment, wastewater, fuel gas, or process cooling systems supporting generation. 
  • Working knowledge of utility-scale and low-voltage electrical power systems, switchgear, protection, metering, and their interface with automation and controls. 
  • Experience designing or reviewing industrial control panels and electrical schematics (NFPA 79 / UL 508A; EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical, or similar) across the full project lifecycle: design, procurement, construction support, commissioning, and operations. 
  • Experience managing EPC and OEM interfaces on multi-discipline power or capital projects, and scaling a controls engineering function in a fast-growing organization. 
  • PE license in Electrical or Controls Engineering (or willingness to pursue); familiarity with ICS cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NERC CIP); experience supporting high-availability generation for critical or data center loads. 
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to remain deeply technical while mentoring engineers. 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights, while remaining focused in hazardous environments and wearing appropriate PPE; ability to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted. 
  • Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed, and to provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies, to support power generation and critical compute operations. 
  • Must be able to work on-site at the Southaven power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceX sites.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking an experienced Mechanical Commissioning Lead to lead the buildout, startup, and handover of mechanical systems for SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this senior hands-on leadership role, you will direct commissioning, testing, troubleshooting, and turnover of critical cooling, air handling, and fluid distribution systems that support next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will lead a team of commissioning technicians while working closely with construction, engineering, operations, EPC contractors, and OEM vendors to deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality mechanical systems. This is a full-time, onsite role with extensive travel to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the United States.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead and execute all mechanical commissioning activities for HVAC systems, chillers, cooling towers, CRAC/CRAH units, pumps, heat exchangers, piping systems, hydronic loops, and associated controls in hyperscale data center environments.
  • Direct functional performance testing, airflow/water flow verification, system balancing, integrated system testing, and system turnover to operations.
  • Oversee troubleshooting and resolution of complex mechanical, controls, and process issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
  • Develop, review, and approve detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, checklists, and documentation in alignment with project specifications, industry standards, and SpaceXAI requirements.
  • Lead coordination with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, design engineers, and SpaceXAI stakeholders for system energization, startup sequences, and integrated system validation.
  • Mentor, supervise, and provide technical direction to Mechanical Commissioning Technicians and other field personnel; conduct performance feedback and support their development.
  • Champion safety by enforcing strict adherence to LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols; lead daily safety briefings and job hazard analyses.
  • Maintain comprehensive as-built documentation, test records, issue logs, and final commissioning reports; present readiness reports to senior leadership.
  • Support and deliver training programs for operations and maintenance teams on commissioned systems.
  • Participate in constructability reviews, design feedback sessions, and lessons-learned meetings to continuously improve installation quality and future project execution.
  • Manage commissioning schedules, resources, and punch-list resolution to meet aggressive project timelines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 7+ years of progressive hands-on mechanical commissioning experience in data centers, power plants, semiconductor facilities, or other mission-critical industrial environments, with at least 3 years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
  • Deep expertise in data center cooling systems including large-scale chillers, cooling towers, CRAC/CRAH units, precision air handling, chilled water plants, and high-density liquid cooling technologies.
  • Strong working knowledge of commissioning test equipment (manometers, anemometers, ultrasonic flow meters, pressure/temperature calibrators, power analyzers, etc.).
  • Thorough familiarity with relevant codes and standards (ASHRAE, SMACNA, NFPA, ASME, IMC, LEED, Uptime Institute).
  • Proven ability to read, interpret, and redline mechanical drawings, P&IDs, control schematics, and sequence of operations.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience coordinating multi-discipline teams and managing contractors/vendors in fast-paced construction environments.
  • Current OSHA 30 certification (or equivalent) and strong safety leadership track record.
  • Willingness to travel extensively and work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical commissioning and startup windows.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Prior leadership on multiple hyperscale data center or mission-critical commissioning projects (100+ MW scale preferred).
  • NEBB, AABC, or equivalent Certification in Testing, Adjusting, and Balancing (TAB).
  • Hands-on experience with BMS/BAS controls troubleshooting and integration (BACnet, Modbus, LON, etc.).
  • Knowledge of refrigerant systems, direct liquid cooling, and advanced heat rejection technologies.
  • Proficiency with commissioning management platforms (CxPro, Procore, PlanGrid, or similar).
  • Technical degree or trade school certification in Mechanical Engineering Technology, HVAC, or a related field.
  • Experience implementing Integrated Systems Testing (IST) and Owner’s Project Requirements (OPR) verification.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite for extended periods during peak commissioning phases.
  • Physical capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders/stairs, lift moderate loads (up to 50 lbs), and wear full PPE for long durations.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to meet SpaceXAI's driver eligibility requirements.

We are hiring Medium Voltage Electricians to join SpaceXAI’s internal construction team supporting the rapid build-out of our data centers. This is a traveling role — you will mobilize with project teams to active construction sites, install and commission medium-voltage systems at 12.47 kV, 13.8 kV, and 34.5 kV, and move with the work as new facilities come online.

You will install e-house medium-voltage switchgear (MVSG), generator step-up transformers (GSUs), 15 kV and 35 kV cable, and duct bank; support hipot/VLF testing; and work adjacent to live campus buses. This is a construction and commissioning role: build new medium-voltage infrastructure from drawings and turn it over. It is not a facilities-maintenance or operating-plant role.

This is an hourly position with overtime. Expect 80% or more travel on a rotation, with per diem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Travel with internal construction and electrical teams to project sites to install, terminate, and test medium-voltage systems, including e-house medium-voltage switchgear (MVSG), generator step-up transformers (GSUs), 15 kV and 35 kV cable, duct bank, and associated control wiring.
  • Pull, rack, land, and terminate 15 kV and 35 kV cable using manufacturer-approved stress cones and terminations.
  • Install medium-voltage duct bank, manholes, and raceway for 12.47 kV, 13.8 kV, and 34.5 kV circuits.
  • Support hipot/VLF and insulation-resistance testing of new medium-voltage cable and gear: prepare, isolate, ground, and stand the work with commissioning.
  • Work adjacent to live campus medium-voltage buses under switching orders, clearances, and LOTO.
  • Read and interpret medium-voltage one-lines, physical drawings, cable schedules, and termination drawings; produce as-builts and test records.
  • Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA 70E, OSHA 1910.269, and SpaceXAI safety and quality standards, including switching, clearance, LOTO, and arc-flash protocols.
  • Collaborate with contractors, engineers, and operations teams to deliver projects on time with zero incidents.
  • Participate in constructability reviews and provide field feedback to improve designs.
  • Mobilize quickly between project locations as construction phases and priorities shift.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5+ years of hands-on electrical construction at 5 kV and above in industrial, data center, utility, or generation environments. Experience at 480 V does not meet this requirement.
  • Documented 15 kV and/or 35 kV terminations (termination logs, QC packages, or manufacturer terminator qualification cards).
  • Experience installing or landing medium-voltage switchgear, transformers/GSUs, and medium-voltage cable at 12.47 kV, 13.8 kV, and/or 34.5 kV.
  • Ability to read medium-voltage one-lines, cable schedules, and termination drawings.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout (LOTO), medium-voltage switching and clearance, and OSHA 1910.269.
  • Ability to lift 50+ lbs, climb ladders, and work in e-houses, duct banks, and industrial environments with PPE.
  • Hourly position with overtime; willingness to work nights, weekends, and extended shifts during construction and energization.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 80% or more on a construction rotation; per diem and/or housing provided while on site.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Manufacturer terminator qualification cards for 15 kV and/or 35 kV.
  • State journeyman electrician license, or lineman/substation qualification, with the ability to work in Tennessee and Mississippi.
  • Data center or industrial campus medium-voltage construction experience, including e-house MVSG, duct bank, and work adjacent to live 15/35 kV buses.
  • Switching and clearance experience on 15 kV or 35 kV systems under OSHA 1910.269.
  • OSHA 30 or equivalent construction safety training in addition to NFPA 70E and OSHA 1910.269.

  • Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; frequent overtime and weekend support is required.
  • Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions, climbing, lifting up to 50 lbs., and working on ladders/lifts at elevated heights.
  • Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, noise, heat, cold, and rain.
  • Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.
  • Stand: up to 6 hours per day.
