A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role
 
Are you passionate about engineering quality, performance, and increasing the impact of engineers around you?
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations around the world use data. As an intern within Palantir’s Foundations organization, you’ll have the opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever imagined, as you build the shared infrastructure that underpins the Palantir Foundry, Palantir Gotham, and Palantir Apollo platforms, and drive investments to improve the velocity and quality of our engineering.
 
Teams within Palantir’s Foundations organization are made up of a small number of engineers, each focused on one of four major categories of our infrastructure:
 
• Backend Infrastructure: Maximizes the productivity of our backend developers and ensures Palantir’s platforms have performant and consistent RESTful services. Think: making the “easy way” the “right way” when developing backend services, including designing infrastructure to build hundreds of micro-service repos performantly, or to ensure we keep reliable audit logs of everything users do in our platforms.
• Developer Infrastructure: Operates the systems and services that underpin all aspects of our developer ecosystem, including off-the-shelf tooling like GitHub and custom tooling for managing automated changes across hundreds of repositories.
• Frontend Infrastructure: Maximizes frontend developer productivity across the entire frontend development stack, from the developer experience in the IDE to the final user experience in the browser. Think: the core infrastructure required to develop and serve our frontends (including features flags, internationalization, and commit previews), performant build tooling for millions of lines of TypeScript, and the Blueprint open source UI framework.
• Storage Infrastructure: Develops Palantir’s database and search systems, which includes supporting storage technologies across cloud, on-premise, and classified or secure environments. This includes evolving our existing technologies to support ever-increasing data scale and latency requirements, and designing the next evolution of our database offering to provide step-change improvements in particular workflows.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As a Software Engineering Intern in Foundations, your projects may include building features to improve the developer experience for other Palantir engineers, or improving the scalability and reliability of Palantir’s platforms.
 
You’ll be involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation and design, to execution and rollout, all while being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our developers' and customers' problems and build infrastructure to tackle them.

The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organisations around the world use data. In this role, you’ll have an opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever envisioned as you contribute high-quality code directly to Palantir Gotham, Palantir Apollo, or Palantir Foundry: products that are deployed at some of the most important institutions across the public and private sectors. You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll also have the opportunity to learn about other business areas.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping, to execution and shipping, all while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.
 
SWE principles include:
 
• Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.
• Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.
• Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.
 
Technologies We Use
 
It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us; what matters is that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university Teaching Assistant, switched to computer science recently, or are a hackathon enthusiast — you'll build your skills to apply the best technology to solve a given problem. Right now, we use:
 
• A variety of languages, including Java and Go for backend and Typescript for frontend
• Open-source technologies like Cassandra, Spark, Elasticsearch, React, and Redux
• Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

• Developer Infrastructure: Operates the systems and services that underpin all aspects of our developer ecosystem, including off-the-shelf tooling like GitHub and custom tooling for managing automated changes across hundreds of repositories.
• Frontend Infrastructure: Maximizes frontend developer productivity across the entire frontend development stack, from the developer experience in the IDE to the final user experience in the browser. Think: the core infrastructure required to develop and serve our frontends (including features flags, internationalization, and commit previews), performant build tooling for millions of lines of TypeScript, and the Blueprint open source UI framework.
• Storage Infrastructure: Develops Palantir’s database and search systems, which includes supporting storage technologies across cloud, on-premise, and classified or secure environments. This includes evolving our existing technologies to support ever-increasing data scale and latency requirements, and designing the next evolution of our database offering to provide step-change improvements in particular workflows.

As a Software Engineer in Foundations, your projects may include building features to improve the developer experience for other Palantir engineers, or improving the scalability and reliability of Palantir’s platforms.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

We've been doing a lot of thinking as a team, and what we've landed on is that this person needs to be someone who takes ownership. Real ownership. Not just "I'll close the ticket", but "I'm going to make sure this never happens again" type of ownership. That's the kind of person we're looking for, and frankly, that's the kind of person who's going to thrive here at Palantir.

As an IT Support Engineer, you take real pride of our internal ecosystem, from individual workstations to conference rooms to the systems employees rely on every day. You're the person people turn to when something isn't working, whether they're at their desk, travelling, or preparing for an important meeting.

You're thorough when it comes to troubleshooting. You don't just close the ticket, you make sure the underlying issue is actually resolved. When something keeps coming back, you dig into why and strive to look for a permanent fix. You're proactive by nature and complacency isn't something you settle for, and it’s not something we settle for either. You're constantly looking for ways to eliminate friction, automate the mundane, and elevate the bar for TechOps.

People feel comfortable coming to you with problems because you're approachable and follow through. You're familiar with the needs of executives and senior staff, and you check in proactively when you know something critical is on the horizon like a board meeting, an earnings call, an internal conference or a big reveal rather than taking a back seat.

What sets you apart is how much you care about the growth of the people around you. When you work through a tough ticket with a colleague, you make it a teaching moment. When you solve something new, you document it and share it because the goal isn't just to fix the problem in front of you, it's to make the whole team more capable. You firmly believe that good support scales when knowledge is shared freely, and you lead by example on that.

Core Responsibilities

    Executive & VIP Support
  • Deliver white-glove IT support to executives and VIP users, developing a deep familiarity with their workflows and technology preferences.
  • Proactively reach out during critical patching windows, major rollouts, and high-visibility events to ensure zero disruption.
  • Support executive travel and on-site needs, including internal conferences and off-site engagements.

    • Environment Ownership & Office Health
  • Have an intimate understanding of all office hardware. If something is broken, aging, or suboptimal, you are the one who notices and acts.
  • Proactively replace ageing hardware and maintain core VTC (Video Teleconferencing) equipment; identify issues early and never kick the can down the road.
  • Manage the printer fleet end-to-end, including setup, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
  • Maintain FOB office environments to ensure they are always in excellent working order.

    • Incident Management & Root Cause Analysis
  • Initiate tracking of potential business blocking issues and partner with engineering teams to drive to full resolution.
  • Go beyond the quick fix — conduct thorough root cause analysis and implement solutions that prevent recurrence.
  • Apply a proactive troubleshooting mindset to identify systemic issues before they affect users at scale.

    • Systems Administration & Automation
  • Install, configure, and maintain Windows and Mac workstations across the organisation.
  • Implementation of process automations that reduce friction and increase team efficiency.
  • Administer and maintain O365 Groups, distribution lists, calendar permissions, and Auto-Reply configurations.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve networking and connectivity issues with a solutions-first approach.

    • Vendor & Product Expertise
  • Serve as a key stakeholder in the evaluation of new vendors, tools, and products. Looped in early to validate, test, and become a certified SME before any company-wide rollout.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of emerging technologies relevant to the enterprise environment.

    • Customer Experience & Relationships
  • Create clear, empowering how-to guides that help employees solve common issues independently.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with key business stakeholders across departments.
  • Mentor and support IT Support Specialists, providing guidance, knowledge-sharing, and a steady hand when things get complex.

What We Value

  • Familiarity with AV systems, Video Conferencing infrastructure, and executive-level support protocols.
  • A proactive, ownership-driven mindset. You spot problems before users do and act without being asked.
  • Strong communication skills and an innate ability to build trust with people at all levels of an organisation.
  • Experience mentoring junior team members.
  • Comfort with automation concepts and a drive to eliminate repetitive manual work.
  • Logical, methodical approach to troubleshooting with a deep commitment to root cause resolution.
  • Professionalism, adaptability, and the ability to thrive under pressure and constant shifting priorities.

What We Require

  • 4+ years of experience in desktop or help desk support in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation and ability to travel up to 30% of the time.
  • Deep knowledge of Windows and macOS operating environments and common networking fundamentals.
  • Hands-on industry experience with LLMs and AI agents, with a deep passion for applying cutting-edge AI technologies to transform IT Support workflows and drive operational excellence.
  • Hands-on experience with Active Directory, Exchange, and O365 administration, including Groups, distribution lists, and licensing.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role
 
Talent Strategists at Palantir don't work from a boilerplate requisition list. They embed with their teams, learn what exceptional actually looks like for a given role, and hire the Engineers building the future.

As a Technical Sourcer, you'll support that work. You'll partner with Talent Strategists and Hiring Managers to build the pipelines and manage the process for some of our hardest-to-fill roles. The job is equal parts research, relationship-building, and attunement — figuring out where the right people are, what's going to resonate with them, and how to get them in the door.

This is an 8-month contract role. It moves fast, the priorities shift, and the standard is high. You will start with two weeks of onboarding before jumping into the deep end.

Core Responsibilities

  • Source passive candidates through direct outreach, referral networks, research, and sourcing tools. Continuously reassess what's working. The talent we need does not sit in obvious places, and the methods that worked last quarter may not work today.
  • Review inbound applicants and referrals, screening candidates with a genuine eye for fit, not just credentials.
  • Own the candidate experience from first outreach through to pre-offer stage. You're their main point of contact, and how you manage that relationship matters.
  • Maintain meticulous candidate records within our ATS.
  • Share pipeline data and market insights with the broader Talent team proactively — not just when asked. Sourcing in a silo is sourcing that fails.

What We Value

  • You generate solutions, not excuses. When the search stalls, you rebuild the approach, not the timeline.
  • You are data-driven about your pipeline and honest about what's working. Intuition matters. So does evidence.
  • You communicate with clarity and conviction to candidates and internal stakeholders.
  • You operate without supervision and without complaint in an environment where priorities shift and the bar does not.
  • You are genuinely curious about technology and the people who build it.

The Role

As a Technical Program Manager (TPM), you are the engine behind Palantir’s engineering teams. You partner with developers to optimize our development process and make sure we’re shipping high quality products every day. You track and stabilize projects, remove roadblocks, and anticipate customer needs to free up our engineers to focus their time and attention on the technical problems they are best equipped to solve.

  • Synthesize concrete technical goals from product vision, mapping global product strategy to granular team tasks and issues. This means triaging requests from the field to create maximum focus for the team, while actioning items that need immediate attention.
  • Keep broad and complete state of everything involving or related to your projects. Pre-empt and resolve any issues that may steer projects off-course.
  • Enhance cross-team collaboration. Read a room of technical experts to align them around shared objectives. Improve efficiency where you see miscommunication or lack of coordination.
  • Work with customer-facing engineering teams on implementation, roll out, and support of your product.

What We Value

  • Demonstrated success managing complex software development projects for an enterprise software company or startup.
  • An ability to engage in technical discussion and invest in learning technical concepts.
  • Excellent judgment and composure in high-pressure situations.
  • A creative approach to project management centered around lightweight frameworks that enable rapid iteration, while operating in harmony with a larger development organization.
  • Building strong relationships with customer-facing teams and possessing high levels of empathy for our end-users’ needs.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, including holding tightly to your team’s vision and maintaining a high product quality bar.

What We Require

  • Relevant technical degree or experience in a software-related field (Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, etc.)
  • 2+ years of project/program management experience, preferably in a fast-paced or dynamic environment
  • Active US Security clearance or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance

As a Technical Program Manager, Security, you are the engine behind Palantir's security engineering teams. Palantir's software is trusted by some of the most critical institutions in the world, and protecting that trust requires a security organization that moves fast, stays ahead of threats, and never loses sight of quality.

You partner with security engineers to drive our security programs forward, ensuring we are building and shipping secure, resilient products every day. You track and stabilize projects, remove roadblocks, and anticipate stakeholder needs to free up our engineers to focus their time and attention on the security problems they are best equipped to solve.
 

Core Responsibilities

  • Partner with Palantir security engineers, infrastructure teams, product managers, and legal to drive key security deliverables through the entire software development and security lifecycle.
  • Synthesize concrete security goals from product and threat landscape vision, mapping global security strategy to granular team tasks and issues. This means triaging requests from the field to create maximum focus for the team, while escalating items that need immediate attention.
  • Keep broad and complete state of everything involving or related to your projects, including vulnerability remediation timelines, incident response obligations, and detection coverage gaps. Pre-empt and resolve any issues that may steer projects off-course.
  • Enhance cross-team collaboration across security engineering, IT, legal, and customer-facing teams. Read a room of technical experts to align them around shared objectives. Improve efficiency where you see miscommunication or lack of coordination.
  • Design, document, and continuously improve security processes and operational frameworks to scale programs without proportional increases in manual effort.
  • Drive incident response coordination, ensuring clear ownership, timely communication, and structured post-incident review processes that result in lasting improvements.
  • Work with customer-facing engineering teams on adoption, roll out, and support of security-related product features and certifications.

What We Value

  • Demonstrated success managing complex security or software development programs for an enterprise software company, startup or otherwise.
  • An ability to engage in technical discussion and invest in learning security concepts, including threat detection, vulnerability management, incident response, and cloud infrastructure security.
  • Excellent judgment and composure in high-pressure situations, including during active security incidents.
  • A creative approach to program management centered around lightweight frameworks that enable rapid iteration, while operating in harmony with a larger security and engineering organization.
  • An ability to develop strong relationships with both technical security teams and customer-facing stakeholders, with a high level of empathy for our end-users' needs.
  • Meticulous attention to detail, including holding tightly to your team's security and product quality bar.
  • A proven track record of building and scaling security programs and processes from the ground up.
  • Relevant technical background or experience in a security or software-related field is a plus, but not required.

What We Require

  • This role requires that you work from the country listed on this job posting and that you are based within a commutable distance of your local Palantir office.
  • Willingness and eligibility to obtain a U.S. security clearance preferred.

As a technical writer and editor, you’ll play a key role in helping our customers succeed by creating, maintaining, and improving documentation that supports users of Palantir’s products.
 
At Palantir, we view documentation as a key part of product development. Working at the intersection of users and Palantir’s products, you will develop an understanding of user needs and help them get the most out of our software. You’ll be a thought partner with our product development teams, combining your communication skills with empathy for users and product knowledge. Your work will primarily be on written documentation, but may also include interactive tutorials, recorded demonstrations, or other communication channels.
 
Teams and individuals at Palantir operate with a high degree of autonomy and independence. In this role, you’ll be responsible for setting priorities for your work, deciding where to allocate your time based on an assessment of stakeholder and organizational needs. You should be comfortable thinking about the “big picture” narrative and structure of our documentation, as well as diving into the details. On any given day, you might find yourself editing a guide drafted by a developer, writing a new tutorial for a critical workflow, or identifying an area that needs improvement and partnering with a team to make the fix. You will also gain exposure to the technical infrastructure for composing and distributing platform documentation.

Core Responsibilities

  • Understand and communicate the value proposition of Palantir’s products.
  • Create user documentation in partnership with developers and business teams.
  • Review and edit documentation to maintain a high level of quality.
  • Identify, triage, and resolve needs in documentation.
  • Maintain style guides and best practices for writing, improving, and publishing documentation.
  • Manage and structure multi-stakeholder documentation projects.
  • Uphold a culture in which developers are engaged with documenting their products, including hosting training sessions and workshops.

What We Value

  • Commitment to quality and accuracy in communication and writing, with the ability to translate complex technical subjects into clear, concise prose suited for the intended audience.
  • Ability to prioritize, adapt, and operate in unstructured environments as part of a fast-moving team.
  • Enthusiasm for learning about and communicating new technology and concepts.
  • Experience working with engineering teams as part of the software development process.

What We Require

  • Outstanding writing and editing skills.
  • 3+ years of technical writing experience or similar experience in software development.
  • Experience with programming, scripting, or statistical packages; previous work in software engineering or data science is a plus.

The Role
 
Palantir's defense product vertical builds mission-critical products for the modern warfighter. We provide a complete ecosystem where customers can securely integrate and visualize their data, and build sophisticated, full-fledged programs such as common operating pictures, alert-triaging inboxes, and resource allocation planning tools driven by rich-ML models. Our customers use our defense offering to perform rich analyses that drive core operations within their organizations - these programs are relied upon for daily operations in the command centers and battlefronts of militaries across the world.
 
This is a frontend engineering role focused on application development for our defense product offering, where you will be responsible for crafting the applications that organizations use every day to keep their countries safe. You will be architecting and developing interfaces to make sophisticated, data-intensive workflows both powerful and approachable, including to non-technical users. You may spend one day talking to users to better understand their needs and identifying product gaps to improve. The next day, you might find yourself putting that customer context to use and brainstorming how to handle intricate UX needs with your teammates. You’ll regularly face sophisticated technical problems, requiring you to scope out the solution design and finding an incremental path to shipping the new features. As part of this, you will own APIs and schemas that power your frontend code, and work with backend engineers in developing them together. You’ll be constantly exploring new horizons and building new skills in service of real world needs: between type theory, operational transforms, 2D and 3D mapping, UI design systems, high-scale graphics rendering, evidence-based performance optimization, and the never-ending need to decompose user asks into rich, sophisticated, and maintainable software, there is always a new challenge to be faced.
 
 
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As a frontend engineer working on our defense product offering, you will be involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping to execution and shipping.

Some examples of product work you could work on are:

  • Build for high-scale, collaborative, geospatial workflows (Gaia)
  • Design sophisticated frameworks to enable complex workflows across applications in a single workspace
  • Develop the next generation of real-time collaborative tooling and data-analysis solutions (Secure Collaboration)

  • Typescript and React are central to our frontend development.
  • Blueprint as a re-usable frontend component library.
  • A combination of open-source and internal technologies that suit the problems at hand.
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle, Webpack, GitHub, and CircleCI.

What We Value

  • Passion for building user interfaces that enable users to tackle their problems.
  • Ability to work optimally in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, e.g. brainstorming and iterating with product designers
  • Skill and comfort working in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users.
  • Experience building high-quality software in a fast-paced CI/CD development environment
  • Proven ability to learn continuously, work independently, and make decisions with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Motivated by unlocking or improving user workflows while still maintaining engineering quality.

What We Require

  • 2+ years of frontend software engineering experience.
  • Strong frontend coding skills. Regardless of which frameworks you use or how you learned them, we’re looking for people who can write clean, effective code. You should already have proficiency in JavaScript and an understanding of how web technologies work.

Build software and deliver customer outcomes. Core Responsibilities

    You have two internship role options.

    Forward Deployed Software Engineer:

    At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

    FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them. Whether it’s “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks to optimize power grids?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global food supply chain to deliver life-saving aid on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.

Job Description:

We are seeking an Aerospace Engineer to own the flight performance, endurance, and mass properties for V-BAT. In this role, you will serve as the technical authority on aircraft performance—translating flight dynamics, aircraft configuration, and environmental conditions into validated models that guide design decisions, payload integration, and autonomous flight software. You will work at the intersection of design, propulsion, guidance and controls, flight test, and go-to-market teams to continuously improve the capability and reliability of the aircraft.

What you'll do:

  • Performance & Endurance Analysis: Develop and refine endurance, range, loiter, and cruise performance calculations based on flight dynamics, aircraft configuration, and operating environment (altitude, temperature, wind, and mission profile).

  • Weight & Balance Ownership: Own the aircraft weight and center-of-gravity (CG) model, including tracking, allocation budgets, and reporting throughout design changes and configuration updates, ensuring CG remains within stable flight limits.

  • Aero & Engine Modeling: Create, validate, and maintain the aerodynamic (lift, drag, and stability) and propulsion (engine) models of the aircraft for use by the Guidance and Controls team, supporting continuous improvement of the flight computer and autonomy stack.

  • Cross-Functional Design Collaboration: Partner with Mechanical and Propulsion Design engineers to assess the weight, drag, and aerodynamic performance impacts of proposed design changes to the airframe, wing, and control surfaces.

  • Payload & Configuration Evaluation: Collaborate with Go-To-Market teams to evaluate new payloads and estimate endurance and performance for new or customer-specific configurations.

  • Flight Test: Plan and drive flight test campaigns to validate operational envelopes, correlate aero/engine models against flight data, and characterize real-world aircraft performance across the flight envelope.

  • Root Cause & Corrective Action: Participate in root cause analysis (RCA) of performance anomalies and test findings, and drive corrective actions to closure.

  • Requirements & Envelope Definition: Analyze large flight and test data sets to establish and refine operational envelope requirements and performance specifications.

Required qualifications:

  • B.S. in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent technical field).

  • 5+ years of experience in the aerospace or defense industry.

  • Demonstrated understanding of fixed-wing flight dynamics, aircraft performance, and aerodynamic/propulsion fundamentals.

  • Proficiency in analyzing large data sets to define operational envelope requirements and validate models (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or equivalent).

  • Experience developing or maintaining aircraft weight and CG models.

  • Demonstrated ability to work with cross-functional teams to drive change.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to varied audiences.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Full lifecycle experience taking a product from concept through development, flight test, and field sustainment.

  • Direct experience with fixed-wing unmanned aerial systems (UAS/UAV) or autonomous aircraft.

  • Experience building or tuning aero and engine models used by guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) systems.

  • Hands-on flight test experience, including test planning, instrumentation, and data reduction.

  • Familiarity with fixed-wing modeling and simulation tools (e.g., MATLAB/Simulink, XFLR5, AVL, or comparable aerodynamic/performance tools).

  • Understanding of relevant airworthiness, safety, or defense acquisition standards.

Are you a passionate and innovative aerospace engineering leader looking to develop next-generation autonomous aircraft? Are you eager to make a positive difference in the world and work alongside mission-driven, values-focused teammates? Shield AI is just the place for you.

As the Air Vehicle Lead for a new aircraft program you will serve as the senior technical leader responsible for the design, development, integration, and maturation of the air vehicle. You will own the technical integrity of the aircraft and lead the multidisciplinary engineering effort required to take the vehicle from requirements and architecture through detailed design, build, ground test, flight test, and production.

This is a highly technical, hands-on leadership role. You will work across aerodynamics, flight sciences, structures, mechanical systems, propulsion, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, manufacturing, and test to ensure the aircraft performs as an integrated system. You will be expected to make difficult technical trades, challenge assumptions, manage risk, and drive the team toward simple, robust solutions at speed.

What you'll do:

  • Own the Air Vehicle: Serve as the technical leader for the aircraft, with responsibility for overall vehicle architecture, technical performance, integration, and design integrity throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Lead Multidisciplinary Engineering: Provide technical direction across aerodynamics and flight sciences, structures, mechanical systems, propulsion, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, and other air vehicle disciplines.
  • Drive System-Level Trades: Lead first-principles engineering trades across performance, weight, range, payload, cost, reliability, manufacturability, schedule, and technical risk. Ensure subsystem decisions optimize the aircraft as a whole rather than individual components.
  • Lead Design Execution: Drive the aircraft from requirements and conceptual design through preliminary and critical design, hardware release, build, integration, ground test, and flight test. Establish clear technical priorities and rapidly resolve issues that threaten program execution.
  • Stay Hands-On: Remain deeply engaged in the engineering work. Participate directly in design reviews, technical problem solving, root-cause investigations, test activities, and critical design decisions.
  • Own Technical Risk: Identify the technical problems most likely to prevent mission success and drive them to closure. Establish appropriate engineering rigor while balancing analysis, test, schedule, and speed.
  • Build-Test-Learn: Create a rapid development environment that uses prototypes, ground testing, flight testing, and real-world data to retire risk and continuously improve the aircraft.
  • Drive Integration: Ensure interfaces between structures, propulsion, avionics, flight controls, payloads, software, and other systems are understood, controlled, and successfully integrated.
  • Design for Production: Partner closely with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and Operations to ensure the aircraft can transition from development into repeatable production. Drive designs that balance performance with producibility, cost, reliability, and maintainability.
  • Lead Suppliers and Partners: Provide technical leadership for critical suppliers and externally developed systems, ensuring supplier designs and hardware meet aircraft-level requirements and program objectives.
  • Set the Engineering Standard: Establish a culture of technical ownership, first-principles thinking, urgency, disciplined engineering judgment, and accountability. Mentor engineers and technical leaders while raising the overall technical capability of the program.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Master's degree or higher preferred.
  • 15+ years of relevant aircraft development experience, including significant technical leadership responsibility on complex aerospace programs.
  • Demonstrated experience leading the development of an air vehicle or major aircraft system through multiple phases of the development lifecycle, ideally including design, build, integration, ground test, flight test, and production.
  • Broad technical understanding of aircraft development with demonstrated ability to make informed trades across multiple disciplines such as aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, flight controls, avionics, mechanical systems, and vehicle integration.
  • Proven ability to operate as a hands-on technical leader, diving deeply into engineering problems while simultaneously maintaining system-level perspective.
  • Demonstrated record of making difficult technical decisions with incomplete information, identifying the highest-value risks, and driving teams toward solutions at speed.
  • Strong understanding of aircraft design principles, system integration, verification and validation, and the relationship between engineering decisions and aircraft-level performance.
  • Experience partnering closely with manufacturing and suppliers to transition complex aerospace hardware from development into production.
  • Demonstrated track record of taking ownership of complex development efforts and delivering hardware, navigating technical challenges and development cycles to achieve program milestones.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearance required for the program
  • A demonstrated record of working hard, being a trustworthy teammate, holding yourself and others to high standards, and treating others with kindness and respect.

Job Description:

The Assistant Product Owner (APO) supports Shield AI's delivery of mission autonomy (MA) to the U.S. Air Force (USAF) Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program — the first time that USAF has decoupled, for procurement purposes, MA from the airframe as a standalone capability. In this context, the ‘product’ is the Autonomy Implementation package, including Mission Autonomy itself, the Human Machine Interface (HMI) software, A-GRA compliance, mission systems, training, cybersecurity, and the full suite of implementation/installation software.

Shield AI’s CCA programs adopt an agile framework and are organized as a leadership tier overseeing multiple shoals (from platform integration to autonomy capabilities), each with multiple feature crews. In the first instance, the APO will support the Platform Integration and Support shoal (Shoal 1), which is responsible for integrating MA with multiple platforms and with the operator interface. The APO will work in collaboration with the Shoal Lead, Systems Engineering Lead, and four Feature Crew Leads and report directly to the Product Owner/Manager, who is part of the program leadership team. The APO owns the day-to-day health of the Shoal 1 product backlog in Jira (and Confluence), and is expected to maintain an integrated picture of how customer priorities, epics, interfaces, dependencies, and milestones relate, and to make ‘product’ legible and accessible to the broader team.

What you'll do:

  • Work with the Product Owner and Chief Engineer to understand customer product needs (across the CCA program office, platform providers, and operational end users) and to determine priority, separating must-have capability from deferrable scope
  • Elicit and validate needs and priorities from the customer, including official guidance and scoping documents, and from operational subject matter experts or surrogate end users as available
  • Translate customer intent into customer needs into user stories and epic descriptions — including value proposition, success criteria, acceptance criteria, expected effort and timeline, dependencies, risks, and preconditions for success — against which feature crews can execute their sprints
  • Own day-to-day management of the Shoal 1 epic backlog across feature crews, including maintaining traceability with customer requirements, refining the backlog, and monitoring backlog updates to ensure changes in priority or scope are surfaced and their rationale documented appropriately
  • Provide a product perspective to feature crews at Shoal 1-specific sprint planning and review ceremonies, by maintaining an informal integrated product map of epics, interfaces, dependencies, and program milestones
  • In collaboration with the Shoal Lead, manage dependencies across shoals, and carry integration decisions and associated implementation implications through to the respective shoal or feature crew leads, or collaboration partner
  • In collaboration with the Shoal Lead, support development and integration of the operator interface, primarily through the backlog — the HMI feature crew owns delivery, the Shoal Lead owns requirements and acceptance, and the APO owns description, communication, and prioritization of epics
  • Keep protected weekly hands-on time in the operator interface, so that HMI-specific epics and instructions can be written from first-hand use rather than second-hand reports
  • Support the platform integration crew in their interaction with vendors
  • Act as translator across disciplines — normalize preferred terminology and make specialist discussion accessible to the whole team, ensuring general consistency
  • Support other shoals (e.g., Systems Engineering, T&E) through observation of operator-in-the-loop (OITL) activity and by providing feedback in review sessions

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, cognitive systems engineering, human factors, or a related technical field; or equivalent military or operational experience
  • 3+ years in product ownership or a related field (e.g., customer experience, human factors, cognitive systems engineering, human-machine teaming, systems engineering, or technical program management for complex software or aerospace systems)
  • Hands-on proficiency with Jira and Confluence as systems of record, including demonstrated experience authoring and managing epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria in an agile environment
  • Demonstrated ability to hold an integrated view of a complex product across distributed documentation and multiple engineering disciplines
  • Willingness to become a hands-on user of the operator interface, independently installing, configuring, and running mission scenarios
  • Working technical fluency in mission autonomy, autonomous systems, flight software, ground control systems or HMIs, or avionics interfaces
  • Exceptional written and oral communication, and proven ability to translate information across technical audiences without diluting technical accuracy
  • Strong problem solving skills, including sound decision making and judgment under ambiguity with minimal supervision
  • Ability to work effectively, both independently and as part of a team
  • Must be a U.S. person as defined under ITAR
  • Active U.S. DoD Secret security clearance is required at time of hire. Must be eligible for, and capable of obtaining and maintaining, Top Secret, SCI, and/or Special Access Program (SAP) level clearance/access
  • Ability to travel domestically approximately 15–25%

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting a U.S. Air Force, Navy, or joint aviation program of record involving uncrewed or autonomous collaborative platforms
  • Familiarity with the A-GRA, A-GRI, UCI messaging, or other modular open systems architectures
  • Experience with airworthiness, functional safety, or assurance-driven software processes and certification artifacts
  • Exposure to flight autonomy, vehicle management systems, or aircraft-level integration and flight test campaigns
  • Experience with C2 or HMI products for uncrewed systems (e.g., STANAG 4586, MAVLink, CoT, TAK)
  • Formal grounding in product, human factors, or cognitive systems engineering methods
  • Experience supporting OITL evaluations, test and evaluation campaigns, or functional check flight activity as a product or human factors representative
  • Proficiency with systems and process modeling tools (e.g., Cameo), and with reading interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Experience establishing decision logs, change control, or product governance in a program that previously lacked them
  • Experience coordinating directly with platform manufacturers, primes, or government program offices
  • Military aviation, flight test, or uncrewed aircraft systems operational experience
  • Advanced degree in engineering, business (e.g., MBA), or related field (e.g.,  computer science, aerospace, cognitive systems engineering, human factors)
  • Current or prior Special Access Program (SAP) or Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access

    ·       Assist with internal and external audit requests by gathering records, validating asset information, and resolving documentation gaps.

    ·       Basic familiarity with software licensing, purchasing, inventory, or asset lifecycle concepts.
    ·       Experience maintaining accurate records in an ITSM, CMDB, ITAM, ERP, procurement, or inventory management system.
    ·       Strong attention to detail and ability to reconcile data, follow procedures, and manage multiple requests or priorities.
    ·       Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document processes and provide professional customer support.
    ·       Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
    ·       Ability to handle company equipment and information responsibly and follow security and compliance requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

    ·       Experience with enterprise IT asset management, service management, CMDB, or workflow automation tools.
    ·       Exposure to procurement processes, vendor coordination, purchase orders, invoices, warranties, or software renewals.
    ·       Familiarity with asset audits, inventory reconciliation, secure device disposition, or software license compliance.
    ·       Basic understanding of lifecycle stages including request, acquisition, assignment, support, refresh, redeployment, reclamation, and retirement.
    ·       Familiarity with enterprise environments subject to SOC, NIST, ITAR, or DoD controls.
    ·       Experience in a technology, aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or other regulated environment.
    ·       Relevant training or certification in IT service management, asset management, procurement, or inventory control.

We are seeking a motivated Associate Manufacturing Engineer to support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes for next-generation aerospace systems. In this role, you will partner with Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain to transition products from design into production while supporting prototype builds, new product introduction (NPI), and production ramp-up. 

This position may support one or more aircraft systems, including airframe structures, electrical systems, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, final integration, or ground support equipment. The ideal candidate is a hands-on problem solver who enjoys working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment and contributing to the production of advanced aerospace products. 

What you'll do:

    • Develop, implement, and optimize manufacturing processes for assigned products or aircraft systems.  

    • Design and improve assembly tools, fixtures, jigs, and manufacturing aids to support safe, repeatable, and efficient production.  

    • Create and maintain work instructions, manufacturing process documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and process flows.  

    • Partner with Design Engineering to improve manufacturability, assembly efficiency, quality, and cost through Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFM/DFA).  

    • Support prototype builds, engineering builds, production readiness activities, and new product introductions.  

    • Troubleshoot manufacturing issues using root cause analysis and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).  

    • Collaborate with Production, Quality, Supply Chain, and Industrial Engineering to improve safety, quality, throughput, and productivity.  

    • Support tooling validation, first article inspections, process qualification, and production validation activities.  

    • Utilize CAD software to develop tooling concepts, manufacturing layouts, and production support equipment.  

    • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing waste, improving quality, and increasing manufacturing efficiency.  

    • Ensure manufacturing processes comply with engineering requirements, quality standards, and company procedures.  

Required qualifications:

    • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.  

    • 0–3 years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, process engineering, or a related field (internship and co-op experience considered).  

    • Understanding of manufacturing processes, assembly methods, and production operations.  

    • Familiarity with CAD software such as CATIA, Siemens NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent.  

    • Basic understanding of engineering drawings, GD&T, and manufacturing documentation.  

    • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.  

    • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative manufacturing environment.  

    • Excellent communication and organizational skills.  

Preferred qualifications:

    • Internship or professional experience in aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, or advanced manufacturing.  

    • Experience supporting prototype builds, NPI, or production environments.  

    • Familiarity with machining, composites, electrical assemblies, mechanical assemblies, or final system integration.  

    • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies.  

    • Experience with ERP, MES, or PLM systems.  

    • Familiarity with AS9100 or other regulated manufacturing environments.

Job Description:

Play a key role in bringing innovative products to life by building strong supplier partnerships and supporting critical supply chain initiatives. In this role, you'll collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and operations to ensure the resources needed for development and production are in place, helping deliver high-quality products in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

What you'll do:

  • Source and procure mechanical commodities including machined parts, sheet metal, welded assemblies, structural components, fasteners, hardware, castings, forgings, and other fabricated components supporting aerospace and defense programs.
  • Solicit supplier quotations, evaluate pricing and lead times, negotiate routine commercial terms, and execute purchase orders to meet program requirements.
  • Manage supplier relationships to ensure on-time delivery, quality, and responsiveness while escalating performance issues as needed.
  • Partner with Engineering to review drawings, specifications, bills of material (BOMs), and engineering changes to ensure suppliers understand manufacturing requirements.
  • Support new product introduction (NPI) activities by coordinating supplier quotes, prototype builds, and material readiness.
  • Work closely with Planning, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supplier Quality to resolve supply chain issues, expedite critical hardware, and support production schedules.
  • Track supplier commitments, monitor delivery performance, and proactively communicate risks affecting production or program milestones.
  • Support supplier qualification activities, First Article Inspection (FAI), and quality requirements in coordination with Supplier Quality and Engineering.
  • Maintain accurate supplier data, pricing, lead times, and purchasing documentation within the ERP system.
  • Identify opportunities for cost savings, lead time improvements, and process efficiencies while supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in purchasing, sourcing, or supply chain management supporting manufacturing or aerospace/defense environments.
  • Experience sourcing one or more mechanical commodity groups such as:
  • Precision machined components
  • Sheet metal fabrications
  • Welded assemblies
  • Structural components
  • Fasteners and hardware
  • Castings and forgings
  • Composites
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, bills of material (BOMs), and manufacturing specifications.
  • Experience obtaining supplier quotations, negotiating pricing and lead times, and managing purchase orders.
  • Basic understanding of manufacturing processes including CNC machining, welding, fabrication, finishing, and assembly.
  • Familiarity with aerospace quality systems such as AS9100 and First Article Inspection (FAI) processes is preferred.
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills with cross-functional teams including Engineering, Manufacturing, Planning, and Quality.
  • Experience using ERP/MRP systems and Microsoft Excel for purchasing and supplier management.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting aerospace, defense, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
  • Familiarity with FAR, DFARS, ITAR, and export compliance requirements.
  • Experience supporting prototype, development, and production programs.
  • Exposure to supplier performance management and continuous improvement activities.
  • APICS/ASCM or CPSM certification is a plus.

Job Description:

This position will be based in our Newton, KS location.

The Associate Systems Administrator provides day-to-day enterprise end-user IT support, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, and asset lifecycle support. This role is responsible for helping maintain a secure, reliable, and efficient IT environment by delivering white-glove technical support to employees, with particular focus on executive users, executive assistants, board-facing support needs, and visiting leaders. The ideal candidate combines solid technical troubleshooting skills, sound judgment within established processes, and a customer-focused approach, and operates effectively in a fast-paced enterprise environment.

What you'll do:

  • Deliver excellent customer service while supporting employees across multiple locations.
  • Provide day-to-day technical support for endpoint and user systems across Windows, macOS, and Linux environments.
  • Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot hardware, software, mobile devices, and peripheral equipment for end users.
  • Support conference room, collaboration, and meeting technology for executive meetings, leadership reviews, and other high-visibility events.
  • Administer user accounts, permissions, and access controls through Active Directory and Azure AD in accordance with established security and compliance requirements.
  • Support endpoint management and security controls to maintain a secure and compliant computing environment.
  • Perform local IT asset lifecycle activities, including device provisioning, deployment, inventory tracking, maintenance, refresh coordination, and secure decommissioning.
  • Maintain accurate asset records and software licensing information using IT service management and asset management tools.
  • Respond to and resolve service requests and technical incidents in a timely manner, escalating more complex issues through established support paths.
  • Create and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and knowledge base content.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, network, and security teams to support enterprise IT operations and coordinated issue resolution.
  • Participate in planned maintenance activities and support occasional after-hours or on-call responsibilities as required.

Required qualifications:

  • 1–3 years of experience in enterprise desktop support, IT support, or junior systems administration.
  • Experience supporting Windows and macOS operating systems; exposure to Linux is a plus.
  • Basic experience administering Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), or similar identity management platforms.
  • Understanding of networking fundamentals including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and VPN connectivity.
  • Familiarity with endpoint management tools such as Microsoft Intune, JAMF, or similar platforms.
  • Strong troubleshooting, organizational, and documentation skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with a customer-first mindset.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple requests in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience with ticketing systems such as Jira Service Management, ServiceNow, or similar.
  • Familiarity with IT asset management platforms such as Snipe-IT.
  • Basic scripting experience with PowerShell or Bash.
  • Exposure to virtualization, Microsoft 365 administration, or cloud technologies.
  • CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+, Microsoft, or other relevant certifications.

As a core member of the X-BAT FoS Capture team, you will partner closely with the  X-BAT FoS Capture Organization to maintain a high-confidence view of the current and future opportunity pipeline and assist in driving decisive action across the portfolio. You will turn pipeline data into actionable insights that inform prioritization, resource decisions, revenue planning, and long-term growth strategy.

This role owns the integrity and quality of X-BAT FoS portfolio pipeline information in Salesforce and related reporting tools and will establish the standards, review the data for completeness and credibility, identify gaps or inconsistencies, and drive corrective actions across the portfolio.

The ideal candidate brings strong analytical skills, experience working with CRM and business-planning data, comfort partnering with Finance, and the ability to translate complex information into clear recommendations. This role will help ensure X-BAT FoS maintains a resilient pipeline across near-term pursuits and a three- to ten-year opportunity horizon.

What you'll do:

    Capture Portfolio Strategy and Management
  • Maintain an integrated view of the X-BAT FoS opportunity pipeline across near-term, mid-term, and long-range pursuits.
  • Analyze opportunities using criteria including timing, estimated value, probability of win, market attractiveness, strategic relevance, expected revenue contribution, and resourcing requirements.
  • Partner with the X-BAT FoS Capture Organization to identify priority opportunities, inform portfolio trade-space decisions, and recommend actions to strengthen the pipeline.
  • Track changes in opportunity value, timing, stage progression, probability of win, customer funding, and other factors that affect forecast confidence.
  • Identify pipeline gaps, timing shortfalls, concentration risks, single-point dependencies, and opportunities that lack sufficient capture activity or next steps.
  • Recommend actions to create pipeline resilience, including alternate pursuits, adjacent customers, related mission areas, acquisition pathways, partner opportunities, and additional sources of demand.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of the X-BAT FoS opportunity space across a multi-year horizon and help identify and track actions needed to mature early opportunities into successful capture efforts.
    • Salesforce Data Quality and Reporting
  • Serve as the X-BAT FoS Capture organization’s lead for pipeline-data integrity, reporting standards, and Salesforce opportunity-management discipline.
  • Establish and maintain common expectations for opportunity stages, required data fields, forecast assumptions, probability assessments, next steps, and update cadence.
  • Review Salesforce opportunity records for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and credibility; coordinate with account and opportunity owners to correct gaps, stale data, and unsupported assumptions.
  • Develop and maintain concise dashboards, trackers, and pipeline-review products that provide visibility into portfolio health, capture status, forecast changes, and key risks.
  • Partner with enterprise business-systems teams, as required, to improve reports, dashboards, workflows, and data structures that support X-BAT FoS pipeline management.
  • Maintain common definitions, reporting guidance, and pipeline-management best practices across the organization.
    • Finance and Revenue Planning
  • Partner closely with Finance to ensure a clear, traceable connection between Salesforce opportunity data, bookings assumptions, revenue forecasts, customer funding expectations, and long-range financial plans.
  • Reconcile pipeline assumptions, forecast timing, probability assessments, and anticipated award values with financial-planning inputs and revenue-recognition assumptions.
  • Support scenario analysis to assess the effect of opportunity delays, funding changes, competitive losses, scope changes, and alternate capture outcomes on the X-BAT FoS forecast.
  • Help maintain a recurring pipeline-to-finance review cadence and track resulting actions, decisions, and assumption changes.
    • Pipeline Risk and Operating Rigor
  • Identify risks to current and future pipeline health, including schedule uncertainty, customer-funding risk, acquisition delays, competitive pressure, overreliance on a limited number of pursuits, and insufficient capture activity.
  • Develop risk-mitigation recommendations and contingency plans with capture leads, account owners, Finance, business development, programs, and other stakeholders.
  • Support recurring pipeline reviews through time-phased analyses and dashboards that show opportunity maturation, anticipated awards, bookings, backlog, revenue contribution, key decisions, and follow-up actions.
  • Support knowledge management by maintaining pipeline assumptions, opportunity histories, risk registers, and lessons learned from wins, losses, cancellations, and schedule slips.

Shield AI builds trusted autonomy for national-security space missions. The Chief Engineer, Autonomy — Space Domain is the senior technical authority responsible for defining, delivering, and sustaining autonomy capabilities that convert distributed space, ground, and payload resources into timely, decision-quality data products. 

This leader owns the technical vision, system architecture, execution rigor, risk posture, verification strategy, and operational readiness of the space-autonomy solution across its lifecycle: concept development, integration, test, launch/commissioning support where applicable, on-orbit operations, software updates, and mission evolution. The role ensures that autonomy performs reliably across multi-constellation and multi-orbit mission environments, supports resilient operation in constrained or contested conditions, and delivers usable information to mission users at operational tempo. 

This is not a research position. This is a position focused on delivering mission-ready autonomy systems that perform in real-world operational environments. 

What You'll Do:

    • Serve as the senior technical authority for space-domain autonomy, accountable for mission architecture, software/system design, technical execution, product quality, technical risk, verification evidence, and customer technical confidence. 

    • Define and evolve an autonomy architecture that supports end-to-end tasking, collection, processing, exploitation, and dissemination across a heterogeneous space enterprise, including satellites, hosted payloads, ground systems, mission applications, communications networks, cloud/edge compute, and external data sources. 

    • Lead the development of automatic and autonomous behaviors for multi-constellation and/or multi-orbit tasking, including prioritization, scheduling, replanning, resource allocation, coordination, conflict resolution, and response to dynamic mission demands. 

    • Define technical approaches for autonomously selecting, cueing, configuring, and coordinating collection from all relevant payload classes, as applicable to mission needs, including but not limited to: electro-optical/infrared, AIS, SAR, RF, SIGINT, communications, environmental, navigation, or third-party/partner payload sources. 

    • Architect and govern hybrid on-board and off-board processing strategies. Establish decision criteria for where inference, data reduction, fusion, storage, prioritization, and dissemination functions execute, accounting for latency, bandwidth, compute, power, thermal constraints, availability, security, mission priority, and degraded communications. 

    • Lead the technical design of advanced exploitation capabilities, including automated triage, sensor fusion, event detection, object/activity characterization, change detection, anomaly detection, provenance, confidence estimation, and analyst-in-the-loop workflows. 

    • Own the technical approach for dissemination of mission products: data-format and interface standards, prioritization, routing, timeliness, quality metadata, access control, product traceability, downstream machine-to-machine integration, and human-user delivery. 

    • Establish coherent autonomy interfaces among spacecraft buses, payloads, avionics, flight software, communications systems, mission planning systems, ground control, cloud/edge infrastructure, data platforms, and customer mission applications. 

    • Drive technical rigor across system requirements, CONOPS, architecture descriptions, interface-control documents, trade studies, test plans, verification matrices, technical performance measures, and technical baselines. 

    • Lead autonomy technical readiness for major milestones, including concept and requirements reviews, preliminary and critical design reviews, test-readiness reviews, operational demonstrations, launch-readiness activities where applicable, commissioning, on-orbit operational assessments, and customer acceptance events.  

    • Define and execute a verification and validation strategy that combines modeling and simulation, digital engineering, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, payload/ground integration, mission rehearsal, operational test, and—in applicable programs—on-orbit validation. 

    • Identify, quantify, and retire autonomy-specific technical risks, including failure or degradation of sensors and payloads; crosslink or ground-link interruption; incomplete, delayed, conflicting, or deceptive data; resource exhaustion; model uncertainty; interface failures; cyber compromise; and unsafe or unexplainable automated action. 

    • Partner with product, program, mission operations, security, safety/mission assurance, payload, spacecraft, ground, cloud, and data-engineering leaders to balance mission performance, technical risk, cost, schedule, and customer commitments. 

    • Serve as a senior technical counterpart for government customers, mission partners, suppliers, and internal executives. Support capture, proposal technical volumes, demonstrations, mission architecture discussions, technical reviews, and customer acceptance. 

    • Build and mentor a high-performing technical organization that may include staff engineers, autonomy developers, mission planners, data/ML engineers, test engineers, and domain experts.  

Required Qualifications:

    • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, aerospace engineering, electrical/computer engineering, systems engineering, applied mathematics, robotics, physics, or a related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred. 

    • 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in autonomy, space systems, aerospace, robotics, mission systems, ISR, satellite operations, distributed systems, or comparable complex technical fields. 

    • Demonstrated experience as a Chief Engineer, Lead Systems Engineer, Technical Director, Principal/Distinguished Engineer, IPT lead, or equivalent senior technical leader responsible for end-to-end system outcomes. 

    • Significant experience designing, developing, integrating, testing, and operationalizing software-intensive mission systems with high reliability, mission assurance, or certifiability requirements. 

    • Demonstrated technical depth in several of the following: 

      • Autonomous planning, scheduling, optimization, decision-making, and multi-agent or distributed coordination. 

      • Space mission planning, spacecraft or payload operations, satellite ground systems, constellation operations, or hosted-payload architectures. 

      • Multi-orbit/multi-constellation tasking and resource management. 

      • Embedded, edge, ground, cloud, and hybrid compute architectures. 

      • On-board data processing, sensor fusion, payload control, and communication-aware autonomy. 

      • ISR, remote sensing, RF, EO/IR, SAR, communications, navigation, or other mission-payload processing and exploitation. 

      • Data-product generation, provenance, quality assessment, dissemination, APIs, and enterprise mission-data integration. 

      • Systems engineering: requirements, CONOPS, architecture, ICDs, trade studies, verification planning, technical reviews, and risk management. 

    • Experience leading a multidisciplinary, matrixed engineering organization and influencing technical outcomes across teams without requiring direct reporting control.  

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs to engineers, executives, government customers, operators, and mission partners. 

    • Experience supporting customer-facing technical work, including proposals, solution architecture, test/demonstration planning, and technical reviews. 

Preferred Qualifications:

    • Experience with national security, defense, intelligence, civil-government, or commercial-space programs. 

    • Experience moving mission autonomy from prototype or research environments into sustained operational use. 

    • Demonstrated experience with operational test, mission rehearsal, launch preparation, satellite commissioning, or on-orbit anomaly response. 

    • Familiarity with safety/mission-assurance methods, cybersecurity engineering, secure software-development practices, and authorization/compliance processes relevant to space or defense systems. 

    • Experience establishing a reusable autonomy platform across multiple programs rather than delivering isolated, bespoke solutions. 

    • Active TS/SCI clearance, or established eligibility to obtain and maintain it, depending on program requirements.

Job Description:

The Configuration and Change Control Manager is a senior individual contributor responsible for owning configuration discipline for the fielded V-BAT fleet, including aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and customer-specific configurations.This role ensures Shield AI maintains an accurate, traceable, and controlled understanding of what hardware, software, payload, and ground system configurations are deployed, which changes apply to which aircraft or customers, and how approved fixes, retrofits, releases, and service actions are controlled through execution.This position is critical to preventing configuration confusion across aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload variants, ground equipment configurations, fielded modifications, maintenance releases, and customer-specific baselines. The Configuration and Change Control Manager partners closely with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to ensure changes are documented, approved, communicated, traceable, and deployed to the correct assets.The role requires strong process discipline, technical fluency, attention to detail, and the ability to drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.

What you'll do:

  • Own and maintain the V-BAT fielded and as-maintained configuration baseline for aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and related sustainment assets.
  • Track aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload configurations, ground system configurations, fielded modifications, retrofit status, and customer-specific baselines.
  • Manage the change control process for fielded V-BAT systems, ensuring approved changes are controlled, traceable, and applied to the correct aircraft, customers, and configurations.
  • Support Engineering Change Requests, Engineering Change Orders, change impact assessments, release readiness reviews, retrofit plans, and service action planning.
  • Ensure fielded fixes, retrofits, software updates, hardware changes, payload changes, and service actions are tied to the correct serial numbers, configurations, customers, and effectivity ranges.
  • Maintain configuration records for deployed aircraft, spares, payloads, ground equipment, support equipment, and field-modified assets.
  • Partner with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to control changes across the V-BAT fleet.
  • Support release readiness reviews for software, hardware, payload, ground system, maintenance, and support equipment updates.
