Job Description:

As a Simulation Framework Engineer on the Simulation Framework Team, you will write the C++ and Python code, design adapters, and build custom plugins for our modeling and simulation (M&S) environments and core autonomy software. Your work is hands-on and technical, creating reusable, robust software patterns that abstract simulation details away from the core autonomy stack. Integration teams own program-level software integration; this role partners with and supports those teams by diagnosing framework, plugin, and interface issues in the simulation software the team designs and maintains.

You will write simulation plugins and software layers for DoD-recognized simulation backends including NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and the emerging Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF). Rather than managing teams, you will focus on the hands-on execution of migrating HMSSimBlocks capabilities to HMSF—building baseline adapters, porting custom modules, and ensuring functional parity—while maintaining active support and backward compatibility for programs currently relying on HMSSimBlocks.

What you'll do:

  • Write, compile, and maintain baseline software adapters, plugins, and interfaces in C++ and Python for AFSIM, NGTS, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF.
  • Execute the hands-on technical migration from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF, porting custom HMS simulation features to HMSF while maintaining active support for legacy HMSSimBlocks users.
  • Design, implement, and maintain a reusable CIGI plugin layer across our simulation frameworks to enable seamless visual communication with Aechelon image generators.
  • Ensure simulation frameworks and baseline plugins are designed for extensibility, writing clear templates and code architectures that allow other portfolios to plug in custom sensors or models.
  • Maintain functional parity across simulation plugins with respect to CSF (Common Scenario Format) file loading, DDS communication capabilities, GRID interface standards, and Hivemind SDK updates.
  • Support integration teams in debugging complex simulation-autonomy issues by analyzing framework behavior, network data, DDS traffic, and API call-stacks.
  • Write robust unit tests, automated integration tests, and clear code documentation to ensure simulation stability.

Required qualifications:

  • Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong software development background in C++ and Python within a Linux environment.
  • Solid software engineering fundamentals, including version control (Git), automated testing, and disciplined debugging.
  • Experience writing or maintaining plugins, baseline interfaces, or modeling frameworks for simulation environments such as AFSIM, NGTS, or similar.
  • Familiarity with network protocols (UDP/TCP), DDS middleware, serialization, or interface standards (such as CIGI).
  • Excellent technical troubleshooting skills and a desire to help other developers resolve integration bugs.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. SECRET security clearance (U.S. citizenship required).

    • Experience with ERP, MES, PLM, or digital manufacturing systems.  

    • Experience with automated manufacturing equipment, robotics, or advanced production technologies.  

    • Previous experience mentoring engineers or leading technical projects.

Job Description:

The Material Review Board (MRB) Engineer supports the evaluation and disposition of nonconforming hardware for fielded unmanned aircraft systems and related equipment. This role works within established engineering, quality, and configuration-control processes to assess damaged or nonconforming parts, develop repair and rework instructions, and help return hardware to service safely and efficiently.The engineer partners with responsible engineers, design and manufacturing engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Fleet Support, and Sustainment to investigate hardware issues and develop clear, technically sound, and traceable dispositions. The role supports post-production, depot, and field sustainment activities and contributes to improvements in repair documentation, inspection criteria, and recurring-issue resolution.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for an engineer who can independently resolve routine and moderately complex issues, contribute to more complex evaluations, and escalate decisions requiring specialized analysis or higher-level technical approval.

What you'll do:

  • Evaluate nonconforming material, damaged hardware, returned components, production escapes, field returns, and repairable assemblies.
  • Develop and document dispositions such as rework, repair, use-as-is, return-to-vendor, or scrap recommendations in accordance with established approval authority.
  • Create or update repair instructions, inspection criteria, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Review engineering drawings, specifications, inspection results, manufacturing records, repair history, photographs, and other field evidence.
  • Coordinate with responsible engineers and cross-functional partners to ensure dispositions are safe, technically sound, executable, and properly approved.
  • Support returned-material evaluations, production-quality deficiency reviews, field-hardware investigations, and production-escape resolution.
  • Maintain complete, accurate, traceable, and configuration-controlled MRB records.
  • Identify recurring nonconformances, manufacturing defects, supplier issues, field damage, and repair challenges; elevate trends for further investigation.
  • Provide technical input to root-cause and corrective-action activities in partnership with Failure Analysis, Reliability and Maintainability, Quality, and other engineering teams.
  • Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to improve repair instructions, inspection methods, acceptance criteria, and test processes.
  • Support supplier-quality investigations when purchased parts or assemblies affect sustainment or fleet readiness.
  • Contribute to standard repair development and the continuous improvement of MRB and sustainment workflows.
  • Balance engineering rigor, safety, quality, configuration control, field urgency, and aircraft-readiness needs.

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical, aerospace, electrical, manufacturing, materials, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant technical experience.
  • 4+ years of relevant experience in Material Review Board, quality engineering, manufacturing engineering, sustaining engineering, aerospace structures, aviation maintenance engineering, hardware product support, or complex hardware sustainment.
  • Experience evaluating nonconforming hardware, damaged components, returned material, production escapes, field failures, or repairable assemblies.
  • Working knowledge of nonconforming-material processes, MRB workflows, repair or rework dispositions, inspection records, engineering documentation, and corrective-action systems.

  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, inspection results, manufacturing records, repair records, and field evidence.
  • Sound technical judgment and the ability to recognize when an issue requires additional analysis or escalation to the appropriate engineering authority.
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills, including the ability to clearly explain a technical disposition and its supporting rationale.
  • Ability to work effectively across Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Fleet Support, Sustainment, and Operations.
  • Ability to manage multiple hardware issues and priorities in a fast-paced operating environment.

Why This Role Exists:

We build and operate the platform that our engineers and our customers rely on.

The platform isn't a product that's ever "finished." It's something we improve continuously. Every deployment, outage, bug, and annoying manual task is an opportunity to make the system better.

An L3 Platform Engineer is a fully contributing member of that effort.

This isn't a ticket factory. We expect engineers to think critically, collaborate closely, and continuously improve both the platform and the way we build it.

 

How We Work:

    Our engineering culture is built on Extreme Programming and Continuous Delivery.

    That means:

  • Pair programming is our default way of developing software.
  • We work in small batches.
  • We integrate continuously.
  • We automate repetitive work.
  • We test first whenever practical.
  • We optimize for learning and feedback instead of individual velocity.
  • The team owns the outcome.

    • If you're looking for a role where you're handed tickets, disappear for a week, and come back with a pull request, this isn't it.

What You'll Do:

  • Build and improve the platform that deploys and operates customer environments.
  • Develop infrastructure as code using Ansible, Terraform, Helm, Zarf, Big Bang, Packer, and related tooling.
  • Improve Kubernetes platforms and the systems around them.
  • Build deployment automation that reduces risk and removes manual work.
  • Pair with other engineers to design, implement, and troubleshoot platform capabilities.
  • Write automated tests for infrastructure and deployment workflows.
  • Improve observability, reliability, security, and recoverability.
  • Write documentation that explains why something exists—not just how to type commands.
  • Leave every part of the system better than you found it.

What We Expect:

    You Build for Change

    Software is never finished.

    Your goal isn't simply to make today's feature work.

    Your goal is to leave the code, infrastructure, and deployment process easier to change tomorrow.

    You Prefer Automation

    If humans perform the same task repeatedly, the system probably needs improvement.

    Manual processes are temporary.

    Automation is the destination.

    You Think in Small Batches

    Large changes hide mistakes.

    Small changes expose them.

    We value engineers who can decompose large problems into safe, incremental improvements.

    You Work as Part of the Team

    Platform engineering is a collaborative discipline.

    You bring potential solutions to the team, clearly explain your reasoning and tradeoffs, and help the team build a shared understanding of the code or design not merely produce it. You are responsible for understanding, validating, and clearly communicating the work you contribute.

    You Improve the System

    When something goes wrong, we don't stop at fixing it.

    We ask:

  • Why did this happen?
  • Why wasn't it detected sooner?
  • How do we make this impossible or at least unlikely next time?

    • Incidents should improve the platform.

Technical Expectations:

    You should be comfortable working across most of these areas:

  • Kubernetes
  • Linux
  • Networking fundamentals
  • Git and trunk-based development
  • GitLab CI
  • Infrastructure as Code
  • Ansible
  • Terraform
  • Helm
  • Zarf
  • Containers
  • PKI and certificate management
  • Secrets management
  • Observability
  • Infrastructure testing
  • Troubleshooting distributed systems

    • No one is expected to know everything.

    We do expect you to learn quickly and become productive in unfamiliar systems.

     

How Success Is Measured:

    Successful L3 engineers consistently help the team:

  • Deploy more frequently.
  • Deploy more safely.
  • Recover from failures faster.
  • Remove manual work.
  • Reduce operational complexity.
  • Improve documentation.
  • Increase confidence through testing.
  • Deliver changes in small, reversible increments.
  • Make the platform easier to operate and easier to evolve.

What We Value:

  • Simplicity over cleverness.
  • Evidence over opinion.
  • Learning over ego.
  • Automation over repetition.
  • Continuous improvement over perfection.
  • Team outcomes over individual heroics.

What Doesn't Fit Here:

  • Building knowledge silos.
  • Defending "the way we've always done it."
  • Optimizing for personal productivity instead of team throughput.
  • Big-bang rewrites when incremental change will work.
  • Manual work that should be automated.
  • Complexity without a clear operational benefit.

Job Description:

We are seeking a Senior Reliability Engineer to lead reliability engineering activities for the development, integration, testing, and operation of aircraft systems. This position will work across engineering disciplines to establish reliability requirements, manage system reliability budgets, perform reliability analyses, and identify design improvements that increase aircraft availability and mission success.

The successful candidate will have direct experience working on aircraft or other complex aerospace systems and be proficient with industry-standard reliability tools and methods. This engineer will serve as the primary reliability point of contact for assigned programs and communicate reliability performance, risks, and improvement plans to engineering leadership and customers.

What you'll do:

  • Develop and maintain aircraft-level reliability requirements, objectives, and program reliability plans.
  • Establish, allocate, and manage reliability budgets across systems, subsystems, and line-replaceable units.
  • Track predicted reliability against program targets and identify components or subsystems driving reliability risk.
  • Perform reliability predictions using component failure-rate data, operating environments, and mission profiles.
  • Conduct Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), and Reliability Block Diagram (RBD) analysis.
  • Support aircraft system safety assessments by providing failure rates, failure modes, and reliability data.
  • Develop and maintain Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF), Mean Time Between Critical Failure (MTBCF), mission reliability, availability, and related reliability metrics.
  • Perform reliability allocation, trade studies, sensitivity analyses, and design assessments.
  • Lead or support Failure Reporting, Analysis, and Corrective Action System (FRACAS) activities.
  • Analyze ground-test, flight-test, supplier, maintenance, and field-performance data to identify reliability trends.
  • Apply Weibull analysis and other statistical methods to evaluate failure behavior and predict component life.
  • Work with design teams to eliminate single-point failures, reduce high-risk failure modes, and improve fault tolerance.
  • Review supplier reliability analyses, test results, and supporting technical data.
  • Define reliability demonstration and growth-test requirements, success criteria, and data-collection needs.
  • Support technical reviews, including SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, and reliability review boards.
  • Communicate reliability performance, budget status, assumptions, risks, and recommended corrective actions to customers and program leadership.
  • Mentor junior engineers and improve organizational reliability processes, tools, and standards.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in reliability engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree 
  • Direct experience supporting aircraft development, integration, testing, sustainment, or operations.
  • Experience developing and managing reliability budgets at the system, subsystem, or equipment level.
  • Proficiency with reliability methods such as FMEA/FMECA, FTA, RBD, Weibull analysis, reliability predictions, and FRACAS.
  • Familiarity with reliability metrics such as MTBF, MTBCF, failure rate, mission reliability, operational availability, and inherent availability.
  • Experience using reliability analysis tools such as ReliaSoft, Windchill Quality Solutions, Isograph, RAM Commander, or equivalent.
  • Ability to interpret aircraft mission profiles, operating environments, duty cycles, and test data.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary engineering teams and suppliers.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, presentation, and customer communication skills.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any security clearance required for the program.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience working on military aircraft, unmanned aircraft, or other defense aerospace platforms.
  • Experience managing aircraft-level reliability allocations and flowing requirements down to suppliers.
  • Familiarity with MIL-HDBK-217, NPRD, EPRD, RIAC 217Plus, or equivalent reliability prediction methods and databases.
  • Experience integrating reliability engineering with system safety, maintainability, logistics, and availability analyses.
  • Knowledge of Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) and condition-based maintenance approaches.
  • Experience supporting environmental qualification, ground testing, flight testing, or reliability growth testing.
  • Familiarity with Model-Based Systems Engineering and requirements management tools.
  • Certified Reliability Engineer credentials or equivalent professional certification.
  • Active U.S. security clearance.

Success in this role:

    The successful engineer will establish a clear aircraft reliability strategy, maintain ownership of the reliability budget, and provide program leadership with an accurate view of reliability performance and risk. They will use analysis and test data to identify the primary reliability drivers and work directly with engineering teams and suppliers to improve the design before failures affect aircraft availability or mission performance.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Sr. Structural Analyst to support the analysis and testing of advanced UAVs. In this role, you will work closely with Mechanical Systems, Propulsion, Mechanisms, and other engineering disciplines to ensure the structural integrity of our lightweight, high-performance aircraft. You will contribute to the design, analysis, testing, and optimization of airframe structures and components, ensuring they meet performance, weight, and safety requirements.

This role is ideal for engineers with 5+ years of experience looking to gain expertise in finite element analysis (FEA), composite and metallic materials, and mechanical testing in a fast-paced, high-tech aerospace environment.

What you'll do:

  • Assist in building and refining finite element models (FEM) to evaluate the structural performance of UAV components.
  • Perform static, modal, fatigue, and vibration analyses to assess stress, deformation, and durability.
  • Conduct hand calculations to validate FEA results, ensuring accuracy and structural reliability.
  • Work with design engineers to optimize airframe structures, balancing weight, strength, and manufacturability.
  • Support the development of test plans for structural validation, including quasi-static, vibration, and shock testing.
  • Analyze flight telemetry and structural test data to improve modeling accuracy and correlate predictions with real-world performance.
  • Assist in defining load cases, material properties, and design margins for UAV airframe and mechanical components.
  • Document and present structural analysis reports and technical recommendations to engineering teams.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure structural requirements align with system performance goals.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of structural analysis methodologies, tools, and best practices.

Required qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in structural analysis, finite element modeling, or aircraft loads analysis AND B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related field. Alternatively, 3+ years of experience AND a M.S. in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering
  • Experience with FEA tools (FEMAP, NASTRAN, HyperWorks, ANSYS, Patran, or similar).
  • Ability to perform hand calculations for structural strength and stability analysis.
  • Knowledge of composite materials and lightweight aerospace structures.
  • Familiarity with mechanical testing methods (static, vibration, and/or fatigue).
  • Proficiency with data analysis tools (Excel, MATLAB, Python, or similar).
  • Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work in a team environment.
  • Ability to obtain a S//SAR level security clearance desired.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in aircraft structural design, UAV airframe development, or aerospace testing.
  • Hands-on experience with structural testing.
  • Exposure to CAD software (NX, Catia, SolidWorks) and PLM tools (Teamcenter or similar).
  • Understanding of aerospace industry standards, structural certification processes, and material selection.
  • Fatigue and damage tolerance (DaDT) experience including crack initiation and crack growth

Job Description:

As a System Integration Test Engineer, you will integrate and verify Shield AI's Hivemind mission autonomy software directly on Autonomous Collaborative Platform (ACP) flight hardware. You will serve as the hands-on technical bridge between autonomy algorithms and physical aircraft systems, working across Shield AI and aircraft platform vendors to verify system interfaces, validate edge compute performance, and resolve integration issues before flight testing. 

You will drive integration across Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) environments, both in Shield AI's internal laboratories and on-site at platform vendor integration facilities (including SIL, HIL, and iron bird test benches). You will turn high-level program objectives into executable integration plans, schedules, and test cards, systematically uncovering interface gaps early and formulating technical solutions to close them. This is an essential, high-impact role for an engineer who excels at the intersection where complex mission software meets real aircraft avionics and hardware. 

What you'll do:

  • Integrate Mission Autonomy on ACP Hardware: Deploy, integrate, and verify Hivemind mission autonomy software with actual ACP software and hardware in Shield AI and platform vendor SIL and HIL labs. 
  • Develop Test & Integration Plans: Develop detailed integration test plans, test cards, schedules, and objective success criteria across lab, ground, and flight test phases. 
  • Identify & Resolve Integration Gaps: Proactively identify architectural, interface, protocol, timing, and hardware/software gaps early; formulate concrete gap-closure plans, risk mitigations, and technical workarounds alongside Shield engineering and platform partners. 
  • Coordinate Joint Vendor Lab Execution: Partner directly with aircraft OEMs and platform vendors to coordinate lab readiness, align entry/exit criteria, deconflict bench time, and co-execute joint integration campaigns. 
  • Conduct Hands-On Lab Triage: Execute integration tests, configure test benches, and lead real-time troubleshooting of multi-system anomalies 
  • Drive Test Automation & Tooling: Coordinate across engineering teams to design and build test automation and simulation scripts to accelerate development 
  • Gate Flight Readiness & Support Flight Test: Enforce empirical test entry/exit criteria to gate delivery to aircraft ground and flight test; support flight test preparation, configuration validation, real-time troubleshooting, and post-flight data analysis. 
  • Support travel to test sites, customer events, and integration activities as required 

Required qualifications:

  • Typically requires 5+ years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Electrical, Computer, Mechanical, Systems Engineering, or related technical field, or 3+ years with a Master's degree. 
  • Lab & Hardware Integration: Demonstrated experience in system integration and test, including SIL, HIL, simulation, and flight test environments. 
  • Test Planning & Documentation: Proven ability to author clear, comprehensive integration test plans, procedures, and test cards, and translate test results into actionable engineering findings and gap closure roadmaps. 
  • Troubleshooting & Analysis: Strong experience troubleshooting complex system interfaces using telemetry, logs, packet capture tools (e.g., Wireshark), or hardware diagnostic equipment. 
  • Scripting & Linux: Proficiency with Linux operating systems and scripting languages (Python preferred) for test automation, data analysis, and hardware bench interfacing. 
  • Communication & Organization: Highly organized and methodical, with the ability to organize integration tasks, track dependencies, and coordinate work across distributed engineering teams and external partners. 
  • Travel Flexibility: Willingness and ability to travel periodically to platform vendor facilities and flight test locations as program needs require. 
  • Clearance & Citizenship: Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. DoD SECRET security clearance; U.S. citizenship required. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Autonomous & Uncrewed Systems: Experience with Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (ACP), Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), UAS (Group 4/5), or military aircraft mission systems. 
  • OEM / Prime Contractor Experience: Experience working directly inside aircraft manufacturer or defense prime contractor integration labs (e.g., Boeing, Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Anduril). 
  • Open Architecture Standards: Familiarity with open systems architectures such as Open Mission Systems (OMS), Universal Command and Control Interface (UCI), and Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA). 
  • Middleware & Frameworks: Experience with inter-process communication and messaging middleware (e.g., DDS, ROS/ROS2, ZeroMQ, gRPC). 
  • Safety & Airworthiness: Understanding of airworthiness processes, safety-of-flight standards, or software assurance guidelines (e.g., DO-178C, DO-254, MIL-STD-882E). 
  • Active Clearance: Active DoD SECRET or TOP SECRET clearance. 

What success looks like:

    Mission autonomy and aircraft hardware/avionics operate reliably and deterministically together in representative SIL and HIL labs well before aircraft ground and flight testing. Integration gaps and interface discrepancies are surfaced and resolved early, configurations and master test schedules are transparent and aligned across vendors, and rigorous lab test results provide the high-confidence empirical evidence needed to clear the aircraft for flight.

Job Description:

The Senior IT Systems Engineer builds, improves, and sustains classified infrastructure supporting engineering work. The role covers compute, virtualization, storage, networking, identity, endpoints, and security tooling in standalone and air-gapped environments.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor position. Responsibilities include racking and imaging hardware, building and hardening systems, automating repeatable work, troubleshooting difficult issues, and helping establish technical standards across sites. The engineer must be comfortable working independently, shifting across infrastructure disciplines when needed, and owning work from design through testing, documentation, and support.

The role sits between IT operations and accreditation. Systems must be secure, reliable, and ready for review by ISSMs and government assessors. Correct implementation the first time, backed by complete documentation and technical evidence, is an expected part of every build.

What you'll do:

    Build and operate classified infrastructure

  • Deploy, configure, and sustain Windows Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux systems, virtualization clusters, enterprise storage, and core infrastructure services in standalone and air-gapped enclaves.
  • Build and support VMware, Nutanix AHV/Prism, or similar virtualization environments. Nutanix experience is preferred.
  • Support high-density compute for AI/ML, simulation, and engineering workloads, including GPU node provisioning, performance troubleshooting, capacity planning, and coordination with facilities on rack space, power, and cooling.
  • Administer and support Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, PKI, certificate services, privileged access, and role-based access for isolated forests with no connection to corporate IT.
  • Build and maintain golden images and hardened baselines for servers, workstations, virtual desktops, and supporting infrastructure.
  • Manage patching, updates, software packages, and security content in disconnected environments through approved transfer and validation processes.
  • Administer backup, recovery, and continuity capabilities. Perform scheduled restore testing and document results and corrective actions.
  • Design, configure, and troubleshoot managed switching, VLANs, firewall rules, network segmentation, and approved network connections between facilities. Coordinate with network and security teams to maintain secure, supportable network standards.

    • Automate and standardize

  • Automate provisioning, configuration, patching, reporting, and compliance tasks using PowerShell, Ansible, Python, Terraform, or similar tools.
  • Create repeatable build processes, system baselines, checklists, and runbooks so systems can be deployed consistently rather than built by hand each time.
  • Improve existing processes by reducing manual steps, preventing common errors, and documenting effective methods for building and supporting systems.
  • Apply and validate DISA STIGs and SRGs using SCAP, STIG Viewer, ACAS/Nessus, scripted remediation, and other approved tools.
  • Maintain configuration-management records, as-built documentation, change records, and scan evidence so system configurations can be understood and defended later.
  • Review technical changes before production implementation, with attention to security, availability, rollback planning, and operational impact.

    • Support accreditation and security operations

  • Work with ISSMs, ISSOs, security teams, and program stakeholders to implement NIST SP 800-53, JSIG, RMF, and program-specific technical controls.
  • Provide technical documentation and evidence for authorization packages, continuous monitoring, assessments, and audits.
  • Implement and maintain audit logging and forwarding, including Elastic or similar centralized logging and SIEM tools.
  • Support vulnerability management through ACAS/Nessus scanning, findings triage, remediation planning, patching, and validation during approved maintenance windows.
  • Help resolve technical POA&M items and document remediation steps, validation results, and remaining risks.
  • Support approved media handling, file transfer, cross-domain processes, and contamination or spillage response alongside the security team.

    • Support users and sites

  • Act as a senior escalation point for classified IT issues that block engineering work or require deeper troubleshooting across multiple systems.
  • Identify and correct root causes rather than relying on repeated fixes or workarounds.
  • Support user-account, privileged-access, and workstation-access requests consistent with least privilege and separation-of-duties requirements.
  • Support new facility and enclave stand-ups from rack layout and cabling through infrastructure deployment, user onboarding, and operational handoff.
  • Mentor junior system administrators and site IT staff, review implementation work before production release, and help improve team standards.
  • Work independently, manage competing priorities, communicate risks early, and bring practical solutions to the team.

Required qualifications:

  • Strong hands-on experience with Windows Server, Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, PKI, and enterprise endpoint management.
  • Experience administering Red Hat Enterprise Linux or similar enterprise Linux systems.
  • Experience with VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V, or similar enterprise virtualization platforms. Nutanix AHV/Prism experience is preferred.
  • Experience with enterprise storage, backup/recovery, and capacity planning.
  • Experience with managed switching, VLANs, firewall administration, network segmentation, and troubleshooting network connectivity.
  • Experience with PowerShell and infrastructure automation. Experience with Ansible, Python, Terraform, or similar tools is a plus.
  • Experience applying DISA STIGs, using SCAP/STIG Viewer, supporting ACAS/Nessus findings, and working in RMF, NIST SP 800-53, JSIG, or similarly regulated environments.
  • Experience operating in disconnected, air-gapped, classified, or highly controlled environments.
  • Ability to document work clearly, follow change control, validate results, and build systems that are easy for others to support.
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-moving environment, shift between infrastructure disciplines when needed, and make sound technical decisions without requiring detailed direction.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Nutanix AHV, Prism Central, Files, Flow, or cluster lifecycle management.
  • GPU server, AI/ML, simulation, VDI, or high-performance compute infrastructure.
  • Elastic, Splunk, or other centralized logging and SIEM platforms.
  • Disconnected WSUS, offline patching, software-repository management, or approved media-transfer workflows.
  • Data-center buildouts, rack-and-stack, structured cabling, power/cooling coordination, and new-facility stand-ups.
  • Relevant technical or security certifications, such as Security+, CISSP, RHCSA/RHCE, VMware VCP, Nutanix NCA/NCP, Microsoft certifications, or CCNA/CCNP.

We are seeking a highly skilled Hardware in the Loop Lab Technician to support the fabrication, instrumentation, and testing of new aerospace products. This role is ideal for a hands-on builder who thrives in dynamic environments, has deep experience working with aircraft systems and fabrication methods, and has a background building and maintaining a Systems Integration Lab.

  • Document test outcomes clearly and report anomalies or irregularities in a timely manner.
  • Ensure a clean, organized, and safe workspace across shop, lab, and composite work areas.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in instrumentation standards, testing procedures, and fabrication workflows.
  • Source and manage inventory for parts and equipment needed for component repair or replacement.

  • Hands-on experience in machine shop operations, including manual and/or CNC tools.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings, schematics, and detailed work instructions.
  • Comfortable working in shop and lab environments with exposure to noise, dust, and chemicals.
  • Ability to lift and move parts and equipment (up to 50 lbs.) and perform physical work for extended periods.

We build advanced autonomous systems for defense markets—complex hardware and software products that demand world-class financial modeling, rigorous planning, and the ability to turn complexity into clarity. 

We seek a Senior Corporate FP&A Lead with deep 3 statement modeling experience, a strong corporate FP&A background in a publicly traded company, and a proven track record architecting and owning financial models and planning processes. You will serve as the analytical engine of Corporate FP&A: designing and owning the company’s fully integrated three statement and consolidated plan, leading the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), owning the company cash model, and producing Board- and Executive-ready outputs that shape decisions at the C-suite and Board level. 

Candidates must bring elite modeling expertise, mastery of complex HW/SW planning and unit economics, end-to-end ownership of the full planning cycle (AOP, forecast, long-range plan), and comfort operating in a fast-paced, high growth environment. This role has a natural path to FP&A and finance leadership as the company scales. 

What you'll do:

    Own and Build the Financial Model & Consolidated Plan 
  • Architect and maintain a fully integrated, scalable, three statement model grounded in operational drivers, unit economics, and industry benchmarks. 
  • Own consolidated planning and end-to-end line-item ownership across the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow—including equity planning (stock-based comp, share count, dilution, and equity roll-forward). 
  • Lead the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), including scenario modeling, sensitivities, and driver-based forecasting. 
  • Translate production ramps, R&D investments, contract timing, government milestones, and GTM strategy directly into financial outcomes. 
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of risks, opportunities, capital needs, and strategic inflection points. 
    • Lead the Annual Operating Plan (AOP) & Forecasting 
  • Own the AOP process end to end—calendar, templates, driver frameworks, consolidation, and executive review. 
  • Partner with functional and business leaders to build bottoms-up budgets that reconcile to top-down targets. 
  • Run the recurring forecast cycle, connecting short-term forecasting with the long-range plan. 
  • Take full accountability for forecast accuracy, improving results with each actualized quarter. 
    • Own the Company Cash Model 
  • Build and own rolling cash flow forecasts across working capital, inventory, milestone payments, production cycles, and CapEx. 
  • Model government contract payment timing, production curves, and program cash profiles. 
  • Identify liquidity risks early and support capital allocation and financing strategies. 
    • Drive Board & Executive Reporting 
  • Own the creation of Board of Directors and eStaff QBR materials—narratives, financial packages, and KPI dashboards. 
  • Translate complex financial and operational results into clear, executive-ready insights. 
  • Deliver Board-ready outputs including plan-vs-actual analysis, variance drivers, and strategic context. 
    • Digitize & Scale Planning Infrastructure 
  • Partner with data engineering/systems teams to evolve planning from Excel into modern cloud-based planning tools. 
  • Design modular, scalable model architectures; use Excel only where it provides meaningful analytical leverage. 
  • Integrate automation and analytics to improve clarity, reduce manual work, and increase decision velocity. 
    • Partner Across the Company 
  • Work closely with senior leaders on forward-looking financial planning and strategy. 
  • Translate engineering, program, and operations plans into financial impacts. 
  • Develop a point of view on unit economics, efficiency, scale, profitability, and capital allocation. 
  • Present insights that accelerate execution and elevate decision quality. 

Required qualifications:

  • 8–10 years of experience, including significant time in corporate FP&A. 
  • Direct FP&A experience in a publicly traded company. 
  • Proven ownership of scalable three statement models, AOP and LRP development, consolidated planning, and line-item ownership (including equity planning). 
  • Ownership of the company cash model and liquidity forecasting. 
  • Exceptional Excel modeling capability; fluent in multi scenario three statement modeling, beat-and-raise frameworks, and driver-based forecasting. 
  • Strong GAAP proficiency and command of financial statement mechanics. 
  • Demonstrated ability to build Board- and executive-ready materials and distill complex financial and technical information into clear insights for executives and the Board. 
  • Thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments with high accuracy and strong judgment. 
  • Systems-oriented mindset; comfortable partnering with data and systems teams. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Familiarity with government contract economics, milestone based revenue, and program accounting. 
  • Experience with equity / stock-based comp planning and share count and dilution modeling. 
  • Exposure to manufacturing scale, supply chain dynamics, and hardware production cycles. 
  • Experience implementing or scaling cloud-based planning tools (e.g., Anaplan, Pigment, Adaptive). 

Who you are:

  • An analytical athlete with exceptional modeling intuition and attention to detail. 
  • A structured, clear thinker who simplifies complexity without losing nuance. 
  • Fast, accurate, and calm under pressure. 
  • Curious, forward-looking, and driven to understand what truly moves the business. 
  • A strong communicator who elevates decision quality across the company. 
  • Mission-driven and energized by solving complex, high impact problems. 

Why this role matters:

    You will build and own the financial model and consolidated plan that define how the business is understood—internally, at the eStaff level, and at the Board. Your work will guide the AOP, capital allocation, cash strategy, investments, and long-range ambitions. This is Corporate FP&A at its highest level: high complexity, high visibility, high impact—and a direct path to FP&A and finance leadership.

Shield AI is seeking an ambitious, experienced Senior Manager, Revenue Accounting to join our growing Accounting team at one of the fastest-growing technology companies in Defense & Aerospace. This role will lead the end-to-end revenue accounting process, including technical revenue accounting, operational revenue accounting, contract review, monthly close activities, and order-to-cash process design. The Senior Manager will serve as a key revenue accounting leader and cross-functional partner to Legal, Business Development, Revenue Operations, Program Finance, Billing, Collections, and FP&A to ensure revenue is recognized accurately, timely, and in accordance with ASC 606. This role will also help design and scale revenue accounting processes, controls, systems, and workflows to support Shield AI’s continued international growth.

What you'll do:

  • Lead the end-to-end revenue accounting process, including customer contract review, revenue recognition conclusions, monthly revenue close activities, and operational execution in accordance with ASC 606.
  • Review revenue-related account reconciliations, including deferred revenue, unbilled receivables, contract assets, contract liabilities, accounts receivable, and other order-to-cash related balances.
  • Manage and lead the preparation, review, and approval of customer contracts, ensuring appropriate revenue recognition while partnering with Sales, Legal, Business Development, Revenue Operations, and Program Finance on deal structure, contractual terms, and revenue guidance implementation.
  • Serve as one of the company’s subject matter experts on ASC 606, providing technical accounting guidance on complex revenue arrangements, non-standard contract terms, variable consideration, contract modifications, performance obligations, and other revenue recognition matters.
  • Own and evolve revenue accounting policies, including SSP analyses, allocation methodologies, and revenue recognition positions as new products, pricing models, geographies, and contract structures are introduced.
  • Design, document, and improve order-to-cash processes to ensure accuracy, scalability, operational efficiency, and strong internal controls across contract review, billing, revenue recognition, collections handoffs, and reporting.
  • Identify process gaps, control risks, and system limitations within the revenue accounting and order-to-cash lifecycle, and lead initiatives to improve process quality, automation, scalability, and audit readiness.
  • Support internal and external audits by preparing and reviewing audit schedules, responding to technical accounting inquiries, and ensuring revenue accounting documentation is complete, accurate, and well-controlled.
  • Mentor and develop revenue accounting team members, providing coaching, review, prioritization, and guidance to support team growth and operational excellence.

Required qualifications:

  • 8+ years of relevant accounting experience, including significant experience in technical revenue accounting under ASC 606 and/or IFRS 15.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA preferred.
  • Strong revenue recognition experience, including experience reviewing complex customer contracts and assessing accounting conclusions under ASC 606.
  • Experience leading or managing revenue accounting close activities, including review of journal entries, account reconciliations, and revenue-related balance sheet accounts.
  • Deep understanding of order-to-cash processes and how technical accounting decisions impact billing, collections, revenue recognition, reporting, and controls.
  • Experience designing, improving, or scaling revenue accounting and order-to-cash processes in a high-growth or complex business environment.
  • Experience with revenue recognition, ERP, CRM, and/or order-to-cash systems, such as Salesforce or equivalent tools.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex technical accounting issues into clear, actionable guidance for cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Legal, Sales, Business Development, Revenue Operations, Billing, Collections, Program Finance, FP&A, Systems, and external auditors.
  • Strong understanding of internal controls, audit requirements, and SOX compliance protocols.
  • Demonstrated ability to balance technical accounting rigor with operational practicality and business partnership.
  • Data-driven mindset with a proactive approach to process improvement, automation, and scalable operations.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Big 4 public accounting experience preferred.
  • Public company experience preferred.
  • Experience with international expansion, including EMEA revenue accounting considerations.
  • Experience in high-growth technology, SaaS, PaaS, Defense, Aerospace, manufacturing, or complex contract environments.
  • Experience with long-term contracts, milestone billing, project-based revenue recognition, government contracts, or complex commercial arrangements.
  • Experience implementing or optimizing revenue recognition, billing, ERP, CRM, or order-to-cash systems.

The role requires someone who can understand technical concepts, dependencies, and delivery risks well enough to coordinate effectively across functional, technical, integration, data, and testing teams, but who is not expected to serve as the hands-on technical lead or provide technical solution ownership. Success is defined by on-time execution, stakeholder alignment, effective governance, and sustainable business adoption of ERP-enabled change.

What you'll do:

  • Lead end-to-end project management for Oracle Fusion ERP implementations, enhancements, migrations, and transformation programs from charter through go-live and hypercare.

  • Build and maintain core project management deliverables including schedules, milestone plans, RAID logs, dependency trackers, RACI matrices, and executive status reporting.  
  • Coordinate closely with business stakeholders, IT teams, systems integrators, and vendor partners to align scope, timing, deliverables, and decisions.
  • Facilitate planning, requirements, fit-gap, and workstream checkpoint sessions with functional leads and business process owners.

  • Actively manage the project schedule, critical path, overdue actions, and cross-workstream blockers to keep delivery on track.
  • Coordinate delivery activities across integrations, reporting, data migration, testing, cutover, and deployment without acting as the technical authority for solution design.
  • Partner with program leadership and finance stakeholders on budget tracking, forecast updates, variance reporting, and go-live readiness activities.
  • Manage vendor and systems integrator performance against plans, milestones, and contractual commitments.

  • Ability to understand technical concepts, integration dependencies, environment readiness, data migration risks, and testing implications sufficiently to coordinate teams and drive delivery, without being the primary technical resource.
  • Strong command of project management fundamentals including scope, schedule, RAID management, dependency tracking, status reporting, and governance.
  • Experience working with executive sponsors, business process owners, IT leaders, vendors, and third-party systems integrators.

    Experience in a PMO or enterprise transformation office supporting large cross-functional programs is preferred. Experience with Oracle Fusion workstreams such as Finance, Procurement, Supply Chain, Projects, HCM, or Reporting/Analytics is helpful. Additional value comes from cloud ERP transformation experience, enterprise governance exposure, and prior experience as a business analyst, functional lead, or ERP power user.

Job Description:

We are seeking a Senior Propulsion Design Engineer to support the development and delivery of propulsion hardware for the X-BAT platform, a next-generation UAV powered by a low-bypass turbofan engine. This role spans the full lifecycle of propulsion system components - from early layout and design through production release, test support, and flight operations.

You will be a key contributor to turning propulsion architecture into manufacturable, testable, and flight-ready hardware across the engine, fuel, oil, and bleed air systems. This role is hands-on, detail-oriented, and highly cross-functional - requiring close collaboration with propulsion REs, technicians, machinists, production, controls, airframe, and flight test teams.

What you will do in this role:

  • Own the design and release of propulsion hardware supporting the engine, fuel, oil, and bleed air systems.
  • Develop and maintain CAD models, drawings, and assemblies using Siemens NX with proper GD&T.
  • Translate propulsion architecture and requirements into hardware that is manufacturable, testable, and robust in flight.
  • Work directly with the machine shop, production, and technicians to support builds, resolve non-conformances, and drive iterative improvements.
  • Support test campaigns by providing hardware design support, instrumentation accommodation, and rapid iteration based on test findings.
  • Apply engineering judgment and analysis (e.g., hand calcs, ANSYS, FEA, GFSSP, REFPROP) to support sizing, load cases, and design validation.
  • Support configuration management, BOM control, and change processes using Teamcenter or equivalent PLM.
  • Participate in design reviews, interface control efforts, and root cause investigations related to propulsion hardware.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in aerospace hardware design, preferably supporting propulsion systems.
  • Proficiency in CAD modeling and drawing creation (NX preferred) with sound application of GD&T.
  • Experience working directly with production, technicians, and machine shops to resolve real-world build issues.
  • Understanding of design for manufacturing, including machining limitations, tolerance stack-ups, and assembly workflows.
  • Some hands-on experience developing assembly guidance and supporting hardware builds and test integration.
  • U.S. Citizenship or ability to comply with ITAR requirements.
  • Ability to obtain a S//SAR level security clearance desired.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with jet propulsion systems on UAVs or tactical aircraft.
  • Familiarity with GFSSP, REFPROP, ANSYS, or FEA to support design trade studies and validation.
  • Ability to write Python scripts for design automation, analysis, or data processing.
  • Experience with interface control, fastener selection for high-vibration environments, and high-temperature materials.
  • Experience designing hardware in test-driven development environments with rapid iteration cycles.
  • M.S. in Aerospace Engineering or a related discipline.

  • Partner with propulsion REs and controls engineers to ensure test coverage closes risk against CONOPS and mission profiles.
  • Drive root cause investigations for test anomalies and implement corrective actions.

Job Description:

The Reliability and Maintainability Engineer is a senior-level individual contributor responsible for driving investigation, root cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement for V-BAT field failures, repeat defects, and complex technical issues requiring deeper engineering analysis.This role owns the technical investigation path for fielded V-BAT issues by using logs, returned hardware, test data, maintenance records, operational context, configuration data, and fleet trends to determine failure modes, root causes, contributing factors, and corrective actions. The Reliability and Maintainability Engineer partners closely with Fleet Support Engineering, Product Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to ensure field failures are understood, contained, corrected, and prevented from recurring.This role is accountable for translating field issues into structured technical investigations, verified corrective actions, reliability improvements, maintainability improvements, and clear product health insights that improve fleet readiness, customer support, and long-term system performance.

What you'll do:

  • Lead engineering investigations for V-BAT field failures, repeat defects, reliability issues, maintainability issues, and complex technical escalations.
  • Drive Root Cause and Corrective Action investigations for fielded V-BAT issues, including containment, root cause identification, corrective action planning, verification, and closure.
  • Reproduce and analyze field issues using logs, returned hardware, test data, maintenance records, operational context, configuration data, environmental conditions, and customer-reported symptoms.
  • Partner with Fleet Support Engineers, Product Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to investigate and resolve fielded system issues.
  • Determine whether issues are caused by design, manufacturing, supplier quality, configuration, software, operator use, environmental exposure, maintenance practices, documentation gaps, or system integration effects.
  • Lead and support returned material analysis, teardown reviews, bench testing, inspection planning, fault isolation, and failure replication activities.
  • Document failure modes, root cause, contributing factors, containment actions, corrective actions, verification plans, and recurrence-prevention measures.
  • Drive corrective actions through closure by ensuring actions have owners, due dates, verification methods, and measurable field-improvement outcomes.
  • Identify reliability and maintainability trends from field failures, repeat defects, maintenance data, test results, and product health indicators.
  • Recommend new tests, inspections, diagnostics, design changes, process changes, maintenance updates, or supplier quality actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Provide technical input to product health reviews, reliability readouts, sustainment reviews, fleet readiness assessments, and leadership updates.
  • Support development and improvement of R&M processes, including field failure review, FRACAS, RCCA, reliability growth tracking, maintainability feedback loops, and corrective action management.
  • Work with Product Engineering to ensure field-failure findings are translated into design improvements, retrofit plans, software updates, service actions, or configuration changes where appropriate.
  • Work with Quality and Manufacturing to determine whether failures are linked to process escapes, inspection gaps, workmanship issues, supplier defects, or production variation.
  • Work with Fleet Support and Operations to understand operational impact, maintenance burden, customer effects, and urgency of fielded system issues.
  • Provide clear technical recommendations on containment, inspection, repair, replacement, retrofit, service guidance, or fleet-level mitigation.
  • Communicate investigation findings, risks, corrective actions, and verification status clearly to technical teams, sustainment leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Support X-BAT lessons learned where V-BAT reliability, maintainability, and field-failure experience can inform future design, sustainment, diagnostics, repairability, and lifecycle planning.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Reliability Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 4+ years of experience in reliability engineering, maintainability engineering, failure analysis, systems engineering, quality engineering, aviation sustainment, product support, manufacturing engineering, or complex hardware sustainment.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting technical investigations for field failures, repeat defects, hardware issues, system-level issues, or complex product performance problems.
  • Experience driving Root Cause and Corrective Action investigations from initial problem statement through containment, root cause, corrective action, verification, and closure.
  • Strong ability to analyze hardware, software behavior, logs, test data, returned material, field reports, configuration history, maintenance records, and operational context.
  • Familiarity with structured problem-solving and failure-analysis methods such as 5 Whys, fault tree analysis, fishbone diagrams, 8D, FMEA/FMECA, FRACAS, fault isolation, or similar methods.
  • Ability to distinguish between design, manufacturing, supplier quality, configuration, software, operator, environmental, maintenance, and documentation-related contributors.
  • Experience working across Product Engineering, Fleet Support, Quality, Manufacturing, Reliability Data Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations to resolve technical issues.
  • Strong technical judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate ambiguous field reports, identify likely failure modes, and define practical next steps.
  • Ability to convert technical findings into clear corrective actions, verification plans, risk assessments, and product or process improvement recommendations.
  • Experience supporting customer-impacting technical issues in aviation, unmanned systems, robotics, defense, manufacturing, aerospace, or complex electromechanical systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical findings, investigation rationale, corrective actions, and leadership-level summaries.
  • Ability to operate independently while partnering with senior technical leaders to drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.
  • Ability to balance engineering rigor, investigation depth, field urgency, customer impact, and fleet-readiness needs.
  • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance as required by customers.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with unmanned aircraft systems, aviation sustainment, aerospace manufacturing, defense products, robotics, or deployed hardware systems.
  • Experience with FRACAS, reliability growth programs, fleet reliability tracking, MTBF/MTBUR analysis, Weibull analysis, reliability block diagrams, maintainability analysis, or product health dashboards.
  • Experience analyzing aircraft logs, flight data, maintenance data, telemetry, software logs, test results, inspection findings, or returned hardware.
  • Familiarity with RCCA, MRB, ECO/ECR processes, configuration management, service bulletins, maintenance releases, retrofit planning, or field service actions.
  • Experience investigating failures in avionics, propulsion, power systems, flight controls, structures, payload interfaces, ground equipment, support equipment, or complex electromechanical assemblies.
  • Experience working with Reliability Data Engineering, data analytics, or fleet health monitoring teams to identify failure trends and emerging risks.
  • Experience supporting fielded products where technical recommendations directly affect readiness, safety, maintainability, or customer operations.
  • Experience working in a startup, high-growth, defense technology, aerospace, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environment.
  • Advanced degree in Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline preferred but not required.

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Site Infrastructure Engineer to plan, design, document, and support physical IT infrastructure across offices, engineering facilities, labs, manufacturing environments, and data centers.
 
As part of the Cloud & Infrastructure team within Enterprise Operations, this role will help deliver scalable and reliable site infrastructure, including rack layouts, structured cabling, power and cooling capacity, MDF/IDF design, DCIM, equipment sizing, and infrastructure documentation. You will partner closely with Network, Systems, Cloud, Security, Facilities, Workplace, and external vendors to support new site buildouts, expansions, relocations, and data center deployments.

What you'll do:

    * Plan and design physical IT infrastructure for offices, labs, manufacturing facilities, and data centers.
    * Lead and support new site buildouts, office expansions and relocations, data center deployments, hardware refreshes, and infrastructure moves.
    * Develop rack layouts, MDF/IDF requirements, equipment placement plans, and infrastructure bills of materials.
    * Create and maintain accurate rack elevations, physical connectivity diagrams, equipment records, cable documentation, and DCIM data across office and data center environments.
    * Support capacity planning across rack space, site and data center power, cooling, cabling, and equipment growth.
    * Administer and improve DCIM/IPAM/CMDB platforms such as Nautobot, NetBox, Device42, or equivalent.
    * Establish and maintain physical infrastructure documentation and labeling standards to ensure environments remain accurately documented throughout their lifecycle.
    * Review floor plans, low-voltage drawings, vendor designs, proposals, and statements of work.
    * Manage site and data center circuit inventory and lifecycle planning, including circuit documentation, utilization and capacity planning, renewal tracking, upgrades, relocations, disconnects, and coordination with carriers and internal procurement teams. 
    * Coordinate with architects, contractors, colocation providers, carriers, OEMs, and field-service vendors.
    * Partner with Network, Systems, and Cloud Engineering teams to ensure site and data center infrastructure supports compute, storage, connectivity, wireless, security, hybrid connectivity, and public cloud requirements.
    * Identify capacity constraints, documentation gaps, and opportunities to improve infrastructure standards and processes.
    * Provide technical guidance to junior engineers and support teams as needed.

Required Qualifications:

    * 5+ years of experience in data center, enterprise site, or physical IT infrastructure engineering.
    * Experience designing and supporting infrastructure across offices, data centers, labs, or similar enterprise environments.
    * Strong experience creating and maintaining rack elevations, physical infrastructure diagrams, cabling documentation, equipment layouts, and infrastructure records.
    * Strong knowledge of rack design, structured copper/fiber cabling, equipment placement, and physical infrastructure standards.
    * Strong working knowledge of data center and site power, including A/B power, UPS/PDU systems, circuit capacity, equipment power draw, redundancy, and related cooling/airflow considerations.
    * Experience designing MDF/IDF environments and sizing infrastructure for new or expanding facilities.
    * Experience with DCIM/IPAM/CMDB platforms such as Nautobot, NetBox, Device42, Sunbird, or similar.
    * Working understanding of enterprise networking, including switching, wireless, WAN connectivity, and carrier services.
    * Ability to interpret architectural drawings, floor plans, low-voltage designs, and equipment specifications.
    * Experience working with colocation providers, low-voltage contractors, carriers, and technology vendors.
    * Strong technical documentation, communication, and organizational skills.
    * Ability to independently execute infrastructure projects from planning through deployment.
    * Ability to travel periodically for site and data center deployments.


Preferred Qualifications:

    * Experience supporting a geographically distributed or rapidly growing enterprise.
    * Experience across offices, engineering labs, manufacturing environments, and colocation data centers.
    * Hands-on experience with Nautobot or NetBox for DCIM, IPAM, rack elevations, circuits, and infrastructure documentation.
    * Experience supporting data center migrations, expansions, or greenfield site deployments.
    * Familiarity with hybrid infrastructure and public cloud platforms such as AWS and Azure, including connectivity between enterprise sites, data centers, and cloud environments.
    * Familiarity with infrastructure from vendors such as Juniper, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Dell, APC, or Vertiv.
    * Experience developing infrastructure BOMs, cost estimates, lifecycle plans, and capacity forecasts.
    * Experience using APIs, scripting, or automation to improve DCIM and infrastructure lifecycle management.
    * Experience within aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or other regulated environments.
    * Relevant certifications such as BICSI, CDCP, CCNA/CCNP, or equivalent.

This role sits at the boundary between hardware and application software. You will own the Linux platform and software delivery foundations of our edge compute systems, from hardware bring-up and operating system configuration through reproducible builds, packaging, deployment and operation in the field. 

NixOS is our primary deployed operating system and a core technology for this role. You will help evolve and maintain our NixOS-based platform, while also supporting and improving other Linux distributions and environments used across our edge systems. You will develop C++ software and platform tooling, package software and hardware dependencies, integrate vendor BSPs and drivers, and ensure we can reliably build, configure and deploy complete systems across our supported hardware and Linux environments. 

You don't need to already be a NixOS expert. We are looking for strong software engineers with experience in Linux systems, embedded Linux or adjacent platform technologies who are interested in developing deep expertise in NixOS. Experience with NixOS is highly valued, as is experience with technologies such as Yocto, Buildroot, Debian/Ubuntu or other Linux build and distribution systems. 

The goal is simple: make the path from hardware to deployed software reproducible, reliable and predictable.

What you'll do:

    • Own and evolve the embedded Linux platforms deployed across our edge compute systems, with NixOS as a primary focus. 

    • Build and maintain operating system images, configurations and software environments for production hardware across multiple Linux distributions. 

    • Evolve and maintain our NixOS platform, including system configuration, packaging and integration of application and hardware dependencies. 

    • Develop C++ systems software and platform tooling that supports the operation, configuration and deployment of our edge systems. 

    • Integrate and maintain vendor BSPs, Linux kernels, device trees, drivers, and hardware-specific dependencies. 

    • Package application software, system components and third-party dependencies using Nix and other platform-appropriate mechanisms. 

    • Develop and improve the mechanisms used to build, configure, version, test and deploy complete software systems onto edge devices. 

    • Bring up new compute platforms and hardware configurations and establish a clear path from initial integration through production deployment. 

    • Define clean interfaces between the operating system, hardware platform and application software so application teams can build on stable and well-supported foundations. 

    • Diagnose challenging problems across application software, userspace Linux, the kernel, drivers and hardware interfaces. 

    • Improve system reliability, boot behaviour, performance, security and resource utilisation. 

    • Develop automated build, test and validation infrastructure for operating system images and hardware/software integration. 

    • Work closely with application, autonomy, perception, hardware and test engineers to integrate new capabilities and hardware into the platform. 

    • Improve the developer experience for engineers building, testing and deploying software onto edge systems. 

    • Establish engineering practices that make deployed systems reproducible, traceable and recoverable.

Required qualifications:

    • Strong understanding of Linux systems, from userspace through to the kernel and hardware interfaces. 

    • Experience building, configuring or maintaining Linux systems used as part of a deployed product. 

    • Experience with Nix/NixOS, Yocto, Buildroot, Debian/Ubuntu or similar Linux build and distribution technologies. Deep NixOS experience is highly valued but not required. 

    • Strong software engineering experience in modern C++, ideally developing systems software, platform software or software for Linux-based edge devices. 

    • Experience with reproducible builds, dependency management, software packaging or software supply chains. 

    • Experience diagnosing difficult problems that cross application, operating system and hardware boundaries. 

    • Experience with CI/CD and automated build and test systems. 

    • Ability to take ownership of complex platform problems and drive them from initial investigation through deployment and long-term support.

As a Senior Software Engineer (Networking & OS) on V-BAT, you will be instrumental in designing, implementing, and optimizing the network infrastructure for our Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) which is deployed in some of the most challenging environments worldwide. V-BAT is designed to operate in contested, GNSS-denied airspace, and our network must maintain highly reliable, secure, and efficient communication between all air and ground devices.

    • Design and build custom, resilient Layer 2 / Layer 3 network topologies optimized specifically for V-BAT mission profiles, focusing on device isolation, dynamic traffic management, and transmitting traffic across multiple links. 

    • Implement networking features directly on embedded Linux operating systems, including custom routing, TUN/TAP interfaces, user-space tunnels, and socket-level applications. 

    • Work backward from operator capabilities to build bandwidth-optimized, low-latency communication paths over lossy or constrained radio and satellite links. 

    • Write clean, production-grade C, C++, or Python code to build things like software-defined network interfaces, traffic shaping policies, and link failover mechanisms. 

    • Partner with software engineers, hardware engineers, and field operators to validate end-to-end network performance in both hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) labs and flight test environments.

You will work from first principles to define requirements, make sound design decisions, and drive the selected solutions through detailed design, integration, qualification, and production. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

  • Actuator and Mechanism Design: Own actuator selection and sizing, sequencing, redundancy management, failure mode analysis, and interfaces with the mechanisms they actuate.
  • Vehicle Mechanism Integration: Drive integration of actuation systems with control surfaces, weapons bay doors, and other vehicle mechanisms, including timing, load, sealing, and structural interface requirements.
  • Power and Thermal Integration: Own actuator power architecture and load-analysis interfaces with EPS, and heat-generation and heat-rejection interfaces with thermal management.
  • Requirements and Verification: Define, allocate, and own verification traceability for actuation system requirements with FCAS, EPS, thermal management, structures, and propulsion IPTs.
  • Targeted Technical Decisions: Perform focused technology assessments when needed to resolve specific actuation design and integration risks.
  • Qualification and Hardware Delivery: Define and execute qualification test plans per MIL-STD-810, using results to mature the design into production-ready hardware and support MIL-HDBK-516 Airworthiness Certification.
  • Program Execution: Lead design-maturity and qualification-status reviews at SRR, PDR, and CDR.

Required qualifications:

  • Clearance required: US Citizens Only & Must have an Active Secret or higher clearance.
  • Experience: 8 to 15 years in aircraft actuation systems design, with hands-on depth in electric actuation, including EMA or EHA, or centralized hydraulics and working knowledge of the other.
  • Education: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Proven track record sourcing COTS/custom aerospace components, driving suppliers to schedule, and assembling benchtop or vehicle-level test setups.
  • Autonomy: Demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize technical tasks without oversight, and deliver functional hardware under tight timelines.
  • Actuation Design Fundamentals: Demonstrated depth in actuator sizing, power and thermal interfaces, FMEA, redundancy management, and mechanical mechanism integration.
  • Systems Integration: Demonstrated experience leading multi-disciplinary actuation design and integration efforts with electrical power, thermal management, structures, and adjacent mechanical systems stakeholders.
  • Standards and Reviews: Familiarity with MIL-HDBK-516 and MIL-STD-810 as applied to actuation and mechanical systems, and experience supporting SRR, PDR, and CDR on a DoD or fighter-class aircraft program.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior fighter or fighter-adjacent program experience, manned or unmanned.
  • Experience developing electric actuation architectures for aircraft control surfaces or other mechanisms.
  • Weapons bay mechanism or store separation-adjacent mechanical systems experience.
