  • Proven track record in market mapping, competitive intelligence, and candidate generation for highly specialized, difficult-to-fill, and business-critical roles.
  • Demonstrated experience sourcing across multiple disciplines, which may include Engineering, Software, AI/ML, Hardware, Manufacturing, Operations, Product, Program Management, Commercial, G&A, and other corporate functions.
  • Deep expertise in advanced Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, HireEZ, SeekOut, GitHub, and other modern sourcing platforms, with the ability to identify talent across diverse EU markets.
  • Strong knowledge of the EU talent landscape, including regional talent hubs, competitor ecosystems, candidate behaviors, market dynamics, and differences in recruiting across countries.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a consultative partner to recruiters, hiring managers, and senior leaders, influencing hiring strategy through market insights and talent intelligence.
  • Hands-on experience building or leveraging AI-powered sourcing workflows, agentic AI tools, workflow automations, or practical AI solutions that improve recruiting or business processes.
  • Direct experience using AI development environments or coding assistants (such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar tools) to create repeatable sourcing workflows, structured research outputs, market intelligence, process automation, or operational documentation.
  • Experience building and maintaining long-term relationships with passive, niche, senior, or otherwise difficult-to-engage talent across multiple markets.
  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills with the ability to engage candidates from diverse professional and cultural backgrounds and influence stakeholders across functions and geographies.
  • Strong judgment, curiosity, cultural awareness, and a continuous improvement mindset with the ability to evaluate and adopt emerging AI technologies to improve recruiting outcomes.
  • Highly organized, data-driven, and able to operate autonomously in a fast-paced, mission-driven, internationally distributed environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior experience supporting aerospace, defense, robotics, autonomy, AI/ML, advanced technology, manufacturing, or other complex hardware/software organizations.
  • Experience sourcing across multiple European talent markets, including established and emerging technology and engineering hubs.
  • Experience navigating cross-border hiring considerations, candidate mobility, work authorization, export control, or other regulatory considerations relevant to hiring across EU.

You will work alongside the air vehicle systems design team, manufacturing and test teams, and applicable suppliers to ensure technical work progresses in alignment with vehicle-level milestones, schedules, and program objectives. This role requires enough aircraft-systems depth to understand the underlying technical solutions, identify cross-system dependencies, and help teams make sound execution decisions, while also bringing the coordination, accountability, and follow-through needed to move the program forward.
 
The ideal candidate has an engineering background and thrives in a hands-on, hardware-centric development environment. They are comfortable working with technical detail, asking the right questions, removing obstacles, and translating complex system work into measurable progress toward aircraft integration and flight readiness.

What you'll do:

Job Description:

We are seeking a highly skilled Air Vehicle Mechanical and Fluid Systems Technician to support the fabrication, instrumentation, and testing of new aerospace products. This role is ideal for a hands-on builder who thrives in dynamic environments, has deep experience working with aircraft systems and fabrication methods, and has a background in machine shop operations and product prototyping.

You will be a key contributor in helping bring cutting-edge designs to life, playing a vital role in everything from early-stage prototype development to detailed testing and validation of final assemblies.

What you'll do:

  • Construct and assemble air vehicle systems and subsystems such as landing gear, mechanisms, fluid systems, test articles in alignment with engineering drawings, engineering instructions, and CAD models.
  • Support the design, prototyping, and fabrication of new products, R&D initiatives, and flight-ready hardware.
  • Work with aerospace-grade materials and perform component repairs using industry-standard techniques and tools.
  • Fabricate fixtures, machine brackets, and execute rapid modifications on prototype hardware as needed.
  • Install strain gauges, thermocouples and various sensors according to precise instrumentation schematics.
  • Route cabling, integrate data acquisition systems, and verify sensor calibration and operational status.
  • Conduct mechanical testing by applying static and dynamic loads per detailed engineering procedures.
  • Document test outcomes clearly and report anomalies or irregularities in a timely manner.
  • Ensure a clean, organized, and safe workspace across shop, lab, and composite work areas.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in instrumentation standards, testing procedures, and fabrication workflows.
  • Source and manage inventory for parts and equipment needed for component repair or replacement.

Required qualifications:

  • 4-6 years of experience in aircraft maintenance, prototype fabrication, test stand design & fabrication.
  • Proficient in metallic and mechanisms fabrication, bearing install & removal.
  • Hands-on experience in machine shop operations, including manual and/or CNC tools.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings, schematics, and detailed work instructions.
  • Comfortable working in shop and lab environments with exposure to noise, dust, and chemicals.
  • Ability to lift and move parts and equipment (up to 50 lbs.) and perform physical work for extended periods.
  • Ability to obtain a S//SAR level security clearance desired.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Familiarity with a variety of mechanical systems (e.g., hydraulic actuators, pumps, fluids, load frames, DAQ systems).
  • Experience in aerospace, automotive, defense, or high-performance prototyping environments.
  • Knowledge of adhesives, fasteners, and bonding processes for composite-to-metal or similar interfaces.
  • Able to work independently and adapt quickly to changing technical needs.

The operator is responsible for the operational readiness, configuration, and safe operation of multi-rotor and fixed-wing UAS, payloads, ground control systems, and supporting test equipment; plans and conducts single- and multi-aircraft missions; supports fly–fix–fly campaigns; validates autonomy capabilities; identifies defects and usability issues; and provides actionable feedback to improve the quality and customer readiness of each release.

      • Plan and conduct missions in accordance with approved test plans, test cards, configuration requirements, release criteria, and safety procedures. 

        • Operate, configure, inspect, and maintain UAS, payloads, ground control systems, communications equipment, and supporting test infrastructure across laboratory, ground, and flight-test environments. 

          • Test pre-release HivemindSDK versions by verifying features, integrations, autonomy capabilities, and performance against defined product and quality requirements. 

            • Develop and execute representative customer workflows and mission scenarios to assess SDK functionality, usability, reliability, and operational performance across aircraft types and multi-agent configurations. 

              • Document test results, defects, anomalies, regressions, and limitations; provide actionable feedback to product, software, systems, autonomy, and quality teams; and support issue reproduction, triage, and corrective-action verification. 

                • Lead operational risk assessments, crew briefings, ground checks, launch and recovery preparations, and post-flight debriefs while serving in designated leadership roles during test conduct. 

                  • Monitor telemetry and system status, collect flight data, evaluate aircraft and autonomy behavior, and support initial anomaly investigation.

          • Experience assessing operational readiness and maintaining configuration control across aircraft, payloads, software, communications equipment, personnel, and test infrastructure. 

            • Experience developing, implementing, and executing SOPs, checklists, risk assessments, hazard mitigations, and operational processes.

Job Description:

Will serves as the regional trade compliance leader for the UK and Europe, providing strategic oversight and execution of the company's international trade compliance program in support of critical defense. This position is responsible for developing and implementing regional trade compliance strategies, ensuring compliance with UK and international export control regulations, sanctions, licensing requirements, and other applicable trade laws throughout the full program lifecycle. The Trade Compliance Manager partners closely with Engineering, Program Management, Legal, Business Development, Supply Chain, and government stakeholders to enable business objectives while mitigating export compliance risk. The role provides leadership across multiple concurrent, high-priority international programs, advises senior leadership on trade compliance matters, and drives consistent compliance processes across the region.

What you'll do:

  • Act as the primary trade compliance point of contact for the UK and support regional compliance activities across Europe.
  • Review, prepare, submit, and manage export authorizations through UK systems (e.g., SPIRE), including SIELs, OIELs, and OGELs, and support European licensing requirements where applicable.
  • Classify products, software, and technical data under UK Strategic Export Control Lists
  • Provide guidance on European export control considerations, including intra-EU transfers and applicable member state regulations.
  • Partner with engineering teams to understand system functionality, data flows, and technical specifications to support accurate classifications and licensing strategies.
  • Develop and maintain classification and licensing documentation, including rationale and audit-ready records.
  • Provide clear, actionable guidance on export control requirements, restrictions, and compliance strategies across UK and European business activities.
  • Implement and manage trade compliance procedures, including visitor controls, international travel guidance, and restricted party screening in accordance with UK, EU, and applicable international regulations.
  • Review export authorizations to ensure alignment with UK government requirements (e.g., ECJU), relevant European authorities, and internal policies.
  • Monitor regulatory developments in UK and European export controls, ensuring ongoing compliance and organizational awareness.
  • Build and improve scalable internal processes and tools to streamline classification and licensing workflows across the region.

Required qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in trade compliance, customs, or export control within aerospace, defense, or advanced technology industries.
  • Experience with UK export control regulations and/or US export control frameworks (ITAR and EAR), including licensing and classification.
  • Experience managing export authorizations and interacting with regulatory bodies such as the UK Export Control Joint Unit (ECJU), EU member state authorities, and/or US State and Commerce Departments.
  • Strong working knowledge of export classification methodologies, jurisdiction determinations, and licensing workflows.
  • Understanding of European export control regimes and cross-border transfer considerations within Europe.
  • Experience collaborating with engineering and program teams to translate technical information into compliant export classifications and documentation.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Business, International Trade, Supply Chain Management, or a related field.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience liaising with UK Government departments.
  • Experience supporting programs involving defense technologies, dual-use items, or autonomous systems.
  • Exposure to compliance operations across multiple jurisdictions (EU, US, APJ).
  • Relevant professional certifications (e.g., Certified Export Specialist, Certified Customs Specialist, or equivalent).

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an experienced leader to oversee Anthropic's global equity administration and payroll operations. In this role, you will lead the teams responsible for our equity compensation administration programs and global payroll operations, ensuring both functions scale accurately, compliantly, and efficiently as we grow — including through listing readiness and public-company operations. You will manage senior functional leaders across equity and payroll, and partner closely with Legal, Tax, HR, and the broader Accounting organization to support our mission to make AI beneficial for humanity.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and develop the equity administration and payroll teams, setting strategy, priorities, and operating cadence across both functions
  • Own the control environment for equity and payroll: design and document to public-company standards.
  • Oversee scaling to public-company standards across both functions.
  • Drive systems strategy across the compensation platforms, from equity to payroll, and surrounding integrations, ensuring a coherent architecture as we scale
  • Serve as the primary escalation point and executive interface for equity and payroll matters with Legal, Tax, HR, and external providers
  • Oversee international expansion of both functions, including new-country payroll setup, cross-border equity compliance, and mobility programs
  • Partner with Accounting on stock-based compensation and payroll accounting, ensuring clean handoffs for close, reporting, and audit
  • Drive automation and continuous improvement of manual processes across both teams through technology solutions
  • Build headcount and resourcing plans that scale with the business

YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

  • Have 15+ years across equity compensation and/or payroll operations, with significant experience leading senior functional leaders
  • Have operated equity and payroll functions to a public company standard.
  • Have deep familiarity with equity management platforms (such as Shareworks or E*TRADE) and Workday payroll, with experience owning cross-system architecture
  • Have built and scaled global operations across multiple jurisdictions
  • Are a strong people leader who develops senior functional experts
  • Thrive in ambiguous, fast-paced environments and default to building scalable processes over adding headcount

STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO

  • Hold CEP (Certified Equity Professional) or CPP (Certified Payroll Professional) certification
  • Have experience with international mobility programs, worker secondments, and cross-border tax considerations
  • Have led complex system implementations or migrations at scale

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$570,000—$610,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

As Partner Account Manager you will help manage and execute the partnerships that accelerate Claude adoption, unlock new capabilities and drive outcomes for our joint customers across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
You will own a defined set of named partners end to end — a mix of (a) in-country DACH practices of our global system integrators (e.g. Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, PwC, BCG), where you work hand in hand with the GSI alliance owners who hold the global relationships, and (b) regional system integrators, consultancies and AI-native boutiques that DACH enterprises and the Mittelstand actually buy from. The DACH partner book is split between you and the Head of Partnerships DACH and CEE; for every partner assigned to you, you own the plan, the enablement path, the co-sell motion with our DACH sales team and the partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline that results from it. This is a builder role: partner-sourced pipeline in DACH is still a small fraction of our open pipeline, and there is a first playbook but no established machine. We need someone who has taken partnerships from zero to a repeatable revenue engine in this market before, not someone who has inherited and administered an existing partner book.

Key responsibilities 

Partner development and execution:

  • Run each partner as a structured pursuit: stakeholder map (country lead, AI/data practice lead, alliance lead, key account partners), joint account plan, agreed target accounts and a quarterly cadence.

  • For your assigned GSI country practices: activate the DACH teams against the global frameworks and translate them into concrete joint accounts. For your assigned regional SIs / boutiques: build the relationship from scratch (selection, onboarding into the Claude Partner Network, enablement, first joint deals).

  • Guide partners in building repeatable Claude offerings (agentic engineering rollouts, agentic use cases, enterprise adoption programs) for the priority DACH industries: automotive and manufacturing, financial services and insurance, public sector, telco, pharma and chemicals.

  • Drive co-selling with the DACH AEs, Applied AI and Technical Success teams: introduce partners into the right accounts, bring partner-sourced opportunities to sales, and make sure every partner-attached deal is tagged correctly in Salesforce.

Performance and KPI ownership:

  • Own and drive the KPIs for your portfolio: Partner delivered use-cases, partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced pipeline and revenue, consultants enabled and certified, partners progressing through CPN tiers, joint proposals submitted.

  • Establish clear success metrics with each partner and drive regular business reviews against targets

  • Report on partnership health, progress, and commercial outcomes with data-driven insights

  • Every deal that runs through your partners must be set up for customer success and expansion: agree success criteria for joint accounts, make sure the partner delivers implementation and adoption support, and feed what you learn back into our partner program and the DACH sales team.

Market development and brand building

  • Represent Anthropic in the DACH partner ecosystem — partner events, joint customer events, and partner-led marketing in German.

  • Adapt the global partner playbook to DACH buying behaviour (Mittelstand vs. DAX/SMI enterprises, long procurement cycles, works councils, preference for local delivery partners) and decide deliberately what not to copy.

  • Navigate the regulatory and sovereignty topics that come up in almost every DACH deal (GDPR, EU AI Act, data residency, regulated industries such as banking and insurance) together with the partner and our internal experts.

  • Build differentiated joint value propositions with partners so that Claude is the default recommendation of the DACH consulting ecosystem.

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Builder mentality — comfortable starting from a small base and turning it into a scaled partner business; you enjoy doing the work yourself.

  • 8+ years of partner / alliances / channel experience with system integrators and consultancies in DACH, ideally at a cloud, data or AI platform company.

  • Existing relationships in the DACH practices of the large SIs and/or with the regional consultancies and boutiques — you know who runs the AI and data practices in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

  • Data-driven, KPI-oriented and comfortable being measured on partner-sourced pipeline; a track record of driving incremental revenue through partners in DACH.

  • History of protecting the customer experience and the brand through partners — you say no to partners that cannot deliver.

  • Competitive drive — obsessed with winning and creating differentiation

  • Collaborative — you work as an extension of the DACH sales team and with Applied AI, Technical Success, partner marketing and the global GSI alliance owners.

  • Business-fluent German (C1+ / native) and English; able to run partner executive conversations and enablement sessions in German.

  • Based in Germany and willing to travel regularly within DE / AT / CH and occasionally to London and San Francisco.

  • Passion for AI and alignment with Anthropic's mission of beneficial AI development

Working Relationships

You will formally report to the International Partnerships leader, while your day-to-day work will be led by our DACH and CEE Partnerships leader who is based in Munich. You will also partner closely with Anthropic's regional sales leader and their Account Executives, as well as the in-region Customer Success and Technical Account Management teams.

Location and Travel

About the role

As a Sales Lead, Canada Public Sector at Anthropic, you'll drive the adoption of safe, frontier AI across the Canadian public sector. You'll leverage your deep understanding of Canadian government operations and consultative sales expertise to propel revenue growth while becoming a trusted partner to customers, helping them embed and deploy AI while uncovering its full range of capabilities. In collaboration with GTM, product, and marketing teams, you'll help refine our approach to the Canadian public-sector market while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance. This is a national role anchored in the National Capital Region, supporting the Government of Canada, provincial/territorial governments, Canada's national security and defence community, crown corporations, and the broader public sector.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive new business and revenue growth across the Canadian public sector, with the Government of Canada as the primary focus and provincial/territorial governments, crown corporations, and the broader public sector as secondary coverage, owning the full sales cycle from initial outreach through deployment
  • Navigate how the Government of Canada buys cloud and AI services, including software licensing supply arrangements, federal cloud brokering, resale through Canadian partners, consumption via cloud provider marketplaces, competitive tendering, and Indigenous procurement considerations
  • Build and maintain relationships with key decision-makers across the Government of Canada, including departmental Chief Information Officers and Chief Data Officers, senior program executives, central agency and procurement stakeholders, and mission owners, becoming a trusted advisor on AI capabilities and implementation
  • Develop and execute strategic account plans that align with departmental mandates and modernization initiatives, positioning Anthropic early in major programs to shape requirements before they are finalized
  • Navigate Canadian security and compliance requirements, including data classification levels, federal security control profiles, assessment and authorization, data-residency requirements, and personnel security clearances
  • Coordinate closely with cloud service providers and system integrators to ensure successful deployment and integration
  • Represent Anthropic at Canadian public-sector and partner events, including industry days, conferences, and cloud provider events, raising Anthropic's profile through speaking engagements and community engagement
  • Provide detailed market intelligence and customer feedback to product teams to ensure our offerings meet Canadian public-sector requirements, including responsible-AI obligations under the Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making and the Algorithmic Impact Assessment
  • Create and maintain sales playbooks specific to Canadian public-sector use cases and procurement processes
  • Generate pipeline and own territory and account planning across your assigned Canadian public-sector accounts, maintaining hands-on engagement with key accounts
  • Collaborate across teams to ensure coordinated delivery of commitments and maintain appropriate documentation of customer engagements, engaging bilingually (English/French) with federal institutions and Quebec public-sector customers where required

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 7+ years of enterprise sales experience in the Canadian public sector, the majority selling to the Government of Canada, with a proven track record of driving adoption of emerging technologies
  • Deep understanding of federal department and agency mandates, challenges, and technology needs, with working knowledge of provincial/territorial and broader public-sector buyers
  • Demonstrated ability to balance strategic account leadership with hands-on sales execution
  • Familiarity with how the Government of Canada buys and secures cloud and AI services, with the judgment to navigate these processes alongside partners, capture, and deal teams
  • Strong track record of exceeding revenue targets and closing large, complex, long-cycle public-sector deals
  • Ability to be based in the National Capital Region, with travel across Canada as needed
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a Government of Canada personnel security clearance (Reliability Status; Secret an asset)
  • Executive presence and relationship-building skills across all levels, from technical teams to senior agency leadership (ADM/DG)
  • Proven ability to coordinate across multiple stakeholders, including cloud providers and system integrators
  • Professional working proficiency in French, sufficient to support Quebec public-sector engagement and bilingual delivery of customer-facing material
  • Strategic thinking combined with attention to detail in execution
  • A passion for safe and ethical AI development, with the ability to articulate its importance in government contexts

About the team

Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.

Within Security GRC, Compliance & Audit Programs run the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework, the single set of controls that the whole program is built on. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and owns the framework and the assurance view across every control domain.

About the role

As part of the Security Audit & Controls team,  you will own the CCF across every control domain, from access and change management to logging, encryption, and people controls: which controls we have, what each one says, how each maps to the frameworks and commitments we hold, and whether each one is actually working. You'll work with control owners and GRC Partners to draft and validate control descriptions and activities that describe reality rather than policy intent, build the monitoring that shows operating effectiveness continuously instead of once a year, and drive what monitoring finds to closure with control owners.

Building with Claude is a normal part of the job: drafting and mapping controls, testing evidence, and monitoring control health, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who works well independently, writes clearly, and gets satisfaction from a control set that is accurate, tested, and trusted by auditors and engineers alike.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the Common Control Framework: the canonical control set, its mappings to SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and customer commitments, and the change process for adding, retiring, or rewording controls

  • Draft and validate control descriptions and control activities with control owners, so each control states who does what, how often, in which system, and what evidence proves it

  • Design and run continuous monitoring of control efficacy: define the metrics and automated tests that show operating effectiveness, tune out false positives, surface failures to owners before an auditor does, and build the controls maturity model that shows where each control domain stands and what it takes to move up a level

  • Verify remediation and carry it into steady state: GRC Partners lead remediation in their domains and control owners implement the fixes. This role advises on control design and implementation, confirms fixes against what the auditor actually asked for, and keeps one source of truth for control and finding status. Once a fix holds, it works with the partner to standardize the evidence pull and, where appropriate, automate it or build continuous monitoring, so the control rolls into the unified audit management program.

  • Map new frameworks and commitments onto the CCF as we commit to them, and support gap assessments when a new framework, certification, product, or entity comes into scope, using the CCF as the baseline and writing the requirements for each delta

  • Support the integrated audit and customer audits: readiness checks, walkthrough preparation, evidence request lists, and the readout of external findings back to GRC

  • Evaluate evidence reliability, including the completeness and accuracy of system-generated reports and AI-generated evidence, and set the standard for what audit-ready evidence looks like here

  • Build with Claude: automate control mapping, evidence testing, and monitoring, and verify machine-drafted control language before it becomes the record

Minimum qualifications

  • Several years in IT audit, security compliance, or controls assurance, including hands-on ownership of a control framework or control library across more than one framework (for example SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, HIPAA)

  • Working command of audit mechanics: scoping, walkthroughs, sampling, design versus operating effectiveness, deficiency evaluation, and evidence reliability

  • Experience writing control descriptions, control activities, and test procedures that other teams and external auditors relied on

  • Experience with continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence collection, whether you built it, ran it, or audited it

  • Enough technical fluency to read a runbook, a configuration, or a pipeline definition and judge whether it enforces what the written control claims

  • Clear writing, because your control language and status reports are what auditors, engineers, and leadership work from

  • Ability to get control owners and partner teams to prioritize and close work without having authority over them

Preferred qualifications

  • Have designed or rebuilt a common controls framework and led the remapping of existing frameworks onto it

  • Have stood up continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence programs and can speak to coverage, false-positive rates, and what changed as a result

  • Have applied LLMs to assurance work, such as control drafting, framework mapping, evidence testing, or monitoring

  • Have defined or assessed controls for AI systems or agents operating in production, or for home-built internal systems

  • Have provided requirements for a homegrown GRC platform and worked with the engineers who build it

You don't need to

  • Have done everything on this list. The scarce combination this role exists for is framework ownership plus the judgment to tell whether a control actually works

  • Write production code. The bar is fluency sufficient to read, query, and challenge

  • Hold every certification. CISA, CISSP, or similar are welcome and not required

  • Have prior AI-industry experience

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Additive Manufacturing team is a high-speed development lab supporting some of our highest-priority programs. We turn evolving designs into physical hardware that engineers can test, learn from, and iterate on immediately.

This is not a production print farm. We operate in a high-mix, low-volume prototype environment where quality, technical judgment, and speed matter more than pushing identical parts through a machine. Our technicians work directly with design engineers across Anduril, helping determine how a part should be built—not simply printing whatever lands in the queue.

We’re looking for an experienced FDM specialist to become the team’s go-to technical owner for our FDM capability.

ABOUT THE JOB

You’ll own FDM prototype builds from initial request through finished hardware.

That means much more than starting a printer…

You’ll review incoming CAD, understand what the engineer is trying to accomplish, identify printability issues, select materials and build strategies, prepare custom toolpaths, operate and calibrate equipment, troubleshoot failures, post-process parts, and verify that the finished hardware meets the original need.

You’ll own a fleet of eight FDM systems, including four industrial machines, while managing a dynamic queue of roughly 10–20 active jobs. Priorities move quickly, designs are not always complete, and the first approach is not always the right one. You’ll be expected to ask the right questions early, make sound technical decisions, and communicate risks before they become rework or missed deadlines.

The best people in this role finish strong: they gather the right requirements up front, execute the build, verify quality and quantity at the end, and make sure the engineer receives exactly what was needed.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
  • Own FDM builds end to end, from CAD and requirements review through file preparation, printing, post-processing, inspection, and delivery.
  • Operate, calibrate, and maintain a fleet of industrial and development-grade FDM printers.
  • Review incoming CAD for printability and identify issues with geometry, wall thickness, orientation, tolerances, mating features, supports, and clearances before machine time is committed.
  • Partner directly with design engineers to understand lead time, end use, and required physical properties, then recommend the right material, orientation, process, and build strategy.
  • Prepare and optimize builds using slicer/build-preparation software, including custom toolpath development when standard settings will not produce the required result.
  • Balance approximately 10–20 active jobs, sequencing work across machines based on priority, machine availability, material, build time, and technical requirements.
  • Troubleshoot failed prints, machine faults, calibration issues, and process drift; identify root causes and drive issues to resolution.
  • Nest and batch work to reduce build time, material waste, and unnecessary machine changeovers.
  • Post-process parts to deliver clean, functional hardware ready for engineering use.
  • Verify completed work against the original request, ensuring the correct part, quantity, quality, and requirements are satisfied before closing the job.
  • Keep job status, expected completion dates, and build risks current so engineers know where their hardware stands.
  • Develop and maintain print profiles, process documentation, and work instructions that improve consistency and repeatability.
  • Perform routine machine maintenance, cleaning, and shop upkeep and coordinate service support when needed.
  • Support material and consumable inventory as needed.
  • Work safely and maintain disciplined shop practices around equipment, materials, PPE, and applicable OSHA and internal safety requirements.
  • Collaborate across the additive team when jobs span multiple printing technologies or require support outside FDM.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • 4+ years of hands-on additive manufacturing experience in a prototype lab, service bureau, development environment, or similar setting; or 2 years of experience, with demonstrated ownership of end-to-end processing
  • Deep hands-on experience with FDM systems, including machine setup, calibration, build preparation, parameter optimization, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience owning additive builds from CAD intake through finished part, including slicer/build-prep software, custom toolpaths, and post-processing.
  • Ability to evaluate CAD for printability and make sound decisions around material, orientation, tolerance, strength, finish, lead time, and cost.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot print failures, manage multiple active jobs, and communicate technical risks and tradeoffs directly with engineers.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Experience with Stratasys industrial FDM systems and/or INSIGHT.
  • Experience with additional additive technologies such as SLA, MJF, SLS, PolyJet, or metal additive.
  • Experience in a high-mix, low-volume prototype environment supporting design engineers directly.
  • Working knowledge of NX, SolidWorks, or similar CAD tools.
  • Experience with composite tooling, dimensional inspection, or additive process documentation.

In this role, you will be responsible for managing the entire value chain, from raw materials to finished goods, to help power the next generation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). You will be responsible for demand forecasting, inventory planning, purchasing, and ensuring accurate material flow through our ERP system.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the planning and on-time delivery of raw materials to internal assembly lines as well as finished goods to customers
  • Develop and maintain accurate demand forecasts and plans
  • Manage day-to-day ordering and inventory for assigned product lines
  • Identify and resolve supply issues, collaborating with cross-functional teams
  • Generate and analyze data to identify trends and support decision-making
  • Develop and maintain processes within MRP and associated master data
  • Support strategic sourcing initiatives and make/buy decisions
  • Issue purchase orders for production and R&D initiatives and manage supplier relationships
  • Participate in S&OP processes and support related strategic initiatives
  • Develop data reporting structures and tools to monitor Demand Planning KPIs and identify key levers for improvement by product or program
  • Understand the product BOM to a level that enables quick decision-making as well as effective questioning and discussion of potential sales opportunities
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives for cost savings, quality improvement, and on-time delivery

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years of significant technical procurement experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Excellent documentation and communication skills and interpersonal relationship skills including negotiating and relationship management skills with ability to drive achievement of objectives
  • Ability to work in cross functional teams and collaborate with across functions / borders
  • Good understanding and interpretation of related design specification
  • Excellent problem-solving, organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills including high discretion/judgment in decision making
  • Ability to work and excel within a fast paced, dynamic, and constantly changing work environment
  • Demonstrated ability to completely own a value chain from start to finish, coordinating among multiple different internal and external parties to achieve on-time deliveries under stringent quality standards
  • Prior knowledge of Oracle or a similar Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system
  • Ability to travel up to 25%
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in any technical field including mechanical/aerospace/manufacturing, electrical, or computer engineering, supply chain, or business with a technical minor or concentration
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Continuous Improvement and Six Sigma principles in action
  • Prior knowledge of Blue Yonder or a similar Supply Chain Planning system; developing statistical models to predict demand in a fast paced, high mix, low volume environment.
  • Knowledge of supply chain planning best practices and data processes that generate business value. Including, but not limited to, demand planning, inventory management, supply planning, S&OP / S&OE and Integrated Business Planning.
  • Knowledge of and experience with big data evaluation and analysis techniques. Experience with SQL databases - storage of information and writing custom queries to pull and analyze data sets to direct focus and action.
  • Knowledge of and experience with leading data reporting applications including Tableau, Power BI, Qlikview, etc.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Maritime delivers platforms, systems, and integrated effects in the maritime domain. Our vehicles (sub-surface and surface) are the cornerstone of these capabilities, and we continually strive to push the boundaries of the possible in terms of endurance, autonomy and mission capability. The Maritime team develops and maintains core products and payloads, and adapts and applies those products to serve a wide variety of defense, IC and commercial customers in US and international markets.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Design Engineer role will be based out of Costa Mesa, CA. As design engineer, you will be responsible for developing CAD models for parts, equipment and tooling designs and layouts to support manufacturing processes, the production system, movement simulations and digital twins of the production environment. You will work closely with manufacturing engineering, suppliers, and production teams to ensure designs are optimized for manufacturability and comply with applicable quality standards including Subsafe, AS9100, and Mil-std specifications.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop comprehensive 3D models using CAD software, incorporating detailed Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), Product Manufacturing Information (PMI), material specifications, finish requirements, and part information.
  • Apply PMI/Model-Based Definition (MBD) to 3D models to support downstream manufacturing and inspection processes.
  • Generate conceptual design layouts and detailed production drawings using GD&T and performing tolerance stackup analysis.
  • Create and manage Engineering Bills of Materials (EBOMs), ensuring proper structure and alignment with Manufacturing Bills of Materials (MBOMs).
  • Establish and configure Teamcenter/CAD Bill of Materials (BOMs) and maintain PLM data integrity.
  • Perform PMI validation and model checking to ensure compliance with relevant industry and military standards such as Subsafe, AS9100, and Mil-std specifications.
  • Interface with vendors and in-house fabrication/assembly teams during design and prototype hardware builds, incorporating producibility lessons learned through design changes and drawing revisions.
  • Generate essential design documentation, including assembly models & drawings, detailed part models & drawings, and manufacturing build-to packages.
  • Conduct drawing package quality reviews and incorporate engineering review feedback and red-line markups.
  • Support configuration management at the system or subsystem level.
  • Work hands-on in a manufacturing environment, collaborating with operations and manufacturing engineering to understand and optimize production systems.
  • Design composite structures, machined components, mechanisms, fluid systems, and electromechanical assemblies.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of experience with detailed mechanical systems from cradle to grave, including structures, mechanisms, fluid systems, and electromechanical systems.
  • Experience with 3D CAD software (e.g. Siemens NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, etc.).
  • Solid understanding and application of GD&T in production drawings.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced environment where products are manufactured.
  • Ability to manage and create large assembly models and 2D drawings.
  • Ability to create workflow releases through Teamcenter Active Workspace.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Siemens NX experience highly preferred.
  • Experience with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems, particularly Teamcenter.
  • Experience creating kinematics and motion simulations.
  • Strong hands-on technical skills - both professional and hobby.
  • Experience with PMI/MBD workflows and model-based design practices.
  • Knowledge of Subsafe, AS9100, or Mil-std drawing and design standards.
  • Experience designing for large-scale manufacturing and working with contract manufacturers.
  • Ability to work well in an integrated team including daily interactions with technicians, engineers, and managers.
  • Creative problem solver that can bring multiple disciplines together.
  • Self-motivated with strong multi-tasking, organizational, communication, and documentation skills.
  • Process improvement experience, including justification of return on investment for design or operational changes.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will lead the technical development of maritime products from concept to delivery. Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience in programmatic level decision will play a key component in making sure the right design/analysis/ and test steps are being completed to ensure success. WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead and manage the initial design, prototyping, capability verification, and delivery of a maritime autonomous system
  • Manage the initial design of the system and subsystems including system architecture development, requirements definition, system and sub-system trades and optimization, risk management etc. to ensure the appropriate consideration of design key performance parameters, schedule, costs, and risks to shape the product
  • Perform systems engineering and trade analyses to enable the exploration and rapid iteration of early conceptual designs, while working closely with technical SME’s and strategic growth team to provide creative solutions to current and future gaps in the DOD capability. Ensure that the warfighter is provided with the best solution for current and future conflicts.
  • Coordinate closely with manufacturing and supply chain teams to ensure design for manufacturing is embedded in early concepts and matured to support full rate production at scale. Drive product differentiation through manufacturing capability and novel manufacturing techniques
  • Work with senior leadership to ensure resource plans are adequate for work scope
  • Oversee technical execution of the generation of a new surface product for Anduril Maritime
  • Define key capabilities, milestones, and demonstrations to enable continuous development and maturation of autonomous systems

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Naval Architecture, Systems Engineering, Marine Engineering, or equivalent, or proven experience in a relevant field
  • Minimum of 15 years experience with technical leadership and systems engineering on defense systems or weapon programs
  • Strong Systems engineering and architecture definition background to bridge software service and hardware product developments
  • Strong working understanding of how product development rolls into program acquisitions, to ensure alignment of HW/SW roadmaps and program requirements
  • Strong leadership qualities and collaborative/integrative leadership demonstrated capacity
  • Experience working with, defining, and fielding sensing payloads and comms architectures
  • Ability to support and/or manage technological roadmaps in critical areas to enable collaborative design and capability alignment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Travel 25% to Customer and Test Sites

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated understanding of multi-domain unmanned and autonomous weapon system development and employment
  • Demonstrated engineering management capability; proven technical and personnel leadership qualities
  • Experience in technical leadership of weapon or defense system programs from initial concept design through transition to full development, testing and qualification, and rate manufacture
  • Strong understanding of autonomous system architecture and overall design approach for unmanned weapons systems
  • Experience working on mission critical DOD systems
  • Experience building and managing cross-functional teams focused around a common vision

About the Team

Anduril's Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, we provide mission critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats. Working across product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains our Family of Systems (FoS) in challenging operational environments worldwide.

About the Job

As a Deployment and Training Lead on the Air Defense team, you are responsible for delivering, training, and sustaining a capability that meets our customers' mission requirements and exceeds their expectations. You own the full lifecycle of a deployment — from planning and installation through new equipment training, sustainment, and continuous improvement. You fulfill this responsibility through rigorous operational execution, detail orientation, proactive communication, deep mission understanding, and hard-won product expertise.

You feel ownership over the health and performance of all assets and technologies deployed to your customers and users, and ensure that the system delivers when they need it most. You are equally invested in ensuring that end users are trained, confident, and proficient in employing the capability. You deliver world-class New Equipment Training (NET) and sustainment training programs that let our customers organically grow and maintain proficiency long after the initial fielding. You identify knowledge gaps and build solutions that drive user proficiency and enduring operational readiness.

You represent Anduril to our customers, building their confidence and trust through your professionalism and commitment to excellence. You also represent our customers back to Anduril, communicating user feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve our product and our team in response to evolving mission needs. Above all, you set the standard for what good looks like for your deployment, and you rally your Anduril teammates to meet that standard every single day.

In this role, you will manage deployments and the associated training enterprise for Anduril's Air Defense products across a region, ensuring mission readiness in support of national security infrastructure. Collaborating closely with the Program Manager and Program Operations Manager, you will play a crucial role in developing long-term deployment, training, and sustainment operations aligned with customer priorities. As a key team member, you will engage across multiple business lines and facilitate customer interactions, making flexibility, humility, and a collaborative mindset essential qualities for success.

What You'll Do

  • Deployment planning and execution: We execute hundreds of deployment events each year, including site installations, test and evaluation exercises, demonstrations, and training and maintenance visits. You will orchestrate these events, leading a cross-functional team that spans hardware supply, logistics, engineering, and more to do whatever it takes to achieve mission success for Anduril and our customers. Meticulous, resourceful, and detail-oriented, you will manage every step of the deployment process, from site survey to testing, pack-out, installation, training, and sustainment. No job is too small. You consistently demonstrate extraordinary judgment, grit, and composure in high-pressure situations. You anticipate every contingency, build lightweight processes, soberly assess and mitigate risk, and deliberately learn from your experiences to continuously improve.
  • New Equipment Training (NET) delivery: You own the NET mission for your deployments. You resource, develop and deliver the initial fielding training that takes customers from zero to operational proficiency on the Anduril Air Defense Family of Systems — building programs of instruction, training schedules, and hands-on individual and collective events tailored to each customer's mission and skill baseline. You ensure every customer that receives our capability is ready to employ it from day one.
  • Sustainment training and readiness: Beyond initial fielding, you build and run the recurring sustainment training that keeps proficiency high as personnel rotate, threats evolve, and product capabilities advance. You establish training gates, proficiency standards, and refresh cycles; you plan and resource realistic sustainment events; and you measure your success by the enduring operational readiness of the forces you support.
  • Relationship management: Build trust with customers, industry partners, users, and Anduril teammates through effective communication, positive attitude, and follow-through. With careful listening and observation, you internalize your counterpart's priorities and requirements. With empathy and responsiveness, you quickly build rapport, trust, and confidence in our capability. You develop relationships across the organization and communicate honestly and directly. You are committed to giving and receiving feedback well. Your partners always know what you expect from them, and know exactly what to expect from you.
  • Mission expertise: Develop a deep knowledge of your customer's mission requirements, including the nature of the threats they face, regulatory challenges, resource constraints, rules of engagement, and more. You will become a subject matter expert and the voice of the customer, capable of effectively communicating requirements and CONOPS to Anduril engineers so they can continue to enhance our capability to meet evolving mission needs. You serve as the counter unmanned systems (cUAS) subject matter expert for your customers, helping them resource realistic training and manage all hardware and software configurations for cUAS-peculiar equipment. You are deeply motivated to shape the future of air defense.
  • Product expertise: Develop a thorough understanding of the capabilities and limitations of Anduril's Family of Systems. You are innately curious about the technology underpinning our capability, and are not satisfied with a superficial understanding of how and why it works. You are constantly educating yourself about the strengths and weaknesses of different sensor modalities, the challenges of sensor fusion, power and networking requirements, and more. You will become an opinionated power user who can reliably forecast how our capability will perform against a broad range of threat profiles, environmental conditions, and mission constraints.

  • Proven experience planning and delivering technical training programs, including new equipment training (NET) and sustainment training
  • Highly organized creative problem-solver with proven project management skills
  • Experienced in the creation and upkeep of documentation for new or developing processes, including training curricula and programs of instruction
  • Proven experience leading tech-enabled teams of peers while building a culture of influence through relationships
  • Deep interest in national security issues and defense technologies, with a commitment to lifelong learning
  • Experience translating technical concepts into operational requirements, performance specifications, and training materials
  • Ownership mentality with strong initiative in managing your own work in potentially remote environments
  • Comfort communicating complex concepts simply across various methods of communication and tools
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize tasks effectively
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance; Top Secret preferred

ABOUT THE TEAM

Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. 

ABOUT THE JOB

We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As Deputy Chief Engineer in Discovery, you lead the technical work on concepts nobody has proven, usually several at once. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, build it, test it, and reach a solution.

You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of building things: taking a concept from an idea to hardware or software that works, across different areas, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role on both internally and externally funded programs within Anduril's Discovery Business Line, on operationally relevant timelines.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own new concepts from first idea through analysis, prototype, and test, and drive them to a validated answer
  • Learn new domains fast enough to do real work in them: read the references, build the model, check it against known results, then extend it
  • Build or adapt the models, simulations, and test setups the question needs, using existing tools where they fit and building where they do not
  • Pressure-test your own and others' work: hunt failure modes, surface hidden assumptions, and stress trade studies before decisions are locked in
  • Use AI tools as a force multiplier for research, code, and analysis, and know when their output has to be checked against a reference
  • Work shoulder to shoulder with Hardware, Software, GNC, and the other teams at Anduril, and translate results into decisions that change the design
  • Communicate results to engineers, leadership, and customers, including strong visual presentation of complex data

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Demonstrated experience working in more than one technical area
  • You have done things: designed, built, tested, or fielded something real, in any field
  • Proficiency in at least one physics-math scripting environment (Python with numpy/scipy, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or similar)
  • Strong written, verbal, and visual communication

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 12+ years in a relevant science/engineering field
  • Math, physics, or engineering degree, or similar
  • Proficiency with AI tools (coding assistants, agents, model-driven research) in day-to-day engineering work, and judgment about when to trust their output
  • Experience in several of: space systems, missiles and missile defense, air vehicles, GNC, sensors and sensor fusion, radar, EW, acoustics, autonomy, or similar. Breadth across these counts for more than depth in any one
  • Familiarity with domain analysis tools as relevant (STK/Astrogator, AFSIM, HFSS, Fluent, or similar)

The Anduril Battlespace Awareness Radar team develops state-of-the-art radar systems, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The Radar team is responsible for all aspects of radar system development, from the ideation stage through initial production. In this role, you will work closely with an interdisciplinary technical team to define test strategies, build automated validation infrastructure, perform testing against representative hardware, and mature prototypes into reliable products.

About the Job

Anduril is seeking a Software Quality Engineer to develop and maintain the test and release infrastructure for our radar software portfolio. This is a hands-on engineering role combining testing against real radar hardware with automated test development, hardware-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop environments, CI/CD, release assurance, and reproducible radar test-data workflows.

You will work directly with software and firmware engineers across multiple radar products to reduce manual validation, detect regressions earlier, shorten feedback cycles, and make releases repeatable, traceable, and auditable.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and execute manual and automated test plans, test cases, and test scripts for radar software and firmware, including functional, regression, integration, and hardware-in-the-loop testing
  • Identify, document, and track software and firmware defects; collaborate with developers to reproduce issues, debug root causes, and verify fixes
  • Support the design and build-out of software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop test infrastructure, including test rigs, emulators, and harnesses that validate radar software against representative hardware and simulated environments
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines that run automated test suites and provide fast, actionable feedback across the radar product portfolio
  • Develop tooling for reliable collection, cataloging, retention, retrieval, and replay of radar test data so results are reproducible across programs and field events
  • Support repeatable deployment of firmware and software updates to lab hardware, test benches, and fielded units
  • Build release-assurance workflows that collect test evidence, generate release notes and software bills of materials, version release artifacts, and maintain traceability between source code, builds, test results, and deployed software
  • Partner with software, firmware, systems, and configuration-management teams to define release criteria and verify that software meets quality standards before deployment
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of testing methodologies, coding standards, and release practices as the radar software portfolio scales

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance, software test engineering, or software development infrastructure
  • Experience developing automated tests at the unit, integration, or system level
  • Proficiency in Python for test automation and scripting
  • Working proficiency in C++ sufficient to understand, instrument, and debug production software
  • Experience with Git and CI/CD tooling
  • Experience with bug-tracking systems such as Jira
  • Experience testing and debugging software in Linux environments
  • Strong debugging, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or operating hardware-in-the-loop or software-in-the-loop test infrastructure
  • Experience collecting, managing, and replaying large or high-volume test datasets
  • Experience with release automation, artifact management, software bill of materials generation, or software configuration management
  • Experience with firmware or embedded-software deployment and update pipelines
  • Familiarity with Nix or NixOS for reproducible build and test environments
  • Experience with containerization technologies such as Docker
  • Experience writing or analyzing code with LLMs such as Claude Code or Codex

ABOUT THE JOB

In your role as a Field Operations Deployment Manager on the Air Defense team, you are responsible for delivering and sustaining large-scale, fixed-site counter-UAS capability that protects our customers' most critical installations and infrastructure. You own the end-to-end execution of persistent, multi-sensor, multi-effector deployments across expansive site footprints — and you ensure the system delivers when our customers need it most.

You fulfill this responsibility through rigorous operational execution, detail orientation, proactive communication, deep mission understanding, and hard-won product expertise. Because fixed-site deployments are enduring rather than transient, you build repeatable, playbook-driven methodology that turns each installation into a standardized, auditable, and continuously improving process — not a one-off. You feel ownership over the health and performance of all assets and technologies deployed to your sites, and you coordinate tightly with on-site security organizations and facility stakeholders to integrate our capability into the site's broader security posture.

You represent Anduril to our customers, building their confidence and trust through your professionalism and commitment to excellence. You also represent our customers back to Anduril, communicating user feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve our product and our team in response to evolving mission needs. Above all, you set the standard for what good looks like for your deployment team, and you rally your Anduril teammates to meet that standard every single day.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Deployment planning and execution: You will orchestrate large-scale, persistent C-UAS installations — leading a cross-functional team that spans hardware supply, logistics, engineering, and more to achieve mission success for Anduril and our customers. Meticulous, resourceful, and detail-oriented, you will manage every step of the deployment lifecycle across an expansive site footprint: site survey, RF and power planning, sensor and effector siting, coverage modeling, pack-out, installation, integration, test, training, and long-term sustainment. You consistently demonstrate extraordinary judgment, grit, and composure in high-pressure situations. You anticipate every contingency, soberly assess and mitigate risk, and deliberately learn from your experiences to continuously improve.
  • Playbook-driven deployment methodology: You will build and own the standardized playbooks, SOPs, and installation templates that make fixed-site deployments repeatable at scale. You codify the site survey, siting, integration, acceptance-test, and sustainment procedures into lightweight, disciplined processes that any deployment team can execute consistently across sites. You treat each deployment as an opportunity to refine the playbook — capturing lessons learned, closing gaps, and driving the methodology toward a predictable, auditable standard.
  • Site security coordination: You will serve as Anduril's primary interface to on-site security teams, facility management, and installation stakeholders. You integrate our capability into the site's existing physical security and force-protection posture — deconflicting sensor and effector placement, coordinating installation access and escorts, aligning on rules of engagement and response protocols, and ensuring our system reinforces rather than complicates the site's concept of security. You build the trust and shared operating picture that let Anduril and site security operate as one team.
  • Relationship management: Build trust with customers, industry partners, users, and Anduril teammates through effective communication, positive attitude, and follow-through. With careful listening and observation, you internalize your counterpart's priorities and requirements. With empathy and responsiveness, you quickly build rapport, trust, and confidence in our capability. You develop relationships across the organization and communicate honestly and directly. You are committed to giving and receiving feedback well. Your partners always know what you expect from them, and know exactly what to expect from you.
  • Mission expertise: Develop a deep knowledge of your customer's mission requirements, including the nature of the threats they face, airspace and regulatory challenges, resource constraints, rules of engagement, and the specific demands of defending fixed, high-value sites. You will become a subject matter expert and the voice of the customer, capable of effectively communicating requirements and CONOPS to Anduril engineers so they can continue to enhance our capability to meet evolving mission needs. You are deeply motivated to shape the future of air defense.
  • Product expertise: Develop a thorough understanding of the capabilities and limitations of Anduril's Family of Systems. You are innately curious about the technology underpinning our capability, and are not satisfied with a superficial understanding of how and why it works. You are constantly educating yourself about the strengths and weaknesses of different sensor modalities, the challenges of sensor fusion, power and networking requirements, and more. You will become an opinionated power user who can reliably forecast how our capability will perform against a broad range of threat profiles, environmental conditions, and mission constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Advanced degree or 4-6+ years experience in a technical field, preferably in the defense, national security, or aerospace domain
  • Highly organized creative problem-solver with proven project management skills
  • Experience planning and executing large-scale, fixed-site installations or infrastructure deployments, ideally involving integrated sensors, effectors, power, and networking
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain deployment playbooks, SOPs, and installation documentation that drive repeatable execution at scale
  • Experience coordinating with site security, physical security, or force-protection organizations and integrating capabilities into an existing security posture
  • Experienced in the creation and upkeep of documentation for new or developing processes
  • Proven experience leading tech-enabled teams of peers while building a culture of influence through relationships
  • Deep interest in national security issues and defense technologies, with a commitment to lifelong learning
  • Experience translating technical concepts into operational requirements and performance specifications
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize tasks effectively
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Willing to travel up to 50% of the time

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with Networking, cUAS, and/or Air and Missile Defense
