ABOUT THE TEAM

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Fleet Integration Manager to join our maritime team.
This is a dual-hatted role: you will perform test engineering duties and lead fleet integration efforts,
bringing hands-on at-sea operating experience into both. You will work closely with program leadership
and across engineering, operations, and business development to build a team focused on solving hard
problems and changing the industry. Join our team and help build the next generation of surface
platforms that redefine maritime operations.

Our team conducts full system-level development testing, new production acceptance testing,
sub-component qualification testing, and more. If it involves test, we support it. If you want to work
in an innovative, fast-paced environment where your work directly shapes the products we field, this is
a fantastic opportunity.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Testing and fleet integration are the same problem seen from two angles. A test plan written without
fleet operating experience misses the failure modes, workflows, and edge cases that matter at sea. In
this role, you’ll apply that experience directly: time spent operating unmanned or manned surface vessels
in real conditions, translated into test plans, demonstration events, and exercises that reflect how the
fleet actually operates.

You also serve as the bridge between the engineering team and the fleet. You identify gaps between our
platforms and existing fleet procedures, equipment, and concepts of employment, and feed that insight
back into design and test planning. You represent the operator's perspective in design reviews and
requirements discussions, and support direct engagement with fleet units and customers during
integration, test, and demonstration events.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support the integration of surface platform subsystems, including sensors, navigation, propulsion, communication systems, autonomy software, and power systems, into a complete surface platform
  • Develop, review, and execute test plans for development, integration, and acceptance testing, informed by hands-on fleet operating experience
  • Support day-to-day test operations, including pre-mission testing, launch and recovery, vehicle tasking, and data analysis for internal and customer-facing efforts
  • Design test and demonstration scenarios that reflect real fleet operating conditions, procedures, and tactics
  • Identify gaps between platform capability and existing fleet equipment, procedures, and concepts of employment, and feed findings back to engineering and program leadership
  • Support hands-on troubleshooting, repair, operation, and maintenance of surface maritime platforms in the field
  • Author and/or review detailed test reports documenting internal and customer-facing test and evaluation efforts
  • Support local and offshore sea testing and operations, including multi-day offshore operations
  • Set up, collect, and refine operational metrics for test and fleet performance
  • Participate in design reviews, requirements analysis, and system verification planning, representing the operator's perspective
  • Collaborate with fleet units, external partners, and customers during integration and test, cataloging their requirements and supporting payload and system integration into the overall mission lifecycle
  • Support configuration control, version control, documentation, and safety processes across land- and sea-based test and integration efforts, including extended hours as required
  • Ability to travel up to 50% of the time, including multi-day offshore operations, with potential for more during key test campaigns and fleet integration events

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience operating unmanned or manned surface vessels at sea, with demonstrated ability to translate that experience into realistic test and demonstration scenarios, ideally as a recent Surface Warfare Officer (SWO) in the United States Navy
  • Familiarity with concepts of mechanical engineering, software development and testing, electrical engineering, and control theory
  • Experience in field test and/or operationally focused environments
  • Knowledge of electronics troubleshooting and ability to use basic test equipment
  • Proficient in reading and understanding engineering drawings and specifications
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, effective across technical and non-technical audiences
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • High ownership and a bias toward action
  • Ability to travel up to 50% of your time, with potential for more during key test campaigns and fleet integration events
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience integrating surface and airborne sensors, surface vessel navigation, and communication systems
  • A genuine interest and 5+ years of experience in systems engineering, integration, and test
  • Experience generating TRRs, test plans, test procedures, and test reports
  • Demonstrated experience with marine operational procedures and equipment, spanning coastal to deep-water operations
  • Experience briefing customers, partners, or fleet stakeholders on emerging capabilities
  • Proficiency in data analysis tools: Python, MATLAB, R, SQL
  • Experience developing and managing a test and evaluation program
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Hardware Test Engineering Manager to join our team. The EW Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare.

We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements. As the Hardware Test Engineering Manager, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of production systems to support high-volume products across the portfolio. You are charged with ensuring rigorous testing protocols are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Furthermore, your leadership guarantees the fulfillment of manufacturing's test throughput requirements. This position demands an innovative approach to resolving complex testing challenges, advancing scalability, and enhancing our automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics methodologies.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Direct the manufacturing test engineering team, set objectives, guide initiatives, and assess team outcomes.
  • Oversee and consistently contribute improvements of the manufacturing test strategy for each product to ensure scalable operations across Anduril, transitioning from pre-production to full-scale output.
  • Collaborate with product SEIT and development engineering for design testability, ensuring seamless production integration.
  • Strategize and implement advancements in manufacturing testing, focusing on automation, uniformity, and operational streamlining.
  • Maintain test capabilities of multiple products across their respective manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation.
  • Evaluate test data, compile findings, and identify opportunities for product and process enhancements.
  • Communicate strategic visions to key stakeholders, guiding the scaling of platforms from pre-production (LRIP) through to mass production (FRP).
  • Lead the procurement and implementation of new test equipment, performing cost-benefit and ROI analyses as needed.
  • Champion initiatives that enhance safety, reduce costs, improve quality, and increase productivity through testing.
  • Cultivate a culture focused on innovation, collaboration, and accountability in the engineering department.
  • Act as the go-to technical authority for manufacturing test matters, advising on and troubleshooting complex issues.
  • Design proactive maintenance and calibration protocols for manufacturing test equipment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of relevant industry experience with emphasis on manufacturing test and product sustainment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 2+ years as a people manager leading manufacturing test engineering or relevant adjacent fields.
  • Experienced in Linux, C#, Python, NixOS, LabView, or other forms of test automation.
  • Experience with computer hardware communication protocols: USB, Ethernet, RS232, RS485, PCIe, HDMI, CAN, etc.
  • Solid experience with PCBA/electronic assembly testing and knowledge of testing standards including and not limited to: acceptance testing, EOL testing, and ESS testing.
  • Proficiency in using electronic and RF test equipment.
  • Strong analytical skills for root cause analysis of non-conforming electro-mechanical hardware
  • Familiar with Test Execution Systems (TES), Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.
  • Experience in managing projects that integrate electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated ability to lead the development of manufacturing test systems and teams.
  • Proficiency in LabVIEW, MATLAB, and test automation.
  • Knowledge of PCBA design and mechanical design
  • Familiarity with various hardware communication protocols.
  • Experience with designing HASS & ESS-related tests (Thermal, Vibration, etc.).
  • Familiarity in using AI tools

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Head of Production to join our team in Santa Ana, CA to stand up a cutting-edge manufacturing site. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will build and lead the production organization from scratch, establishing manufacturing processes, quality systems, and the infrastructure needed to scale from prototype builds through full-rate production.

As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must bear the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Your spectrum of support will be exceptionally diverse and require you to rapidly drive aggressive deliverables to completion.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a Lab Manager to join our team. The Space Manufacturing team is responsible for the assembly, integration, and test of ground support equipment, PCBA, unit-level, and integrated systems that are vital for our aerospace and defense operations. This role owns the day-to-day operation, readiness, and discipline of our Space Manufacturing lab spaces across three locations that support development and low-rate builds of spaceflight hardware.

As the Lab Manager, you will own the facility systems, the cleanroom and contamination-control program, safety, equipment, and the flow of materials and consumables that keep build and test running across three sites. You will also build and lead your own team over time — but in the near term this is a working-manager role: you will do much of the hands-on work yourself while hiring and developing the technicians and specialists who keep these spaces running, scaling the team as the sites grow. This is a hands-on ownership role for someone who wants to be the person the floor relies on to keep demanding lab and cleanroom environments operating to spec, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • This role owns the day-to-day operation, readiness, and discipline of our Space Manufacturing lab spaces across three locations that support development and low-rate builds of spaceflight hardware — including gowning/anterooms, air showers, test bays, subassembly and assembly zones, and storage, so build and test run without facility-driven downtime.
  • Build and lead the site support team — contamination-control, facilities/maintenance, and lab technicians and specialists: hire to plan, set direction and priorities, develop and mentor the team, and manage performance. In the near term, operate as a working manager — performing the hands-on facility, cleanroom, and equipment work directly while standing up and scaling the team.
  • Serve as the single site point of contact for facilities at each location: coordinate building services, maintenance and repairs, moves, space changes, and outside vendors, and keep each space configured for the work it hosts.
  • Own the contamination-control program for each cleanroom (graded ISO 5–8): gowning protocols and throughput, continuous particle monitoring, cleanroom certification cadence, and consumables (garments, gloves, wipes) stock and flow.
  • Coordinate cleanroom and facility systems and their upkeep across sites — AHUs, environmental monitoring, compressed and specialty gases (including nitrogen purge), and building support systems — with facilities/maintenance and vendors to keep systems in spec and serviced.
  • Serve as the day-to-day safety point of contact for each site: enforce safe work practices, coordinate hazardous-material and specialty-gas handling and storage, and interface with EHS on chemical handling, permits, and audits.
  • Manage lab equipment, assets, and material flow across the sites: check-in/check-out and asset tracking, calibration and metrology scheduling (in-house and vendor), preventive maintenance, tool/fixture readiness, and receiving/kitting/stores/consumables flow in coordination with supply chain and quality.
  • Drive lab and facility standards and documentation: cleanroom operating procedures, gowning and contamination-control work instructions, safety procedures, and the certification/monitoring records that keep every space audit-ready.
  • Lead the transition of work into the new facility as it comes online — plan space, systems, and support-staff needs for each phase, help stand up new areas, and manage the wind-down of temporary space as capability moves.
  • Partner with AI&T, manufacturing engineering, and program teams to sequence work across the sites and keep WIP moving.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • 5+ years operating or managing a manufacturing lab, cleanroom, or comparable controlled production environment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, a technical/science discipline, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience operating or managing an ISO-classified cleanroom (ISO 5–8 or equivalent) or other contamination-controlled environment.
  • 2+ years working with cleanroom facility systems — HVAC/AHUs, environmental and particle monitoring, gowning and air-shower discipline, and cleanroom certification requirements.
  • Hands-on safety experience with hazardous-material and compressed/specialty-gas handling and storage, including 1+ year acting as a floor- or lab-level safety point of contact.
  • Experience managing lab equipment, a calibration/metrology program, and asset tracking across 50+ tools/assets (or a comparable-scale lab), plus receiving/inventory/consumables flow.
  • Experience owning facilities and readiness for 2+ distinct lab or cleanroom spaces (or a multi-room/multi-building site) at once, including coordinating moves and stand-up of new space.
  • 2+ years leading or mentoring a team (formal management or team-lead), with the ability to operate as a working manager — hands-on in the day-to-day while hiring, developing, and building a team.
  • Strong organization and documentation discipline (able to build and enforce procedures and keep a lab audit-ready), and willing to work on-site full-time in a fast-paced hardware environment, coordinating across engineering, operations, quality, and vendors.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • 2+ years in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, medical-device, or optics/sensor manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with ISO 5 (Class 100) operations and open-die / optical / sensor assembly cleanliness requirements.
  • Experience standing up a new lab or cleanroom, or bringing 1+ new cleanroom phases/areas online.
  • Familiarity with quality and workmanship standards relevant to the work (e.g., IPC-610/620, AS9100, NASA-STD-8739 series).
  • Experience coordinating EHS programs and specialty-gas / hazmat storage at scale.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance,

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manager of Manufacturing Test Engineering to join our team. The EW Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare.

We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements. As the Manager of Manufacturing Test Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of production systems to support high-volume products across the portfolio. You are charged with ensuring rigorous testing protocols are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Furthermore, your leadership guarantees the fulfillment of manufacturing's test throughput requirements. This position demands an innovative approach to resolving complex testing challenges, advancing scalability, and enhancing our automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics methodologies.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Direct the manufacturing test engineering team, set objectives, guide initiatives, and assess team outcomes.
  • Oversee and consistently contribute improvements of the manufacturing test strategy for each product to ensure scalable operations across Anduril, transitioning from pre-production to full-scale output.
  • Collaborate with product SEIT and development engineering for design testability, ensuring seamless production integration.
  • Strategize and implement advancements in manufacturing testing, focusing on automation, uniformity, and operational streamlining.
  • Maintain test capabilities of multiple products across their respective manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation.
  • Evaluate test data, compile findings, and identify opportunities for product and process enhancements.
  • Communicate strategic visions to key stakeholders, guiding the scaling of platforms from pre-production (LRIP) through to mass production (FRP).
  • Lead the procurement and implementation of new test equipment, performing cost-benefit and ROI analyses as needed.
  • Champion initiatives that enhance safety, reduce costs, improve quality, and increase productivity through testing.
  • Cultivate a culture focused on innovation, collaboration, and accountability in the engineering department.
  • Act as the go-to technical authority for manufacturing test matters, advising on and troubleshooting complex issues.
  • Design proactive maintenance and calibration protocols for manufacturing test equipment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of relevant industry experience with emphasis on manufacturing test and product sustainment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 2+ years as a people manager leading manufacturing test engineering or relevant adjacent fields.
  • Experienced in Linux, C#, Python, NixOS, LabView, or other forms of test automation.
  • Experience with computer hardware communication protocols: USB, Ethernet, RS232, RS485, PCIe, HDMI, CAN, etc.
  • Solid experience with PCBA/electronic assembly testing and knowledge of testing standards including and not limited to: acceptance testing, EOL testing, and ESS testing.
  • Proficiency in using electronic and RF test equipment.
  • Strong analytical skills for root cause analysis of non-conforming electro-mechanical hardware
  • Familiar with Test Execution Systems (TES), Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.
  • Experience in managing projects that integrate electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain US DoD clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Advanced degree in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead the development of manufacturing test systems and teams.
  • Proficiency in LabVIEW, MATLAB, and test automation.
  • Knowledge of PCBA design and mechanical design
  • Familiarity with various hardware communication protocols.
  • Experience with designing HASS & ESS-related tests (Thermal, Vibration, etc.).
  • Familiarity in using AI tools

ABOUT THE JOB
As the Manager of Product Quality Engineering you will lead a team of product quality engineers and quality specialists who will work inside & outside the organization to define, develop, and execute processes that deliver high quality & reliable products. Your leadership will impact how Anduril delivers production quality and sustaining support for a portfolio of products that support Intelligence Systems. You will build partnerships with heads of production, manufacturing engineering, program management, deployments, sourcing and multiple engineering teams. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing, product development, sub-system performance criteria and metrology, and leadership experience to contribute to Anduril's mission.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Test, and Supply Chain leadership teams and execute to Product Development Process (PDP) to meet all gate readiness review criteria (CDR, BRR, MRR/PRR) engaging from early prototype testing to full rate production.
  • Be the voice and leader for product development, production quality, supplier quality, and all the functions that contribute to an efficient and effective NPI/production process and delivery of product to Anduril customers.
  • Lead & manage a team to champion continuous improvement and failure mode elimination in the development & production phases, driving part and system level quality readiness for production scaling, and supporting customer / deployment quality issues.
  • Own and utilize Supplier Quality Engineering resources to own and track supplier quality control and development program for the product(s) as well as supplier part qualification and risk management programs
  • Own and lead Quality Control process, frame work, and execution starting from detailed engineering requirements and risks all the way to managing inspection methods and tooling by collaborating with systems design partners and providing leadership and prioritization to quality control teams
  • Set daily and weekly priorities for the quality teams and establish culture of best-in-class product quality by driving the adoption and consistent use of quality tools and processes.
  • Drive production readiness by detailed design reviews, process development, verification/validation, and qualification of processes and parts, sub-assembly, and system deployments
  • Drive clarity & resolution for performance ambiguities associated with product maturity, process stability, and field performance that impact the product meeting it’s quality & reliability goals for production.
  • Drive ongoing quality performance for incoming quality control, in-process quality control, and end of line quality.
  • Own the elimination of product risk to by reducing process contribution to quality & reliability across the product lifecycle.
  • Lead Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), Non-Conformance Reviews (NCRs), Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA), and Material Review Board (MRB) activities. Review the effectiveness of actions and share lessons learned across the product team.
  • Own and lead cross functional alignment of within Corrective Action Board (CAB) activities to drive ownership to investigations and resolutions of quality issues regarding design, integration, process, and supply chain
  • Lead product health data analysis and improvement activities. Establish metrics for measuring quality and the factors that predict quality performance. Drive performance when out of goal/out of specification conditions occur.
  • Support the continuous improvement of the Quality Management System needed to support the process and product. Define and improve required documentation and activities
  • Develop strategies and resource plans with heads of production, program management, deployments, sourcing and chief engineers & architects to meet customer & product requirements.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelors degree in a technical Engineering discipline
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience leading organizations including teams of direct report engineers to address NPI and production execution and quality issues that impact delivery or product quality at our customer
  • Minimum total of 10+ combined years of experience working in technical/engineering disciplines related to product quality/engineering as an individual contributor engineer or working engineering manager
  • Working knowledge of design review and quality management of PCBA, harnessing, mechanical structures, systems integration, power/battery systems, radar, vision system/optical image capture, networking/communication protocol, and remote management systems.
  • Experience driving product quality and performance requirements to test and measurement system development and optimization. Leading the transition from engineering qualification to manufacturing variance testing for product quality coverage.
  • Working knowledge of product development methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Inspection & measurement systems, Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) elements such as Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), Gauge Repeatability & Reproducibility (GR&R), Statistical Process Control (SPC), and Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T).
  • Working knowledge of precision mechanicals, composites, motors, and/or PCBA and Cable harnessing manufacturing processes.
  • Ability to read and drive clarity for technical drawings, requirements, Quality Clauses, and SOWs used to describe quality requirements
  • Working knowledge of Manufacturing Execution systems, Configuration Management and Document Control/Data Management
  • An extreme ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive projects from start to completion.
  • Analytical skills and experiences for data mining, data quality, metrics generation, issue management systems, and statistical analysis tools (MatLab, JMP, MiniTab, etc)
  • Eligible to obtain and/or maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance (clearance not required to start)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Masters degree in a technical engineering discipline
  • Contractual knowledge in ITAR and EAR applications regarding product technicalities
  • Experience in design/integration/test of sensors/cameras/gimbals
  • Experience recruiting, hiring, and developing a team of engineers and specialists.
  • 8+ years of experience with developing quality systems for high volume, high complexity manufacturing environments.
  • Working knowledge of AS9100/ ISO 9001-based Quality Management System requirements.
  • Experience with IPC standards, mastery of ESD and FOD prevention and mitigation programs.
  • Experience with government contracts and military standard requirements.
  • Experience with Teamcenter/PLM, Oracle, Warehouse management, Non-Conformance management systems, and Altassian work stream tools

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own lifting and handling equipment design for a maritime autonomous vehicle. Reporting to the Structural Mechanical lead, you will design fixtures, cradles, and rigging solutions that enable safe handling of the vehicle during manufacturing, transport, and field operations.

The vehicle gets lifted dozens of times between the factory floor and the water, by people who did not design it. The fixtures and lift plans this role produces are what keep those lifts from damaging the vehicle or hurting someone. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own lifting and handling equipment design: fixtures, cradles, spreader bars, slings
  • Perform load analysis and sizing for lifting equipment
  • Define rigging procedures, lift plans, and safety documentation
  • Design for interface with vehicle structural attachment points
  • Coordinate with production, logistics, and deployment teams on handling requirements
  • Support proof load testing and equipment qualification
  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, Navy, or equivalent rigging standards
  • Travel up to 25% to manufacturing, test, and operational sites

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Anduril, we are developing unmanned systems for subsurface, surface, land, and air domains that will leverage unsupervised autonomy for the delivery of multi-mission capability to our customers. Deciding what to build — and in what order — requires people who can connect operational problems, threat-informed scenarios, customer needs, and product employment concepts to the capability we field. We are looking for a Mission Operations Engineer to do that work at the enterprise level, based at our Costa Mesa, California headquarters.

ABOUT THE JOB

Our next Mission Operations Engineer has built and executed plans in the maritime domain, has stood watch, and has been to sea, preferably using uncrewed systems. That background is what separates an analytic product that operators recognize as real from one that reads well and gets ignored. Equally important is the ability to carry that work into a room of senior military and civilian decision-makers and hold it there: this role briefs Commanding Officers, high-level civilians, and our own executive team, and it is expected to give direct answers under hard questioning.

Customer engagement is key, with opportunity to embed directly with our warfighters to provide real-time analysis and feedback on Anduril products. You will normalize how mission problems are framed so that competing programs can be compared on the same terms, and so that investment, roadmap, and capture decisions rest on a defensible operational argument rather than on whichever program briefed most recently.

Being co-located with product leadership, engineering leads, growth, and program directors is the point of the job. You will spend your days in the rooms where trades get made: pressure-testing a concept of employment with the engineers who have to build it, reconciling a program director’s field reality with a product lead’s roadmap, and giving executives the one-page operational case they need to commit capital. Expect up to 50% travel across company facilities, test and demonstration sites, waterfront and fleet concentration areas, and customer locations — the analysis has to survive contact with the water, not just the whiteboard.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Represent the operational perspective in cross-functional reviews, gate decisions, and portfolio planning cycles, and serve as a trusted interpreter between customer language, operational need, product strategy, and engineering implications
  • Partner with systems analysts, engineers, operators, program directors, and business-line leaders to ensure technical solutions remain anchored to real warfighting needs as programs mature
  • Convert results from at-sea demonstrations, field test events, and program execution into portfolio-level lessons that change what we build, closing the loop between the deck plate and the roadmap
  • Understand the enterprise-level mission analysis for the maritime portfolio — identify operational problems, capability gaps, and opportunities for differentiated system employment, and maintain a coherent picture of them across programs rather than one program at a time and be able to communicate them to the customer across the Maritime suite of products
  • Develop and refine concepts of operation, concepts of employment, operational vignettes, mission threads, and use cases for current and future systems, and keep them current as designs and customer priorities move
  • Inform capability roadmaps, IRAD and investment prioritization, and product-market fit assessments by making the operational case for where the next dollar and the next engineer should go
  • Analyze threat environments, customer missions, force structure, operational constraints, and campaign-level context, and translate that context into capability priorities and defensible requirements for product and engineering teams
  • Compare alternative capability approaches and assess trade-offs in mission utility, feasibility, scalability, cost, survivability, and operational relevance — including the approaches we should decline to pursue

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience supporting maritime, undersea, or autonomous systems mission areas; experience across air, surface, C2, ISR, fires, or logistics is also valued
  • 5+ years of maritime operational planning experience — building, staffing, and executing operational or campaign plans in the maritime domain at a unit, strike group, numbered fleet, MOC, or component command level
  • Experience tactically employing AUV capabilities or equivalent autonomous system experience including water space coordination in the undersea domain
  • Demonstrated ability to brief and defend operational objectives, and platform capabilities and limitations in front of senior military and civilian decision-makers —Commanding Officers, high-level civilians, and corporate executives — including under direct and skeptical questioning
  • Ability to decompose ambiguous operational problems into structured executable strategies at the tactical level
  • Strong understanding of maritime missions, operational concepts, threat-informed planning, and the relationship between technology and warfighting outcomes
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce executive-level briefings
  • Demonstrated ability to influence decisions across technical, operational, and business stakeholders without owning them — this role earns its authority through the quality of its analysis
  • Ability to hold a portfolio-level view: comfort working several programs, mission areas, and time horizons in parallel and prioritizing among them
  • Strong judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort operating with incomplete information in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to translate between customer language, operational need, product strategy, and engineering implications
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% to multiple company facilities, test and demonstration sites, customer locations, and at-sea or field events
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Watch floor experience — TAO, watch officer, battle watch captain, or equivalent time in a maritime operations center, fleet or component watch floor, or afloat combat information center, where decisions were made on incomplete information against a clock
  • Significant at-sea operational experience, including underway deployments, and credibility with the operators who will employ these systems
  • Prior military, DoD, defense industry, intelligence community, operational test, or tactical level development experience
  • Familiarity with CONOPS development, campaign analysis, wargaming, modeling and simulation, operational test, or requirements development
  • Experience working directly with government customers, senior military leaders, product teams, or engineering organizations
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE JOB

We’re looking for a Senior Weapons Integration Engineer to join the Thunder team in Costa Mesa, CA. As a Senior Weapons Integration Engineer, you will lead the end-to-end technical execution and tactical integration of kinetic stores and weapon systems onto an advanced autonomous aircraft program co-developed with our airframe partner.

You will architect critical Store Management System (SMS) trades, define digital and physical interfaces (e.g., MIL-STD-1760, UAI), and ensure the platform's mission software reliably interfaces with diverse modern armaments. Serving as the platform's weapons authority, you will interface closely with our internal autonomy teams, our partner’s airframe structures group, weapons suppliers, and government customers to synchronize mechanical bay constraints, safe separation dynamics, and fire-control architectures. You will drive integration test plans, hazard and system-level analyses, and regulatory flight safety baselines required for technical design reviews and weapon safety boards (e.g., WSESRB/NNMSB). This high-impact role is instrumental in transforming an autonomous platform into an operationally decisive, airworthy combat capability.

  • Adjudicate conflicting design/development requirements with broader team
  • Develop and present technical material for reviews and meetings
  • Support lab, ground, and flight test events
  • Develop/maintain Interface Control Documents, Software Requirement Specifications, Performance Specifications, presentations and review test plans/procedures
  • Coordinate and interface with customers, contractors, and engineering groups assigned to projects

  • 5+ years of combined work experience with post-graduate study in an engineering discipline
  • Familiarity with Air-to-Air/Air-to-Ground weapons, MIL-STD-1553, MIL-STD-1760, and logical Interface Control Documents

You will be rapidly inserted into fresh, dynamic, and at times chaotic situations on a weekly basis. You will wear many hats.

You will also be the face of Anduril to many of our end-users and our customers, capable of articulating the capabilities and limitations of Anduril’s products at both an executive and a layman’s level. We are seeking a Cyber Enablement Lead to help government cyber professionals turn Daybreak’s capabilities into stronger defenses and measurable mission outcomes. This role combines technical credibility, hands-on teaching, strategic communication, and cross-functional leadership.

You will own Daybreak’s government product enablement strategy and personally design and deliver the training that brings it to life. Your work will span audience research, curriculum design, recorded demonstrations and courses, hands-on workshops, executive briefings, and cyber councils. You will work directly with U.S. and international government cyber leaders to translate frontier AI capabilities into practical workflows that address operational challenges.

You will engage across the government cybersecurity ecosystem, including Authorizing Officials (AOs), CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior executives. Practitioners need practical proficiency; executives need a strategic understanding of our cyber products, their value, and their implications for mission and risk. Success means demonstrated capability, sustained adoption, and better cyber outcomes.

We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work.

You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. About the Role

As an ITAV Event Technical Producer at OpenAI, you will lead technical production for complex internal and external events across multiple sites, from early planning through rehearsal and live delivery. You will partner with internal stakeholders and technical teams to translate event requirements into clear production plans. You will coordinate internal and external crews, direct large, distributed shows and coordinate cross-site handoffs, and use your technical expertise to resolve production challenges and make informed tradeoffs. You will also build reusable production practices and AI workflows, improve how teams deliver events, and mentor peers and junior crew members.

This is a full-time, onsite role requiring five days per week in San Francisco. Travel to other OpenAI locations is required as needed for assigned events.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead technical production for complex internal, hybrid, and distributed events from early planning and scoping through rehearsal, live delivery, and debrief.

  • Align Internal Comms, Marketing, Brand Experience, and Workplace on audience goals, requirements, scope, dependencies, and decision owners. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into an agreed production plan and readiness criteria.

  • Configure and operate live audio, video switching, cameras, playback, conferencing, streaming, and recording systems for the agreed production.

  • Integrate the run of show across sites and lead multiple crews globally for all-company events. Align technical cues, rehearsals, content handoffs, schedules, and contingencies with partner teams to deliver one cohesive event.

  • Lead rehearsals and validate the complete audience experience, including remote contribution, playback, recording, and tested backup paths.

  • Independently prioritize technical production tradeoffs and lead risk reviews and incident response. Resolve ambiguity within your scope, and seek guidance for complex situations or decisions owned by event, staffing, budget, or engineering partners.

  • Build reusable production plans, show files, runbooks, and change-control practices. Coach peers and junior crew members to use them independently and verify improvements in readiness, troubleshooting, and execution.

  • Set a prioritized roadmap for production improvements using audience feedback, debriefs, and recurring failures. Lead workflow changes across teams and define permanent-system improvements with AV Engineering.

  • Identify repeatable production work and build AI and agentic workflows with partner teams. Validate results, establish operating and maintenance ownership, support adoption, and measure preparation effort or reliability improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience leading complex live or hybrid productions across multiple teams, from ambiguous requirements through rehearsal, delivery, and debrief.

  • Advanced expertise in multiple live-production domains, such as audio, video, conferencing, streaming, or AV-over-IP, and the ability to diagnose complex interactions across the complete signal path.

  • Experience configuring and operating professional production systems and creating reusable show files or control workflows.

  • Practical AV-over-IP and networking knowledge sufficient to troubleshoot live media, timing, and connectivity with engineering partners.

  • Experience independently resolving ambiguous production problems, setting detailed plans, and prioritizing tradeoffs while seeking guidance when complexity or decision authority requires it.

  • Demonstrated ownership of rehearsals, technical readiness, failover testing, and calm incident response for high-priority productions.

  • Ability to lead crews and influence partner teams without reporting authority, with clear boundaries for content, brand, budget, staffing, and engineering decisions.

  • Experience working with communications, marketing, brand or creative experience, Workplace, and technical partners on complex events, including sensitive planning and late changes.

  • Experience building reusable production frameworks and validated AI workflows, guiding team adoption, and mentoring peers or junior staff with measurable improvements in their capability.

  • Experience with multi-space or multi-location productions and sensitive executive events is a plus.

  • Experience with systems such as Q-SYS, Dante, Ross, Vizrt, or comparable production platforms is a plus.

As a Technical Program Manager, Robotics Facilities, you will serve as the Robotics point-of-contact for cross-functional partners supporting the design and construction of Robotics sites. You will consolidate requirements, priorities, and decisions across Robotics disciplines and route those inputs through your counterpart, who manages design and construction partners and coordinates their workstreams.

You will clarify requirements, coordinate technical and operational inputs, manage dependencies and changes, and drive timely decisions through planning, design, construction, commissioning, and handover. This role calls for sound program judgment as research and operational needs evolve.

About the role

As Revenue Operations Manager for Enterprise GTM, you will own the measurement layer of our go-to-market engine. You will be the key to what is in the pipeline, what is converting, what is slipping, and, most importantly, why, and the . Your primary customers are our enterprise new logo and expansion teams across healthcare and life sciences, financial and professional services, TMT and energy, and public sector.

We treat go-to-market as an engineered system. Architecture and design sit with the Director you report to. Instrumentation, measurement, and diagnosis sit with you.

This is an individual contributor role with a wide mandate and real exposure. You will not manage a team. You will own numbers that go to the VP of Enterprise GTM, the executive staff, and the board.

 

What you'll do

Own the enterprise reporting layer

  • Build and maintain dashboards that give real-time visibility into pipeline health, stage conversion, sales velocity, coverage ratios, and attainment against plan, cut by vertical, segment, and rep.
  • Establish a single agreed definition for every core metric (pipeline created, qualified pipeline, coverage multiple, win rate, cycle time, ACV, committed vs. consumed) and defend it. One number, one source, one definition.
  • Report bookings, recognized revenue, and consumption as the distinct measures they are, and make the bridge between them legible to people who do not live in the model.
  • Run the operating cadence: weekly pipeline reviews, forecast calls in Salesforce and Clari, MBRs, QBRs, and the enterprise section of board reporting.
  • Build stakeholder-specific, self-serve views so vertical leaders, sales development, and partnerships can answer their own routine questions without opening a ticket with you.

Turn the data into insight

  • Answer the hard "why" questions, e.g., why Stage 3 conversion dropped in financial services, which sourcing motions produce the highest-ACV enterprise deals, where multi-year agreements stall in legal review.
  • Build leading indicators and early-warning triggers so leadership sees a coverage or velocity problem 60 days out rather than in the last week of the quarter.
  • Pressure-test the forecast. Deliver an independent bottoms-up call and be willing to disagree with the field's number in front of senior leaders.
  • Diagnose where to reallocate capacity, headcount, and pipeline generation effort across verticals, and bring the recommendation, not just the chart.
  • Produce the analysis behind strategic bets: segmentation changes, territory restructuring, pricing and packaging shifts, new vertical entry.

Instrument the funnel and the systems that feed it

  • Own top-of-funnel reporting for Sales Development: lead conversion loops, sourced vs. influenced pipeline, meeting-to-opportunity rates, and adherence to the Sales Development Playbook.
  • Champion CRM data integrity. Set and enforce completeness standards for qualification fields, next steps, close dates, and competitive tags. No insight survives a dirty pipeline.
  • Work hands-on in the GTM stack: Salesforce, Clari, Outreach, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and Clay.
  • Partner with GTM Engineering to automate reporting and enrichment, and use AI aggressively to compress your own analysis cycle, e.g., signal-based enrichment, automated variance commentary, first-draft narratives for business reviews.

Support planning and compensation

  • Support the Director of Enterprise GTM Architecture through annual and quarterly planning: capacity modeling, territory design, headcount planning, and quota setting.
  • Partner with Finance and Legal on the design and modeling of Enterprise and Sales Development commission plans, and own the reporting that tracks whether those plans are driving the intended behavior.

 

Who you are

  • 8+ years in revenue operations, sales operations, GTM strategy, or a highly quantitative business operations role at a high-growth B2B SaaS, PaaS, or AI infrastructure company. Time in management consulting, investment banking, or PE counts toward this when paired with in-house operating experience.
  • Analytically hands-on. Deep Salesforce reporting fluency, strong command of at least one BI layer (Looker, Hex, Tableau, Sigma), and comfort writing SQL against a warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). You build the analysis yourself.
  • Enterprise sales fluency. You know pipeline coverage math cold, you have worked inside a stage-gate qualification framework such as MEDDIC, and you understand what actually moves a seven-figure, multi-threaded, multi-year deal.
  • A track record of reporting people use. You have built dashboards that changed decisions, not dashboards that nobody opens. You can tell the difference and you optimize for the former.
  • Structured under ambiguity. You can take a vague, badly-posed question, structure it from scratch, find the root cause, and build a system that keeps it from recurring.
  • Commercially and technically curious. You will need to speak credibly about our AI products, our differentiators, and the objections enterprise buyers raise around deployment, security, and data.
  • Persuasive with executives. You can challenge the field's forecast with data in a room of senior leaders and keep the relationship intact.
  • Genuinely interested in using AI to do this job better, not just to report on selling it.

Nice to have

  • Experience in a business with a mixed revenue model (services, platform, consumption) where bookings, revenue, and recognized revenue diverge meaningfully.
  • Experience supporting regulated verticals (healthcare and life sciences, financial services) or public sector, where procurement cycles and compliance gates distort the funnel.
  • Experience standing up reporting for a sales development organization from scratch.

 

What success looks like

By 90 days. Core metric definitions are agreed and documented. Weekly enterprise pipeline review runs off a single dashboard you own. You have found and named at least one thing about the funnel that leadership did not know.

By 6 months. Leadership has leading indicators for coverage and velocity by vertical. Your forecast call is one leadership actively wants to hear. Data completeness standards are enforced and measurably improving.

By 12 months. Enterprise reporting is largely self-serve. Your time has shifted from producing reports to answering the strategic questions that shape next year's plan.

Most complex opportunities. Lead technical strategy and execution on the largest and most complex deals in your vertical, measured by revenue, product scope, or data volume. Act as the final technical authority on whether Scale can deliver what is being proposed.

Evaluation methodology for the vertical. Executive workshops and high-stakes engagements. Lead workshops, technical deep dives, and executive presentations on strategic opportunities. Build or direct the prototypes that make complex solutions tangible.

Technical standards and reusable solution patterns. Build reference architectures, demo environments, discovery patterns, and solution blueprints that become standard practice across the team. Where appropriate, drive solutions that graduate into Scale's product and solution stack.

About the Collective

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC)’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI – because the future of AI depends not only on powerful models, but on the people who teach them to think.
We bring together researchers, academics, and domain leaders across 70+ fields – over 90% of members hold doctorates – to shape how frontier AI systems are built, evaluated, and governed. HFC members have since co-authored published work including SciPredict, PropensityBench, and Professional Reasoning Benchmark.

 

Why join the HFC

HFC centers on three core pillars: the network itself, participation in selected AI/ML projects, and opportunities to publish with our research team.

  • Join a unique and exclusive expert network: You’ll become a part of an interdisciplinary community, consisting of over 90% doctorates and field leaders representing 70+ fields from the leading institutions. We’re a collective of top innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI to power the world’s most important decisions.
  • Participate in AI/ML projects: Beyond the collective network, you’ll be regularly invited to work on high-impact projects with Scale AI and its affiliated lab and platform: building AI safety and policy guardrails, helping models understand real-world deep learning workflows by designing, reviewing, and optimizing PyTorch models, evaluating complex ML code and AI-generated implementations for efficiency and correctness, and more.
  • Co-author selected research publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition.

 

Who should apply

  • Background: PhDs, postdoctoral researchers, and professors with domain expertise in STEM fields such as Computer Science, Machine Learning, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, Humanities, or other related disciplines. 
  • Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion in applied AI research and a commitment to collaboration.

 

How it works

  • Duration: This is a fully remote opportunity with no fixed end date; engagements continue as long as there's mutual interest. This is a 1099 independent contractor engagement.
  • Work authorization: We do not sponsor visas for Fellows. To participate in the HFC Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the US.
  • Community Network: Once you’ve received an invitation to join the HFC, you’ll also gain access to our newsletters, discussion channels, virtual sessions, IRL events, and much more.
  • Projects Logistics: 
    • Project selection: You’ll regularly get matched to carefully selected projects from our partners. Depending on the partner, projects range from evaluating AI models to designing experiments, building RL environments, co-authoring research papers, and more. 
    • Flexible schedule: There's no minimum commitment – you decide whether to take on a project. Most fellows spend 10–25 hours per week, on a schedule they set themselves.
    • Competitive pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to: projects, scope, skillset, and location. You’ll receive the pay information upon receiving project matching notifications.

 

Application process

  1. Apply: We review applications on a rolling basis.
  2. Interview: Candidates will get to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI. Note: If we invited you directly, your invitation will say whether this step applies.
  3. Join the Collective: Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking an Electrical Commissioning Engineer to execute the buildout, startup, and handover of electrical systems for SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. This is a hands-on role where you will commission, test, troubleshoot, and turn over critical systems that support next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with construction, engineering, operations, EPC contractors, and OEM vendors to deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality electrical systems. This is a full-time, onsite role with travel to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the United States.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Execute all electrical commissioning activities for MV/LV switchgear, generators, UPS systems, PDUs, ATS/STS, transformers, relays, busway, and associated controls in hyperscale data center environments.
  • Execute functional performance testing, pre-functional testing, site acceptance testing, load-bank testing, protection-relay testing, integrated system testing, and system turnover to operations.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex electrical, controls, and process issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
  • Develop and review detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, checklists, and documentation in alignment with project specifications, industry standards, and SpaceXAI requirements.
  • Coordinate with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, design engineers, and SpaceXAI stakeholders for system energization, startup sequences, and integrated system validation.
  • Champion safety by enforcing strict adherence to LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols; participate in daily safety briefings and job hazard analyses.
  • Maintain comprehensive as-built documentation, test records, issue logs, and final commissioning reports.
  • Support and deliver training programs for operations and maintenance teams on commissioned systems.
  • Participate in constructability reviews, design feedback sessions, and lessons-learned meetings to continuously improve installation quality and future project execution.
  • Support commissioning schedules and punch-list resolution to meet aggressive project timelines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering.
  • 5+ years of experience in commissioning for electrical systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Working knowledge of commissioning test equipment (power analyzers, insulation testers, hipot testers, torque tools, IR cameras, load banks, relay test sets, etc.), or demonstrated aptitude to learn it in the field.
  • Familiarity with relevant codes and standards (NEC, NFPA 70/70B/70E, IEEE, NETA, NESC, Uptime Institute).
  • Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical drawings, one-lines, three-lines, control schematics, and sequence of operations; update as-built models after commissioning.
  • Experience coordinating with multi-discipline teams, contractors, and vendors in construction environments.
  • Ability to work safely in industrial construction environments and follow LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols.
  • Commissioning experience, including functional performance testing, pre-functional testing, site acceptance testing, load-bank testing, protection-relay testing, integrated system testing, and system turnover.
  • Data center systems and prior work on mission-critical projects 
  • Hands-on experience with EPMS, BMS/BAS, and power-system controls troubleshooting and integration (Modbus, BACnet, etc.).
  • Knowledge of refrigerant systems, direct liquid cooling, and advanced heat rejection technologies.
  • Current OSHA 30 certification or equivalent.
  • Proficiency with commissioning management platforms (CxPro, Procore, PlanGrid, or similar).
  • Experience implementing integrated systems testing, owner’s project requirements verification, and feeding as-built data back into the sitewide power model (load flow, short-circuit, coordination, arc-flash).

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willingness to travel extensively and work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical commissioning and startup windows.
  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite for extended periods during peak commissioning phases.
  • Physical capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders/stairs, lift moderate loads (up to 50 lbs), and wear full PPE for long durations.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to meet SpaceXAI's driver eligibility requirements.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Data Center Engineering team designs training and inference compute clusters from first principles, pushing thermal, electrical, and optical systems to the limit of physics. We operate as a highly cross-disciplinary team of mechanical, electrical, optical, and software engineers, all working to maximize the efficiency, reliability, and deployment speed of terrestrial computing to serve rapidly scaling demand.

This team owns compute architecture, datacenter network design, rack builds, connectivity, in-house design of our own computers, and the manufacturing line that builds that compute. As an Optical Engineer, you will own the physical optical layer of that computer: fiber layout, link design, connector and polarity architecture, optics selection, and production of a plant that can be built, tested, and repaired at AI cluster scale.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end optical and fiber design for AI training and inference fabrics: fiber cabling, cassette/panel architecture, polarity, breakout, reach, and connector strategy (MPO-12/16, SN, MDC, LC, OSFP / QSFP-DD)
  • Write and verify link budgets for scale-out and scale-up interconnect (SMF/MMF, AOC/DAC, DR/FR/LR, InfiniBand and Ethernet), including loss, reflections, FEC, and realistic install margins
  • Develop and implement factory tests for optical interconnects including insertion loss, return loss, and polarization
  • Select and qualify optics, fiber, and connectivity (transceivers, patch, trunks, cassettes, harnesses); own vendor bring-up, failure analysis, and fleet reliability of the optical layer
  • Deploy and verify end-to-end optical interconnect into the manufacturing line
  • Lead commissioning and debug: inspect/clean, power meter, OTDR, BER/FEC stats, and volume failure modes (dirty connectors, wrong polarity, wrong map, damaged end-face)
  • Evolve connectivity toward the next speed and density (800G / 1.6T, CPO/NPO awareness, tighter reaches, higher fiber count per rack)
  •  Work with mechanical and network teams to design structured cabling and raceways with the rack and facilities teams: tray fill, bend radius, pre-term vs field-term, labeling, and a plant that can be built and repaired at hall scale

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, optical engineering, physics, or a related engineering discipline
  • 2+ years of professional experience in fiber layout, optical link design, and/or datacenter/HPC optical engineering

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Demonstrated ownership of fiber or optical design that was installed and turned up in a datacenter, HPC, or AI-compute environment
  • Working command of single-mode vs multimode, MPO polarity, insertion/return loss, and 100G+ transceiver classes
  • Hands-on optical test: inspect/clean, power meter, OTDR or equivalent
  • Fiber interconnect ownership for AI / high-compute clusters (GPU scale-out fabric, InfiniBand NDR/XDR, RoCE Ethernet 400/800G)
  • High-density pre-terminated trunk/cassette design and rack-to-spine optical mapping at hall scale
  • Optics vendor qualification at volume (OSFP, 800G DR8/2xFR4, AOCs, and the failure modes that show up in a real fleet)
  • Experience designing optical harnesses or cassettes for a manufacturing line, including test coverage and yield
  • DWDM / campus DCI for cluster-to-cluster or building-to-building connectivity
  • Familiarity with CPO/NPO, linear-drive optics, and next-gen packaging as it hits the rack
  • Time at a high-velocity AI cloud, GPU cloud, or custom-compute hardware team

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support design releases, line bring-up, and cluster deployments
  • Must be willing to travel to manufacturing and datacenter sites
  • Ability to work in active datacenter and factory environments, including fiber inspection, cleaning, and live debug

As a Rack Design Engineer, you will own the rack as a product: structure, power, cooling, service paths, and the physical integration of servers, switches, optics, and liquid cooling from first sketch through production rate.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own mechanical, structural, and integration design of high-density AI compute racks and associated chassis, frames, busbars, manifolds, and cable/fiber raceways
  • Integrate compute, networking, power distribution, and liquid cooling into a buildable, serviceable, high-yield rack architecture
  • Design for the in-house manufacturing line: DFM/DFA, fixtures, work instructions, incoming inspection, first article, and production ramp
  • Close thermal, structural, and power constraints with cooling, electrical, optical, and network counterparts at the cluster level (CDUs, cold plates, quick disconnects, PDUs/busbars, high-current distribution, tray and bend-radius limits)
  • Drive vendor and in-house parts from concept to qualified production, including sheet metal, extrusions, busbar, manifolds, cable management, and rack accessories
  • Stand on the floor during prototype and production builds: debug fit, leak, cable dress, airflow/liquid balance, and service time; fold issues into the next revision the same day
  • Produce and maintain CAD, BOMs, drawings, and build documentation that a line can run at volume
  • Support cluster deployment of the racks you design, including first-site bring-up and feedback into the next hardware generation
  • Partner with network, optical, electrical, and firmware teams to deploy custom compute for inference and training across SpaceX programs

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline
  • 2+ years of professional experience designing electromechanical hardware that was built and shipped (internship and project experience counts toward this if the hardware was physically produced)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Ownership of rack, chassis, or similarly dense electromechanical products through prototype and production
  • Experience or background in ethernet switching, networking, interconnects, and high power distribution
  • CAD fluency in SolidWorks, Creo, or NX, with released drawings a shop and a factory can build from
  • AI / HPC / GPU rack design: NVIDIA HGX/GB-class, custom OCP, or equivalent high-power liquid-cooled compute
  • Liquid cooling design: cold plates, manifolds, CDUs, quick disconnects, leak detection, and coolant compatibility
  • High-power rack electrical integration: busbar, PDU, 48V, high-current 3-phase, grounding, and service safety
  • Cable and fiber physical design inside the rack (MPO/OSFP dress, bend radius, service loops) in partnership with optical and network engineers
  • Experience taking a rack from NPI onto an in-house manufacturing line (fixtures, cycle time, poka-yoke, rework loops)
  • Thermal and structural analysis (CFD, FEA) used to make a design decision
  • Time at a high-velocity hardware organization: AI/GPU cloud, custom compute, or an OEM/ODM team that owned the product end to end
  • Comfort in a factory or datacenter build environment, including first articles, yield, and hardware debug on the floor

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support design releases, line bring-up, and cluster deployments
  • Must be willing to travel to manufacturing and datacenter sites
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted and work around active factory and datacenter hardware

Job Description:

The International Market Intelligence Analyst develops and maintains consistent, decision-ready budget and competitive information for international autonomous combat aircraft markets. The role supports GTM leads and Mission Success with current evidence on funding, programs, competitors, acquisition pathways, and industrial expectations. 

This is a cumulative knowledge role that brings together two related analytic disciplines. The analyst maintains structured international budget and competitive data, applies established methods to heterogeneous public and commercial sources, and produces recurring country and regional reads for priority markets. 

Regional and country GTM leads own their customers, captures, and win strategies. This role supports those leads with the budget and competitive evidence needed to shape pursuits and inform capture strategies. It does not own Price-to-Win, final pricing posture, customer engagement, or execution of customer-funded programs. 

What you'll do:

  • Maintain international budget coverage. Track partner-nation defense budgets, relevant program lines, and multi-year procurement and sustainment plans for priority autonomous combat aircraft markets. 
  • Maintain international competitive coverage. Keep competitor profiles, competition and award trackers, product comparisons, and teaming and industrial-partnership maps current for assigned countries and regions. 
  • Develop integrated country and regional reads. Combine budget and competitive data into decision-ready products covering funding, timing, competitors, acquisition path, and industrial expectations for GTM and Mission Success teams. 
  • Work from primary sources. Collect and extract data from defense budgets, white papers, parliamentary and legislative records, procurement notices, and reputable open-source reporting, supplemented by commercial market data when available. 
  • Curate the knowledge base. Maintain a structured, cumulative, and queryable international budget and competitive knowledge base using AI-enabled tools for ingestion, organization, and upkeep. 
  • Publish on cadence and on demand. Deliver recurring updates and respond to scoped rapid-turn requests supporting pursuits, campaign reviews, proposal inputs, and leadership decisions. 
  • Track market developments. Monitor programs, competitions, awards, teaming, industrial partnerships, offsets, and co-production developments in assigned markets and elevate material changes. 
  • Support the international campaign system. Provide reliable inputs that help country and regional leads shape pursuits, identify intelligence gaps, and establish collection priorities. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 

Decision rights and interfaces:

    This role is accountable for the quality, currency, and consistency of assigned international budget and competitive data; recurring country and regional products; maintenance of the international knowledge base; and timely response to scoped analytic requests. 

    Regional, country, and opportunity GTM leads are accountable for customer relationships, in-country strategy, partner and industrial development, win strategy, pricing posture, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their pursuits. 

    The designated Price-to-Win lead and responsible GTM and pricing leaders are accountable for PTW positions and final pricing posture. This role provides relevant international budget and competitive evidence but does not perform or own PTW. 

    The U.S. Market Intelligence & Price-to-Win role is accountable for the U.S. market picture and coordinates common methods and knowledge standards with this role. 

    Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for interagency and embassy engagement, export authorizations, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 

    Engineering and Product are accountable for technical solution definition, configuration decisions, and performance commitments. 

    External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead. 

Required qualifications:

  • 3–6 years of relevant experience in international defense budget analysis, competitive intelligence, market research, business development analysis, or closely related work in defense or aerospace. 
  • Working knowledge of international defense budgets and public budget documentation, with the ability to extract useful signal from incomplete and heterogeneous sources. 
  • Experience conducting competitive or market analysis, including competitor profiles, market assessments, or product comparisons. 
  • Working familiarity with international defense acquisition and pursuit dependencies, including FMS, DCS, or hybrid pathways and associated approval, disclosure, and exportability considerations. 
  • Strong research, data-handling, analytic writing, and briefing skills, with the ability to produce clear products for senior and non-specialist audiences. 
  • Ability to manage recurring production while responding to short-notice, well-scoped internal requests. 
  • Experience using AI tools to organize and maintain structured, reusable knowledge resources. 
  • Bachelor's degree in international affairs, security studies, economics, finance, political science, business, engineering, or a related field. 
  • Demonstrated alignment with Shield AI core values: Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, Pursue Excellence. 
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required and to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. 

Preferred qualifications:

  •  Experience supporting defense business development, capture, or strategy. 
  •  Exposure to large UAV, unmanned, or autonomous aircraft programs. 
  •  Familiarity with offset, co-production, or industrial-participation frameworks in one or more priority markets. 
  •  Regional expertise or language skills relevant to Europe, the Middle East, or Asia-Pacific. 
  •  Familiarity with foreign disclosure, security cooperation, embassy or country-team coordination, or interagency advocacy. 

Success in this role:

  • Country and regional GTM leads and Mission Success have current, reliable, and consistent budget and competitive information for priority autonomous combat aircraft markets. 
  •  Country and regional products are delivered on cadence, use traceable sources, and identify material gaps or uncertainty. 
  •  Budget and competitive context is present early enough to help shape pursuits and inform capture strategies rather than being appended after key decisions. 
  •  The international knowledge base grows in coverage and quality quarter over quarter, and recurring questions take less time to answer. 
  •  Material funding shifts, competitor moves, and industrial dynamics in assigned markets are identified and elevated in time for the campaign system to respond.
