Shield AI’s mission is to protect service members and civilians with intelligent systems. We develop autonomy software and advanced aircraft to help U.S. and allied forces accomplish their missions in challenging environments.

About the Role

Shield AI is seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead execution of our aircraft development efforts supporting the U.S. Air Force’s MMA program. This leader will translate customer objectives into an integrated execution plan spanning concept development, aircraft and mission systems integration, prototype demonstration, flight test, and production readiness.

You will partner closely with the program leader, Chief Engineer, engineering teams, manufacturing, supply chain, and government stakeholders to deliver against technical, schedule, and cost commitments. Success requires balancing mission capability with affordability, modularity, and speed—making disciplined decisions about what must be developed, what can be reused, and what is required to demonstrate readiness for the next phase.

The ideal candidate combines engineering depth with program leadership experience and a record of delivering complex aerospace systems under demanding timelines. You can challenge assumptions, resolve competing priorities, and build alignment across organizations while maintaining clear ownership of program outcomes.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own integrated program execution. Establish and maintain the program baseline, connecting engineering deliverables, hardware availability, supplier commitments, integration activities, test events, and customer milestones.
  • Translate customer needs into executable plans. Partner with systems engineering and technical leadership to define program scope, measurable success criteria, requirements priorities, and verification milestones as the program evolves.
  • Drive multidisciplinary coordination. Align air vehicle, propulsion, avionics, flight controls, autonomy, mission systems, and ground systems teams around dependencies and interface commitments.
  • Keep affordability and production at the center of execution. Incorporate unit-cost targets, component availability, manufacturing complexity, and sustainment considerations into program planning and decision-making.
  • Manage customer and partner commitments. Lead program reviews with government stakeholders and industry partners, communicate progress candidly, and coordinate contractual deliverables with contracts and program leadership.
  • Anticipate and retire risk. Identify critical-path threats, immature technologies, supplier constraints, and resource gaps early; assign mitigation owners and drive timely resolution.
  • Build the path to production. Align development schedules with tooling, long-lead procurement, manufacturing readiness, configuration control, and quality requirements.
  • Provide clear executive visibility. Present concise assessments of milestone confidence, financial performance, technical progress, and decisions requiring leadership action.

 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in aerospace engineering, technical program management, or complex hardware and software development.

  • Technical breadth sufficient to evaluate integration dependencies, understand engineering tradeoffs, and challenge execution assumptions across disciplines.
  • Demonstrated ownership of integrated schedules, budgets, program risks, and cross-functional delivery.
  • Experience working directly with government customers or major aerospace partners on requirements, reviews, and delivery commitments.
  • Ability to lead through influence, establish accountability, and make sound decisions with incomplete information.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including executive briefings and customer-facing technical discussions.
  • Has lived and experienced a demo-build cycle

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Group 5 unmanned aircraft, clean-sheet aircraft development, or rapid aerospace prototyping.
  • Familiarity with Air Force acquisition programs and competitive prototype-to-production efforts.

  • Experience preparing for flight-test campaigns and coordinating airworthiness and safety-review activities.
  • Demonstrated success applying design-to-cost principles and transitioning development hardware into repeatable production.

Job Description:

The Senior Analyst, U.S. Market Intelligence & Price-to-Win develops and sustains Shield AI's integrated understanding of U.S. defense funding, competition, and pricing for the X-BAT Family of Systems. The role turns primary-source budget data, competitor intelligence, program history, and market evidence into decision-ready inputs for strategy, capture, pricing, and go-to-market leaders. 

This is a cumulative knowledge role, not a series of one-off studies. The analyst maintains an authoritative U.S. budget, competitive, and PTW knowledge base and keeps it current across the full budget and acquisition cycle, from President's Budget release through congressional marks, enactment, execution, competitions, and awards. 

U.S. X-BAT FoS GTM leads own their customers, captures, and final pricing posture. This role owns the analytic layer beneath those decisions: the integrated view of available funding, competitors, likely bid strategies, and defensible Price-to-Win positions. It is a pre-award enablement role and is not the primary customer or congressional interface. 

What you'll do:

  • Own the integrated U.S. market picture. Maintain one product-line-aligned view of DoW funding, competitors, programs, acquisitions, awards, and pricing signals relevant to the X-BAT Family of Systems. 
  • Lead U.S. budget intelligence. Track requested, marked, appropriated, and executed resources across the PPBE and congressional cycle, including budget releases, marks, enactment, execution, reprogrammings, and budget line item adjustments. 
  • Work from primary budget sources. Extract and interpret data from J-books, P-1/R-1/O-1 exhibits, committee reports and marks, appropriations acts, reprogramming actions, and OMB and Treasury reporting. 
  • Lead competitive intelligence. Develop and maintain competitor profiles, product-line baselines, differentiation analyses, competitor courses of action, teaming maps, and market assessments for the U.S. defense market. 
  • Lead Price-to-Win analysis. Build and defend PTW positions for priority pursuits, including competitor cost structures, likely bid strategies, most-probable price ranges, and pricing sensitivities, and translate them into recommendations on scope, teaming, and pricing posture. 
  • Deliver integrated assessments. Combine budget, competitive, program, and company financial data into coherent judgments for pursuit shaping, capture reviews, proposal color teams, gate reviews, and executive decisions. 
  • Curate the knowledge base. Design and maintain a cumulative, structured, queryable repository of U.S. budget, competitive, market, and PTW content using AI-enabled tools for ingestion, organization, and upkeep. 
  • Publish on cadence and on demand. Deliver recurring cycle-event and market updates, while responding to fast-turn requests for funding, competitive, and PTW analysis. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 

Decision rights and interfaces:

    This role is accountable for the integrated U.S. budget and competitive picture for the X-BAT Family of Systems; PTW positions and pricing recommendations on assigned U.S. pursuits; recurring intelligence products; the curated knowledge base; and rapid-turn analysis supporting pursuit and executive decisions. 

    U.S. GTM leads are accountable for customer relationships and engagement strategy, win strategy, proposal content, the bid/no-bid recommendation, and final pricing posture for their pursuits. 

    Government Relations is accountable for the comprehensive DoW budget picture and engagement with congressional staff, OSD, and the Services; this role provides product-line analysis and does not lead those engagements. 

    Finance and Contracts are accountable for internal pricing policy, cost buildup, financial planning, and contracting terms; this role provides the external funding, competitive, and pricing baseline that informs those decisions. 

    The International Market Intelligence Analyst is accountable for maintaining allied and partner-nation budget and competitive data; this role coordinates methods and integrates relevant context when required. 

    Engineering and Product are accountable for technical solution definition and performance commitments that shape the competitive comparison. 

    External customer and congressional engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead or Government Relations owner. 

Required qualifications:

  • 6–10 years of experience spanning competitive intelligence, defense budget analysis, capture strategy, market assessment, Price-to-Win, or closely related work in defense or aerospace. 
  •  Demonstrated prior experience conducting Price-to-Win analysis on active captures, including competitor cost modeling, bid strategy analysis, and most-probable-price recommendations used by capture and pricing leadership. 
  •  Deep working familiarity with the U.S. defense budget process, including PPBE and the congressional authorization and appropriations cycle, and experience analyzing primary budget documents. 
  •  Demonstrated experience in competitive intelligence, market assessment, and product differentiation analysis in aerospace, unmanned, or autonomous systems. 
  •  Familiarity with parametric cost estimating, should-cost analysis, or related cost-analytic methods. 
  •  Strong data-handling, analytic writing, and briefing skills, with the ability to turn incomplete evidence into defensible recommendations for senior audiences. 
  •  Demonstrated experience using AI tools to build and sustain structured, reusable knowledge resources. 
  •  Bachelor's degree in economics, finance, public policy, political science, business, engineering, security studies, or a related field. 
  •  Demonstrated alignment with Shield AI core values: Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, Pursue Excellence. 
  •  Ability to travel domestically as required and to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior PTW experience across multiple pursuit types, including production, sustainment, and services, in the U.S. Government context. 
  • Experience in congressional appropriations, DoW/OSD resource management, service headquarters programming, or defense-industry budget analysis. 
  • Familiarity with Home | SAM.gov , USAspending, FPDS, and other programmatic data sources that complement budget and competitive analysis. 
  • Experience supporting business development, capture, strategy, or executive decision-making in the defense industry. 
  • Advanced degree in a relevant field; PMP or comparable certification. 

Success in this role:

  • U.S. GTM, capture, and pricing leaders work from one current, defensible picture of funding, competition, and likely pricing for the X-BAT Family of Systems. 
  • Budget-cycle events and competitive developments are anticipated and covered on cadence, with implications delivered early enough to shape pursuit, solution, teaming, and pricing decisions. 
  • Capture and pricing leadership use the role's PTW positions as a reference point and can trace recommendations to defensible evidence. 
  • The integrated knowledge base grows in coverage and quality quarter over quarter, and rapid-turn questions take less time to answer. 
  • Budget, competitive, and PTW judgments are consistent across U.S. pursuits, and discrepancies are visible and reconciled.

The Human Machine Teaming (HMT) Group within Hivemind Solutions’ Strategic Product Development department at Shield AI is hiring an Engineer II or Senior Engineer to build out our developer experience and development capabilities. At Shield AI, HMT refers to the design, development, management, and assurance of the adaptive relationships between end users and the systems they operate—not just an interface problem, or a function-allocation exercise. As part of the HMT group, this role will work with SDK and HMI development teams and product managers across Shield AI to enable effective product design, and to ensure the end product will satisfy customer and market needs before its developed. 

Working alongside the HMT Design, Experimentation, and Operations Leads, you will interact with developers as a user population. You will elicit how they build, evaluate, and deploy autonomy using SDK tools such as Forge and Commander, and characterize the requirements their tooling has to meet. You are the conduit between the engineers who build development tools and HMIs, the HMT capabilities that define what effective teaming requires, and the customers whose operational needs we serve. 

If you have developed software yourself and would rather raise the HMT quality of everything the organization ships than own a single service, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact. 

What you'll do:

  • Become a skilled user of the Hivemind SDK and its autonomy modules, building with the same tools the development teams and our customers do. 
  • Conduct knowledge elicitation and applied human factors and front-end analysis with developers as users of the Hivemind SDK, tools such as Forge and Commander, and with other HMIs. 
  • Translate developer, operator, and customer needs into design and development requirements that SDK and HMI teams can implement and test. 
  • Specify HMT requirements for developer-facing and operator-facing interfaces, and review proposed designs against them. 
  • Assess whether delivered tools, code, and systems satisfy the stated user and HMT requirements, and document gaps with recommended remedies. 
  • Define acceptance criteria and evaluation methods for HMT requirements, and maintain traceability from developer and operational need through requirement, acceptance and robustness testing. 
  • Develop and maintain HMT design and development guidance, documentation, and training materials that developers can apply without you in the room. 
  • Represent HMT in design reviews, architecture decisions, and trade-off discussions, making the HMT case in engineering terms. 
  • Convert recurring friction in the development toolchain and the HMIs it produces from one-off complaints into durable, prioritized requirements. 
  • Roll up your sleeves and work alongside the development team as needed, implementing requirements in the code yourself, and working through integration and API issues alongside them, so that effective HMT is built into the user experience from the outset. 
  • Feed implementation constraints and technical realities back into HMT design and experimentation, so that requirements stay buildable. 
  • Support field events and operator engagements, and carry what you learn there into requirements for the development teams. 
  • Travel to company, test, demonstration, and customer locations to conduct project work (approximately 40%). 

Required qualifications:

  • Engineer II: typically requires a minimum of 2 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 0 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience. Senior Engineer: typically requires a minimum of 3–5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 2–4 years and a Master's degree; or 2 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience. 
  • A degree in computer science, software engineering, a related field, or equivalent practical experience, with a minor in human factors engineering, cognitive systems engineering, or human-computer interaction. 
  • Hands-on software development experience sufficient to earn credibility with engineers, reason about feasibility and cost, and read the code and interfaces under discussion. 
  • Proficiency in Python and C++, and familiarity with at least one other relevant language and tools, such as JavaScript, C#, HMTL, CSS, or docker. 
  • Demonstrated experience eliciting user needs, translating them into design or development requirements that an engineering team implemented, and assessing whether the delivered system met them. 
  • Working knowledge of human machine teaming and human factors concepts, including collaborative work requirements, and ability to reason about operator-autonomy interaction, not screens alone. 
  • Appreciation for the methods and contributions of human factors practitioners, designers, and operators, and the ability to act as a conduit between engineering, HMT, and customer audiences. 
  • Experience in multidisciplinary settings, and ability to work in complex, ambiguous problem spaces and produce clear and structured artifacts. 
  • Strong teamwork and collaboration skills, and written and verbal communication skills. 
  • U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required, with the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret, SCI, and/or SAP-level access. U.S. citizenship required. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in an applications, integration, or solutions engineering role, working between customers and product engineering. 
  • Experience with autonomy, robotics, or simulation software, and with build, simulation, and test toolchains. 
  • Hands-on experience with human machine teaming, MUM-T, human-robot interaction, or applied artificial intelligence, specifically in mission autonomy applications such as UAV Groups 3–5. 
  • Experience with mission planning, C2, and battle management concepts, processes, and doctrine, and with ground control stations or HMIs. 
  • Experience with developer-experience research, developer productivity measurement, or qualitative study of how engineering work gets done.

  • Familiarity with traceability methods, or with AI assurance frameworks.

Bring promising AI research into autonomous systems that operate in the real world.  Shield AI’s Perception team is looking for an engineer who enjoys exploring new ideas and making them work on real hardware. You’ll help turn advances in multimodal computer vision, visual foundation models, and embodied AI into useful capabilities for autonomous aircraft and vehicles. 

Working alongside researchers and autonomy engineers, you’ll evaluate promising approaches, build prototypes, and carry successful ideas into the Hivemind product. You’ll combine learned methods with established perception techniques, working through the sensor, software, and compute challenges that make edge robotics different from a benchmark.

  • Evaluate emerging models and methods against representative sensor data and autonomy needs. 
  • Build prototypes and experiments that reveal strengths, limitations, and practical deployment opportunities. 
  • Combine learned and classical approaches to improve detection, tracking, geometric vision, or sensor fusion.

  • Help deliver tested, documented capabilities and stay involved as other teams adopt them.

  • Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or a comparable ML framework. 
  • A thoughtful approach to experiments, evaluation data, and understanding why models fail.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Principal Autonomy Engineer to define and lead the technical strategy, architecture, development, integration, and fielding of advanced autonomy capabilities for high performance systems. This role will focus on the sensing, perception, decision, guidance, and control functions that enable reliable operation in complex, contested, and dynamically changing environments.

The Senior Principal Autonomy Engineer will serve as a technical authority for autonomy architectures that incorporate advanced RF sensing, signal processing, electronic protection, state estimation, sensor fusion, guidance, navigation, and end to end vehicle simulation. This individual will shape multi year technical roadmaps, solve the organization’s most complex autonomy and RF performance challenges, and connect algorithm development with embedded implementation, hardware integration, simulation, test, and operational deployment.

The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in radar and RF signal processing with demonstrated leadership in autonomous system development. They bring a record of taking algorithms from early concept through requirements, design reviews, high fidelity modeling, hardware integration, test, and fielded capability, while building and mentoring strong technical teams.

What you'll do:

  • Define the technical vision, architecture, and development roadmap for autonomy capabilities that combine RF sensing, perception, state estimation, sensor fusion, decision logic, guidance, navigation, and vehicle control.
  • Lead the development and maturation of advanced radar and RF signal processing algorithms, including waveform design, adaptive beamforming, direction finding, target detection and tracking, clutter mitigation, electronic protection, and sensor performance optimization.
  • Serve as the senior technical authority for autonomy and RF system performance, leading high consequence trade studies, requirements decisions, architecture reviews, algorithm reviews, and technical risk resolution across the full system lifecycle.
  • Establish and govern end to end simulation, modeling, and verification approaches, including RF scene generation, electronic attack and protection modeling, sensor models, 6 degree of freedom vehicle simulation, Monte Carlo analysis, software in the loop, hardware in the loop, and field test correlation.
  • Lead cross functional technical integration across autonomy, software, RF hardware, avionics, embedded computing, vehicle systems, flight sciences, systems engineering, test, and manufacturing to ensure subsystem performance supports mission level autonomy outcomes.
  • Translate mission and vehicle needs into rigorous technical requirements, performance budgets, interface definitions, algorithm specifications, verification plans, and measurable success criteria.
  • Guide the technical development of real time algorithm implementations in MATLAB, Python, C, C++, and DSP environments, balancing performance, compute resources, latency, reliability, integration constraints, and operational needs.
  • Lead technical engagement with customers, partners, suppliers, and executive stakeholders, communicating technical strategy, performance evidence, maturity, risks, tradeoffs, test outcomes, and recommended decisions.
  • Build organizational capability by mentoring engineers, establishing technical standards, recruiting specialized talent, and raising the quality of algorithm development, systems engineering, modeling, verification, and test practices.
  • Influence investment decisions, technical proposals, and growth initiatives by defining differentiated autonomy and RF capabilities, assessing technical feasibility, shaping solution architectures, and supporting customer facing technical engagements.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
  • 15 or more years of professional experience in autonomy, radar, RF sensing, signal processing, guidance and navigation, sensor fusion, aerospace systems, robotics, or related complex technical fields.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership for the architecture, development, integration, and fielding of advanced autonomous, RF sensing, radar, electronic warfare, avionics, aerospace, or defense systems.
  • Expert knowledge of radar and RF signal processing, including waveform design, adaptive processing, beamforming, direction finding, target detection and tracking, clutter modeling, interference mitigation, and performance assessment.
  • Experience developing and validating algorithms through high fidelity end to end simulation, including sensor models, RF environmental models, vehicle dynamics, 6 degree of freedom simulation, and operationally representative scenarios.
  • Demonstrated experience translating mission needs into system and subsystem requirements, performance allocations, interface definitions, algorithm specifications, verification plans, and test objectives.
  • Substantial hands on experience with MATLAB and Python, along with experience developing or transitioning algorithms into C, C++, real time DSP, embedded computing, or hardware accelerated environments.
  • Experience leading technical teams, mentoring engineers, driving design reviews, and resolving complex cross functional technical issues involving software, hardware, systems engineering, simulation, integration, and test.
  • Strong communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior technical leaders, program leaders, external customers, and executive stakeholders through clear technical recommendations and evidence based decisions.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field, with emphasis in radar, RF systems, signal processing, control systems, autonomy, estimation, or optimization.
  • Experience leading radar seeker, RF sensing, autonomy, guidance, navigation, or electronic warfare capability development from early research through system design, critical design review, qualification, test, and production or operational deployment.
  • Expertise in advanced adaptive signal processing techniques, including space time adaptive processing, adaptive beamforming, optimal estimation, multi sensor tracking, waveform optimization, mismatched filtering, cognitive sensing, or machine learning enabled signal processing.
  • Experience with electronic warfare and electronic protection algorithm development, including interference modeling, jamming assessment, clutter modeling, RF scene generation, and resilient sensing methods.
  • Experience planning and executing laboratory, chamber, ground, hardware in the loop, field, and flight test activities, including instrumentation, test design, data analysis, model correlation, anomaly resolution, and readiness decisions.

  • Experience building and leading technical teams of engineers across algorithm development, systems engineering, simulation, embedded software, integration, and test.
  • Active U.S. Secret or higher security clearance.

Aechelon is seeking a Simulation Specialist to help drive growth of the Aechelon simulation portfolio across the AMER defense, aviation, and synthetic training markets. This role serves as a specialist seller and business development resource within the Go-To-Market team, partnering with sales leaders, account owners, program leadership, product, and technical teams to identify, qualify, shape, and advance simulation opportunities with U.S.-based customers, primes, simulator OEMs, integrators, and partners. 

The Simulation Specialist combines simulation and training market knowledge, visual systems and geospatial awareness, and disciplined commercial execution. The role requires a customer-facing professional who can translate Aechelon capabilities into mission-relevant value, support complex pursuits, and help build a credible pipeline while maintaining accurate forecasts and strong internal alignment. 

Why this role matters:

    Simulation is a key growth lever for Aechelon and Shield AI. Customers rely on high-fidelity simulation, visual systems, terrain databases, sensor simulation, and mission rehearsal tools to improve readiness and mission outcomes. This position provides dedicated specialist sales and business development support to accelerate Aechelon simulation growth across accounts and programs. 

What you'll do:

  • Serve as the specialist business development resource for the Aechelon simulation portfolio across assigned accounts and priority pursuits. 
  • Partner with sales leaders, account owners, business development, program management, product, marketing, contracts, and technical teams to identify, qualify, and advance simulation opportunities. 
  • Support achievement of annual sales goals by helping develop new customers, partners, and opportunities aligned with current and planned product offerings. 
  • Maintain visibility into a two-year sales forecast and opportunity funnel, including named programs, estimated value, budget timing, customer stakeholders, procurement path, technical fit, competition, risks, and next steps. 
  • Actively pursue new customers and partners outside Aechelon's traditional customer base while supporting existing customer relationships. 
  • Participate in customer meetings, capability discussions, demonstrations, trade events, and follow-up actions to progress opportunities. 
  • Articulate Aechelon's simulation value proposition in a clear, mission-relevant, and customer-oriented manner. 
  • Help connect customer requirements to product capabilities and coordinate technical support for demonstrations, solution definition, and pursuit shaping. 
  • Manage or support preparation of customer-facing materials, presentations, proposals, quotations, white papers, and competitive positioning. 
  • Provide regular opportunity updates and reports to senior management, including pipeline status, forecast changes, customer engagement activity, and support needs. 
  • Contribute market, customer, and competitive insight to improve messaging, campaign focus, product positioning, and win probability. 
  • Drive disciplined follow-up across active opportunities and ensure internal stakeholders are aligned on priorities, owners, schedules, and customer commitments. 
  • Exercise sound commercial judgment, protect Aechelon from poorly scoped commitments, and avoid overpromising on technical, schedule, or contractual matters. 

Customer and partner engagement:

  • Ensure customer engagement plans, demonstration requests, proposal support, and internal actions are clearly communicated and tracked.

  • Provides strong specialist support to sales and business development teams for Aechelon-related customer discussions, positioning, and pursuits. 
  • Clearly connects simulation capabilities to training, rehearsal, readiness, mission outcomes, and customer value. 
  • Maintains disciplined forecasts, timely CRM or reporting updates, and clear internal coordination across active pursuits.

  • Demonstrated ability to identify and qualify new business opportunities, manage key accounts or pursuits, and contribute to sales targets. 
  • Strong communication, presentation, public speaking, active listening, and interpersonal skills. 
  • Commercial acumen and ability to position technical solutions in terms of customer value, mission relevance, and operational outcomes. 
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, organizational, and follow-through skills. 
  • Ability to work cross-functionally, influence stakeholders, and manage multiple active opportunities and customer needs. 
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office tools, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project or equivalent planning tools.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, aviation, defense, a technical field, or equivalent practical experience preferred.
  • Prefer software engineering experience related to training simulation.
  • Must be eligible to work in the United States and meet company, customer, and program access requirements as applicable.
  • Ability to comply with applicable export-control, security, confidentiality, and customer-site requirements.

  • Experience in simulation and training, visual systems, geospatial databases, mission rehearsal, sensor simulation, autonomy, aerospace, or defense technology. 
  • Experience building relationships with partners, contractors, end users, primes, simulator OEMs, and systems integrators. 
  • Experience supporting proposals, quotations, demos, technical evaluations, capture efforts, or large business opportunities. 
  • Respected network or credibility within the simulation and training industry. 
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001:2015 quality management systems or experience operating in a quality-driven defense/aerospace environment. 
  • Experience in a specialist seller or overlay role supporting sales leaders and account teams.

This role is focused on developing new business and strong technical understanding of simulation systems and interfaces.  

    The ideal candidate is collaborative, technically curious, disciplined in follow-up, and comfortable operating in a matrixed and fast-moving environment. This person should be able to build technical credibility with customers, support opportunity development, and represent Aechelon's simulation portfolio with consistency and professionalism.

Job Description:

Are you a passionate and innovative thermal engineer looking to help develop state of the art AI and aircraft products? Are you eager to make a positive difference in the world? Do you want to work alongside mission driven and values focused teammates?  Shield AI is just the place for you!

As a Staff  Thermal Engineer at Shield AI, you will be the technical authority for aircraft avionics thermal management and electronics cooling. You will define thermal architecture, set analysis and test standards, and carry avionics thermal solutions from concept through qualification and production.

This role is best suited for an engineer who solves problems from first principles, turns ambiguous, open-ended challenges into clear technical plans, and influences design decisions across mechanical, electrical, PCBA, and systems teams. You will mentor other engineers and raise the thermal capability of the organization.

What you'll do:

  • Serve as technical owner and authority for avionics thermal management across V-BAT, from concept through design, analysis, qualification, and production.
  • Define avionics thermal architecture, derive thermal requirements, and establish thermal environments and interface requirements for avionics bays, enclosures, and components.
  • Develop, review, and approve analytical, numerical, and computational heat transfer and fluid flow models using hand calculations and CFD tools such as FloEFD. Set modeling standards, assumptions, and margin policies for the team.
  • Lead trade studies, system architecture decisions, and risk assessments. Balance thermal performance against power, weight, volume, cost, maintainability, and schedule.
  • Define qualification and verification strategy. Lead test planning, instrumentation, and data analysis, and correlate models with test data. Support environmental qualification to standards such as MIL-STD-810 and RTCA DO-160.
  • Influence electrical and PCBA design direction early, including component placement, power dissipation budgets, and thermal design rules.
  • Author thermal specifications and statements of work. Evaluate suppliers and provide technical direction to them for thermal hardware such as heat sinks, cold plates, heat pipes, vapor chambers, and fans.
  • Lead thermal content at design reviews and produce clear, traceable technical reports and analysis records.
  • Mentor and develop junior and senior engineers. Review their analyses and test plans and guide cross-disciplinary teams in applying thermal and fluid fundamentals.
  • Identify program-level thermal risks early, propose mitigations, and drive them to closure.

Required qualifications:

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 8 years of professional experience in avionics or electronics thermal engineering, including technical ownership of thermal solutions carried through qualification and into production.
  • Expert knowledge of heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) and fluid mechanics, with the ability to validate complex models using first-principles calculations.
  • Proven experience defining and integrating active and passive cooling solutions at component, subsystem, and system level.
  • In-depth knowledge of thermal management design elements, including TIMs, spreaders, heat sinks, cold plates, vapor chambers, heat pipes, and fans, and how they are selected, qualified, and manufactured.
  • Advanced proficiency with thermal analysis and CFD tools (e.g., ANSYS Icepak, FloEFD, STAR-CCM+), including setting up, reviewing, and correlating models against test data.
  • Experience with CAD design tools such as NX, SolidWorks, or similar, and with PLM-controlled design release.
  • Demonstrated experience planning and executing thermal qualification and verification testing, including instrumentation and data acquisition.
  • Track record of technical leadership: leading trade studies, presenting at design reviews, and influencing cross-functional design decisions.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and reviewing their technical work.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical findings clearly to engineering teams, program leadership, and customers.
  • Proven ability to self-direct, prioritize without oversight, and deliver in a fast-paced, startup environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • M.S. in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Experience with high-altitude aircraft avionics cooling and thermal design.
  • Experience with aerospace environmental and airworthiness requirements, including MIL-STD-810, MIL-HDBK-310, RTCA DO-160, and MIL-HDBK-516.

Job Description:

Shield is scaling fast, and our internal systems, security posture, and ways of working are changing with it. We're looking for a hands-on change management lead to build our OCM function from the ground up for IT, Enterprise Operations, and Cybersecurity. This person is not a generic change practitioner. They understand the technology well enough to earn credibility with engineers, anticipate where a rollout will break, and translate technical change into something every employee can act on.

What you'll do:

  • Build Shield's OCM program for technical functions: frameworks, templates, playbooks, intake process, and success metrics.
  • Own change strategy and execution for major initiatives, such as identity and access changes, endpoint and device management, security controls and compliance requirements (e.g., CMMC/NIST 800-171), ERP and business system rollouts, collaboration tool migrations, and new IT service models.
  • Partner with IT, EntOps, and Cyber leaders early in project planning to assess impact, readiness, and risk, rather than joining at launch.
  • Run stakeholder analysis and change impact assessments across engineering, manufacturing, flight ops, and corporate teams.
  • Create communications, training, and enablement: announcements, FAQs, how-to guides, short videos, office hours, and change champion networks.
  • Measure adoption with real data (ticket volume, usage telemetry, compliance rates, surveys) and adjust course.
  • Coordinate release and change calendars so employees don't get hit with five disruptions in one week.
  • Act as the voice of the end user in technical decisions, and push back when a rollout plan isn't ready for humans.

Required qualifications:

  • 8+ years in organizational change management, with at least 3 years supporting IT, security, or enterprise technology programs.
  • Real technical fluency. You can hold your own in conversations about SSO/MFA, identity providers (Okta, Entra ID), MDM (Intune, Jamf), ITSM (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management), SaaS migrations, and security controls. You don't need to configure them, but you need to understand them.
  • A track record of building a change function or program, not just executing someone else's.
  • Strong writing skills. You can turn a dense technical spec into a clear two-paragraph announcement.
  • Comfort operating with ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
  • Familiarity with a change methodology (Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter, or similar), applied pragmatically rather than dogmatically.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in defense, aerospace, or other regulated environments (CMMC, ITAR, FedRAMP, NIST).
  • Prosci or CCMP certification.
  • Background in IT project management, service delivery, or technical training.
  • Experience supporting security awareness or compliance programs.

How we measure success in year one:

  • An OCM framework and intake process adopted by IT, EntOps, and Cyber.
  • Measurable adoption and reduced support tickets on major rollouts.
  • Leaders across these functions pulling you in by default at project kickoff.

Job Description:

The Staff Paralegal will serve as a key member of the Legal team, providing senior-level paralegal support across four core areas: (i) general corporate matters, including entity management; (ii) litigation; (iii) employment; and (iv) support of stock administration. This highly experienced professional will partner with the Chief Legal Officer, in-house attorneys, and a broad network of internal and external partners—from the board and executive team to finance, people, security and administrative teammates, outside counsel, and service providers. The Senior Corporate Paralegal will be an action-oriented, highly organized operator who thrives on managing multiple projects and workflows at once, moves quickly on urgent and shifting priorities, and brings the judgment, discretion, and precision required to drive mission outcomes at a high-growth defense technology company. 

What you'll do:

    General Corporate, Governance & Entity Management 
  • Manage Shield AI’s domestic and international entity portfolio, including formations, foreign qualifications, annual reports and franchise taxes, registered agent matters, name changes, and dissolutions. 
  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready corporate records, minute books, organizational charts, officer and director slates, and the entity management system of record. 
  • Support Board of Directors and committee meetings. 
  • Maintain signature authority matrices and delegations of authority; prepare officer’s and secretary’s certificates, incumbency certificates, and certificates of good standing. 
  • Respond to KYC, banking, customer, and vendor requests for corporate documentation, and coordinate with local counsel on jurisdiction-specific requirements. 
  • Support financings, M&A, joint ventures, and strategic transactions, including due diligence, data room management, closing checklists, signature packets, and post-closing integration of entities and records. 
  • Support corporate records and documentation needed for government contracting and security compliance, such as ownership, officer and key management personnel records, and registrations, in partnership with the security and compliance teams.

  • Support in-house counsel and outside counsel on litigation, arbitration, pre-litigation disputes, and internal investigations. 
  • Issue, track, and release legal holds, and coordinate collection and preservation of electronically stored information (ESI) with IT and security teammates. 
  • Manage litigation calendars and docketing, and track deadlines, court filings, and matter status across the portfolio. 
  • Coordinate intake and response to subpoenas, service of process, demand letters, and third-party information requests. 
  • Assist with discovery, document review and production. 
  • Maintain the litigation matter tracker and support reporting on active matters, reserves, and outside counsel spend. 
    • Employment 
  • Support employment counsel and People teammates on agency charges and inquiries (e.g., EEOC and state agencies), demand letters, and employment-related disputes. 
  • Assist with tracking of separation, release, and settlement agreements, offer letter and restrictive covenant documentation, and related approvals. 
  • Assist with workplace investigations, including document collection, interview logistics, and organized recordkeeping. 
  • Help maintain employment policies, handbooks, and required notices, and track multi-state employment compliance obligations. 
    • Stock Administration & Equity 
  • Assist and provide support to Legal, Finance and HR teammates as they administer the Company’s equity plans and equity management platform (e.g., Carta), including option and RSU grants, exercises, vesting, cancellations, and terminations. 
  • Assist with maintenance of an accurate, audit-ready capitalization table, and reconciliation of equity records with Board approvals, HR, payroll, and finance. 
  • Assist with equity grant approvals and supporting documentation, and coordinate with finance on 409A valuations and equity reporting. 
  • Process stock transfer requests and support secondary sales, tender offers, and liquidity programs, including transfer restrictions, rights of first refusal, and required notices and consents. 
    • Collaboration, Execution & Legal Operations 
  • Work confidently and collaboratively with board, executive team, executive assistants and administrators, and outside counsel, investors, and service providers. 
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects and workflows, often under tight timelines, and quickly re-prioritize as business needs and urgent requests shift. 
  • Take ownership of matters from intake to completion, anticipating next steps, escalating issues early, and following through without needing to be reminded. 
  • Build and improve scalable legal processes, templates, checklists, and trackers, and use legal technology and AI-enabled tools to increase speed and accuracy. 
  • Handle highly confidential and sensitive information with the utmost discretion and professionalism. 

Required qualifications:

  • 12+ years of legal experience as a corporate paralegal or other legal professional, including substantial in-house experience at a high-growth technology company, venture-backed private company, and/or leading corporate law firm. 
  • Broad, hands-on experience across legal issues, preferably with experience regarding general corporate and entity management, litigation support, employment matters, and stock administration. 
  • Proven ability to communicate confidently with internal and external partners and collaborate up and down the organization. 
  • Highly action-oriented, with a track record of managing many projects and workflows at once and delivering quickly on urgent and frequently shifting priorities. 
  • Exceptional attention to detail, organization, and written and verbal communication skills, with sound judgment about when to escalate. 
  • Willingness to learn and adopt new technologies. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Familiarity with Delaware corporate law and private company governance, including Board and stockholder consents, minutes, and corporate recordkeeping. 
  • Experience supporting equity administration for a private company, including cap table maintenance, option and RSU administration, and stock transfers. 
  • Experience supporting venture financings, secondary transactions, tender offers, and M&A due diligence and integration. 
  • Experience in the defense, aerospace, government contracting, or other highly regulated industries. 
  • Experience supporting an international subsidiary footprint and working with local counsel across multiple jurisdictions. 
  • Experience designing or improving legal operations processes and implementing new legal technology. 

What makes this role exciting:

  • Play a central role in the building and scaling one of the most consequential AI companies in the world. 
  • Work directly with the Board, executive leadership, and a world-class legal team at the forefront of AI autonomy and defense technology. 
  • Gain broad, high-impact exposure across corporate, litigation, employment, and stock administration matters in a fast-growing company. 
  • Help ensure Shield AI advances technology that protects service members and civilians globally.

This role is ideal for a hands-on builder who thrives in dynamic environments, has deep experience working with test stands, understands precision instrumentation techniques, and has a background in machine shop operations, 3D printing, and product prototyping.

You will be a key contributor in helping bring cutting-edge designs to life, playing a vital role in everything from early-stage prototype development to detailed testing and validation of final assemblies.

What you'll do:

  • Construct and assemble large-scale structures and test articles in alignment with engineering drawings and CAD models.
  • Support the design, prototyping, and fabrication of new products, R&D initiatives, and flight-ready hardware.

  • Document test outcomes clearly and report anomalies or irregularities in a timely manner.
  • Ensure a clean, organized, and safe workspace across shop, lab, and composite work areas.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in instrumentation standards, testing procedures, and fabrication workflows.
  • Source and manage inventory for parts and equipment needed for component repair or replacement.

Required qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in fabrication or aerospace-grade instrumentation.
  • Strong background in strain gauge installation and sensor wiring.
  • Hands-on experience in machine shop operations, including manual and/or CNC tools.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings, schematics, and detailed work instructions.
  • Comfortable working in shop and lab environments with exposure to noise, dust, and chemicals.
  • Ability to lift and move parts and equipment (up to 50 lbs.) and perform physical work for extended periods.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Familiarity with mechanical testing systems (e.g., load frames, DAQ systems).
  • Experience in aerospace, automotive, defense, or high-performance prototyping environments.
  • Knowledge of adhesives, fasteners, and bonding processes for composite-to-metal interfaces.
  • Able to work independently and adapt quickly to changing technical needs.
  • Hands-on experience performing MIL-STD testing including vibration, shock, thermal testing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Head of Production to join our team in Santa Ana, CA to stand up a cutting-edge manufacturing site. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will build and lead the product line organization from scratch, establishing and managing manufacturing processes, quality systems, and the infrastructure needed to scale from prototype builds through full-rate production.

As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must bear the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Your spectrum of support will be exceptionally diverse and require you to rapidly drive aggressive deliverables to completion.

The ideal candidate will leverage a deep expertise in large-scale manufacturing of a number of large, complex assemblies. You need to have experience in heavy fabrication, be able to lead the complex integration of different structures, and have a background spanning structural fabrication, joining and assembly across a variety of metals, alloys, and exotic materials. You need to have led an organization of hundreds, not dozens, and come from an operation comparable to the scale we are building at Anduril. You are a builder, not a caretaker.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Implement and optimize production systems (ERP, MES, QMS).
  • Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent methodologies.

  • Interface with engineering, program management, and customer organizations.
  • Travel over 75% to manufacturing facilities and customer sites.

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or equivalent.
  • Minimum 10+ years of experience in manufacturing or production for complex electromechanical systems.
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience building and leading production teams and organizations.
  • Experience managing production budgets in the $10M+ range.
  • Demonstrated experience scaling production from NPI through full-rate production.
  • Deep expertise with production systems (ERP, MES, QMS).
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience in maritime, naval, or aerospace defense, with knowledge of NAVSEA or MIL-SPEC standards.
  • Experience with MES and ERP systems for production and material planning: working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle or equivalents.

As our Generative Machine Learning organization has continued growing, we are looking for more Technical Program Managers to join the team!

At Cohere, TPMs are pivotal to our success, being seen as operational experts specializing in cross-functional efforts. Great TPMs at Cohere are well-rounded, executing with precision at the tactical level, while partnering with senior leaders and shaping the big picture at a strategic level, and the opportunities are endless in growing the scale and impact of their work. Cohere’s TPMs would often be described as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic leaders who are adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead.

Job Description:

As a Hivemind Solutions Flight Test Leader (ACP Programs), you will serve as the end-to-end technical leader responsible for the integration, verification, and operational test of Hivemind AI Pilot capabilities on portfolio of group 5 UAS/Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (ACP).

You will own the strategy, planning and execution of complex, multi-phase test campaigns supporting the transition of autonomy capabilities from simulation and lab environments to full-scale flight test and operationally relevant mission scenarios, including multi-vehicle coordination. Using a disciplined fly–fix–fly methodology, you will drive rapid capability maturation while maintaining rigorous safety, configuration control, and mission assurance standards. 

This role will serve as the single technical authority for test execution across the portfolio of ACP efforts, responsible for managing risk, test readiness and driving test execution  Here, you will serve as primary focal to facilitate coordination across OEM partners, government customers and internal functional teams rs to deliver high-impact autonomy capabilities at scale.

  • Serve as primary coordinator working with platform OEMs to define and enforce test readiness criteria (entry/exit), define safety-of-flight and mission risk management, airspace coordination and test hazard identification, analysis, and mitigation to ultimately make go/no-go decisions for progression into ground and flight test events
  • Establish and scale test processes, standards, and best practices aligned with DoD DT&E/OT&E expectations and operational test rigor

  • Strong background in full-scale aviation test environments, including aircraft integration, ground test, and flight operations
  • Experience with system-level verification & validation across multiple test environments (SIL, HIL, simulation, and flight)
  • Proven ability to plan and execute complex, multi-phase flight test campaigns involving multiple stakeholders and dependencies
  • Experience working cross-functionally across software, hardware, avionics, systems engineering, safety, and program teams

  • Prior role as Flight Test Director, Test Conductor, or Lead Flight Test Engineer on full-scale aircraft programs
  • Familiarity with military aviation test processes, including DT&E and OT&E frameworks
  • Experience operating in or supporting government flight test ranges and operational environments
  • Background in autonomy, AI/ML-enabled systems, or human-machine teaming in aviation contexts
  • Experience with airworthiness processes, flight clearance, and configuration control for aircraft systems
  • Familiarity with tools such as Git, Jira/Azure DevOps, and CI/CD pipelines
  • Active SECRET clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maritime Manufacturing Technology team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an Electrical Assembly Technician, you'll wear two hats. On the product side, you'll assemble panels and switchboards, pull and route cable, terminate connectors, hook up motors, and outfit marine compartments with complete electrical systems. On the facility side, you'll size transformers, run high-voltage feeds to CNC machines and production equipment, install distribution panels, and keep the shop floor powered and operational. You'll be expected to own the work from sizing through installation and energization.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Assemble electrical panels, switchboards, junction boxes, and controller enclosures. Install components, wire per schematics, and dress/lace wiring.
  • Pull, route, and secure cable through compartment foundations, hangers, stuffing tubes, and penetrations.
  • Terminate cables at connectors, terminal blocks, lugs, and equipment interfaces.
  • Hook up motors, controllers, and actuators: verify phasing, megging, and continuity.
  • Support electrical testing.
  • Groom completed electrical systems for company, customer, and government inspections.
  • Install, wire, and terminate high-voltage equipment feeds for CNC machines, welding equipment, overhead cranes, and production tooling.
  • Size and install transformers (480V to 240V step-down) for production equipment requirements.
  • Install conduit, cable tray, wireways, and raceways per NEC.
  • Wire distribution panels, disconnects, motor starters, and VFDs.
  • Perform facility electrical troubleshooting and repair — identify faults, replace components, restore service.
  • Coordinate with equipment vendors on power requirements, connection diagrams, and commissioning.
  • Ensure all facility electrical work meets NEC, OSHA, and local code requirements.
  • Complete hardcopy and electronic documentation: assembly travelers, test records, cable logs, termination sheets.
  • Maintain compliance with NAVSEA, SUBSAFE, and SOC requirements as applicable to submarine electrical systems.
  • Red-line drawings and report discrepancies through proper channels.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 7+ years of electrical experience: industrial, shipboard, or manufacturing environments.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, single-line diagrams, and cable schedules.
  • Experience with 480V 3-phase and 208/240V single- and 3-phase systems — installation, termination, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience pulling, routing, and terminating electrical cable.
  • Proficiency with wire harness fabrication: crimping, soldering, connector assembly.
  • Working knowledge of NEC for facility electrical installations.
  • Experience using meggers, multimeters, hi-pot testers, and phase rotation meters.
  • Willing to work any shift and overtime as production requires.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • California licensed electrician (journeyman or master).
  • Experience with NAVSEA, SUBSAFE, or SOC-controlled electrical systems.
  • Military shipbuilding, submarine, or naval shipyard experience.
  • IPC/WHMA-A-620 certification (Certified IPC Specialist or Trainer).
  • Experience sizing and installing transformers and coordinating protective devices.
  • Background in CNC machine or heavy industrial equipment electrical hookup.
  • Background in aerospace, defense, or AS9100 / ISO 9001 environments.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Manufacturing Engineering team is responsible for rapidly iterating, scaling, and sustaining cutting-edge defense hardware, including static sensor towers, autonomous ground systems, and high-performance flight vehicles. We bridge the gap between design engineering and physical hardware execution. 

As a Manufacturing Engineer on 1st Shift (6:00 am to 3:00 pm), you will serve as the primary mechanical and assembly authority on the factory floor. You will have a dual mandate: partner deeply with R&D during early architecture to drive rigorous Design for Assembly and Manufacturing (DFA/DFM), and architect the physical assembly processes, precision tooling, and integration lines required to scale complex mechanical hardware from prototype to high-rate production.  

This is a heavily mechanical, hands-on role. You will design assembly fixtures in 3D CAD, perform tolerance stack-up analyses, define structural joining and bonding procedures, integrate smart-tooling systems, and establish repeatable, error-proofed mechanical assembly lines. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Design for Assembly & Manufacturability (DFA/DFM): 
    • Embed directly with Mechanical Design Engineering during early R&D phases to influence product architecture, driving aggressive part reduction, standard fastener consolidation, and modular sub-assembly design. 
    • Conduct detailed 1D and 2D worst-case and statistical (RSS) tolerance stack-up analyses to ensure mechanical interfaces, datum structures, dynamic clearances, and pin/hole alignments assemble consistently without force-fitting. 
    • Define hardware assembly strategies, joint clamping designs, thermal interface material (TIM) applications, structural bonding, and torque sequencing early in the CAD development cycle. 
  • Tooling, Jigs, & Assembly Fixture Design: 
    • Own end-to-end mechanical design of production tooling—including precision assembly jigs, alignment nests, press-fit tooling, ergonomic lift/handling equipment, and mechanical verification fixtures using 3D CAD (NX or SolidWorks). 
    • Apply finite element analysis (FEA) where necessary to validate fixture rigidity, deflection under clamping loads, and stress concentrations. 
    • Produce fully detailed 2D fabrication drawings utilizing ASME Y14.5 Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) for internal machine shops or external toolmakers. 
  • Mechanical Assembly Process Engineering: 
    • Line Architecture & Flow: Design, sequence, and balance complex, multi-stage mechanical assembly lines. Define takt times, line layouts, and ergonomic workstations to transition hardware seamlessly from sub-assembly to final structural integration. 
    • Joining & Fastening Technologies: Establish and qualify robust fastening processes, including torque-tension specifications, torque-angle control, bolt pre-load engineering, and press-fit/interference-fit operations (bearings, bushings, dowels). 
    • Adhesives, Sealing, & Dispensing: Develop repeatable application methods for chemical assembly processes, including structural bonding (epoxies, urethanes), thread locking, environmental gasketing/RTV sealing, potting, and Thermal Interface Material (TIM) dispensing. 
    • Precision Mechanical Alignment & Calibration: Develop standard processes, measurement techniques, and alignment procedures for precision kinematic mechanisms, optical/sensor payloads, gimbals, and dynamic structural joints. 
    • Error-Proofing & Quality Integration: Lead Process Failure Mode and Effects Analyses (pFMEAs) for mechanical assembly workflows. Design physical error-proofing (Poka-Yoke) mechanisms, go/no-go verification gauges, and smart-tool integration (DC electric torque tools with digital data logging) to eliminate assembly errors. 
    • Work Definition & Operator Enablement: Author visual, step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and digital work instructions that clearly define mechanical assembly sequences, critical tool callouts, fastener specs, and quality inspection gates. 
  • NPI Ramp, Sustainment, & Root Cause Analysis:
    • Lead technical disposition and first-principles root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone) on mechanical assembly failures, binding mechanisms, structural interferences, and joint integrity issues. 
    • Bridge the gap between engineering intent and production execution by converting Engineering Bills of Materials (eBOMs) into logical, modular Manufacturing Bills of Materials (mBOMs) within PLM (Teamcenter). 
    • Author and implement Engineering Change Orders (ECOs/ECRs) for mechanical modifications, hardware deviations, and assembly drawing updates. 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a closely related technical field. 
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing or mechanical design role with heavy exposure to mechanical assembly and hardware integration (aerospace, defense, automotive, dynamic robotics, or precision industrial hardware). 
  • Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (Siemens NX strongly preferred; SolidWorks, CATIA, or Creo acceptable) with a strong portfolio of designed and deployed assembly tooling, nests, or fixtures. 
  • Advanced working knowledge of ASME Y14.5 GD&T—ability to design assembly datum reference frames, analyze tolerances, and inspect mating parts. 
  • Deep understanding of mechanical assembly techniques: threaded fastener engineering, interference/press fits, structural adhesives/bonding, torque-tension monitoring, precision shimming, and mechanical alignment techniques. 
  • Demonstrated experience conducting tolerance stack-up analyses and applying DFA/DFM principles to mechanical assemblies. 
  • Strong mechanical problem-solving ability grounded in first-principles physics (mechanics of materials, kinematics, statics).
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export-controlled data. 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of experience taking complex structural or electro-mechanical assemblies from initial prototyping through full-rate production (NPI lifecycle). 
  • Experience implementing smart assembly tooling and integrating digital torque/angle tracking into Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES). 
  • Hands-on machining and fabrication skills (mill, lathe, 3D printing, press brakes) for rapid prototype tooling and shop-floor iteration. 
  • Experience with mechanical process validation, including Measurement System Analysis (Gage R&R) and Statistical Process Control (Cpk/Ppk). 
  • Working familiarity with PLM systems (Siemens Teamcenter) and modern ERP/MES platforms.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surfaces, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking an experienced Metal Former/Machine Operator to join the team, working in a cutting-edge production environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in maritime manufacturing. You will play a key role in delivering our products to our customers by working hands-on with our engineering team on a multi-disciplinary workflow. This role will include fabricating high-quality parts in a cutting-edge production system as well as building assemblies to support the production floor.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Read and interpret technical drawings and CAD models.
  • Program/set-up/operate manual, semi-automated and CNC plate rollers, hydraulic presses, and shears.
  • Design/spec out and lead implementation of various work holding and fixture methods.
  • Act as SME on the rolling/forming/contouring fabrication of pressure vessels, alloys, or varying materials.
  • Troubleshoot issues and make adjustments during the manufacturing process.
  • Perform quality control both during and at completion of the manufacturing process.
  • Lead the organization, machine maintenance, and cleanliness of the work area.
  • Collaborate with the Quality and Engineering teams to identify and implement safety policies and procedures.
  • Help build, supervise, and mentor the fabrication team on rolling, forming, contouring, safe handling, etc.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years' experience as a metal forming technician.
  • Proven experience in setting up and operating plate rolling machines to form cylinders, cones, and other curved shapes of various metal thicknesses (up to 4-6”).
  • Extensive experience in operating hydraulic press brakes for forming and bending.
  • High level of familiarity with various alloys, metals, etc.
  • Knowledgeable in Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).
  • Proficient in using precision measuring tools (calipers, micrometers, protractors, tape measures).
  • Can own the completion of an assigned manufacturing task from start to finish.
  • Ability to flex between R&D fabrication and production tasks.
  • Able and willing to jump in on production assembly integration tasks as needed.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs unassisted.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience working with exotic materials like Inconel, Monel, Titanium, and HY-80).
  • General fabrication experience (cutting, forming, welding).
  • Forklift and/or overhead crane certification or ability to obtain.
  • Experience with CAD software like Siemens NX (Unigraphics).
  • Prior work with architecture and infrastructure engineering partners and/or general contractors to build, improve or modify machining systems.
  • Hobbyist fabricator, welder, builder.

The right person for this role has extensive supply chain knowledge, has implemented or improved ERP/WMS, and has a track record of managing complex, high-value inventory.   • Develop processes to optimize workplans for highly variable demands across multiple sites.
  • Translate tools and reports into actionable tasks that impact the health of warehouse operations across a plethora of processes and sites.

  • Ability to read technical documentation such as drawings and CAD data, understanding of a variety of hardware manufacturing processes for both electronics (PCBAs, sensor hardware, etc.) and structures, mechanical components, and electromechanical systems

  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Columbus, OH

  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills are crucial for collaborating with different teams.
  • Experience with department or factory design and set up - value stream mapping, flow lines, continuous flow, one piece flow, workstation design
  • Ability to completely own a value chain from start to finish, measuring each step of the process, creating actionable tasks that culminated in a significant and sustainable business improvement
  • Demonstrated ability of presenting project results to a cross functional team with clearly relating data to proposed next steps
  • Prior experience with a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) for production operations or Warehouse Management System (WMS)
  • Prior knowledge of NetSuite, Oracle or a similar Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system
  • Have direct experience scoping, buying off and commissioning warehouse automation.

  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance

Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, and operations, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits.

This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive this novel business line's success. You will be required to learn technical concepts and employ them quickly. You will be expected to use your technical knowledge in conjunction with your program management skills to lead cross-functional efforts and deliver exceptional outcomes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Technical Ownership: Drive technical outcomes through meticulous understanding of system performance, managing incident response and after-action, using metrics to derive insights into areas for improvement, quantifying the improvements made through investment in those areas, and maintaining a clear understanding of the state of the system that can be communicated to the customer.
  • Project Planning: Develop project scope and manage changes through the life of the project. Identify, track, and manage project risks. Generate and maintain project schedules. Ensure successful execution of programs in accordance with desired requirements, on schedule, and on budget.
  • New Product Integration: Lead NPI teams to ensure the end-to-end systems integration and manufacturing readiness of new products through to sustained high-rate production ensuring processes, work instructions, test coverage, and tooling are mature enough to rapidly scale complex hardware products. Design, implement, and continuously improve a standardized NPI knowledge transfer framework, including checklists, templates, communication plans, and stage-gate reviews.
  • Cross Functional Partnership: Deeply embed with the Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality and Manufacturing teams from early development through the initial production run to gain expert-level product and process knowledge.
  • Contract Management: Provide contract management support including statements of work, change orders, financial management, terms and conditions, data rights assertions, etc. Manage deliverables, including routine status updates and final delivery to the customer.
  • Autonomous Execution: Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from internal and external clients. Demonstrate high ownership on all pieces of work. Become a trusted partner to Anduril’s engineers.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years of experience specifically in technical project management and/or systems engineering, or related project management and/or systems engineering experience in a relevant industry.
  • Demonstrated success leading NPI teams and scaling multiple complex hardware products into high-rate production.
  • Hands-on experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Data Management (PDM) software.
  • Proven track record using first-principles problem-solving to balance aggressive timelines, budgets, and resource allocation in a fast-paced environment.
  • Extremely organized and detail oriented with exceptional communication skills.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience in maritime, naval, or aerospace defense, with knowledge of NAVSEA or MIL-SPEC standards.
  • Experience with MES and ERP systems for production and material planning: working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle or equivalents.
  • Background in supply chain and/or procurement in a high-rate production environment producing large finished electromechanical goods.
  • Hands-on technical credibility having personally built, debugged, or repaired hardware in a production environment, and is comfortable being on the floor with technicians as the default operating mode.
  • Technical foundation in mechanical assembly, electrical integration, heavy metal or composite fabrication, or precision machining.

As a Partner AI Deployment Engineer focused on AWS, you will operate at the center of one of our most strategic partnerships, driving joint customer success and enabling AWS and partner ecosystems to scale adoption of OpenAI-powered solutions.

We are looking for a highly experienced technical leader to serve as the primary technical counterpart to AWS field leadership (Solutions Architects, Specialists, and Partner teams).

This role goes beyond individual deal support—you will shape strategy, define engagement models, and build repeatable systems that scale across AWS globally. You will work across pre- and post-sales, guiding complex enterprise customers from ideation to production while enabling AWS and partners to independently drive deployments.

You will combine deep technical expertise, strong judgment, and ecosystem leadership to maximize impact across a portfolio of high-priority opportunities.

This role can be based in either Bangalore, Mumbai or Delhi.

In this role, you will:

Strategic AWS Engagement & Influence

  • Serve as the senior technical counterpart to AWS field leadership, building trust and credibility across regions and teams.

  • Influence joint account strategy and technical direction for high-priority opportunities.

  • Shape how OpenAI engages with AWS by defining engagement models, prioritization frameworks, and best practices.

  • Proactively identify and drive net-new opportunities and high-impact use cases across the AWS ecosystem.

Complex Deal Leadership & Execution

  • Lead technical strategy for large, ambiguous, and high-stakes enterprise engagements.

  • Guide customers from early ideation through architecture design, prototyping, and production deployment.

  • Act as a technical decision-maker and escalation point, de-risking complex implementations.

  • Apply strong judgment to prioritize opportunities and allocate limited technical resources for maximum impact.

Solution Architecture & Hands-On Building

  • Design and communicate end-to-end AI architectures leveraging OpenAI and AWS services.

  • Build and guide development of prototypes, POCs, and reference implementations to accelerate adoption.

  • Ensure solutions are designed for repeatability, extensibility, and partner-led delivery.

Ecosystem Enablement & Scale

  • Enable AWS and partners through scalable technical motions (workshops, playbooks, reference architectures, demos).

  • Develop reusable solution patterns and assets that can be deployed independently by AWS teams and SIs.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Feedback

  • Partner closely with Alliances, Product, Engineering, GTM, and Enablement to align on strategy and execution.

  • Contribute to internal knowledge systems and help define standards, patterns, and playbooks for the ADE function.


You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 8+ years of technical consulting (or equivalent) experience, managing C-level technical and business relationships with complex global organizations.
