Anduril Maritime delivers platforms, systems, and integrated effects in the maritime domain. Our autonomous vehicles (sub-surface and surface) are the cornerstone of these capabilities, and we continually strive to push the boundaries of the possible in terms of endurance, autonomy and mission capability. The Maritime team develops and maintains core products and payloads, and adapts and applies those products to serve a wide variety of defense, IC and commercial customers in US and international markets.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Senior Director, Maritime (International Programs) to own and lead an international growth strategy for a portfolio of Anduril Maritime’s products (subsurface and surface). You will engage foreign navies and ministries of defense at the senior-leader level to translate operational requirements into shaped opportunities, own the capture across the international portfolio from qualification through ink, and build the partner relationships and teaming strategies that turn first wins into long-term international programs and programs of record. This role turns capability into enduring international programs: you must be credible going deep on the product with a partner navy's engineers, fluent in deal structure and price-to-win across the table from their acquisition leads, and conversant in the export and licensing machinery that makes a program legal and deliverable.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own your portfolio’s international growth strategy. You will own a Maritime international growth strategy and annual growth plan for your portfolio across partner-nation accounts, including ACV targets, pipeline conversion, and forecast. You will lead international long-range planning and Growth Quarterly Business Review inputs for your portfolio, prioritize markets and strategic captures within it based on market, partner-nation budget, and operational analysis, and run regular pipeline and forecasting reviews aligned with Revenue Operations. You will contribute to the Division's overall international strategy alongside peer international growth leads.
  • Engage at the technical and operational level. You will be the expert level technical and operational voice with a partner navy's requirements officers and engineers, able to go deep on vehicle endurance, autonomy, payload integration, and concept of employment, then translate that capability into an operational effect the customer will pay for. You will own the commercial side in parallel: structuring deals, shaping price-to-win, and selecting the right pathway (FMS vs. DCS, teaming, offset, financing), while running the international machinery that makes a sale legal and deliverable (ITAR/EAR licensing, releasability, end-use management) in close partnership with trade compliance. You will represent Anduril with senior partner-nation leadership (flag officers, senior MOD officials, national armaments directors) and with U.S. stakeholders including DSCA, NIPO, and embassy Security Cooperation Offices.
  • Generate and capture business opportunities. The BD team is ultimately responsible for growing revenue. You will own the identification, pursuit, and shaping of opportunities and end-to-end capture of international opportunities in your portfolio across for our business lines. You will grow a deep understanding of the existing and prospective client base, know the current and planned programmatic and technical roadmap, and be cognizant of the current and changing competitive landscape. You will plan, initiate, and manage continuous engagements with current clients and prospective customers and monitor buying cycles and partner-nation budget cycles for opportunities. You will direct, prioritize, and delegate cross-BL contributors on international pursuits, and own proposal strategy, pricing rationale, and narrative, including oversight of RFI, RFP, RFWP, and other customer responses and drive closure on new business.
  • Lead international program creation. Build the business plans and execution models that outline the acquisition path, align to the customer's investment strategy, and drive toward program-of-record execution. You will shape requirements with key stakeholders, identify and secure relevant funding, and develop the win themes and supplier strategies that win competitive captures. You will lead program creation activities in collaboration with company leadership, the Strategic Growth team, and Government Relations and Global Defense, and drive strategic starts with BL and Division leadership.
  • Lead partnership and teaming strategy. You will develop the partnership and teaming strategy for your portfolio’s international markets, including foreign primes, in-country industrial partners, and offset and industrial participation arrangements, and lead cross-BL and cross-Division collaboration on integrated solutions, investment, and new product development. Where partners, primes, or customers span portfolios, you will coordinate with peer international growth leads so Anduril presents one integrated approach.
  • Grow existing business. You will partner with adjacent business lines and product engineers to identify opportunities for business growth with current clients. This doesn’t just include expanding on current work, but interfacing with existing partners to explore new opportunity areas by sustaining and building on the strong foundation of client relationships.
  • Lead international go-to-market. You will own the international go-to-market approach for your portfolio, including product marketing, narrative, presence at major international defense exhibitions, and customer engagement strategy, and contribute to the Division's broader international narrative.
  • Shape investment and the product roadmap. You will be a liaison between a current or prospective client and the engineering organization, and as such must be able to translate their problem set into an actionable internal plan and product roadmap. You will integrate international demand, including exportability and releasability requirements, into BL investment strategies and product roadmaps in collaboration with GMs and functional leads. You will need to interpret and convey various client needs to the growth and engineering teams, help to inform and manage priorities and execution, regularly communicate pipeline, program, and forecast information to GM, SVP, and C-suite stakeholders, and make sure that performance stays aligned to key milestones and to the transition from first sale to program of record.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10–15 years of relevant industry, military operations, or government experience, including demonstrated excellence leading large cross-functional teams.
  • Proven track record turning technical capability into closed business: a demonstrated history of winning complex, technical product competitions where you personally carried both the technical conversation (system performance, integration, CONOPS) and the commercial one (deal structure, pricing, terms), with personal ownership of closed international awards at program-of-record scale. ABOUT THE ROLE

Anduril is seeking exceptional, hands-on Senior Mechanical Design Engineers to design, test, and scale mission-critical hardware across our autonomous air, sea, ground, and strike platforms. 

We are hiring across three core work-streams. Depending on your background, technical depth, and career focus, you will align with one of the following hardware teams:

  • Core Technology Products: Architect foundational hardware platforms spanning aircraft, missiles, maritime vessels, and ground systems. You will lead blank-sheet mechanical packaging, tight electro-mechanical integration (thermal, RF, PCBAs), and rapid hardware iteration.
  • Lethality (Warhead Design): Design and mature advanced warheads, ordnance, and munitions systems. You will bridge mechanical engineering, dynamic modeling, energetic material packaging, safety constraints, and live-fire test operations.
  • Design for Excellence (DFM / DFA): Sit at the critical interface between initial CAD concepts and production reality. You will drive high-rate manufacturability, assembly optimization, drawing standards, and tooling strategies to ensure hardware can scale at the speed of mission need.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • End-to-End Hardware Ownership: Own components and complex mechanical assemblies from requirements definition, hand calculations, and conceptual design through prototyping, testing, and volume manufacturing.
  • Rigorous Mechanical Design: Create high-fidelity 3D models and fully defined 2D drawing packages in strict accordance with ASME Y14.5 (GD&T) standards.
  • Multi-Discipline Engineering: Design parts across diverse fabrication processes—including precision 3/5-axis CNC machining, complex weldments, sheet metal, injection molding, composite layups, and structural adhesive bonding.
  • Analysis & Simulation: Apply first-principles engineering and FEA/hand calculations to validate structural, thermal, vibrational, and tolerance-stackup performance under harsh operational conditions.
  • Design for Manufacturing & Assembly (DFM/DFA): Perform 1D/3D tolerance stacks, DFMEAs, and tool-access assessments early in development to de-risk production bottlenecks and scale throughput.
  • Prototyping & Test Execution: Build physical prototypes, author detailed test plans, and run functional testing (environmental, dynamic, bench-top, or live arena/range tests depending on track).
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Collaborate shoulder-to-shoulder with Electrical, Manufacturing, Quality, Safety, and Test teams, as well as external suppliers, to solve urgent hardware bottlenecks.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Working knowledge of engineering drawings and practical application of ASME Y14.5 GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis.
  • Demonstrated hands-on prototyping and fabrication skills with a track record of root-causing manufacturing and hardware defects.
  • Strong foundation in engineering first principles (statics, dynamics, material selection, heat transfer, and structural mechanics).
  • Clearance: Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance (Secret or Top Secret depending on division).

  • Active U.S. Security Clearance (DoD Secret, Top Secret, or DOE Q).
  • Willingness to travel for field/range testing when required (up to 25% for Lethality workstreams).

An Ideal candidate will be able to derive the effective radiated power or receiver sensitivity link budgets and then decide what to do with it -- which emitters matter, which technique defeats them, at what geometry and range, and what that demands of the airframe's power, SWaP, and mission profile. The right person has deep, specific electronic warfare experience: fluency in the algorithms inside electronic support and electronic attack systems, and real understanding of how those systems are tasked, planned, and employed against a live threat laydown. You will begin with mission-level outcomes and drive to solutions through appropriate modeling of the solution, domain expertise, and vendor engagement. This will require taking ownership of subcontractor and/or internal technical development efforts and working across various Anduril internal teams to appropriately integrate capabilities. If you are someone who enjoys defining and delivering compelling next-generation autonomous capabilities through rigorous modeling and exploration of system trades followed by hands on integration in the lab and on the vehicle, then this role is for you.

 
WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Define the electronic warfare capability of Group 5 autonomous platforms — threat sets to be countered, effects to be delivered, and the mission-level EW requirements that follow from them
  • Own the electronic support chain end-to-end — wideband channelization, pulse descriptor word generation and deinterleaving, emitter classification and specific emitter identification, and direction finding and geolocation — and specify the onboard processing needed to close it
  • Define and validate electronic attack employment — technique selection and generation, DRFM-based deception, jamming assignment and power management — and the geometry, timeline, and J/S and burn-through conditions under which each technique actually works
  • Run and review EW link budgets — ERP, receiver sensitivity and dynamic range, probability of intercept, and antenna pattern and aperture placement — and translate the available margin into concrete employment options and range envelopes for the mission planners
  • Build and maintain modeling, simulation, and threat-emulation environments to evaluate EW effectiveness against representative threat laydowns, and lab benches to characterize payload performance in contested and degraded conditions prior to flight
  • Own the selection, integration, and lab-to-flight qualification of EW payloads — including vendor and subcontractor technical direction — within the power, cooling, SWaP, and mission-duration budgets of a Group 5 airframe
  • Collaborate with RF, networking, avionics, autonomy, and software engineers to deconflict EW operation against the platform's own datalinks and sensors, and translate mission requirements into EW system engineering specifications traced through design, test, and flight

 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • 10+ years experience in electronic warfare systems engineering, EW capability development, or EW systems analysis
  • Expert level understanding of the algorithms underlying electronic support and electronic attack systems — including channelization, pulse deinterleaving and PDW processing, emitter classification, direction finding and geolocation, and technique generation
  • Expert level understanding of EW methods of employment — how ES and EA capabilities are tasked, planned, and employed against a threat laydown, and how technique selection changes with threat mode, geometry, and range
  • Demonstrated ability to build and critically review EW and RF link budgets, including ERP, receiver sensitivity and dynamic range, J/S ratio, burn-through range, and probability of intercept
  • Experience translating spectrum and power availability into mission-level employment recommendations and range envelopes
  • Experience with RF and EW test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, signal generators, vector network analyzers, and threat simulators
  • Advanced knowledge of systems engineering processes including test case development, requirements enumeration, unit vs. system level testing
  • Ability to decompose mission-level and system-level requirements into EW engineering specifications and coordinate with requirements management to ensure traceability
  • Proficiency in test script development and signal analysis using common languages (Python, Bash, MATLAB)
  • Must hold a U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel up to 30% as needed to support various efforts

 
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS  

  • Experience with electronic order of battle development, ELINT and ESM parametric data, or threat library generation and maintenance
  • Experience with DRFM-based systems and digital technique generation
  • Experience with electronic protection — radar warning receivers, self-protect suites, EMCON discipline, and LPI/LPD, anti-jam, or anti-spoof measures for the platform's own links
  • Experience with EW modeling and simulation or campaign analysis tools (e.g., AFSIM, Suppressor, or equivalent) for effectiveness assessment and trade studies
  • Experience with spectrum deconfliction between EW payloads and onboard communications, navigation, and sensor systems
  • Operational or mission-planning background in EW or SIGINT — for example as an EWO, EW mission planner, or analyst supporting employment of these systems
  • Familiarity with COMSEC procedures, key management infrastructure (KMI/SKL), and handling of cryptographic material
  • Experience managing vendor or subcontractor technical deliverables, including COTS/GOTS evaluation, technical interchange meetings, and integration milestone tracking
  • Hands on experience integrating EW payloads onto UAS or other autonomous platforms

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the full technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system (ArsenalOS) that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

MDP is building the manufacturing digital thread that connects engineering release to the machines and inspection systems on the factory floor. You'll own the integration layer between Teamcenter and Anduril's production platform so CAM programs, machine dispatch and inspection results move automatically instead of by hand.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Build and own the integrations that carry CAM data out of Teamcenter and onto the shop floor, including NX CAM outputs, DNC dispatch to machine controls and the return path for as-run data.
  • Develop custom Teamcenter extensions using ITK and SOA, along with BMIDE data model changes and Active Workspace interfaces, to support manufacturing workflows that off-the-shelf configuration can't reach.
  • Close the inspection loop by integrating CAI and metrology systems so measured results land back in the digital thread as structured data rather than static reports.
  • Make EBOM to MBOM propagation and model-based definition data flow automatically into downstream manufacturing and quality systems.
  • Unblock partner teams across scheduling, applied AI and manufacturing systems by exposing manufacturing data through APIs they can build on.
  • Partner with manufacturing engineers and factory operators to understand production workflows and translate them into software requirements.
  • Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participating in code review and architectural discussions.
  • Deploy and operate your systems in factory environments, including edge compute clusters and OT networks.
  • Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices.
  • Join an on-call rotation supporting production factory systems.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • 8+ years of experience in a software engineering role building production systems, ideally in a fast-paced environment.
  • Deep expertise in Teamcenter development: 5+ years hands-on with ITK and SOA customization in C++ and Java, BMIDE data modeling and Active Workspace.
  • Demonstrated experience building custom Teamcenter handlers, services and integrations, not only configuring workflows and templates.
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing data domains, including CAM and NC programming outputs, machine dispatch, metrology and inspection data, and the relationship between EBOM and MBOM.
  • Strong technical fluency in modern software architectures, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD, and cloud or edge infrastructure.
  • Experience building systems that must operate reliably under real-world operational constraints (high availability, low latency, or constrained environments).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and operations teams.
  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related technical field, or equivalent practical
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or OT-adjacent domains (MES, SCADA, PLC integration, factory automation, IoT).
  • Hands-on experience with CAM and CAI toolchains such as NX CAM, Vericut and PolyWorks, and with industrial data protocols such as MTConnect and OPC-UA.
  • Familiarity with model-based definition standards including STEP AP242, ASME Y14.41 and CAD PMI, and with QIF for inspection data exchange.
  • Familiarity with frontier AI tooling, AI coding assistants, and AI-enabled software development workflows.
  • Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, with demonstrated success balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term system health.
  • Familiarity with enterprise systems such as ERP, MES, WMS, or manufacturing planning systems.
  • Experience in manufacturing industries with hands-on exposure to assembly lines or production environments.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Analytics team models Anduril’s internal data into reusable entities that describe how the company actually operates, in effect a digital twin of our operations. Those entities power the workflows, metrics and applications that help Anduril make better decisions faster. We believe the most valuable thing a unified data model can do is serve as the foundation for products people rely on every day.

ABOUT THE JOB

Most data work stops at the dashboard. For this role, that’s where the work begins.

As a Product Engineer on the Data team, you’ll build internal products on top of Anduril’s unified data model. These are tools that people across Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, People and Sustainment use to run their part of the business, not just monitor it. You’ll own products end to end: talking to users, deciding what to build, designing the data underneath, shipping the interface on top and measuring whether it worked.

You’re an engineer who cares more about the problem than the tech. You know data modeling well enough to extend the foundation, and you’re comfortable across the stack when a product needs it. What drives you is taking a messy operational problem, figuring out what should exist and getting it into users’ hands quickly.

We care less about the stack you already know than about how you handle problems you haven’t solved before. Maybe you’ve built React frontends, or worked with optimization algorithms. If you used them to solve real problems for real users, great. We’re looking for people who see a hard problem and think, “I want to solve that, and I’ll learn whatever it takes.”

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own products from 0 to 1. Find a high-leverage problem, scope it, prototype it, get it in front of users and iterate until it’s something people depend on.
  • Treat operators as your customers. Spend time with the people doing the work, learn their domain in depth, and turn what they actually need (as opposed to what they first ask for) into software.
  • Build across the stack. Work across the data model, backend logic and user interface. Use whatever the problem needs: a frontend, an optimization model, a forecasting engine, an LLM-powered workflow or something we haven’t thought of yet.
  • Build on the ontology and extend it. Use Anduril’s unified data model as the base for your products, and push changes back into the model when a product reveals a gap.
  • Ship fast and measure impact. Favor small releases and tight feedback loops. Success means the business runs differently, not just that the feature went live.
  • Make product calls. Decide what’s worth building, what “good enough” looks like, what to cut and when to kill an idea.
  • Raise the bar for the team. Show the rest of Analytics what’s possible when data models become products.

OUR STACK

You don’t need to know all of this on day one. You’ll pick it up quickly, and you’ll probably add to it.

  • Databricks: our central foundation for data applications, visualization and large-scale analysis
  • dbt: SQL transformations with version control, testing and CI/CD
  • Dagster: asset-based, event-driven orchestration

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Mission Command team is part of the Connected Warfare Division. We build the command and control (C2) tools that help warfighters understand what is happening around them, make faster decisions, and direct their forces. We spend a lot of our time with the people who actually use these tools: in the field, during exercises, wherever they are.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is not a product manager who happens to spend some time forward. The forward work is the product work. As a Forward Deployed Product Manager, you own the path from a warfighter problem to a fielded solution. That covers applications, data models, user experiences, integrations, and infrastructure.

Most of all, you work as a translation layer between the warfighter and the engineering teams. You embed with units, build real expertise in how they fight, and earn enough trust that influence runs both ways. You are there to solve their problems, not to sell them something, and you build an open, trusting relationship by doing exactly that. Sometimes an introduction is made for you. You have to be comfortable with walking into a unit that has never heard of Lattice, and earn your footing from the bottom up.

The profile we are hiring for: a product manager who can walk into a formation, understand the fight, earn the trust of the people in it, map the workflow and the data underneath it, and then pull the right parts of Anduril together to solve it. You walk in with a strong sense of ownership and responsibility, but you back it up with real curiosity and humility.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own warfighter outcomes, not features. Embed with units, learn the mission, find the problems that matter most, and own them through development, fielding, and the work that comes after.
  • Build real relationships with the people in the fight. Earn the trust of warfighters, commanders, staff, and subject matter experts. Become a partner who understands how the unit actually fights, not just what shows up in a requirements document.
  • Do the research in the field. Learn by watching, asking questions, and taking part in real workflows. Turn what you learn into clear priorities.
  • Connect the fight to the product. Map the users, decisions, workflows, systems, data, and dependencies behind an outcome, and use that to drive what gets built and integrated.
  • Design across the whole stack. Do not default to a new app or a new screen. Work out whether an outcome needs an application change, a new or richer data model, an integration, a workflow that spans applications, or a change in how data moves across the Mesh.
  • Use the data model as a product tool. Get to know what data exists, how it is represented, where it comes from, who uses it, and what has to change to make a workflow possible.
  • Design for the tactical edge. Understand how the network and the hardware affect what the user sees and does. Account for degraded conditions, bandwidth, latency, and compute when you define a solution.
  • Pull the right people together. Get warfighters, engineering, design, and the other teams around the same problem, and drive them toward one coherent answer.
  • Make ambiguous problems workable. Be just as comfortable writing a strategy, sketching a workflow, working through a data flow with an engineer, or standing at a whiteboard with the people who will use the product.
  • Run the room. Lead workshops, working groups, and design sessions. Get useful information out of a room, settle competing views, and leave with decisions and next steps.
  • Brief well and tell the story. Communicate clearly to a few operators, to a large room, and to senior leadership. Adjust the level of detail for the audience without losing the substance.
  • Prototype before you spend engineering time. Test ideas quickly with users so you get to the right answer faster.
  • Stay with it through fielding. Watch whether the solution actually helps the mission, find where it breaks under real conditions, and feed that straight back into the product.
  • Look past the single request. Spot the patterns that can become reusable across units and programs, instead of building a one-off every time.

WHO YOU ARE

Anduril moves fast and is scaling fast. We value ambition, hard work, a high bar, and a willingness to disrupt how things are normally done. The people who do well here tend to show these traits:

  • Bias for Action. You ask for forgiveness, not permission, and you hate waiting around to be told what to do.
  • Outcome-Oriented. You figure out what the business needs and work backward from there.
  • Customer Focused. You have real empathy for users and build things they actually want to use.
  • Dive Deep. You sweat the details and get into the weeds to find the root cause of a problem.
  • Ownership. You care about your products and about everything the business depends on them for. You hold yourself accountable for what your systems do and for what they fail to do.
  • Agility. You change direction without drama when the priorities change.
  • First Principles Thinking. You solve problems based on what is actually best here, not because a vendor recommended it or because it is how your last company did it.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance.
  • 4 to 8 years in product management, product scope definition, or service design, or an equivalent record of turning hard user problems into fielded solutions.
  • A track record of translating technical and domain-specific information into narratives, CONOPS, mission threads, and feature definitions.
  • Experience doing research and synthesis with users and SMEs, and building a roadmap from what you learn.
  • A history of earning trust with non-technical, operational users and partnering with them, not just collecting their requirements.
  • The ability to balance needs across engineering, data, and business stakeholders.
  • Comfort working with people across a wide range of technical backgrounds, and the willingness to learn technical systems well enough to use them in your product decisions.
  • Strong facilitation and whiteboarding skills, including leading interactive planning and decomposition sessions.
  • The ability to do your own design work in common tools such as Figma.
  • Strong organizational skills and reliability.
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% of the time, including to field and training environments.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Military experience, or direct experience working alongside operational military units, with a feel for how a unit fights and for Army staff processes, TTPs, and doctrine.
  • A range of product experience across internal tools, customer-facing applications, and tools for technical users.
  • Working knowledge of data models, system integrations, networking, or distributed and edge systems, enough to reason about data flows and network constraints.
  • A self-starter who does well with ambiguity and loose organizational structure.
  • Experience fielding capabilities and improving them based on real operational feedback.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time sensitive, multi domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kills chains and enable mission autonomy.

Most Warfighting capabilities assume connectivity, compute, power, or a secure space to work in. On a base or near a data center, these exist. At the edge, they do not. Our warfighters need capabilities that can fight where they do. Anduril Expeditionary Systems is the business line that solves this. We build Menace, a containerized system that arrives by truck, ship, plane, or helicopter, powers on in under ten minutes, and delivers command, compute, or effects with no site prep, no bespoke basing equipment, and no specialized personnel. 

The Containerized Effects team focuses on clandestine transport, storage, and launch of containerized effects. You’ll work with engineers to build enclosures, launch infrastructure, operating interfaces, and communications that let a small team proliferate munitions and non-kinetic effects with minimal support or reachback. Effect is the outcome, not the mechanism: a missile is an effect, and so is electronic warfare.

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are looking for a Senior Recruiter to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA, Seattle, WA, Boston, MA or Washington, DC. In this role, you will be responsible for owning the Recruiting for Recruiting function.

As a Senior Recruiter on our Talent Acquisition team, you are the person who builds the team that builds the teams. Your mission is to own the end-to-end hiring process for our recruiting organization itself — sourcing, assessing, and closing the Recruiters and Recruiting Coordinators who will become the backbone of our hiring engine across every division.
This is a uniquely meta role: you need to be an exceptional recruiter to credibly evaluate other recruiters. You will know what great looks like because you live it every day — from sourcing strategy to candidate experience to close. You will be the quality bar for the people who set the quality bar for the rest of the company.

You will operate within our matrixed model, aligned to a Business Line Lead for day-to-day priorities and business context while reporting to a Functional Manager who will guide your long-term skill development and career growth. This structure ensures you are solving our most pressing TA hiring challenges while continuing to sharpen your craft as a senior member of the recruiting function.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • End-to-End Hiring Execution

    • Own the full recruiting lifecycle (with sourcing support) for Recruiter and Recruiting Coordinator roles across divisions — from sourcing and screening through offer negotiation and close — ensuring a world-class candidate experience that reflects the standard we expect our hires to deliver.
    • Develop and execute creative sourcing strategies to build robust pipelines for TA talent, recognizing that the best recruiters are rarely active applicants and require differentiated outreach, not just InMail volume.
    • Manage the interview process end-to-end: conduct in-depth screens that assess recruiting craft (not just career narrative), prepare candidates and interviewers, and facilitate calibrated debriefs that separate strong operators from strong interviewees.
    • Assess candidates against our competency framework — evaluating not just what they’ve done, but how they think about sourcing, stakeholder management, data, and candidate experience at a level that matches or exceeds our bar.

    Embedded Business Partnership

    • Partner closely with TA leadership and hiring managers across divisions to understand current and future recruiting capacity needs, team composition gaps, and the specific recruiting profiles that will succeed in each business context.
    • Act as a talent advisor for TA hiring, using market data on recruiter compensation, availability by specialization (technical, G&A, cleared, etc.), and competitive intelligence to shape job descriptions, calibrate expectations, and influence headcount planning.
    • Provide transparent, regular updates on pipeline health, search progress, and market conditions to your stakeholders — particularly when the news requires recalibrating timelines or expectations.
    • Advise on role design and leveling for TA positions, helping hiring managers distinguish between an IC3 and IC4 recruiter profile, or when a Recruiting Coordinator role should be scoped as a sourcer hybrid.

    Functional Craft & Collaboration

    • Contribute to the TA Center of Excellence by sharing market intelligence on recruiting talent trends, compensation benchmarks, and sourcing strategies that work for hiring recruiters specifically.
    • Mentor junior recruiters on the team — not just on process, but on the judgment calls that separate a good recruiter from a great one: when to push back on a hiring manager, how to read a passive candidate’s motivations, when to walk away from a search that’s mis-scoped.
    • Partner with your Functional Manager to set development goals and grow your career toward Staff-level impact.
    • Uphold data integrity in our ATS/CRM to ensure accurate reporting, capacity planning, and pipeline analytics for the TA function.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • 5-8+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Direct experience recruiting recruiters, recruiting coordinators, sourcing specialists, or other TA/People Operations roles. You know where to find strong recruiting talent and how to assess craft, not just career narrative.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, senior-level searches and calibrate candidates against a competency-based framework — not just pattern-matching on resume keywords.
  • Track record of mentoring junior team members on recruiting craft, interview technique, and stakeholder management.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to advise, push back on, and build trust with hiring managers across levels — including TA leaders who know the function as well as you do.
  • A data-informed mindset: you track pipeline metrics, use conversion data to diagnose search health, and can present market intelligence to influence decisions.
  • Ability to operate with a high sense of urgency and bias for action while maintaining quality and candidate experience.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to build rapport with candidates who are themselves expert communicators and relationship-builders.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Experience recruiting in the defense, aerospace, or a related high-tech industry where cleared talent and mission-driven positioning are factors.
  • Experience hiring for TA roles across multiple specializations (technical recruiting, G&A, executive, cleared, coordination/operations).
  • Experience working in a matrixed or dual-reporting organizational structure.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve TA hiring processes — interview design, assessment frameworks, onboarding — not just execute them.
  • Familiarity with recruiting competency models and the ability to articulate what “great” looks like at each level of the TA career ladder.

As a Senior Supplier Quality Engineer on the Sentry products team, you will work inside and outside the organization to define, develop, and execute processes that deliver high quality and reliable products for Anduril's Sentry autonomous surveillance systems and the critical components that make successful sourcing solutions. You will play a critical role in ensuring the reliability, quality, and performance of components and sub-assemblies across Sentry's core commodity families — PCBA, structures and power, radar, and imaging — that enable Sentry to operate in demanding field environments. Everything comes down to clarity and action with our suppliers, and partnering with them for world-class results is essential across the supply chain. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing across multiple commodity types, supply management, supplier development, sub-system performance criteria and metrology, and continuous improvement. If you are someone who loves to build world-class quality processes, work hands-on, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Drive the supplier quality development processes throughout the product development stages with the Sentry product engineering team through design reviews, supplier process development, testing, and qualification for components and sub-assemblies across Sentry's commodity families: PCBA, structures and power, radar, and imaging. Review supplier processes and capabilities to ensure alignment to product, part, and sub-assembly requirements.
  • Provide technical expertise for manufacturing and outsourcing processes across commodities — including printed circuit board assemblies, structural and power systems, radar modules, and imaging sensor assemblies. Drive the gathering of data and insights from suppliers to conduct top-tier evaluations of manufacturability, quality, cost-efficiency, capability, and audit compliance.
  • Partner with development engineering (mechanical, electrical, RF, and optical/systems), product quality engineering, and program management to deliver predictable supply to Sentry development programs and production programs, and manage exceptions, containments, and deviations for supplier technical performance.
  • Drive supplier quality readiness by analyzing key and critical characteristics for drawings, schematics, and supplier specifications, develop measurement systems and inspection criteria, and lead supplier qualification activities (PPAP, FAIR, MSA, Audit, inspection development, PFMEA & AS9102, etc.).
  • Partner with Category Management and Sourcing Engineering to drive overall supplier performance for cost, quality, delivery, and fulfillment of strategic goals across all four commodity families.
  • Own the elimination of supplier risk to improve quality and reliability across the Sentry product lifecycle, from early prototyping through scaled production. Utilize audits, readiness reviews, and training and documentation to ensure compliance.
  • Work cross-functionally to define and execute the technology/vendor capability roadmap and delivery schedules needed for future Sentry variants, proof-of-concepts, prototypes, and explorations.
  • Support Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) and Material Review Board (MRB) activities. Review supplier effectiveness of actions and share lessons learned across the Sentry product team. Drive supplier corrective action and response (SCAR) process.
  • Audit the Quality Management System at our suppliers as it pertains to supplier quality and performance. Define and improve required documentation and activities as needed to ensure Anduril's compliance to flow-down requirements from customers.
  • Prepare, support, and lead supplier onsite audits and reviews for contract deliverables for quality management and compliance.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or similar technical field (Mechanical, Electrical, Optical, or Manufacturing Engineering preferred)
  • Experience in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Quality in aerospace/defense or similar hardware across one or more of the following commodities: PCBA, structures and power, radar, or imaging
  • Experience driving high quality assembly and/or disassembly of complex projects and mechanical or electronic structures through developing drawings, schematics, and work instructions with other engineering functions
  • Experience with driving supplier performance and evaluation. Experience with Statement of Work (SOW), quality clauses, intellectual property (IP), and government regulations such as ITAR, etc.
  • Working knowledge of product development methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) elements such as Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), Automotive Industry Action Group (AIAG) quality improvement techniques, and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T)
  • A strong ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive projects from start to completion
  • Analytical skills and experience with data mining, data quality, metrics generation, issue management systems, and statistical analysis tools (MatLab, JMP, MiniTab, etc.)
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. TS/SCI security clearance
  • Must be able to travel up to 50% of the time to suppliers, sourcing partners, and manufacturing locations


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master's degree in a technical field
  • 5–7 years of experience with developing quality systems for low volume, high complexity manufacturing environments and suppliers
  • Experience across multiple Sentry commodity families (PCBA, structures and power, radar, imaging)
  • Working knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001) and AS9100/ISO 9001-based Quality Management System requirements
  • Experience with government contracts and MIL standard requirements
  • Experience with Teamcenter, SolidWorks, Oracle/Netsuite, Jira, Tableau, and Foundry

Anduril is a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Launched Effects team at Anduril is responsible for scaling the manufacturing and delivery of the ALTIUS family of systems (including the ALTIUS-600 and ALTIUS-700). As the premier Air-Launched Effects (ALE) platform for the U.S. military and its allies, ALTIUS is redefining modern warfare. These tube-launched, autonomous aerial systems must be built to survive extreme deployment environments, requiring precision manufacturing of advanced composites, complex avionics, and modular payload integrations for ISR, Electronic Warfare, and kinetic strike capabilities.

As part of the Launched Effects manufacturing team, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge R&D and high-rate production. We are a fast-moving, mission-driven group of manufacturing engineers, quality specialists, and production operations experts who refuse to accept traditional, slow defense manufacturing timelines. We continuously optimize our assembly lines, implement automated testing, design for manufacturing (DFM), and build resilient supply chains to deploy reliable systems to the front lines at unprecedented speed. If you want to work on a team where your production and manufacturing decisions directly impact global security, this is it.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Senior Supply Quality Engineer, you will work inside & outside the organization to define, develop, and execute processes that deliver high quality & reliable precision machined parts used in our missile and high-speed aircraft programs. This role focuses on collaborating and driving early engagement with our design teams and suppliers to meet our quality requirements the first time. Everything comes down to clarity and action with our suppliers and partnering with them for world class results across the supply chain. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing, supply management, supplier development, sub-system performance criteria, metrology, and continuous improvement. If you are someone who loves to build world-class quality processes with suppliers, work hands-on with engineering, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.

This position is permanently based in Santa Ana, Ca, and requires candidates to temporarily relocate for a comprehensive 2-month training program in Atlanta, GA. To support your transition, Anduril will fully provide and cover all corporate housing, transportation, and travel accommodations during this training period. Your recruiter will discuss the logistics of this program with you in detail during the hiring process.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Partner with our design teams to support the design development process, provide design for manufacturability feedback, and help generate product data (drawings details, BOM information, and part requirements) for precision mechanical parts that lead to supplier quality success.

Provide leadership to manage technical risks, proof of concepts, prototyping, and scaling designs for volume production.
  • Drive the supplier quality development processes throughout the product development stages with the product engineering team through design reviews, supplier process development, testing, and qualification for components and sub-assemblies for precision mechanical parts. Review supplier processes and capabilities to ensure alignment to mechanical & sub-assembly requirements can be achieved.
  • Partner with development engineering, product quality engineering, sourcing engineering, category management and program management to deliver predictable supply to the development programs, production programs, and manage exceptions/containments/deviations for supplier technical performance, particularly in the development phases.
  • Drive supplier quality readiness by analyzing key and critical characteristics for drawings and supplier specification, develop measurement systems, and supplier qualification activities (PPAP, FAIR, Audit, inspection development, etc.).
  • Partner with Global Strategic Sourcing and Product Sourcing Engineering to drive overall supplier performance for cost, quality, delivery and fulfillment of strategic goals.
  • Own the elimination of supplier risk to improve quality & reliability across the product lifecycle. Utilize audits, readiness reviews, and training & documentation to ensure compliance.
  • Support Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) and Material Review Board (MRB) activities, while owning containments derived from purchased goods.
  • Review supplier effectiveness of actions and share lessons learned across the product team. Drive supplier corrective action and response (SCAR) process.
  • Audit the Quality Management System at our suppliers, as it pertains to supplier quality and performance. Define and improve required documentation and activities as needed to ensure Anduril’s compliance to flow-down requirements from customers.
  • Prepare, support, and lead supplier onsite audits and reviews for contract deliverables for quality management and compliance.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy or similar technical field.
  • Experience with producing precision mechanical parts for aerospace or defense.
  • Experience in scaling supplier capabilities and quality from prototype and proof of concept parts to low rate production to high rate production. Experience performing source inspection at mechanical manufacturing suppliers, aerospace and defense suppliers is a plus. Experience flowing down Source Control requirements to Suppliers
  • Working knowledge of AS9100/ ISO 9001-based Quality Management System requirements. AS9100 Lead / Internal Auditor Certification or equivalent is a plus.
  • Experience performing First Article Inspection to AS9102 Industry Standard and ensuring suppliers have control plans and inspection processes that are capable of meeting product requirements.
  • Experience with driving supplier performance and evaluation. Experience with Statement of Work (SOW), quality clauses, intellectual property (IP), and government regulations such as ITAR, etc..
  • Working knowledge of product development methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) elements such as Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), quality improvement techniques, and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).
  • A strong ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive projects from start to completion.
  • Analytical skills and experiences for data mining, data quality, metrics generation, issue management systems, and statistical analysis tools (MatLab, JMP, MiniTab, etc)
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. TS/SCI security clearance
  • Must be able to travel up to 50% of the time to suppliers, sourcing partners, and manufacturing locations.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree in a technical field
  • Experience in creating material and process specifications
  • Experience with managing special processes including heat treatment, polishing, anodize, coating and paint.
  • Process Failure Modes Effects and Analysis (PFMEA) experience and developing source inspection plans and qualifying the inspection process capabilities.
  • Experience with government contracts and MIL standard requirements
  • Experience with Teamcenter, NX, Oracle/Netsuite, Jira, and Foundry

About the Team

The Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) team determines whether Anduril's capabilities can be exported, to whom, and on what authority. We secure the approvals that turn a product into a releasable product: Low Observable and Counter-Low Observable Tri-Service Committee decision memoranda, Critical Program Information assessments, service export baselines, and the disclosure policy that governs what may be said to a partner nation and when.

We work across every business line and every service. Our counterparts are SAF/IA, NIPO, DTSA, DASA DE&C, the program executive offices, and the security assistance enterprise. We partner daily with International Trade Compliance on licensing, and with Global Defense capture teams whose pursuits depend on the approvals we obtain. When exportability is the constraint on a campaign, we are the path off it.

About the Job

This role owns the systems engineering product description and performance review supporting OUSW technology release. You will run the assessment and approval pipeline end to end: scoping product reviews, assembling the artifacts and stakeholders, driving classified assessments to a signed decision, and tracking every open action to closure across dozens of concurrent capabilities and partner nations.

You will navigate complex Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) pipelines, the Low Observable/Counter-Low Observable Tri-Services Committee (LO/CLO TSC), and Anti-Tamper (AT) frameworks to enable Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS).

What You'll Do

  • Collaborate and interface with the Anduril Global Defense TSFD and International Trade Compliance teams to serve as an engineering focal point navigating Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) pipes and approval processes across the military departments and joint agencies.
  • Lead engineering engagements with Business Line Engineering Leads and author technical data packages for the Low Observable / Counter-Low Observable Tri-Services Committee (LO/CLO TSC).
  • Interface with platform engineering teams to educate, apply, and enforce the requirements of DoDM S-5230.28 across the Anduril portfolio.
  • Collaborate and interface with the Anduril Global Defense TSFD and International Trade Compliance teams to structure platform release roadmaps supporting both Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Letters of Offer and Acceptance (LOAs) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) export licenses.
  • Interface with platform engineering teams to identify and classify Critical Program Information (CPI).
  • Collaborate with Anti-Tamper (AT) engineers to understand AT architectures (hardware, software, and cryptographic barriers) designed to protect CPI throughout export platform lifecycles.
  • Run the action-tracking discipline across the team: owners, due dates, and follow-through on commitments made to program offices and internal stakeholders.
  • Build the repeatable process, templates, and artifact standards that shorten time from assessment request to approval as the number of capabilities under review grows.

Required Qualifications

  • 5-10 years of relevant experience in defense systems engineering, export control, technology transfer, foreign disclosure, or security assistance.
  • Working knowledge of the U.S. export control regime, including ITAR and EAR, and of the authorities governing technology release to foreign partners.
  • Demonstrated systems engineering expertise in an environment with many concurrent efforts, external dependencies, and hard deadlines set by others.
  • Experience coordinating across government stakeholders such as program executive offices, service international affairs organizations, DTSA, or the security assistance enterprise.
  • Exceptional written communication, with the ability to turn regulatory and classified detail into concise decision-ready reporting for senior leaders.
  • High-integrity judgment handling controlled and classified information, and the discipline to be precise about what is approved versus what is merely expected.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • US Citizen with active Secret clearance with eligibility for TS/SCI.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with Tri-Service Committee processes, Low Observable and Counter-Low Observable equities, and Critical Program Information assessments.
  • Proven portfolio level systems engineering expertise developing technical briefs, performance specification sheets, and platform descriptions supporting product design reviews (SRR,PDR,CDR,TRR).
  • Prior service in a foreign disclosure officer, technology control officer, or international programs role in DoD or industry.
  • Familiarity with Foreign Military Sales case development, from Letter of Request through Letter of Offer and Acceptance.
  • Experience with Anduril product families, particularly autonomy, munitions, or command and control software.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance.
  • Comfort building trackers and reporting in Salesforce, Confluence, or similar tooling rather than waiting for a system to be provided.

Anduril's Air Dominance and Strike (AD&S) mission systems team is seeking a Senior Mission Systems Engineer with a focus on Electronic Warfare to join our team. The AD&S mission systems team is responsible for developing end-to-end "mission-ized" autonomous air systems capable of delivering exceptional warfighter outcomes to our customers.

As a Senior Mission Systems Engineer for Electronic Warfare, you will own how our Group 5 autonomous platforms sense, characterize, and act on the electromagnetic spectrum. An Ideal candidate will be able to derive the effective radiated power or receiver sensitivity link budgets and then decide what to do with it -- which emitters matter, which technique defeats them, at what geometry and range, and what that demands of the airframe's power, SWaP, and mission profile. The right person has deep, specific electronic warfare experience: fluency in the algorithms inside electronic support and electronic attack systems, and real understanding of how those systems are tasked, planned, and employed against a live threat laydown. You will begin with mission-level outcomes and drive to solutions through appropriate modeling of the solution, domain expertise, and vendor engagement. This will require taking ownership of subcontractor and/or internal technical development efforts and working across various Anduril internal teams to appropriately integrate capabilities. If you are someone who enjoys defining and delivering compelling next-generation autonomous capabilities through rigorous modeling and exploration of system trades followed by hands on integration in the lab and on the vehicle, then this role is for you.

 
WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Define the electronic warfare capability of Group 5 autonomous platforms — threat sets to be countered, effects to be delivered, and the mission-level EW requirements that follow from them
  • Own the electronic support chain end-to-end — wideband channelization, pulse descriptor word generation and deinterleaving, emitter classification and specific emitter identification, and direction finding and geolocation — and specify the onboard processing needed to close it
  • Define and validate electronic attack employment — technique selection and generation, DRFM-based deception, jamming assignment and power management — and the geometry, timeline, and J/S and burn-through conditions under which each technique actually works
  • Run and review EW link budgets — ERP, receiver sensitivity and dynamic range, probability of intercept, and antenna pattern and aperture placement — and translate the available margin into concrete employment options and range envelopes for the mission planners
  • Build and maintain modeling, simulation, and threat-emulation environments to evaluate EW effectiveness against representative threat laydowns, and lab benches to characterize payload performance in contested and degraded conditions prior to flight
  • Own the selection, integration, and lab-to-flight qualification of EW payloads — including vendor and subcontractor technical direction — within the power, cooling, SWaP, and mission-duration budgets of a Group 5 airframe
  • Collaborate with RF, networking, avionics, autonomy, and software engineers to deconflict EW operation against the platform's own datalinks and sensors, and translate mission requirements into EW system engineering specifications traced through design, test, and flight

 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • 12+ years experience in electronic warfare systems engineering, EW capability development, or EW systems analysis
  • Expert level understanding of the algorithms underlying electronic support and electronic attack systems — including channelization, pulse deinterleaving and PDW processing, emitter classification, direction finding and geolocation, and technique generation
  • Expert level understanding of EW methods of employment — how ES and EA capabilities are tasked, planned, and employed against a threat laydown, and how technique selection changes with threat mode, geometry, and range
  • Demonstrated ability to build and critically review EW and RF link budgets, including ERP, receiver sensitivity and dynamic range, J/S ratio, burn-through range, and probability of intercept
  • Experience translating spectrum and power availability into mission-level employment recommendations and range envelopes
  • Experience with RF and EW test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, signal generators, vector network analyzers, and threat simulators
  • Advanced knowledge of systems engineering processes including test case development, requirements enumeration, unit vs. system level testing
  • Ability to decompose mission-level and system-level requirements into EW engineering specifications and coordinate with requirements management to ensure traceability
  • Proficiency in test script development and signal analysis using common languages (Python, Bash, MATLAB)
  • Must hold a U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel up to 30% as needed to support various efforts

 
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS  

  • Experience with electronic order of battle development, ELINT and ESM parametric data, or threat library generation and maintenance
  • Experience with DRFM-based systems and digital technique generation
  • Experience with electronic protection — radar warning receivers, self-protect suites, EMCON discipline, and LPI/LPD, anti-jam, or anti-spoof measures for the platform's own links
  • Experience with EW modeling and simulation or campaign analysis tools (e.g., AFSIM, Suppressor, or equivalent) for effectiveness assessment and trade studies
  • Experience with spectrum deconfliction between EW payloads and onboard communications, navigation, and sensor systems
  • Operational or mission-planning background in EW or SIGINT — for example as an EWO, EW mission planner, or analyst supporting employment of these systems
  • Familiarity with COMSEC procedures, key management infrastructure (KMI/SKL), and handling of cryptographic material
  • Experience managing vendor or subcontractor technical deliverables, including COTS/GOTS evaluation, technical interchange meetings, and integration milestone tracking
  • Hands on experience integrating EW payloads onto UAS or other autonomous platforms

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, the Air Defense Team provides mission critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) threats. Working across product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains the Anduril Air Defense Family of Systems (FoS) in challenging operational environments worldwide.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

We are hiring a Tactical Networking Engineer to lead the design and implementation of a networking stack to enable command and control (C2) and collaborative autonomy of distributed unmanned systems.

You will:

  • Design, implement, deploy, and troubleshoot networking solutions focused on Layer-1 (Physical), Layer-2 (Data), Layer-3 (Network), and Layer-4 (Transport) of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model
  • Perform trade-off studies of different comms and networking solutions including government provided technologies
  • Design network laydowns and configurations decomposed from complex design reference missions (DRMs) involving large scale unmanned systems and forward-deployed C2 systems.
  • Build robust tooling for benchmarking and analyzing network traffic
  • Analyze test network infrastructure, develop recommendations, and implement improvements for network reliability and throughput for edge network
  • Collaborate extensively with software engineers to build a representative modeling and simulation environment including hardware-in-the-loop lab infrastructure

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Expertise in tactical LOS and BLOS RF systems especially in maritime environment for ship-to-ship and ship-to-shore comms
    • SatCom
    • VHF + UHF
    • LPI/LPD and anti-jamming
    • MIMO
    • Antenna theory
  • Experience with networking protocols and technologies, including:
    • Ad-hoc mesh networking
    • Secure communication protocols - IPSec / MACSec
    • Software-Defined Networking / SD-WANs
    • Internet protocols - TCP/IP, DNS, etc.
    • Routing protocols (small and large scale - e.g. mesh routing as well as internet-scale routing across autonomous systems)
  • Must be willing to travel for test field events up to 25%
  • Eligible to obtain and hold a DoD security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Active clearance status
  • Experience with existing middlewares (e.g., DDS, ROS, MQTT)
  • Experience with network modeling and simulation tools and frameworks
  • Experience with electronic warfare (EW) technologies
  • Experience with unmanned aerial or surface systems

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Treasury Analyst with 2–5 years of experience in corporate cash management and banking operations. You will run our day-to-day global treasury operations. Operating in a high-volume, multi-currency environment, you will be responsible for hands-on execution of daily cash positioning, payment processing, and bank portal administration across our banking and financial institution relationships.

The role demands precision and control discipline to safeguard Anduril's cash. You will play an integral part in the Treasury Management System implementation process and ultimately be responsible for its day-to-day management post go-live. This position reports to the Treasury Lead.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Manage and execute daily global cash positioning across our legal entities and multiple currencies, ensuring adequate funding for daily operations with recommendation of daily short term investment redemption/investment activities
    • Prepare and initiate daily domestic and international wire transfers, ACH payments, and intercompany funding movements.
    • Process multi-currency notional cash pooling and FX trade settlements.
    • Act as the primary processor for corporate debt/revolver drawdowns, interest payments, and short-term yield investments.
    • Perform daily bank reconciliations and coordinate cash application with Accounting.
    • Support the compilation and variance analysis of the short-term cash flow forecast.
  • Bank Account Administration & Controls
    • Maintain Anduril's global bank account inventory, supporting account opening and closing workflows in multiple jurisdictions.
    • Coordinate the gathering and submission of Know Your Customer (KYC) documentation and bank account signer updates.
    • Manage user access across banking platforms – granting access and entitlements to new users as well as deactivating users immediately upon employee termination.
  • Treasury Systems & Project Support
    • Partner with cross-functional teams on the implementation of the automated Treasury Management System (TMS).
    • Manage Bloomberg terminal maintenance and user administration.
    • Maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for daily cash operations and banking configurations.
  • Compliance & Audit Support
    • Gather bank statements, signatory lists, and bank audit confirmation letters for internal and external auditors.
    • Support month-end close with cash, interest, and bank fee reconciliations and related journal entries.
    • Support SOX and internal-control walkthroughs and testing for treasury processes. 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Experience: 2–5 years of progressive, hands-on experience in corporate treasury operations, cash positioning, or commercial banking.
  • Technical Skills:
    • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (financial modeling, standard formulas, pivot tables).
    • Experience in navigating and initiating transactions within global banking portals.
    • Direct hands-on experience with treasury management systems (FIS, GTreasury/Ripple, Kyriba, or similar); familiarity with ERP systems (Oracle Fusion, SAP, or similar) is a plus. 
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Certification: Certified Treasury Professional (CTP), or active progress toward it.
  • Analytical & Problem-Solving: Exceptional quantitative skills with meticulous attention to detail; able to spot cash discrepancies and bank transmission issues quickly.
  • Security & Control Focus: High integrity with a firm understanding of segregation of duties, security policies, and internal control frameworks.
  • Adaptability: Ability to maintain operational accuracy under pressure in a fast-paced, high-growth environment while shifting from manual processes to automated system modules.
  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills to collaborate cross-functionally.

We’re looking for people who are customer-focused, technically proficient, and proactive in enhancing IT processes. You should excel at clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, have robust expertise in IT systems (with a strong background in macOS, and ideally Windows), and thrive in collaborative, fast-paced environments.

  • Are highly driven and motivated, with a proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement.

  • Exhibit precision and attention to detail in your work, consistently delivering high-quality results.

As the Manager of Applied AI Architects in London, you will lead a team of senior technical leaders responsible for the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value for OpenAI's largest and most complex customers across the North EMEA region. Your team will act as the “CTO of the book of business,” partnering with customer executives and technical teams from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will set the operating model for how Applied AI Architects own technical account plans across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with Sales leadership and Account Directors, you will help prioritize customer portfolios, allocate technical resources, and ensure business priorities translate into focused use cases, credible architectures, actionable adoption roadmaps, and durable customer value and growth.

You will remain accountable for the team's technical outcomes while developing its people and bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, research, and partners. You will serve as an executive technical sponsor for critical engagements, a senior voice of the customer inside OpenAI, and a cross-functional leader who can move confidently between regional strategy, executive decision-making, architectural depth, and hands-on coaching.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Architects, creating an environment of technical excellence, sound judgment, continuous learning, accountability, and strong customer stewardship.

  • Define and continuously refine the strategy and operating model for Applied AI Architecture across Europe, aligning company priorities with the evolving needs of strategic customers and the regional go-to-market.

  • Partner with Sales leadership and Account Directors to prioritize accounts and opportunities, allocate technical resources effectively, and establish clear technical strategies for the region's most consequential engagements.

  • Ensure Applied AI Architects serve as the primary technical advisors for their portfolios, owning technical account plans, technical milestones, adoption priorities, account health, and expansion opportunities.

  • Lead complex, multi-threaded customer journeys that connect executive vision and business outcomes with use-case qualification, solution evaluation, enterprise governance, and a credible path to production.

  • Coach the team on Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

  • Build trusted relationships with C-suite and board-level stakeholders, as well as senior AI, technology, data, security, and engineering leaders, serving as an executive technical sponsor when needed.

  • Mobilize Deployment Engineering, implementation, enablement, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, Legal, Privacy, partners, and other specialists to remove blockers and deliver a cohesive customer experience.

  • Establish a rigorous view of portfolio health, including technical wins, qualified use cases, production readiness, adoption, usage, risks, measurable customer impact, and the technical contribution to growth.

  • Translate patterns from the field into actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, Research, and go-to-market teams, while developing reusable architecture guidance and customer practices.

  • Foster a culture that balances ambitious customer outcomes with responsible AI deployment, clear ownership, thoughtful prioritization, and effective specialist handoffs.
