About the Job

We are looking to hire a Systems Safety Engineer to join our rapidly growing team in Broomfield, CO. The Battlespace Awareness team develops tactical sense- and decision-making software that provides advanced capabilities for Anduril's command and control (C2) products. This software must work with various combinations of compute hardware, connected sensor/effector hardware, and supporting software services. It must be effective, robust, and safe across various configurations, mission sets, and customer experiences.

Because our C2 products issue tasking to kinetic and non-kinetic effectors, integrate with autonomous platforms, and operate in human-on-the-loop and human-in-the-loop decision cycles, safety is a first-class engineering discipline, not a downstream compliance check. We need a Systems Safety Engineer who can own end-to-end safety assurance: from requirements decomposition and hazard analysis through software performance characterization, validation against government standards, and evidence packages that hold up under customer, regulatory, and legal scrutiny.

What You'll Do

  • Own systems safety end-to-end for C2 software and its interfaces to sensors, effectors, and autonomous platforms — identify and solve problems between the seams and push through to reach desired outcomes
  • Lead safety requirements gathering, decomposition, and traceability across cross-functional teams, translating mission-, system-, and government-level requirements into subsystem-level functional, performance, and safety specifications. Define success in the face of ambiguity
  • Validate that our systems are safe — architect and execute performance-characterization campaigns for safety-critical software behaviors (classification, sensor/effector management, threat forecasting, autonomous tasking) using both simulated data and field-testing data
  • Apply industry and government safety standards rigorously — including MIL-STD-882E (DoD System Safety) and adjacent frameworks, where relevant.
  • Conduct and document safety analyses: Functional Hazard Analysis (FHA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), Failure Modes & Effects Analysis (FMEA/FMECA), Preliminary Hazard Analysis (PHA), System Safety Assessment (SSA), and Common Cause Analysis (CCA).
  • Characterize software-driven performance for safety — quantify false-track rates, misclassification consequences, latency-under-load, degraded-mode behavior, and human-machine teaming failure modes; translate results into risk assessments and mitigation strategies that protect the warfighter and limit liability exposure to Anduril.
  • Validate compliance with government requirements — partner with program offices (Army, MDA, Air Force, Navy) to establish means of compliance, author certification and verification artifacts, and represent Anduril at safety review boards and design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR).
  • Develop test plans, acceptance criteria, and analysis tools to evaluate system safety and performance; use data-driven analysis to verify customer safety requirements are met, and create artifacts to trace safety performance as the system evolves
  • Integrate safety up front into the development lifecycle — not as a side group, but as a discipline embedded with algorithm engineers, software engineers, and product teams; build lightweight, high-velocity safety processes that match Anduril's product cadence without compromising rigor.
  • Develop and implement modeling and simulation frameworks to validate safety-critical algorithmic performance, test system behavior under nominal and adversarial scenarios, and provide data-driven insights for continuous safety improvement

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of systems safety, systems engineering, or safety-critical software engineering experience. Degree in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related field
  • Demonstrated application of MIL-STD-882 (preferably 882E) across a defense program lifecycle — including hazard tracking, risk assessment codes, and closure of safety-significant items.
  • Hands-on experience performing Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) and at least two of: FHA, FMEA/FMECA, PHA, SSA, CCA — with artifacts you can walk us through.
  • Requirements engineering fluency — decomposition, traceability, and verification/validation. Comfortable translating vague customer intent into testable safety requirements
  • Experience validating that safety and performance requirements are actually met — through analysis, simulation, HITL/SITL, and field testing
  • Familiarity with government/customer requirements processes and ability to engage credibly with DoD program offices, safety review boards, and regulatory authorities on means of compliance and certification basis
  • Proficiency with Python (and/or MATLAB) for data parsing, modeling & simulation, data analysis, and visualization of safety and performance evidence
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating across cross-functional teams and communicating complex technical findings clearly to developers, system leads, and customers
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity, evolving priorities, and challenging problems
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States
  • Up to 25% travel to customer sites and test events

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience applying MIL-STD-882 to software-intensive or AI/ML-enabled systems (software safety, autonomy assurance, algorithmic risk)
  • Prior systems safety work on C2, battle management, air & missile defense, counter-UAS, or autonomous systems programs
  • Familiarity with MBSE using e.g. AFSIM, and confident applying Monte Carlo analysis
  • Familiarity with Linux OS and comfort obtaining data from software platforms using command-line tools
  • Familiarity with processes and constraints for real-time and safety-critical software
  • Working knowledge of C/C++ or Rust — coding full-time is not required, but understanding is valuable; our C2 stack uses Rust, C++, Python, etc.
  • Understanding of the full software development lifecycle, CI/CD, and modern software safety practice (safety cases, assurance arguments, GSN)
  • Previous experience in a defense, aerospace, or naval environment
  • Experience with any of the following: radar, tracking systems, sensor fusion, distributed systems, autonomous systems, ML/AI systems

We are looking for a Transportation Associate Manager to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, Ca. WHAT YOU’LL DO 

Day-to-Day Operations of Shuttle and Parking Programs:

  • Provide operational support for the wider Facilities and Campus Operations team as needed.

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and rapid-response problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including early mornings, nights, and weekends, to support transit operations and events as required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook); experience with project management tools or space/transit management software is a plus.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Real Estate & Workplace (REW) team creates and operates the spaces that support our people and our mission. Within REW, the Strategic Occupancy Planning team connects business needs, workplace strategy, and space data to help shape where and how our teams work.

We partner closely with business leaders, Finance, People, Workplace Operations, and Design & Construction to anticipate growth, optimize space utilization, and deliver a thoughtful, scalable workplace experience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Occupancy Planning & Workplace Strategy Manager to lead strategic space planning for our Go-to-Market (GTM) and General & Administrative (G&A) organizations.

In this role, you’ll translate evolving business needs into actionable occupancy strategies, capacity scenarios, and workplace recommendations. You’ll serve as a trusted partner to business leaders, balancing growth projections, operational requirements, and employee experience to inform decisions about how our teams use space.

You’ll own planning across a complex, evolving portfolio while leveraging CAFM/IWMS systems and data analytics to drive accurate, scalable decision-making. This role requires a combination of strategic thinking, hands-on technical expertise, and strong cross-functional partnership to turn planning recommendations into operational outcomes.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week, with approximately 10–20% travel.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own strategic occupancy planning for GTM and G&A organizations, translating headcount forecasts, business priorities, and workplace needs into actionable space plans.

  • Develop and evaluate capacity scenarios, neighborhood strategies, team adjacencies, seating models, and space allocation recommendations to support organizational growth.

  • Partner with business leaders and executive stakeholders to understand evolving requirements, communicate trade-offs, and align workplace strategies with business objectives.

  • Collaborate with Finance, People, Analytics, Design & Construction, and Workplace Operations to reconcile forecasts, assess capacity constraints, and guide planning decisions through implementation.

  • Translate workplace needs into practical stacking, blocking, and move plans, ensuring recommendations account for operational feasibility, timing, and employee experience.

  • Leverage CAFM/IWMS platforms and analytical tools to maintain accurate space inventories, floor plans, seating allocations, and utilization data.

  • Identify and resolve space data discrepancies, establish quality controls, and partner with internal system owners and external vendors to improve data reliability.

  • Develop dashboards, planning workflows, and reporting tools that improve visibility into occupancy trends, capacity risks, and portfolio performance.

  • Drive continuous improvement in occupancy planning processes, including opportunities for automation, system enhancements, and scalable planning practices.

  • Support workplace change initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams to ensure clear communication, coordinated execution, and successful transitions.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Bring 5–8+ years of experience in occupancy planning, workplace strategy, space management, or a related field, with experience independently managing complex, multi-team or multi-site portfolios.

  • Have a strong track record of translating business growth, headcount projections, and workplace requirements into practical, data-informed space strategies.

  • Possess hands-on experience with CAFM/IWMS platforms, including space inventory management, floor plans, seating allocations, data reconciliation, and reporting.

  • Are highly analytical and comfortable developing scenarios, evaluating trade-offs, and translating complex data into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.

  • Excel at building trusted relationships with business leaders and cross-functional partners, influencing decisions without direct authority.

  • Can balance long-term strategic planning with hands-on execution in a fast-paced environment where priorities and requirements evolve quickly.

  • Have experience supporting workplace transitions, flexible seating strategies, organizational growth, or large-scale space planning initiatives.

  • Communicate clearly and effectively, whether presenting recommendations to executives, documenting planning assumptions, or coordinating implementation across teams.

  • Are comfortable navigating ambiguity, identifying opportunities for process improvement, and building scalable solutions.

Experience with OfficeSpace or comparable CAFM/IWMS platforms, CAD or floor-plan tools, business intelligence platforms, system migrations, and vendor management is a plus.

Working directly with the Head of Creative, Business, you will lead resource planning and allocation across our internal creative team, contractors, and agency partners—balancing ongoing campaigns with rapidly emerging launches and requests.

You’ll develop a deep understanding of our creative talent and capabilities, translate business priorities into thoughtful staffing plans, and help teams navigate competing demands without sacrificing craft or quality. This requires both strong judgment and resourcefulness: knowing when to shift capacity, bring in specialist expertise, adjust scope, sequence work differently, or recommend a different delivery model.

AI will be an important part of how you work. You’ll partner with creatives, producers, and Strategy & Operations to build better visibility into demand and capacity, improve resource planning, and reduce repetitive coordination. Your success will show up in how effectively talent is deployed, how clearly staffing decisions are made, and whether the team can deliver excellent work at a sustainable pace.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Own creative resource planning and allocation across internal teams, contractors, and agencies, matching each project with the appropriate skills, experience, and capacity.

  • Maintain a clear, current view of team availability, capabilities, assignments, and upcoming demand across design, copy, motion, video, and web.

  • Build capacity forecasts and staffing scenarios that help creative leadership anticipate gaps, make informed tradeoffs, and plan for both sustained programs and fast-moving launches.

  • Partner with Strategy & Operations, creative leads, and producers to assess incoming work, understand its resource needs, and develop clear staffing recommendations.

  • Develop a deep understanding of each team member’s strengths, development goals, and workload, using that context to make thoughtful assignments and identify opportunities for growth.

  • Recommend the right resource model for each need—internal talent, contractors, agencies, specialists, or self-service—based on priorities, complexity, timing, cost, and creative ambition.

  • Build and maintain a strong network of contractors, freelancers, and agency partners so the team can quickly access specialized skills or additional capacity.

  • Manage contractor and agency assignments in partnership with creative leadership and producers, ensuring clarity on scope, timing, cost, and expected outcomes.

  • Manage the creative resourcing budget within agreed funding, forecasting commitments, surfacing risks, and recommending adjustments to the talent mix in partnership with Business Operations.

  • Identify and resolve resource conflicts, workload imbalances, and capability gaps before they put team sustainability, quality, or timelines at risk.

  • Create clear reporting and decision-making rhythms around demand, capacity, utilization, and resource needs.

  • Build and improve AI-enabled tools and workflows that make forecasting, talent matching, allocation, and resource coordination faster and more effective.

  • Use staffing data and team feedback to improve resource decisions, strengthen planning, and support a sustainable creative organization.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • 10+ years of experience personally owning creative resource management, workforce planning, or talent allocation across multiple disciplines and concurrent programs.

  • A strong understanding of design, copy, motion, video, and web production, including the skills, roles, and collaboration required to deliver different kinds of creative work.

  • A track record of building and running capacity-planning, forecasting, and resource-allocation systems that teams trust and use.

  • Strong judgment in matching people to work, balancing individual strengths and development opportunities with business priorities, timelines, and team capacity.

  • Experience developing and managing a flexible talent ecosystem that includes internal teams, contractors, freelancers, specialists, and agencies.

  • Sound judgment about when work should be handled in-house, externally, or through a self-service model—and how to balance speed, cost, team sustainability, and craft.

  • Experience managing creative resourcing budgets, contractor rates, agency fee models, and related commercial tradeoffs.

  • Hands-on experience using AI or automation to improve resource planning, forecasting, coordination, or creative capacity, with an understanding of where human judgment remains essential.

  • The ability to build trust with creative leaders, individual contributors, producers, marketers, and external partners while communicating staffing decisions and tradeoffs clearly.

  • High ownership, discretion, composure, and flexibility in ambiguous environments, with a bias toward solving problems and helping creative talent do its best work.

We are seeking a technically deep, creativity-driven Applied AI Engineer who is already a power user of AI coding tools and passionate about pushing the boundaries of developer productivity. You will partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on builders to design, validate, and scale advanced AI workflows, often using Codex to prototype and build the very demos, integrations, and automations customers ultimately adopt.

This is a highly cross-functional role that blends technical architecture, product strategy, and customer-facing leadership. You’ll work closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Applied Engineering, and the broader Codex organization to advocate for customer needs, shape product direction, and accelerate the successful deployment of intelligent coding systems across some of the world’s most influential companies.

This role is based in Singapore. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

About the team

The OpenAI for Government team brings frontier AI to public institutions to help them achieve their missions. We partner with government leaders, mission owners, and technical teams to deploy AI tools responsibly, with the reliability, security, and support needed for meaningful use.

Our Federal Civilian and State & Local Government business supports public institutions across a broad range of missions. We help these customers apply frontier AI to public services, knowledge work, research, and mission operations through hands-on delivery, tailored enablement, and collaboration with their teams.

About the Role

The Strategic Delivery Lead (SDL), Federal Civilian & State and Local Government, will shape and deliver high-impact AI engagements across federal civilian agencies and state and local governments. You will turn customer priorities into practical deployments and sustained use, helping government leaders and mission teams apply OpenAI technology to public services, knowledge discovery, and operational workflows.

This individual contributor role reports to the leader of Federal Civilian and State & Local Government. You will work alongside Account Directors and Applied AI Architects across assigned engagements, coordinating Research, Product, Engineering, Policy, Security, and Enablement resources. Account Directors own commercial strategy, contracts, and quota; you own delivery coordination, adoption, and customer outcomes, without an individual sales quota.

You will lead execution across customer and OpenAI workstreams: define scope, milestones, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and success measures; surface risks; resolve blockers; and communicate progress to agency executives, program leaders, and working teams. You are accountable for agreed delivery commitments and customer acceptance. Engineering and Product teams remain responsible for technical implementation and operation of the systems they own.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role combining senior relationship leadership with hands-on execution. Success requires sound judgment, technical fluency, strong program management, and the ability to turn executive alignment into useful technology in government teams’ hands.

This role is based in Washington, DC, with domestic travel for high-value customer engagements, workshops, and delivery milestones.

In this role, you will:

  • Build trusted relationships with senior government leaders, program owners, and technical and mission teams to identify priorities and turn senior alignment into actionable engagements.

  • Own delivery plans for assigned federal civilian and state and local government engagements, with clear milestones, accountable owners, customer acceptance criteria, and measurable mission or operational outcomes.

  • Translate customer and mission needs into requirements and decisions that engineers, domain experts, and senior leaders can act on; communicate progress, limitations, risks, and dependencies clearly.

  • Connect customer mission and technical teams with OpenAI Research, Product, and Engineering teams to assess promising applications and move feasible opportunities into scoped, supported projects.

  • Coordinate the Applied AI Architect, specialist engineers, and customer technical teams on architecture, data access, evaluation, integration, and deployment requirements.

  • Build sustained adoption through practical enablement, user feedback, workflow support, and repeatable playbooks that can be applied across agencies and government customers.

  • Lead executive reviews and focused workshops in Washington and at customer sites, bringing the right decision-makers and technical experts together to resolve issues and advance delivery.

  • Identify security, data, infrastructure, contractual, and resourcing risks early; work with the accountable teams to resolve them and escalate decisions promptly.

  • Prioritize across a small, matrixed team, make clear trade-offs, and maintain momentum as customer needs and model capabilities evolve.

  • Coordinate with Account Directors, policy colleagues, and partners on broader government engagement, while keeping delivery commitments aligned with available resources and approved capabilities.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience leading complex technical programs, customer delivery, or transformation initiatives, including substantial work with federal civilian agencies, state or local governments, or comparable public institutions.

  • Can meet customer-specific access requirements. An active DOE Q and/or U.S. Government TS/SCI clearance is preferred for engagements involving national security missions.

  • Are willing to travel domestically when an in-person engagement materially advances customer priorities, relationships, or delivery; use Washington-based engagement and remote collaboration effectively.

  • Understand how government executives, program owners, acquisition stakeholders, and technical teams make decisions and deliver work; navigate organizational boundaries to turn priorities into execution.

  • Have led complex AI/ML, enterprise software, API, cloud, scientific computing, or digital transformation engagements through implementation and sustained adoption.

  • Bring executive presence and a record of influencing senior government leaders, while remaining personally accountable for follow-through with working teams.

  • Translate mission goals into practical execution plans, acceptance criteria, and measures such as workflow adoption, staff productivity, output quality, and time to a validated outcome.

  • Have enough technical fluency to evaluate AI use cases, challenge assumptions, and work credibly with architects and domain experts on data integration, model evaluation, and deployment trade-offs.

  • Are curious about frontier AI and actively experiment with the technology to understand its capabilities, limitations, and applications to government work.

  • Build durable partnerships across mission teams, engineers, security teams, program owners, and executives; thrive in ambiguity and take initiative in a fast-moving environment.

  • See yourself as a bridge between frontier AI research and practical mission impact, with the judgment to distinguish a promising demonstration from a validated outcome.

  • Help customers use AI responsibly, with appropriate data protection, human review, provenance, reproducibility, and validation suited to the mission and use case.

  • Existing relationships across federal civilian agencies or state and local governments are valuable. Experience with DOE, national labs, NASA, or NSF is one relevant area of expertise.

OpenAI’s Education team is building products and programs that advance how people learn with AI. We work across students, educators, institutions, and education communities to help people use AI thoughtfully and effectively.


About the Role

We’re looking for an Education Content Marketing Lead who combines exceptional editorial and curriculum judgment with strong content-marketing instincts, a builder’s mindset, and an engineer’s approach to scale. You’ll create high-quality content and the systems that move it from idea to published asset quickly and consistently.

This is a hands-on role spanning long-form editorial, curriculum, video, visual content, channel strategy, and content operations. You’ll turn strategic briefs and expert input into useful work for students, educators, institutional leaders, and education communities; grow the channels that reach them; and use data to improve both the content and the engine behind it.

Education needs a coherent, measurable content engine across audiences, formats, and channels. This role will turn fragmented requests and one-off production into a prioritized portfolio, reusable workflows, dependable creative capacity, and education-specific channels that compound over time. The goal is not simply to produce more content, but to create work that earns attention, supports learning and engagement, and improves through evidence.


In This Role, You Will

  • Build and continuously improve a scalable content operating system spanning intake, prioritization, resourcing, production, review, publishing, versioning, and reuse.

  • Maintain a single source of truth for the roadmap, editorial calendar, briefs, source material, production status, approvals, assets, and metadata.

  • Produce and edit content across formats, including long-form articles, blogs, case studies, web and email copy, social posts, educator stories, GIFs, images, and carousels.

  • Develop practical curriculum and professional-learning resources, including lesson plans, educator guides, AI literacy materials, decks, and train-the-trainer content.

  • Lead video development from concept through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, interview preparation, and oversight of production and post-production partners.

  • Own and grow education-specific channels across social, email, websites, and blogs through clear audience strategies, editorial plans, and consistent publishing programs.

  • Set ambitious growth and engagement goals, define measures of content quality and efficacy, instrument tracking, analyze performance, and use experiments to improve results.

  • Turn goals and expert input into clear briefs, plans, timelines, and review paths in partnership with Content, Customer Education, Design, Marketing, Product, Research, Policy, Safety, Sales, Partnerships, and Customer Success.

  • Scale production by sourcing, onboarding, and managing a flexible bench of writers, editors, curriculum developers, designers, video partners, agencies, and other vendors.

  • Have built or materially improved content systems, workflows, templates, governance, tooling, automation, or publishing operations.

  • Have owned digital channels and used audience and performance data to set ambitious growth goals, design experiments, and deliver measurable results.

  • Are a strong video storyteller, with experience in scripting, structural editing, interview preparation, and collaboration with production and post-production specialists.

  • Can turn ambiguous, cross-functional input into clear requirements and polished work while sequencing priorities across multiple workstreams.

  • Have experience sourcing and onboarding external partners and are fluent with content-management, digital-asset-management, project-management, analytics, and automation tools.


Nice To Have

  • Experience working in education, edtech, AI, or another technical field.

  • Experience creating both curriculum or professional-learning resources and audience-facing marketing content.

About Scale AI

Scale AI is the data foundation for AI, helping organizations build and deploy reliable production AI applications. We partner with the world's leading enterprises and government organizations to accelerate their AI transformation through frontier AI systems that solve real business problems.

Every day, we work with organizations across finance, healthcare, manufacturing, media and telecommunications to build production AI agents that automate complex workflows, help humans, reason over enterprise knowledge, and operate safely at scale.

The Opportunity

Applied AI is moving faster than ever. New foundation models, reasoning techniques, agent architectures, and research papers emerge every week. Yet building AI systems that reliably solve real-world problems remains one of the hardest engineering challenges.

As a Staff Frontier Agent Engineer (Applied AI), you'll bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and production deployment. You'll work directly with enterprise customers to design, evaluate, and deploy intelligent systems that combine frontier models with structured knowledge, retrieval, traditional machine learning, and enterprise software.

Unlike traditional ML roles that focus on a single model or product, you'll work across a diverse portfolio of AI challenges spanning multiple industries and use cases. You may build a multi-agent research system and then participate in designing a customer intelligence platform, a healthcare copilot, or an autonomous workflow for a Fortune 100 company.

If you enjoy reading new AI papers, experimenting with the latest models, and shipping production systems that create measurable business impact, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Build

Frontier AI Systems

  • Design and deploy production AI agents that leverage the latest advances in large language models, reasoning, retrieval, memory, and tool use.
  • Architect intelligent systems that combine LLMs, traditional machine learning, structured knowledge, enterprise data, and deterministic software into reliable production workflows.
  • Engineer customer intelligence layers, retrieval pipelines, memory systems, and knowledge representations that allow agents to reason over large, heterogeneous enterprise data.
  • Develop multi-agent systems that coordinate reasoning, planning, tool execution, and human oversight.
  • Translate frontier AI research into production systems by rapidly evaluating new models, prompting techniques, reasoning paradigms, and agent architectures.

Experimentation & Evaluation

  • Own the full experimentation lifecycle, from hypothesis generation to production rollout.
  • Design rigorous evaluation frameworks using offline benchmarks, online A/B experiments, golden datasets, regression suites, LLM-as-a-Judge, and human evaluation.
  • Run controlled experiments and ablation studies to understand the contribution of different models, prompts, retrieval strategies, reasoning techniques, memory systems, and agent architectures.
  • Continuously evaluate newly released frontier models and determine where they meaningfully improve quality, latency, reliability, or cost.
  • Develop confidence estimation, reflection, and continuous learning systems that improve agents over time using real-world feedback.
  • Measure success through business outcomes, not benchmark scores.

Production AI Engineering

  • Build production-quality AI systems with a strong emphasis on reliability, observability, latency, safety, and cost.
  • Design agent guardrails, fallback strategies, tracing, monitoring, and evaluation pipelines that enable safe deployment in high-stakes environments.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure engineers to deploy AI systems securely within enterprise cloud environments.
  • Build human-in-the-loop workflows that effectively combine AI automation with expert oversight.

Customer Innovation

  • Partner directly with enterprise customers to understand their business, data, and operational challenges.
  • Translate ambiguous customer problems into production AI architectures.
  • Rapidly prototype new ideas, validate them with customers, and evolve successful solutions into scalable production systems.
  • Identify reusable patterns that become core capabilities across many enterprise deployments.

What Makes This Role Different

You'll work across the full lifecycle of modern AI systems:

  • Designing reasoning and agent architectures
  • Building retrieval, memory, and customer intelligence systems
  • Developing predictive models that work alongside LLMs
  • Running experiments and ablation studies
  • Shipping production systems into enterprise environments
  • Measuring business impact through online experimentation
  • Continuously improving agents using real-world feedback

We believe the fastest way to grow as an Frontier Agents engineer is to solve many different AI problems, not the same problem repeatedly. You'll work across diverse industries, datasets, model architectures, and agentic systems, rapidly developing intuition for what makes AI systems successful in production.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of software engineering, machine learning, or applied AI experience.
  • Strong Python programming skills.
  • Experience building production AI systems using LLMs.
  • Experience with modern AI tooling, including OpenAI, Claude, MCP, agent frameworks, vector databases, or retrieval systems.
  • Strong understanding of machine learning fundamentals and modern language models.
  • Experience designing or evaluating AI systems using quantitative metrics.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work directly with enterprise customers.

Preferred Qualifications

Applied AI

  • Experience building production AI agents or autonomous systems.
  • Deep understanding of reasoning, retrieval, memory, planning, and tool use.
  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks for LLMs and agentic systems.
  • Experience with RAG, semantic search, knowledge graphs, customer intelligence systems, or structured knowledge representations.
  • Experience with fine-tuning, distillation, reinforcement learning, small language models, or model optimization.
  • Familiarity with multimodal AI systems and frontier foundation models.

Software Engineering

  • Experience building distributed production systems.
  • Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and production observability.
  • Experience integrating AI systems into enterprise software environments.

Customer Engineering

  • Experience working directly with enterprise customers.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous business problems into technical architectures.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience leading technical workshops, architecture reviews, or customer design sessions.

Dual Fluency

While this role initially emphasizes Applied AI and machine learning, every Frontier Agent Engineer develops expertise across both Applied AI and Forward Deployed Engineering.

Over time, you'll gain hands-on experience integrating AI systems into enterprise environments, deploying production infrastructure, and working directly with customer engineering teams. Our goal is to develop engineers who can move seamlessly between cutting-edge AI research and real-world production systems.

As Architect for the Data Centers & Workplace, you will lead the strategic planning, design, and execution of facilities and infrastructure solutions for SpaceXAI's data centers and site builds. Drawing on expertise in complex, multi-stakeholder projects, you'll collaborate across engineering, procurement, construction, and business teams to deliver integrated, compliant designs that align with aggressive timelines and innovation goals. This position reports to the Facilities Leadership team and is an opportunity that requires travel to different locations and cross-site collaboration.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Plan, design, and support the construction of advanced data centers and AI infrastructure, including high-performance computing facilities at new and existing sites.
  • Collaborate with civil, structural, MEP, and fire protection disciplines, as well as procurement and construction teams, to develop integrated solutions optimized for scalability, efficiency, and reliability.
  • Create Basis of Design documents and Request for Quotation (RFQ) packages for external consultants, architects, and vendors; respond to RFIs and iterate based on feedback.

  • Ensure compliance with local building codes, zoning, and environmental standards while providing technical guidance on architectural elements.
  • Initiate, scope, design, estimate costs, and execute facility and infrastructure projects critical to AI operations, production ramps, and business continuity.

  • Drive strategic workplace program planning and delivery, overseeing CAPEX/OPEX budgets, financial reporting, and space optimization for SpaceXAI's workforce across multiple sites.
  • Partner with real estate and leasing teams on site selection, due diligence, and lease negotiations for new facilities, contributing architectural insights to strategic expansion decisions.
  • Lead global portfolio management for offices, labs, and data centers, including scenario planning for lease renewals, fit-outs, and adaptive reuse projects.

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in architectural design and project management, with direct hands-on involvement in data center development, site construction, and workplace planning in high-tech environments.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Expertise in high-performance computing facilities, such as supercomputer deployments or AI-optimized data centers.
  • Proficiency in design and collaboration tools: AutoCAD/Revit, SketchUp, Jira/Bluebeam, Adobe Creative Suite, Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Experience delivering flagship projects for leading tech companies (e.g., HQ relocations, R&D labs, wellness centers with integrated data infrastructure).
  • Strong background in global portfolio management, including lease scenario planning and cross-functional collaboration with IT, security, HR, and legal teams.
  • Familiarity with agile project methodologies for rapid prototyping, site adaptations, and vendor negotiation.

Job Description:

As a Simulation Framework Engineer (L1) on the Simulation Framework Team, you will help develop and maintain the software that connects modeling and simulation (M&S) environments with core autonomy software. You will work alongside experienced engineers to write C++ and Python code, build adapters and plugins, and support reusable software components that reduce the simulation-specific complexity exposed to autonomy developers.

This is a hands-on software engineering role intended for an early-career engineer who is interested in defense simulation, autonomy, distributed systems, and technical integration. You will contribute to simulation environments and frameworks such as NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and the emerging Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF).

You will support the team’s migration of HMSSimBlocks capabilities to HMSF by helping implement baseline adapters, port selected modules, test functionality, and maintain compatibility for programs that continue to use HMSSimBlocks. You will also assist integration teams by investigating framework, plugin, interface, and data-exchange issues under the guidance of senior engineers.

What you'll do:

  • Develop, compile, test, and maintain C++ and Python software for simulation adapters, plugins, and interfaces.
  • Contribute to baseline integrations for simulation backends such as AFSIM, NGTS, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF.
  • Assist with the transition from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF by porting simulation features, updating interfaces, validating behavior, and documenting migration considerations.
  • Help maintain and improve existing HMSSimBlocks integrations for programs that still depend on the legacy framework.
  • Support the development of reusable simulation components and plugin patterns that enable other engineering teams to integrate custom sensors, vehicle models, effects, or mission capabilities.
  • Assist with implementation and maintenance of CIGI-based plugins and interfaces that enable communication between simulation frameworks and Aechelon image generators.
  • Help verify functional behavior across simulation plugins, including Common Scenario Format (CSF) file loading, DDS communications, GRID interface requirements, and Hivemind SDK compatibility.
  • Diagnose simulation and autonomy integration issues by reviewing application logs, network traffic, DDS messages, API behavior, configuration files, and call stacks.
  • Write and maintain unit tests, automated integration tests, developer documentation, and example configurations.
  • Participate in code reviews, engineering design discussions, bug triage, and collaborative debugging with simulation, autonomy, and integration teams.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
  • Foundational programming experience in C++ and Python through coursework, internships, personal projects, research, or professional experience.
  • Familiarity with Linux development environments, including command-line tools, compiling software, and basic scripting.
  • Understanding of core software engineering practices, including Git-based version control, debugging, code review, and automated testing.
  • Familiarity with object-oriented programming, software interfaces, APIs, and modular software design.
  • Exposure to networking concepts such as TCP, UDP, client-server communication, message passing, or data serialization.
  • Interest in modeling and simulation, autonomy, robotics, distributed systems, game engines, visualization systems, or defense technology.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn from senior engineers and cross-functional partners.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. SECRET security clearance; U.S. citizenship is required.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Internship, academic project, research, or personal-project experience involving simulation, robotics, autonomy, game engines, embedded systems, or vehicle modeling.
  • Exposure to modeling and simulation tools or frameworks, including AFSIM, NGTS, Unreal Engine, Unity, Gazebo, ROS/ROS 2, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar environments.
  • Familiarity with middleware or distributed communications technologies such as DDS, ROS 2, ZeroMQ, gRPC, or message queues.
  • Basic familiarity with CIGI, DIS, HLA, CSF, or other simulation and interoperability standards.
  • Experience writing unit tests or automated tests using tools such as GoogleTest, pytest, CTest, or similar frameworks.
  • Experience using build systems such as CMake, Make, Bazel, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with containerized development environments, including Docker or Podman.

The Hivemind Solutions HIL Infrastructure and Test Engineering Team is seeking an Integration Engineer II to develop and test the systems that bring Hivemind mission autonomy and vision capabilities onto real aircraft. You'll build Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) infrastructure, develop automated tests, and validate mission autonomy software in HIL and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) environments. You'll also support vision system development through HIL testing and hands on integration of imaging sensors, onboard processing, camera pods, and gimbals for crewed and uncrewed aircraft. Working across software, electrical, and mechanical disciplines, you'll own integration and test tasks from setup through validation, collaborating with experienced engineers to resolve issues and prepare systems for ground and flight testing. We're looking for someone who enjoys building and debugging complex systems, embraces learning, and takes ownership of delivering reliable results.

What you'll do:

Job Description:

As a Simulation Framework Engineer (L2) on the Simulation Framework Team, you will help develop and maintain the software that connects modeling and simulation (M&S) environments with core autonomy software. You will work alongside experienced engineers to write C++ and Python code, build adapters and plugins, and support reusable software components that reduce the simulation-specific complexity exposed to autonomy developers.

This is a hands-on software engineering role intended for an early-career engineer who is interested in defense simulation, autonomy, distributed systems, and technical integration. You will contribute to simulation environments and frameworks such as NGTS, AFSIM, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and the emerging Hivemind Simulation Framework (HMSF).

You will support the team’s migration of HMSSimBlocks capabilities to HMSF by helping implement baseline adapters, port selected modules, test functionality, and maintain compatibility for programs that continue to use HMSSimBlocks. You will also assist integration teams by investigating framework, plugin, interface, and data-exchange issues under the guidance of senior engineers.

What you'll do:

  • Develop, compile, test, and maintain C++ and Python software for simulation adapters, plugins, and interfaces.
  • Contribute to baseline integrations for simulation backends such as AFSIM, NGTS, Aechelon, HMSSimBlocks, and HMSF.
  • Assist with the transition from HMSSimBlocks to HMSF by porting simulation features, updating interfaces, validating behavior, and documenting migration considerations.
  • Help maintain and improve existing HMSSimBlocks integrations for programs that still depend on the legacy framework.
  • Support the development of reusable simulation components and plugin patterns that enable other engineering teams to integrate custom sensors, vehicle models, effects, or mission capabilities.
  • Assist with implementation and maintenance of CIGI-based plugins and interfaces that enable communication between simulation frameworks and Aechelon image generators.
  • Help verify functional behavior across simulation plugins, including Common Scenario Format (CSF) file loading, DDS communications, GRID interface requirements, and Hivemind SDK compatibility.
  • Diagnose simulation and autonomy integration issues by reviewing application logs, network traffic, DDS messages, API behavior, configuration files, and call stacks.
  • Write and maintain unit tests, automated integration tests, developer documentation, and example configurations.
  • Participate in code reviews, engineering design discussions, bug triage, and collaborative debugging with simulation, autonomy, and integration teams.

Required qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
  • Foundational programming experience in C++ and Python through coursework, internships, personal projects, research, or professional experience.
  • Familiarity with Linux development environments, including command-line tools, compiling software, and basic scripting.
  • Understanding of core software engineering practices, including Git-based version control, debugging, code review, and automated testing.
  • Familiarity with object-oriented programming, software interfaces, APIs, and modular software design.
  • Exposure to networking concepts such as TCP, UDP, client-server communication, message passing, or data serialization.
  • Interest in modeling and simulation, autonomy, robotics, distributed systems, game engines, visualization systems, or defense technology.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn from senior engineers and cross-functional partners.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. SECRET security clearance; U.S. citizenship is required.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Internship, academic project, research, or personal-project experience involving simulation, robotics, autonomy, game engines, embedded systems, or vehicle modeling.
  • Exposure to modeling and simulation tools or frameworks, including AFSIM, NGTS, Unreal Engine, Unity, Gazebo, ROS/ROS 2, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar environments.
  • Familiarity with middleware or distributed communications technologies such as DDS, ROS 2, ZeroMQ, gRPC, or message queues.
  • Basic familiarity with CIGI, DIS, HLA, CSF, or other simulation and interoperability standards.
  • Experience writing unit tests or automated tests using tools such as GoogleTest, pytest, CTest, or similar frameworks.
  • Experience using build systems such as CMake, Make, Bazel, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with containerized development environments, including Docker or Podman.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Product Portfolio Analyst, X-BAT Family of Systems (FoS)  to strengthen the analytical rigor, long-range planning, and operating discipline of the X-BAT FoS Capture organization.

As a core member of the X-BAT FoS Product team, you will partner closely with the  X-BAT FoS Product Organization to maintain a high-confidence view of the current and future opportunity pipeline and assist in driving decisive action across the portfolio. You will turn pipeline data into actionable insights that inform prioritization, resource decisions, revenue planning, and long-term growth strategy.

This role owns the integrity and quality of X-BAT FoS portfolio pipeline information in Salesforce and related reporting tools and will establish the standards, review the data for completeness and credibility, identify gaps or inconsistencies, and drive corrective actions across the portfolio.

The ideal candidate brings strong analytical skills, experience working with CRM and business-planning data, comfort partnering with Finance, and the ability to translate complex information into clear recommendations. This role will help ensure X-BAT FoS maintains a resilient pipeline across near-term pursuits and a three- to ten-year opportunity horizon.

What you'll do:

    Product Portfolio Strategy and Management
  • Maintain an integrated view of the X-BAT FoS opportunity pipeline across near-term, mid-term, and long-range pursuits.
  • Analyze opportunities using criteria including timing, estimated value, probability of win, market attractiveness, strategic relevance, expected revenue contribution, and resourcing requirements.
  • Partner with the X-BAT FoS Capture Organization to identify priority opportunities, inform portfolio trade-space decisions, and recommend actions to strengthen the pipeline.
  • Track changes in opportunity value, timing, stage progression, probability of win, customer funding, and other factors that affect forecast confidence.
  • Identify pipeline gaps, timing shortfalls, concentration risks, single-point dependencies, and opportunities that lack sufficient capture activity or next steps.
  • Recommend actions to create pipeline resilience, including alternate pursuits, adjacent customers, related mission areas, acquisition pathways, partner opportunities, and additional sources of demand.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of the X-BAT FoS opportunity space across a multi-year horizon and help identify and track actions needed to mature early opportunities into successful capture efforts.
    • Salesforce Data Quality and Reporting
  • Serve as the X-BAT FoS Capture organization’s lead for pipeline-data integrity, reporting standards, and Salesforce opportunity-management discipline.
  • Establish and maintain common expectations for opportunity stages, required data fields, forecast assumptions, probability assessments, next steps, and update cadence.
  • Review Salesforce opportunity records for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and credibility; coordinate with account and opportunity owners to correct gaps, stale data, and unsupported assumptions.
  • Develop and maintain concise dashboards, trackers, and pipeline-review products that provide visibility into portfolio health, capture status, forecast changes, and key risks.
  • Partner with enterprise business-systems teams, as required, to improve reports, dashboards, workflows, and data structures that support X-BAT FoS pipeline management.
  • Maintain common definitions, reporting guidance, and pipeline-management best practices across the organization.
    • Finance and Revenue Planning
  • Partner closely with Finance to ensure a clear, traceable connection between Salesforce opportunity data, bookings assumptions, revenue forecasts, customer funding expectations, and long-range financial plans.
  • Reconcile pipeline assumptions, forecast timing, probability assessments, and anticipated award values with financial-planning inputs and revenue-recognition assumptions.
  • Support scenario analysis to assess the effect of opportunity delays, funding changes, competitive losses, scope changes, and alternate capture outcomes on the X-BAT FoS forecast.
  • Help maintain a recurring pipeline-to-finance review cadence and track resulting actions, decisions, and assumption changes.
    • Pipeline Risk and Operating Rigor
  • Identify risks to current and future pipeline health, including schedule uncertainty, customer-funding risk, acquisition delays, competitive pressure, overreliance on a limited number of pursuits, and insufficient capture activity.
  • Develop risk-mitigation recommendations and contingency plans with capture leads, account owners, Finance, business development, programs, and other stakeholders.
  • Support recurring pipeline reviews through time-phased analyses and dashboards that show opportunity maturation, anticipated awards, bookings, backlog, revenue contribution, key decisions, and follow-up actions.
  • Support knowledge management by maintaining pipeline assumptions, opportunity histories, risk registers, and lessons learned from wins, losses, cancellations, and schedule slips.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of relevant experience or Master’s degree with 2+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience in business development, capture, sales operations, program management, finance, consulting, or another analytical operating environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate incomplete or changing data and develop clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Experience using Salesforce to analyze opportunity data, maintain pipeline visibility, develop reports or dashboards, and support business-planning decisions.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, including development of concise analyses, trackers, dashboards, and briefing materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage data quality, establish reporting standards, and coordinate updates across multiple record owners or stakeholders.
  • Experience evaluating opportunities based on timing, value, probability, customer funding, strategic relevance, and expected business impact.
  • Experience leading and delivering cross-functional deliverables, decision points, and follow-up actions across multiple concurrent efforts.
  • U.S. citizenship required, with the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting U.S. Government capture, defense business development, or government-contracting pipeline management.
  • Aviation, aerospace, defense, autonomy, uncrewed systems, tactical aviation, mission systems, AI-enabled capability, or advanced-manufacturing experience.
  • Familiarity with DoD or U.S. Government acquisition processes, budget cycles, requirements development, solicitations, and program-of-record pathways.
  • Experience developing or improving Salesforce reports, dashboards, opportunity-management processes, data governance, workflow automation, or CRM reporting.
  • Experience supporting domestic and international defense pursuits, including Foreign Military Sales, Direct Commercial Sales, or allied defense-market development.

Job Description:

The Demonstration Team - Senior Associate Air Vehicle Operator (AVO) is responsible for planning, executing, and leading domestic and international unmanned aircraft operations in support of customer demonstrations, evaluations, training events, operational exercises, and business development activities. 

This position serves as one of the primary customer-facing representatives of the company and plays a critical role in showcasing the capabilities of the V-BAT system to military, government, and commercial customers worldwide. The successful candidate must consistently demonstrate exceptional aviation judgment, professionalism, technical expertise, and adaptability while operating in dynamic and often austere environments. 

Unlike traditional flight operations, Demonstration Team AVOs are expected to independently execute missions with limited support while simultaneously serving as operators, instructors, maintainers, mission planners, technical advisors, and customer liaisons. Success in this role requires the ability to rapidly solve complex technical and operational problems while maintaining a relentless commitment to safety and customer satisfaction. 

The ideal candidate thrives in fast-paced environments, enjoys frequent travel, embraces uncertainty, and is motivated by building customer confidence through exceptional operational execution. 

What you'll do:

  • Customer-Focused Flight Operations- Safely executes complex demonstrations while building customer confidence through professional, disciplined, and mission-focused flight operations.
  • Mission Planning & Operational Leadership- Plans and leads all aspects of flight operations including risk management, airspace coordination, contingency planning, crew coordination, and mission execution.
  • Technical Troubleshooting & Systems Knowledge- Rapidly identifies, diagnoses, and resolves aircraft, payload, datalink, and ground system issues to maximize mission success and aircraft availability.
  • Instruction, Mentorship & Team Development- Develops customers and teammates through classroom instruction, simulator training, live-flight instruction, mentorship, and standardization.
  • Adaptability & Independent Decision-Making- Thrives in rapidly changing domestic and international environments by exercising sound judgment, solving problems independently, and maintaining operational effectiveness under pressure. 

Required Qualifications:

    • Minimum 1,000 documented unmanned flight hours or 250 manned flight hours   

    • Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA Class II Medical Certificate  

    • Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret DoD Security Clearance  

    • Ability to pass required background investigations, drug screenings, and customer medical/dental requirements  

    • Willingness and ability to travel 60–75%, including frequent CONUS and OCONUS deployments  

    • Demonstrated experience operating independently in dynamic, high-tempo, and austere environments  

    • Strong aviation decision-making, operational risk management, and safety mindset  

    • Excellent verbal communication and professional customer engagement skills

Preferred Qualifications:

    • FAA Private Pilot Certificate (PPL) or FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate 

    • FAA Instrument Rating and/or Commercial Pilot Certificate  

    • Previous instructor qualification in manned or unmanned aviation  

    • Prior military aviation or UAS operational experience  

    • Experience supporting DoD, allied, or international military operations  

    • Maritime or shipboard UAS operational experience  

    • Experience leading customer demonstrations, operational evaluations, or flight operations  

    • Experience troubleshooting aircraft, payload, datalink, or ground control systems 

    • Familiarity with ISR payloads, SATCOM, BVLOS operations, and tactical communications  

    • Experience coordinating international deployments, logistics, or expeditionary operations

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Network Architect to define and evolve the secure, scalable, and resilient network architecture supporting our engineering, manufacturing, autonomy development, and enterprise operations environments.

As part of the Cloud & Infrastructure team within Enterprise Operations, this highly technical individual contributor will establish network strategy, standards, and reference architectures across Shield AI's offices, engineering labs, manufacturing facilities, data centers, public cloud environments, and international locations. You will remain hands-on for first-of-kind, complex, and high-risk deployments while partnering closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Infrastructure, Cloud Platform, Site Infrastructure, Facilities, and Cybersecurity teams.

What you'll do:

    Enterprise Network Architecture

  • Define and maintain Shield AI's enterprise network architecture, technical strategy, standards, roadmaps, and reference designs.
  • Architect scalable LAN, WAN, wireless, internet edge, data-center, VPN, SASE, NAC, and network security solutions across a globally distributed environment.
  • Develop high-level and low-level designs for new offices, engineering labs, manufacturing facilities, data centers, cloud environments, acquisitions, and site integrations.
  • Design resilient routing and connectivity architectures using BGP, OSPF, IPsec, private circuits, cloud interconnects, diverse internet services, and related technologies.
  • Establish standards for segmentation, IP addressing, naming, routing, high availability, quality of service, observability, capacity, and lifecycle management.
  • Lead architecture reviews, technology evaluations, proofs of concept, and design decisions for strategic network initiatives.

    • Manufacturing IoT and Hybrid Connectivity

  • Develop secure network architectures for manufacturing, IoT, industrial, engineering, lab, and operational technology environments.
  • Define segmentation and access patterns for manufacturing equipment, sensors, robotics, test systems, building systems, cameras, and other connected devices.
  • Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Facilities, and Cybersecurity teams to integrate operational environments without introducing unacceptable risk to enterprise or controlled networks.
  • Design hybrid connectivity across AWS, Azure, data centers, colocation facilities, and on-premises environments, including cloud transit, private connectivity, routing integration, secure ingress and egress, and shared services.
  • Support the integration of acquired companies, legacy networks, international locations, and newly constructed facilities into enterprise standards.

    • Technical Leadership and Delivery

  • Serve as the senior technical authority for complex network designs, escalations, performance issues, and resiliency improvements.
  • Lead and actively participate in first-of-kind, complex, or high-risk deployments, migrations, cutovers, validation testing, incident response, and advanced troubleshooting.
  • Translate architecture into implementation plans, reusable configurations, operational standards, and clear handoffs for Network Engineering and Network Security teams.
  • Advance network automation and infrastructure-as-code practices using Terraform, Ansible, Python, APIs, and configuration-management platforms.
  • Produce and maintain architecture diagrams, design documents, decision records, implementation standards, and operational documentation.

Required qualifications:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise network engineering and architecture across complex, multi-site environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading network architecture from requirements and design through implementation, validation, and operational handoff.
  • Deep expertise in enterprise routing, switching, wireless, WAN, internet edge, VPN, network segmentation, and high-availability design.
  • Advanced knowledge of BGP, OSPF, VLANs, VRFs, QoS, IPsec, DNS, DHCP, NAT, route redistribution, and resilient traffic-engineering patterns.
  • Experience architecting networks across offices, engineering facilities, manufacturing environments, data centers, colocation facilities, and public cloud environments.
  • Strong experience with firewall architecture, zero-trust principles, network access control, secure remote access, and layered segmentation.
  • Experience with AWS and Azure networking, including transit architectures, private connectivity, cloud routing, and network security controls.
  • Ability to create clear architecture diagrams, reference designs, technical standards, implementation guidance, and decision documentation.
  • Experience evaluating network technologies, vendors, carrier services, and professional-services designs.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives, mentor engineers, and influence outcomes across teams without direct authority.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain architecture decisions, alternatives, and risks to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Ability to travel periodically and support planned after-hours implementations or critical incidents.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience designing secure IoT, Industrial IoT, operational technology, or manufacturing networks, including segmentation of production equipment, sensors, robotics, test systems, building systems, and other connected devices.
  • Experience applying manufacturing or OT security architecture practices such as zone-and-conduit segmentation, the Purdue model, or ISA/IEC 62443 principles.
  • Hands-on experience with Palo Alto Networks, Panorama, Prisma Access, Juniper, Mist, Aruba, ClearPass, or comparable enterprise platforms.
  • Experience designing high-density or industrial wireless networks for manufacturing, warehouse, lab, or engineering environments.
  • Experience supporting aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, government contracting, or another regulated environment.
  • Knowledge of CMMC, NIST 800-171, ITAR, controlled unclassified information, and network designs supporting regulated or isolated environments.
  • Experience integrating acquisitions, legacy environments, or international locations into global enterprise standards.
  • Experience with network automation, source-controlled configuration, validation testing, and infrastructure-as-code.
  • Relevant advanced certifications such as CCNP, CCIE, JNCIP, JNCIE, PCNSE, AWS Advanced Networking, or equivalent experience.

Job Description:

The Regional ICT Lead is accountable for the design, delivery and secure operation of all information and communications technology supporting Shield AI’s Australian regional hub and its programs across the Asia Pacific and Middle East. The role leads a small, high-calibre ICT team and is the single point of regional accountability for network, cloud, endpoint and identity services, and for the compliance controls that allow a US-parented business to deliver sovereign Australian defence outcomes.

This is a hands-on leadership role. It combines people and vendor management with deep technical credibility, and it requires the judgement to reconcile global enterprise standards with Australian sovereignty, export-control and need-to-know obligations. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable in a server room, in front of a customer or certifier, and in a policy discussion with the parent company’s security and IT leadership.

What you'll do:

    Team leadership and ICT management
  • Lead, develop and grow a small team of ICT professionals; own hiring, performance management, workload allocation, on-call rostering and capability development.
  • Set the regional ICT strategy, roadmap and annual operating plan; own the regional ICT budget, forecasting and capital planning.
  • Manage local vendors, managed service providers, carriers and licensing agreements, including commercial negotiation and service-level accountability.
  • Establish and enforce regional standards for documentation, change management, incident response and service delivery, aligned to ITIL or an equivalent framework.
    • Network and infrastructure
  • Own the end-to-end regional network: campus and access-layer switching, wireless, routing, SD-WAN and WAN services, firewalls, VPN, DNS, DHCP, and monitoring.
  • Design and maintain segmented network enclaves that separate corporate, program and test environments in line with data-handling and need-to-know requirements.
  • Own site-to-site connectivity with the US parent company and partner organisations, including the controls that govern what traverses those links.
  • Deliver connectivity and compute for deployed, remote and flight-test locations, including transportable and low-bandwidth environments.
  • Manage server, storage, virtualisation and colocation infrastructure supporting regional engineering and program workloads.
    • Cloud and platform operations
  • Own regional cloud architecture and operations across AWS and/or Azure, including landing-zone design, tenancy and subscription structure, identity federation and network integration.
  • Ensure workloads and data reside in appropriate sovereign regions, and that data residency, jurisdiction and access constraints are enforced by design rather than by policy alone.
  • Drive infrastructure-as-code, automation and configuration management; use scripting and agentic AI tooling to reduce manual operational load.
  • Own cloud cost governance, capacity planning, backup, resilience and disaster recovery for the region.
    • Export control, data classification and sovereignty
  • Act as the regional ICT authority for export-control compliance, working with Trade Compliance and Legal to implement ITAR, EAR and Australian Defence Trade Controls Act obligations in the technical environment.
  • Design and operate access controls that reliably segregate data by nationality, program, clearance and need-to-know — including AUS-only, US-only and AUS/US-EYES-ONLY handling.
  • Translate Technical Assistance Agreements, licences and program security instructions into enforceable IT controls, and evidence that enforcement to auditors and customers.
  • Manage the interface with the US parent company on global tooling, tenancy and security policy; negotiate regional variations where sovereignty or export control requires them, and articulate the rationale clearly to both sides.
  • Support onboarding of foreign nationals, visitors and seconded personnel with correct system access, monitoring and offboarding.
    • Security and compliance
  • Maintain regional alignment to the ASD Essential Eight and the Information Security Manual, and support Defence Industry Security Program (DISP) membership obligations.
  • Own identity and access management, privileged access, endpoint security, logging, and patch and vulnerability management for the region.
  • Partner with global security and the regional security officer on incident response, insider-risk controls, audits, assessments and certification activity.
  • Support the accreditation and ongoing assurance of program-specific and classified environments.
  • Service delivery and program support
  • Deliver reliable day-to-day IT services across Windows, macOS and Linux endpoints, identity, collaboration tooling and asset management.
  • Provide high-touch support to regional executives, visiting leaders, customers and board members.
  • Provide ICT input into new site establishment, facility fit-out, program bids and customer engagements, including cost and schedule estimates.
  • Manage the regional IT asset lifecycle from procurement and deployment through inventory, licensing, refresh and secure decommissioning or destruction.

Required qualifications:

  •  Australian citizenship, and an NV1 security clearance held or the demonstrated ability to obtain and maintain one.
  • 10+ years in enterprise ICT across infrastructure, network and systems administration, with progressive increases in scope and accountability.
  • 3+ years directly leading technical teams, including hiring, performance management and development of engineers.
  • Demonstrated ownership of enterprise networking: routing and switching, SD-WAN or WAN services, firewalls, VLANs and segmentation, wireless, VPN, DNS, DHCP and network monitoring.
  • Hands-on cloud engineering and operations experience in AWS and/or Azure, including identity federation, network integration, IaC and cost management.
  • Strong administration across Windows, macOS and Linux, with Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, group policy, IAM, Intune and Jamf.
  • Practical experience working inside a multinational structure — ideally as the in-country lead reconciling a foreign parent company’s global standards with local regulatory obligations.
  • Working knowledge of export control and data-classification regimes, and the ability to translate them into technical controls: ITAR, EAR, the Defence Trade Controls Act 2012, and Australian Government classification and handling requirements.
  • Experience operating in classified, need-to-know or otherwise access-restricted environments.
  • Scripting and automation capability (PowerShell, Bash or Python) and a strong bias toward automating operational work.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the credibility to brief executives, customers and certifiers, and the clarity to explain constraints to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Willingness to travel domestically and regionally, participate in an on-call rotation and support scheduled after-hours maintenance.

  • Experience with a defence prime, defence SME or Defence itself, delivering ICT into Australian Defence programs.
  • Familiarity with AUKUS Pillar 2 arrangements, licence-free environment provisions, or equivalent bilateral technology-sharing frameworks.
  • Experience establishing or maintaining DISP membership, or supporting IRAP assessments and ISM-aligned accreditation.
  • Experience standing up ICT for a new site, facility or country entry.
  • Exposure to Indo-Pacific delivery, partner-nation engagement or deployed operations.
  • Experience automating IT operations and workflows using agentic AI capability.
  • Relevant certifications: AWS or Azure architecture, CCNP or equivalent, CISSP, ITIL.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We're looking for a Commercial Counsel, GTM to join our legal team at the forefront of shaping how cutting-edge AI technology reaches users, researchers, and enterprises worldwide. You'll work alongside experienced colleagues who operate as true strategic partners—moving quickly, thinking creatively, and collaborating to support deals that matter. In this role, you'll focus heavily on supporting our Go-to-Market teams, handling enterprise agreements and customer negotiations while gaining exposure to a range of commercial work including research collaborations, product partnerships, and procurement. You'll also have opportunities to work on AI safety and research agreements, including threat-sharing frameworks with leading security organizations and collaborations that shape and advance responsible AI development standards.

This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated attorney to develop deep expertise in commercial transactions while contributing directly to responsible AI development.

Key responsibilities

  • Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, with a primary focus on GTM/Sales transactions including enterprise customer contracts
  • Partner closely with Sales and Go-to-Market teams to support deal velocity and provide practical legal guidance
  • Help build and maintain our commercial legal infrastructure, including contract templates, playbooks, and process improvements
  • Potentially partner with Policy, Safeguards, and Research teams on novel AI governance initiatives
  • Identify and escalate legal risks appropriately while supporting business momentum
  • Stay current on legal developments affecting AI technologies

Minimum qualifications

  • Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based

  • Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial agreements

  • Demonstrated ability to provide clear, practical legal guidance to non-lawyers on complex commercial law matter

Preferred qualifications

  • Active membership in the California bar
  • At least 5 years of legal experience with exposure to commercial contracts, SaaS agreements, or technology transactions
  • Clear communication skills and comfort translating legal concepts for non-lawyer audiences
  • A collaborative approach to working with colleagues and external partners
  • Genuine curiosity about AI technology and AI policy, and a commitment to responsible AI development
  • Experience navigating multi-stakeholder agreements involving technical and policy considerations
  • Willingness to take initiative and pitch in wherever the team needs support

In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day.
