How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Growth at Anthropic is about helping people discover what Claude can do and make it part of how they work, from someone's first session to an entire company rolling out Claude. We're a small design team working across all of Anthropic's products, on problems that often don't have established playbooks, because the products and the capabilities behind them change so quickly.

We drive growth by making the product itself better, favoring foundational changes and new product experiences over small optimizations. Our focus spans whatever most limits Anthropic's growth, and priorities can shift quickly.

About the Role

As a Senior Analyst, Travel & Expense, you will run the day-to-day financial controls, audit program, and executive reporting behind Anthropic's T&E function. T&E touches every employee, every legal entity, and every executive, and it runs on Navan, Brex, and negotiated supplier agreements. Spend and transaction volume have grown several-fold in the past six quarters, and the controls need to scale to meet a public-company standard.

You will report to the Head of Travel & Expense in Finance Operations and work daily with Accounting, Tax, Payroll, Talent, Security, Legal, Finance Systems and Administrative Business Partners.

Responsibilities

Controls & SOX Compliance

  • Own the day-to-day operation of key T&E controls, including approvals, card issuance and spend limits, segregation of duties, and policy exceptions, within the control framework set by the Head of T&E, who owns the overall T&E process
  • Maintain the T&E process narratives and risk and control matrix, and keep them current as systems and policies change
  • Ensure correct GL coding and complete, accurate month-end reconciliations across Navan, Brex, and Workday, and support close, flux analysis, and accruals
  • Act as the preparer for T&E controls and the day-to-day contact for internal and external auditors: gather and retain evidence, support walkthroughs and sample requests, and track remediation, escalating significant issues to the Head of T&E

International Expansion Controls

  • Set up and maintain entity-level coding and approval flows in Brex and Navan as new legal entities and countries come online
  • Document and operationalize country-specific rules for per diems, VAT reclaim, non-USD cards, receipt requirements, and local tax treatment
  • Partner with Tax, Payroll, and Global Mobility to ensure compliance
  • Support accurate intercompany treatment of T&E costs across entities

T&E Audit Program

  • Help design, build, and run a risk-based audit program covering sampling, anomaly detection, misuse escalation, and remediation tracking
  • Define and monitor pre-spend rules, duplicate and split-transaction checks, and receipt and 30-day submission compliance
  • Build dashboards and reporting on policy compliance, exceptions, and control performance for Finance leadership
  • Partner with the Head of T&E to deploy Claude to review transactions, flag policy exceptions, and automate recurring reporting

Program Operations

  • Own day-to-day T&E operations, supporting the growing volume of travel and expense activity and platform configuration and automation, so operations keep running without pulling focus from controls
  • Own transaction-level review and receipt follow-up, and help shape what should be automated rather than staffed
  • Partner with Benefits, Payroll and Legal to ensure the T&E program is compliant with relevant local and country requirements

Preferred qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in travel and expense, corporate accounting, internal audit, or finance operations, ideally at a high-growth technology company
  • Hands-on SOX or internal-controls experience: writing process narratives, testing or operating key controls, and working with external auditors
  • Strong accounting fundamentals, including GL coding, account reconciliations, accruals, and month-end close support
  • Deep platform expertise in Navan and/or comparable TMC platforms, plus Brex or equivalent expense management tools, and working knowledge of ERP integrations (Workday preferred)
  • Strong analytical skills: comfort with large transaction datasets, sampling methods, and anomaly detection
  • Sound judgment and discretion with sensitive information, and the ability to work credibly with senior executives and their support teams
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain a control or an exception to Finance leaders, auditors, and employees
  • An AI-curious, builder mindset: experience automating finance workflows with AI tools, or real enthusiasm for doing so, and comfort creating structure where none exists
  • CPA, CIA, or equivalent certification
  • Experience with multi-entity, multi-currency environments, including per diem rules, VAT reclaim, and cross-border tax considerations
  • Experience with pre-IPO or newly public company readiness
  • M&A integration experience a huge plus

About the role

Anthropic is seeking Software Engineers to join our Observability team within the Infrastructure organization. The Observability team owns the monitoring and telemetry infrastructure that every engineer and researcher at Anthropic depends on, from metrics and logging pipelines to distributed tracing, profiling, error analytics, alerting, and the dashboards and query interfaces that make it all actionable. By joining this team, you'll have a direct impact on the reliability and operational excellence of Anthropic's research and product systems.

As Anthropic scales its infrastructure across large GPU, TPU, and Trainium clusters, the volume and complexity of operational data is growing by orders of magnitude, and an increasing share of the most challenging problems live below the application layer. We're building next-generation observability systems, including high-throughput telemetry pipelines, fleet-wide continuous profiling, eBPF-based tracing and network visibility, and agentic diagnostic tools, so engineers can detect, diagnose, and resolve issues in minutes rather than hours, even when the answer lies in the kernel, the network stack, or an accelerator rather than on a dashboard.

Key responsibilities

  • Design and build scalable telemetry ingest and storage pipelines for metrics, logs, traces, and error data across Anthropic's multi-cluster infrastructure
  • Build observability solutions that give engineers deep, low-overhead visibility into system behavior across the fleet
  • Own and evolve core observability platforms, leading migrations and architectural improvements that improve reliability, reduce cost, and scale with organizational growth
  • Build instrumentation libraries, SDKs, and eBPF-based auto-instrumentation to emit high-quality telemetry, with and without code changes
  • Reduce mean time to detection and resolution by building cross-signal correlation (from kernel-level events up to application traces), unified query interfaces, and AI-assisted diagnostic tooling
  • Improve fleet-wide efficiency by turning continuous profiling and utilization telemetry into actionable optimization insights across CPU, memory, and accelerator fleets
  • Partner with Research, Inference, Product, and Infrastructure teams to ensure observability solutions meet the unique needs of each organization

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience building and operating large-scale observability or monitoring infrastructure
  • Hands-on experience with observability signals end to end, from instrumentation through ingest to query and analysis
  • Understanding of high-throughput telemetry pipelines and the tradeoffs involved in collecting, storing, and querying operational data at scale
  • Comfort debugging below the application layer, in the kernel, the network stack, or the hardware
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to partner with internal teams to improve their operational visibility and incident response capabilities
  • Ability to work independently on ambiguous, high-impact technical challenges

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building or operating eBPF-based observability in production, such as tracing, profiling, or network visibility
  • Experience running continuous profiling at fleet scale, including managing overhead budgets and symbolization
  • Kernel- and syscall-level debugging experience and performance engineering skills
  • Experience profiling or instrumenting accelerator workloads
  • Experience operating metrics systems at very high cardinality, or large-scale telemetry storage backends
  • Experience with log storage migrations or operating columnar databases (e.g., ClickHouse, BigQuery) for analytics workloads
  • Experience with OpenTelemetry instrumentation, collector pipelines, and tail-based sampling strategies
  • Interest in applying AI/LLMs to operational workflows such as automated root cause analysis, anomaly detection, or intelligent alerting
  • Enthusiasm for building foundational infrastructure

About the role

We are looking for a Vendor Admin Lead to own vendor master data for our global Finance Operations team. Reporting to the Director of Global Accounts Payable, you will be the single point of accountability for who our vendors are and get paid: onboarding, bank-detail verification, supporting documentation vetting, data quality and the controls around all of it. Anthropic's vendor base is growing quickly across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific, and a clean, verified vendor data is what keeps a fast-growing company scale with the necessary controls. 

This role is deliberately separate from invoice processing and payments. You will control vendor records and bank details; you will not book invoices or move money. That separation is the point of the role, and you will own the SOX controls that enforce it and help design the access model that keeps it that way.

This is an opportunity to build a vendor-master function from the ground up and leverage process automation with Claude while supporting the team making AI safe.

Responsibilities

Supplier onboarding

  • Run intake for every new vendor and payee: validate completeness, collect and verify supporting documentation, and enable records in the ERP backbone system against agreed service levels

  • Validate supporting documents; set 1099-reportable and tax flags correctly

  • Confirm third-party risk and restricted-party screening before activation

  • Set up one-time and non-vendor payees with the right record type rather than forcing them through full onboarding

  • Partner with TPRM and IA teams on control requirements and continuous process improvement  

  • 1099 annual reporting 

Bank details and fraud prevention

  • Own every bank-detail setup and change; validate against a bank letter on letterhead or an approved equivalent (void checks,  etc.)

  • Run independent callbacks per policy using contact details sourced independently of the request, and record the evidence

  • Validate international bank formats and addresses (IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, ABA, SEPA, BSB, IFSC, Japanese bank/branch codes)

  • Identify and escalate business-email-compromise attempts and other payment-fraud red flags

Data quality and maintenance

  • Maintain vendor structure: parent/child and remit-to relationships, entity and country records, contacts and payment terms

  • Lead vendor consolidation: eliminate duplicate vendors and bank accounts, execute merges and inactivations in batched, logged, reviewed changes

  • Run periodic health reviews for dormant vendors, stale bank letters, missing tax forms and incomplete records; drive 1099 and TIN readiness for year-end

  • Own periodic vendor deactivation campaigns

Controls and audit

  • Own the vendor-master SOX controls as the named control owner: maker-checker on every create and change, change-log review, evidence retained on every record

  • Prepare the periodic review of bank-detail changes paid, and address Internal Audit and external auditor requests

  • Partner with Finance Systems to design and maintain ERP security roles so vendor master, invoicing and payments stay separated

  • Flag any suspicious vendor set-up activity through the appropriate channels

Process, systems and improvement

  • Own vendor-master documentation, intake checklists, requester guidance and service levels

  • Serve as the vendor-data expert through process migrations, including data conversion and post-migration fixes

  • Partner on automation: AI-assisted intake validation, document extraction, bank-format checks and a vendor self-service portal

  • Report monthly on onboarding volume, cycle time, bank changes, exceptions and data quality, and use the data to improve the process

Minimum qualifications

  • 7+ years in vendor master or AP operations with 3+ years of ownership

  • Owned a vendor master in an ERP end to end — process, controls and data — across multiple entities and countries

  • Hands-on experience verifying bank details and preventing payment fraud: bank letters, independent callbacks, BEC red flags, international bank formats

  • Experience with vendor tax documentation: W-9/W-8 validation, TIN matching, VAT/GST IDs, 1099 flagging

  • Working knowledge of procure-to-pay controls — segregation of duties, maker-checker, change logs, audit evidence — and have performed or owned a SOX control

  • Led a vendor data cleanup, consolidation or ERP migration and can show the outcome

  • The confidence to hold the line with requesters, vendors and senior stakeholders under time pressure while staying clear and helpful

  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills with large datasets (dedupe, lookups, reconciliations) and exceptional attention to detail

Preferred qualifications

  • Workday Financials vendor management, and experience with Zip, Coupa or a similar procure-to-pay platform

  • SOX experience at a public company or one preparing to go public

  • Experience supporting APAC and EMEA vendors in a high-growth, multi-entity company

  • Experience designing or reviewing ERP security roles with a systems team

  • Comfort using AI tools to automate validation, follow-ups and reporting

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

We are seeking an Electrical Engineering Intern for Summer 2026 - 2027! This is a paid, in-person, 12-week internship.

  • Build and lead a high-performing team. Set a high bar, establish clear ownership/priorities/timelines, develop people, and build an organization capable of absorbing increasing scope under the Chief of Staff.
  • Turn CEO priorities into executable work. Take loosely defined priorities or emerging issues, determine what needs to happen, identify the right owners and decision-makers, establish a plan, and drive the work to a conclusion.
  • Lead high-priority special initiatives. Take ownership of ambiguous problems or opportunities that matter to the CEO but do not sit cleanly within one organization. Determine the objective, build the plan, assemble the right internal and external stakeholders, drive decisions, and carry the effort through execution.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Global Material Movement team is responsible for every movement of material from a supplier's dock to the point of use on Anduril's production lines. We receive, inspect, store, count, kit and deliver the parts that build Anduril's products, and we hold custody of government property along the way. The team exists so that production never stops for material. As Anduril adds production lines and new buildings, warehouse capacity limits how fast each new product can ramp. Site Execution and Production Supply is the operating core of that team: the people, the floor and the daily results at Anduril's headquarters and Orange County facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Director, Material Movement & Production Supply (internally known as Director, Warehousing Operations & Production Supply) to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for warehouse and production supply operations across our headquarters and Orange County facilities: receiving, put away, picking, kitting, line side delivery and outbound shipping. You will lead a team of managers and supervisors and several hundred hourly associates, and you will open a new campus in Long Beach. Government property and export controlled material stay in custody the whole way. This will require experience running high volume, multi site warehouse operations by the numbers: labor planned against demand, productivity measured by process, and every miss traced to a root cause. If you are someone who walks the floor before you read the dashboard, can launch a building and get it to rate quickly, and builds supervisors who run their shifts through standard work and continuous improvement, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Run daily operations across our headquarters and Orange County sites: receiving, put away, storage, picking, kitting, line side delivery, and outbound shipping to other Anduril sites and to deployment.
  • Own the result production cares about most: zero line stoppages caused by material, with dock to stock, kit on time and line side fill rate held to the service levels agreed with each production team. Every miss gets an A3 with a root cause, a countermeasure, an owner and a date.
  • Run the operation from data. Build the daily view of labor, productivity by process, backlog and service level by site, pulled from the system rather than from spreadsheets, and use it to staff every shift.
  • Lead from the floor through daily Gemba walks, tier meetings at every site, and a steady pace of kaizen events that each target a measured problem.
  • Own safety and cost at every site you run: zero recordables as the standard, the operating budget for labor, overtime, supplies and equipment, and cost per unit handled reported monthly to Finance.
  • Hold transaction discipline and location control in every flow you run, so the counts run by our Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team find nothing to fix. Execute quality at the point of handling: receiving checks, damage prevention and segregation of nonconforming material.
  • Keep government furnished property and export controlled material segregated, serialized and traceable in every flow you run.
  • Hire, train and develop hourly associates and the supervisors who lead them. Manage labor to the productivity standards and staffing guidelines set for each process, and manage overtime and attrition against plan.
  • Launch the Long Beach campus: hire its leaders, write its standard work, and run it to the same measures as headquarters from the first shift.
  • Act as the first user of every new system and layout. Test warehouse system changes on the floor before they go live, and accept or reject layout and automation handovers from Material Flow Engineering.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, industrial engineering, business or a related field, OR 15+ years of equivalent operations experience
  • 12+ years of experience in fulfillment, distribution, 3PL or warehouse operations, including leadership of a high volume site
  • 6+ years leading managers or supervisors across multiple shifts or sites, with 200+ hourly associates and full ownership of safety, labor and productivity results
  • Experience managing labor to engineered or measured productivity standards by process
  • Experience running warehouse operations on a warehouse management system
  • Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet production milestones
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • This position is based in Costa Mesa, CA and requires being onsite. Remote work not considered. Candidates outside the area must be willing to relocate to Costa Mesa, CA
  • U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export controlled material and data

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Launched a new fulfillment, distribution or production supply site from pre opening through steady rate
  • Builds own analysis in SQL, Python or a BI tool
  • Experience supplying a manufacturing production line through kitting, kanban and line side replenishment
  • Aerospace, defense or regulated manufacturing experience, including custody of government furnished property
  • Led the operations side of a warehouse management system implementation or migration
  • Lean or Six Sigma certification, or a documented record of kaizen results
  • Supervisors you hired and developed were later promoted
  • Master's degree in supply chain, engineering or business
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

We are looking for a Director of Finance to lead financial planning, reporting, and cost strategy for RMS, HW Eng, and SWP. You will own the P&L and investment planning for these platform organizations, and you will be the leader Divisions turn to when they want to understand the ROI of these shared capabilities.   • Partner with platform engineering and operations leadership on strategic decisions, including build-vs-buy, insourcing/outsourcing, and capacity expansion

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field
  • Experience building or operating cost allocation, shared-services, or chargeback models within a multi-business-unit organization
  • Strong financial modeling skills, including the ability to independently build unit-economics and make-vs-buy analyses
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with both technical/engineering leadership and finance peers across other business units
  • Advanced Excel and financial systems/ERP proficiency
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Familiarity with aerospace/defense manufacturing cost structures
  • MBA, CPA, or CFA
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

In this position, you will oversee the development and adoption of scalable planning processes that ensure efficient, secure, and compliant demand, supply, materials and production planning within the Divisional Planning teams. This role is critical to allow our divisions to seamlessly coordinate across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, finance, and deployments, ensuring that Anduril systems are delivered on time and operate flawlessly in mission-critical environments. This role is ideal for a seasoned process and systems driven leader who thrives in high-growth, high-stakes environments and is passionate about optimizing planning processes to support mission and organizational success. You will directly impact Anduril’s ability to rapidly and effectively deliver critical defense solutions worldwide. An individual with a strategic mindset, driven by the challenge of scaling and refining processes and teams, and who flourishes in a high-stakes, mission-oriented setting will excel in this role.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop & Optimize Supply Chain Planning Processes
    • Design and implement scalable, standardized S&OP, S&OE, and Materials Planning processes to ensure efficiency, quality, and repeatability across the company.
    • Establish requirements and new use cases that push our processes and tools to be a game changer for the company, and ensure seamless coordination between supply chain, manufacturing, engineering, finance, and deployments.
    • Set the standards, then identify gaps against that standard across the company using data, scorecards, metrics under full transparency. Identify (create, copy, etc) elegant solutions to complex problems and dissect all components in order to drive change and improvements, ensuring alignment with divisions and business units.
    • Support the expansion of the Central Planning team and tools to enable our businesses for real-time decisioning and risk mitigation as we hyperscale across the enterprise.
  • Drive Process Integration
    • Partnering with Planning Systems Leadership, enable the integration and adoption and integration of various digital tools and analytics platforms to enhance operational effectiveness and accuracy.
    • Ensure that Planning has a seat at the table and voice on multiple ongoing companywide initiatives impacting planning.
    • Establish and run standardized Planning processes for new Business Lines and acquisitions (including staffing decisions, process implementation/adoption, and tools usage) until Business Line is capable to assume ownership.
    • Spearhead the development of a centralized knowledge repository for existing and new processes, best practice sharing, guidelines, and onboarding training materials across the organization.
  • Partner Cross-Functionally & Promote Stakeholder Engagement
    • Build a team to serve as the primary interface between engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, finance, and deployments to align planning strategies, planning tools, and process inputs/outputs with business and customer needs.
    • Develop and maintain planning playbooks and SOPs, ensuring consistency and adherence to best practices.
    • Work with internal and external partners to implement scalable, effective, and cost-efficient planning solutions.
  • Build Team Leadership & Development Pathways
    • Build and lead a high-performing planning process team, fostering a culture of excellence, innovation, speed, accuracy, and urgency.
    • Represent Planning needs, requirements, and deliverables within executive leadership forums.
    • Be an integral part of setting the 2-5 year strategic plan for your function and team.
    • Collaborate, lead, and positively influence cross-functional stakeholders to achieve results that are in the best interest of processes & strategy at all levels.
    • Provide mentorship and training to ensure team members are equipped with the technical and operational expertise to execute at the highest level.
    • Develop standardized onboarding and training programs for teams to improve operational effectiveness and consistency.
    • Maintain leadership effectiveness and efficiency while demonstrating the adaptability, flexibility, and versatility required in our dynamic work environment.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree (or Bachelors with multiple years and role experience) in planning, supply chain, operations planning, operations finance, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of direct leadership experience in S&OP, S&OE, Supply Chain (or eqivalent experience leading enterprise Supply Chain consulting engagements), or Materials Planning in a fast-growing industries
  • 8+ years of proven experience in leading teams (direct or indirect) that manage the implementation of complex or large-scale planning systems and practices. (ex SAP, Oracle, IBP, Kinaxis, Manugistics, Palantir, etc)
  • Expertise in Planning & Inventory Systems. Designing, implementing, adopting, and scaling complex systems and processes across an enterprise. (Kinaxis, IBP, Manugistics, etc).
  • Experience in the practical integration/utilization of AI in a process environment. Automation of process, reporting, presentations to drive planning productivity.
  • Track record of developing and implementing scalable, repeatable planning frameworks, processes, and strategies to improve efficiency and mission success within a global environment.
  • Ability to manage directly and by influence across divisional and functional leadership teams.
  • Exceptional communication, leadership, presentation, and interpersonal skills are required to enable effective change management with key stakeholders, other departments, and all levels of management.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Global Material Movement team is responsible for every movement of material from a supplier's dock to the point of use on Anduril's production lines. We receive, inspect, store, count, kit and deliver the parts that build Anduril's products, and we hold custody of government property along the way. The team exists so that production never stops for material. As Anduril adds production lines and new buildings, warehouse capacity limits how fast each new product can ramp. Site Execution and Production Supply is the operating core of that team: the people, the floor and the daily results at Anduril's headquarters and Orange County facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Director, Warehouse Operations and Production Supply to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for warehouse and production supply operations across our headquarters and Orange County facilities: receiving, put away, picking, kitting, line side delivery and outbound shipping. You will lead a team of managers and supervisors and several hundred hourly associates, and you will open a new campus in Long Beach. Government property and export controlled material stay in custody the whole way. This will require experience running high volume, multi site warehouse operations by the numbers: labor planned against demand, productivity measured by process, and every miss traced to a root cause. If you are someone who walks the floor before you read the dashboard, can launch a building and get it to rate quickly, and builds supervisors who run their shifts through standard work and continuous improvement, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Run daily operations across our headquarters and Orange County sites: receiving, put away, storage, picking, kitting, line side delivery, and outbound shipping to other Anduril sites and to deployment.
  • Own the result production cares about most: zero line stoppages caused by material, with dock to stock, kit on time and line side fill rate held to the service levels agreed with each production team. Every miss gets an A3 with a root cause, a countermeasure, an owner and a date.
  • Run the operation from data. Build the daily view of labor, productivity by process, backlog and service level by site, pulled from the system rather than from spreadsheets, and use it to staff every shift.
  • Lead from the floor through daily Gemba walks, tier meetings at every site, and a steady pace of kaizen events that each target a measured problem.
  • Own safety and cost at every site you run: zero recordables as the standard, the operating budget for labor, overtime, supplies and equipment, and cost per unit handled reported monthly to Finance.
  • Hold transaction discipline and location control in every flow you run, so the counts run by our Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team find nothing to fix. Execute quality at the point of handling: receiving checks, damage prevention and segregation of nonconforming material.
  • Keep government furnished property and export controlled material segregated, serialized and traceable in every flow you run.
  • Hire, train and develop hourly associates and the supervisors who lead them. Manage labor to the productivity standards and staffing guidelines set for each process, and manage overtime and attrition against plan.
  • Launch the Long Beach campus: hire its leaders, write its standard work, and run it to the same measures as headquarters from the first shift.
  • Act as the first user of every new system and layout. Test warehouse system changes on the floor before they go live, and accept or reject layout and automation handovers from Material Flow Engineering.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, industrial engineering, business or a related field, OR 15+ years of equivalent operations experience
  • 12+ years of experience in fulfillment, distribution, 3PL or warehouse operations, including leadership of a high volume site
  • 6+ years leading managers or supervisors across multiple shifts or sites, with 200+ hourly associates and full ownership of safety, labor and productivity results
  • Experience managing labor to engineered or measured productivity standards by process
  • Experience running warehouse operations on a warehouse management system
  • Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet production milestones
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • This position is based in Costa Mesa, CA and requires being onsite. Remote work not considered. Candidates outside the area must be willing to relocate to Costa Mesa, CA
  • U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export controlled material and data

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Launched a new fulfillment, distribution or production supply site from pre opening through steady rate
  • Builds own analysis in SQL, Python or a BI tool
  • Experience supplying a manufacturing production line through kitting, kanban and line side replenishment
  • Aerospace, defense or regulated manufacturing experience, including custody of government furnished property
  • Led the operations side of a warehouse management system implementation or migration
  • Lean or Six Sigma certification, or a documented record of kaizen results
  • Supervisors you hired and developed were later promoted
  • Master's degree in supply chain, engineering or business
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

Anduril is seeking an experienced, hands-on Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Manager to support our Australian Operations.

As the EHS Manager, you will work directly with operations, engineering, maintenance, project teams and leadership to maintain a strong safety culture, ensure regulatory compliance, manage risk and provide practical solutions that enable the business to operate safely and efficiently.

Anduril operations present a diverse range of high-risk activities, including heavy manufacturing, lifting operations, offshore testing, electrical work, lithium-ion battery systems, machinery and general industrial activities.

The successful candidate will be equally comfortable on the factory floor, working autonomously, in a management meeting, reviewing technical documentation or leading an incident investigation.

This position reports to the EHS Senior Manager for Australia.

What You’ll Do

Safety Leadership & Culture

  • Own and lead the site’s EHS strategy, programs, standards and continuous-improvement initiatives
  • Serve as the primary EHS interface to site leadership and operational teams
  • Develop a strong, proactive safety culture where employees and contractors actively identify and control hazards
  • Conduct regular workplace inspections, safety observations, risk reviews and leadership safety engagements
  • Coach leaders, supervisors and employees in effective risk management and safe work practices
  • Develop and deliver EHS training, inductions, toolbox talks and awareness programs

High-Risk Operations

Provide specialist EHS oversight and practical guidance for activities including:

  • Lifting operations
  • Electrical work, electrical safety, isolation/LOTO
  • Lithium-ion batteries, including charging, storage, handling, and emergency response
  • Offshore testing and field activities, including mobilization, travel, contractor management and emergency planning
  • Heavy manufacturing equipment, machinery guarding, hazardous energy and maintenance activities
  • Hot work, working at heights and other high-risk work as applicable
  • Contractor and visitor safety management

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Maintain the site’s risk management framework and ensure critical risks have effective controls
  • Lead the development and review of risk assessments
  • Monitor compliance with applicable Australian legislation, regulations, codes of practice and relevant standards
  • Maintain the site’s EHS management system, documentation and records
  • Prepare for and support internal, external and regulatory audits
  • Track corrective actions are closed effectively

Incident Management

  • Lead investigations of incidents, injuries, near misses and environmental events
  • Identify root causes and implement corrective and preventive actions
  • Manage incident reporting, notifications and follow-up in accordance with legal and company requirements
  • Analyse trends and use data to identify opportunities for risk reduction
  • Coordinate emergency preparedness, drills and response arrangements

Environmental & Occupational Health

  • Manage the site’s environmental compliance obligations and programs
  • Support waste management, hazardous substances, spill prevention and pollution-control initiatives
  • Monitor occupational health risks such as noise, hazardous chemicals, dust, ergonomics and other workplace exposures
  • Coordinate occupational hygiene assessments and health surveillance where required
  • Promote employee wellbeing while maintaining a strong focus on prevention and risk control

Contractor & Project Support

  • Establish EHS requirements for contractors and verify contractor compliance
  • Review equipment specifications, layouts and processes from an EHS perspective
  • Support management of change to ensure risks are identified before changes are implemented
  • Provide EHS input into new technology, equipment and process introductions

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, Safety/Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline
  • Progressive EHS experience in engineering, manufacturing, maritime, defence, aerospace, or other complex technical/industrial environments
  • Experience conducting hazard analyses or risk assessments integrated with engineering and program decision-making, not purely after-the-fact compliance work
  • ICAM Lead Investigator certification
  • Demonstrated ability to influence multidisciplinary teams without direct authority
  • Strong communication, facilitation, and relationship-building skills
  • Ability to translate technical risk into actionable business and engineering recommendations
  • Natural tendency towards challenging the status quo; leans into hard problems instead of walking away

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Direct experience in maritime, shipbuilding, or naval engineering/operations environments (vessel construction, shipyard operations, marine systems)
  • Experience with ISO 45001, ISO 14001
  • Advanced degree in Safety Engineering, Environmental/Occupational Health, Systems Engineering, or a related field

  • Reliable, organized and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills

Anduril is seeking a Lead Quality Inspector to join our rapidly growing manufacturing team. In this role, you will work with cutting-edge technology aimed at advancing the state-of-the-possible. You will lead and mentor a team of highly talented Quality Inspectors to produce advanced Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) and other defense assets for strategic military and commercial customers.

 

This is a highly dynamic, hands-on role that requires a unique blend of frontline technical expertise and strong leadership.   • Industry Experience: Background working in fast-paced, high-standard aerospace/defense environments

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking talented Legal Counsel to support the Advanced Effects business line in Costa Mesa, CA. Advanced Effects works on some of Anduril’s most cutting-edge products, including the Roadrunner, which is a reusable take-off and landing autonomous air vehicle (AAV), and the Barracuda family of air-breathing AAVs. Secret required, Top Secret clearance preferred.

Anduril is a fast-growing company at the early stages of growth. Consistent with this fast growth, members of Anduril’s Legal Team must be resourceful, creative, and eager to take ownership of complex matters. The Legal Counsel role will require thoughtful approaches to navigating US and Foreign Government complex procurement and compliance rules, with a singular focus on helping Anduril deploy its path-making technology into operational settings for the United States and its allies. In addition to helping capture and execute new government deals, you will work on all other aspects of Anduril’s business, from negotiating license and services agreements, to bid protests and litigation, to handling intellectual property, compliance, and innovative software and hardware product launch matters. Experience across all of these areas is not expected, but a willingness to learn and adapt is.

Our team is passionate about the law and policy of defense technology and you should have an independent interest in the key issues in this field. Anduril fosters a diverse, collaborative, culture with tremendous opportunities for ownership and professional growth.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Be a key member of Anduril’s small, dynamic Legal Team.
  • Drive customer growth by executing new government contracts and growing existing ones. Use your expertise in federal procurement law to help the Business Development, Proposal, and Engineering Teams efficiently capture new contracts, grow existing contracts, and set up follow-on opportunities for future contracts. Assist in the strategy development for new business.
  • Manage relationships with procurement office representatives at Government agencies. High-trust professional relationships with Government contracting and procurement offices are critical to Anduril’s continued success, and you will be called upon to develop and foster these relationships throughout your tenure.
  • Provide legal counsel and day-to-day management of the entire acquisitions lifecycle. Oversee and evaluate major proposals, monitor large contracts, lead or assist in key negotiations, resolve performance issues, identify risks and mitigations, and ensure compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
  • Work on all legal aspects of Anduril’s business, from negotiating license and services agreements, to bid protests and litigation, to handling deal-related intellectual property, compliance, and employment matters. You will represent the legal team in relationships with outside counsel, vendors, engineers, executives, customers, and regulators.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of work on US Government contracts matters, preferably with a law firm or in-house at a government contractor (more senior lawyers are also encouraged to apply, the position may be adjusted based on experience)
  • A solid understanding of the government procurement process; particularly contract vehicles and types, including non-traditional and CAS coverage, software acquisition approaches, and data rights issues
  • The judgment and initiative required to own multiple projects from end-to-end, whether guiding the Product and Business Development Team through the lifecycle of a deal or handling unexpected legal issues that may arise in defense or start-up companies
  • Strong communication, writing, and interpersonal skills.
  • Quick learner and independent performer, able to contribute to the broader start-up legal function, including topics that may be completely new to you: everything from IP and litigation to financing, securities, compliance, and employment law, depending on the needs of the day.
  • Licensed to practice law in CA or ability to gain admission
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Pre-law school professional experience
  • Combination of law-firm and in-house or government experience
  • Experience working with the government
  • Experience with engineering, software, or other technology
  • An interest in the law and policy of defense acquisitions with opinions about what is right or wrong in the field and how to fix it
  • The ability and grit to operate independently within a rapidly evolving company

Anduril's Maritime Division has recently been awarded a major multi-billion dollar shipyard contract that requires standing up a new company structure, managing complex government contracting relationships, and coordinating large-scale financing and real estate transactions.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril has just secured a landmark shipyard contract. This is a significant and complex program, and we need a lawyer who can operate at the intersection of government contracts law and corporate transactions.

In this role, you will provide legal counsel across four critical lines of effort: (1) government contracting; (2) corporate formation and governance; (3) financing and credit documentation; and (4) entity structure. This role demands someone who can move fluidly between negotiating FAR/DFARS flow-downs in the morning and drafting company governance documents in the afternoon. The Legal Counsel, Maritime will be expected to take ownership of significant, material projects with major impact on the Maritime Division and Anduril's future. This is not a pure government contracts role, nor a pure corporate role, it requires the rare combination of both skill sets and the judgment to know when each applies.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Government Contracts Work

  • Execute complex government contracts, including FAR Part 12 and FAR Part 15 contracts
  • Manage compliance and risk across multiple CLIN structures and document accepted risks
  • Build relationships with procurement office representatives at Government agencies and prime contractor legal/contracts teams

Corporate & Transactional Work

  • Support corporate formation and governance
  • Negotiate IP license agreements and intercompany Services Agreements
  • Coordinate financing transactions

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as a key legal advisor on Anduril's most strategic Maritime transaction
  • Coordinate with external counsel on specialized matters while maintaining primary ownership

  • 5+ years of combined experience in government contracts law and corporate/transactional law (more senior lawyers are encouraged to apply; the position may be adjusted based on experience)
  • Strong government contracts foundation: Deep understanding of FAR/DFARS, contract vehicles, UCAs and definitization, FAR Part 12 vs. Part 15, flow-down requirements, and data rights
  • Corporate and transactional experience: Demonstrated experience with entity formation, operating agreements, equity structures, IP licensing, or M&A transactions
  • Experience negotiating complex agreements with sophisticated counterparties (government agencies, prime contractors, lenders, or corporate partners)
  • Strong project management skills: Ability to own multiple parallel workstreams, manage interdependencies, and drive to closure on compressed timelines
  • Licensed to practice law in D.C. (or willing to obtain admission)

  • Maritime, shipbuilding, or Jones Act experience: Familiarity with the unique legal and regulatory environment of U.S. maritime and shipbuilding industries is a strong plus but not required
  • Experience with complex financing transactions, credit agreements, or real estate/lease transactions
  • An entrepreneurial mindset: Comfort with ambiguity, ability to build processes from scratch, and excitement about working on novel legal structures

We are seeking a Manufacturing Optimization Manager to support in the development and deployment of the Anduril Production System (APS) to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence across our manufacturing sites in the US. This role will work closely with manufacturing/production leadership teams to develop, implement, and sustain lean manufacturing systems, coach frontline leaders, and build tools to help drive operational performance in the business.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in manufacturing operations and would have held roles leading production teams on a shop floor.   • Establish a scalable operating/manufacturing/production system (tiered accountability, daily management, KPI trees, visual management, problem solving, governance) aligned to Safety, People, Quality, Delivery, and Cost

  • Standardize processes, tools, and templates that will be used by all Operations teams across the company

  • Strong working knowledge of standard work development, writing, and creation for frontline hourly teams on the shop floor
  • Organized and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • Passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff

  • Lean six sigma green belt certified

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret Security Clearance
  • Experience in small electronic assembly and drones a plus
  • Ability to develop cross functional relationships as a well-respected, trusted partner

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed at which autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America's defense industrial base, strengthening America's warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril's Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air-breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVs) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family consists of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range, and payload capacity, but all Barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Barracuda Launch Team (BLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. As Barracuda transitions from low-rate initial production at Anduril HQ to high-rate manufacturing at Arsenal-1, this team will own the technology transfer, stand up production lines, and sustain the floor operations that make that ramp possible. You will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for up to 2 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Manufacturing Engineer, you will support the transfer of Barracuda production from Anduril HQ to Arsenal-1 and help stand up the processes that enable high-rate manufacturing. This is a hands-on floor role — you'll execute complex electromechanical assemblies, maintain build documentation, collect and analyze production data, and assist in optimizing line performance. Working alongside senior engineers, you'll develop deep expertise in the manufacturing processes, tooling, and quality systems that keep production moving and scaling.

** This role requires relocation to Costa Mesa, CA for an initial training program of up to 2 months. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute manufacturing of Barracuda products and sub-assemblies involving complex electromechanical integration — including mechanical assembly, harness routing, avionics installation, and functional test.
  • Follow and maintain build documentation including work instructions, MBOMs, and process specifications; flag gaps or inaccuracies to senior engineers for resolution.
  • Support RCCA and 5-Why investigations on floor issues; collect data, document findings, and help implement corrective actions that improve yield and throughput.
  • Monitor and record production metrics — takt time, cycle time, first-pass yield, and defect rates — and surface trends to the engineering team.
  • Assist in line optimization efforts by identifying process waste, bottlenecks, and opportunities for efficiency improvements in assigned work areas.
  • Support MES (Manufacturing Execution System) data entry and transaction accuracy; ensure production status and traceability are maintained in real time.
  • Apply basic Lean manufacturing tools (5S, standard work) to maintain organized, efficient workstations and production cells.
  • Participate in technology transfer activities as production moves from HQ to Arsenal-1, learning established processes and helping validate them in the new facility.
  • Engage with the operations team to understand requirements and pain points; communicate manufacturing constraints to design and engineering teams.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 2+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware production environments.
  • Degree in an engineering or technical field preferred, or equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings and GD&T; foundational understanding of DFM, work instructions, and tooling.
  • Hands-on experience physically building hardware — mechanical assembly, cable/harness fabrication, soldering, or similar. Personal or extracurricular projects count.
  • Familiarity with production documentation systems (work instructions, MBOMs) and willingness to learn MES platforms.
  • Strong attention to detail and a quality-first mindset.
  • A genuine hunger to learn and grow, with flexibility for critical pushes.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Manufacturing experience in aerospace, automotive/EV, industrial, or medical device environments.
  • Exposure to Lean tools such as 5S, value stream mapping, or FMEA.
  • Harness or PCBA fabrication experience, including familiarity with SMT processes.
  • Hands-on experience with R/C and/or autonomous flight vehicles, flight controllers, or related control systems.
  • Familiarity with statistical process control (SPC) techniques and yield analysis.
  • Experience with MES or ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or similar).
  • Current active U.S. Secret security clearance.

We are seeking a senior NNPI Control Officer (NNPICO) to build, lead, and enforce the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Information (NNPI) Protection Program across Anduril’s Maritime business line.This is a high-authority, mission-critical role. The NNPICO acts as the primary authority responsible for ensuring full compliance with Naval Reactors, NAVSEA, and Department of the Navy security directives.This position spans both program architecture (designing compliant security plans and procedures) and active enforcement (ensuring operational and technical compliance across engineering, manufacturing, and IT environments).

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the NNPI Protection Program: Architect, implement, and maintain the NNPI Security Plan in strict alignment with NAVSEA NN-801, OPNAVINST N9210.3, and applicable security classification guides.
  • Exercise Marking Authority: Serve as the designated authority for determining, applying, and verifying NNPI/NOFORN markings on all technical data, drawings, hardware, and digital files.
  • Enforce Access Control and Need-to-Know: Establish and manage rigorous access-control protocols. Actively grant, monitor, and revoke NNPI access based on verified citizenship, clearance, and operational necessity.
  • Prevent Foreign Disclosure: Enforce strict controls prohibiting the disclosure or exposure of NNPI to foreign nationals, foreign entities, or unauthorized personnel in accordance with export control laws and government directives.
  • Partner with Information Security and IT: Collaborate with Information Security and IT Teams to ensure digital environments, air-gapped networks, and storage media processing NNPI meet accredited federal standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-171/CMMC Level 2+).
  • Lead Audits and Incident Response: Serve as the primary liaison to government security officers for compliance inspections. Direct the investigation, containment, and reporting of security infractions, data spills, or unauthorized disclosures.
  • Drive Training and Security Culture: Develop and deliver mandatory NNPI handling and awareness training for all cleared personnel, engineers, and program managers.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • U.S. Citizenship: Must be a U.S. Citizen.
  • Security Clearance: Active U.S. Secret clearance (or higher), or the ability to obtain and maintain one.
  • Prior NNPICO Experience: Proven experience as a designated NNPICO or Assistant NNPICO with an organization routinely handling NNPI (defense contractor, shipyard, or military command).
  • Regulatory Expertise: In-depth working knowledge of NAVSEA NN-801, OPNAVINST N9210.3, and DoD CUI handling guidelines.
  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical military/defense industry experience) with 5+ years of security compliance or classified program management experience.
  • Authority and Leadership: Demonstrated ability to independently enforce compliance across cross-functional engineering, executive, and operational teams.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior service in the U.S. Navy Nuclear Propulsion Program (Submarine, Surface, or Shipyard/Naval Reactors facility).
  • Direct experience establishing an NNPI environment for a new program or facility from the ground up.
  • Familiarity with NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), ITAR, and NIST SP 800-171 compliance frameworks.
  • Active Top Secret/SCI clearance.

About The Team

The Voyager team is an elite engineering and design division specializing in cutting-edge computing and communication solutions at the network edge. We integrate enterprise networking capabilities with robust hardware and software platforms built to thrive in the most demanding environments. The company is scaling rapidly, and we are looking for an NPI Engineer who is excited to solve complex scaling challenges and build the future of defense hardware.

The Mission

As an NPI Engineer, you will be the vital technical bridge connecting our Product Development (R&D) team, the Production Department, and our external contract manufacturers. 

We don't just build things on a lab bench; we scale them for the real world. Your mission is to take ambiguity, incomplete designs, and early prototypes from R&D and translate them into solid, high-yield, and repeatable builds that can be seamlessly scaled in production. You will work with cutting-edge technology—including next-generation processors that haven't even been released to the wider market yet—and play a key role in delivering high-stakes hardware programs

What You Will Do

  • Bridge the Gap: Act as the technical anchor between R&D, test engineering, production, contract manufacturers, finance, and legal.
  • Manage Product Data: Create and maintain Bills of Materials (BOMs) and drive the Engineering Release and Engineering Change Order (ECO) processes using our PLM systems.
  • Lead Scale Up & Validation: Design and execute product and process validations to prove that a design built once on a desk can be successfully built by the hundreds on the production floor.
  • Active Project Ownership: Partner with experienced engineering mentors to run prototyping, initial engineering builds, and design verification. You will start with more straightforward products (like radio brackets and accessories) to master our systems, eventually taking full, autonomous ownership of major product lines.
  • Collaborate in Agile Environments: Attend product development SCRUMs and cross-functional meetings, keeping all stakeholders aligned on schedule, quality, and technical requirements.
  • Optimize Manufacturing: Analyze existing products and processes for failure analysis, identifying opportunities for design-for-manufacturability (DFMA) and continuous improvement.

Who You Are (Required Qualifications)

  • Education: Degree in Electronic, Mechatronic, or Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent).
  • Experience: 3 to 5 years of experience in the electronics industry, specifically working with printed circuit boards (PCBs/PCBAs), cables, fan assemblies, and complex electromechanical integrations.
  • Systems Savvy: Proven experience managing data within PLM systems such as PTC Windchill or Teamcentre. Experience working with MRP systems (like Oracle or SAP Business One) is highly desired.
  • Standards & Validation: Solid working experience in an ISO9001 certified environment, with a strong grasp of product and process validation methodologies.
  • The "T-Shaped" Engineer: You possess a broad understanding of multiple business domains (from hardware engineering to supply chain and finance) alongside deep technical competence in electronics manufacturing.
  • Assertive Communicator: You are articulate and have the confidence to "stand your ground." You can collaborate with brilliant R&D designers, but you aren’t afraid to professionally push back when a design is not optimized for assembly.

The Factory Services team is part of the Shared Services, Systems & Infrastructure (3SI) organization within the Maritime Division. This team owns the shared technical services that support all production business lines on site, including machining, hydrostatic testing, tooling, and 3D printing. The hydrostatic test chamber is a critical shared resource used to validate the integrity of pressurized vessels and components before they are integrated into undersea systems. As the site scales to support multiple product lines, demand on this capability will grow and this role will be essential to keeping production on schedule.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Pressure Vessel Test Technician to operate and maintain our hydrostatic test chamber, performing pressure testing on sealed vessels, housings, and other pressurized components used in autonomous underwater vehicles. Our undersea platforms are flooded vehicles, meaning the electronics and other water-sensitive subsystems are housed inside individually sealed, pressurized enclosures. This role is responsible for verifying the structural integrity and watertight seal of those enclosures before they are integrated into production vehicles. You will set up and execute test procedures, monitor pressure data, document results, and work closely with production and engineering teams to ensure components meet specifications. This is a hands-on role that requires mechanical aptitude, comfort working with high-pressure systems, strong attention to detail, and the discipline to follow test procedures precisely. If you are someone who takes pride in getting the details right and understands that your work directly impacts the reliability of fielded systems, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Hydrostatic Test Execution: Set up, operate, and monitor the hydrostatic test chamber to perform pressure testing on sealed vessels, housings, and pressurized components. Follow established test procedures to pressurize components to specified levels, hold for required durations, and monitor for pressure loss or leaks.
  • Test Preparation and Fixturing: Prepare components for testing by installing fittings, plugs, seals, and connections. Verify test setup is correct before pressurization. Maintain and organize test fixtures, tooling, and support equipment.
  • Inspection and Defect Identification: Visually inspect components before, during, and after testing for leaks, pinholes, seal failures, weld deficiencies, or other nonconforming conditions. Identify and clearly document any anomalies found during testing.
  • Data Recording and Documentation: Accurately record all test parameters, results, and observations. Complete test reports and quality records in accordance with standard operating procedures. Interpret pressure gauge readings and calibration data to ensure testing accuracy.
  • Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Perform routine maintenance on the test chamber, pumps, gauges, fittings, and related equipment. Support calibration activities and flag equipment that is out of tolerance or in need of repair.
  • Safety Compliance: Adhere strictly to all safety protocols for high-pressure testing operations. Maintain a clean and organized work area. Report any safety concerns, near-misses, or equipment malfunctions immediately.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Work with production teams, quality, and engineering to schedule tests, communicate results, and support troubleshooting when components do not pass. Provide feedback to engineering on recurring test failures or design concerns.
  • Process Improvement: Contribute to the development and refinement of test procedures, fixturing, and workflows. Identify opportunities to improve test efficiency, throughput, or reliability as the site scales.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of experience in a hands-on testing, inspection, or manufacturing technician role
  • Familiarity with pressure testing (hydrostatic or pneumatic), leak detection, or similar quality verification processes
  • Ability to read and work from technical documentation, engineering drawings, and test procedures
  • Strong attention to detail with a disciplined approach to following procedures and recording data accurately
  • Mechanical aptitude and comfort working with high-pressure systems, pumps, fittings, and gauges
  • Effective communicator who can clearly document and convey test results to engineering and production teams
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in defense, aerospace, or maritime manufacturing
  • Experience with pressure vessel testing, proof testing, or burst testing of sealed enclosures or housings
  • Familiarity with subsea, AUV, UUV, or underwater robotics systems
  • VT (Visual Testing) or PT (Penetrant Testing) certification, or willingness to obtain
  • Experience with ERP or MES systems for test record management and work order closeout
  • Confined space, crane, or rigging certification
  • High school diploma or technical certificate in a relevant trade; associate degree in a technical field is a plus

This role spans both Air Strike and Air Dominance product lines — from cruise missiles and loitering munitions to autonomous aircraft — and is an excellent opportunity for a recent engineering graduate to develop deep expertise in how complex defense hardware moves from design through production.

Working under the guidance of Staff and Senior-level Project Engineers, you will learn the stage gate process from the inside — helping coordinate, prepare, and track the deliverables that determine whether programs are ready to advance. You are a manufacturing engineer at heart, and this role will build your understanding of what manufacturing readiness looks like at every phase of product development. You will work with Product Program Managers, Program Managers, Chief Engineers, and Manufacturing Engineering managers and their teams to assemble review materials, track action items, and support gate content through to completion.

You will also support ad-hoc, cross-functional projects as the Manufacturing Engineering representative — gaining exposure to design, quality, supply chain, and operations challenges that will accelerate your growth as an engineer. This role is built for someone who is eager to learn, comfortable working across teams, and ready to take on real responsibility from day one.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Prototype Manufacturing Engineer to execute first builds and prototype manufacturing across our mechanical, structural, thermal management, and fluid systems (fuel, hydraulics, pneumatics) subsystems. This role spans the full AD&S portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions – and is designed for an engineer who thrives in ambiguity, builds hardware with incomplete inputs, and treats every first build as an opportunity to generate the manufacturing knowledge that makes future production possible.

As a Prototype ME, you are the first manufacturing engineer on a new build. You will work from incomplete design definitions – often without released drawings or established work instructions – to figure out how hardware goes together, build the first units, and document what you learn. Your output is not just a built prototype; it is the MVP work instructions, preliminary BOM structure, buildability feedback, and lessons learned that the DFx and SME teams use to drive producibility improvements and prepare for rate production. You are the bridge between a design engineer's intent and the physical reality of how something gets built for the first time.

This is a cross-program role. You will move between AD&S programs based on where first builds are happening, bringing a consistent methodology to new hardware regardless of the product line. You will work closely with design engineers, DFx engineers, SME manufacturing engineers, and production technicians. The pace is fast, the inputs are messy, and the expectation is that you bring order to chaos – one build at a time.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute first builds of new mechanical, structural, thermal, and fluid system hardware across AD&S programs, working from preliminary or incomplete design inputs (unreleased models, draft drawings, verbal direction from design engineers).
  • Develop MVP work instructions during and immediately after first builds – capturing assembly sequences, tooling needs, critical dimensions, torque values, and process notes sufficient for a technician to repeat the build.
  • Establish preliminary BOM structures (Make/Buy determinations) based on first-build experience, identifying which components should be fabricated internally, procured, or sent to contract manufacturers.
  • Provide structured design feedback to design engineers based on first-build observations – specifically addressing buildability, checkability (can you inspect it?), and repeatability (can someone else build it the same way?).
  • Document lessons learned from every first build and feed them directly to DFx engineers for incorporation into formal DFM/DFA reviews and design trade studies.
  • Build and support Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) units – Ironbirds, Copperbirds, and similar integration test articles – where the build method is undefined and must be figured out from scratch.
  • Identify and resolve manufacturing issues in real time on the shop floor during first builds, including fit/interference problems, fastener access issues, routing conflicts, and assembly sequence challenges.
  • Develop or source prototype tooling, fixtures, and assembly aids needed for first builds – balancing speed with enough rigor that the tooling concept can inform production tooling decisions later.
  • Work with SME manufacturing engineers to validate process assumptions – confirming that the manufacturing processes assumed in design (welding methods, composite layup approaches, tube forming techniques, adhesive bonding sequences) are feasible as designed.
  • Support the transition of hardware from prototype to early production by ensuring first-build documentation, lessons learned, and BOM structures are complete and transferred to the product-owning ME team.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to identify inspection points and acceptance criteria that emerge from first-build experience – particularly for characteristics not yet captured in drawings or specifications.
  • Travel to production sites, supplier facilities, and integration locations to support first builds and prototype campaigns (~15-20%, depending on program needs).

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, prototype/development manufacturing, or NPI with hands-on involvement in building new hardware – not just sustaining existing production lines.
  • Demonstrated experience executing first builds or first-article production of mechanical or electromechanical hardware with incomplete or evolving design inputs.
  • Practical knowledge of mechanical manufacturing and assembly processes: CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, mechanical fastening, composite fabrication, tube bending/swaging, adhesive bonding, and mechanical integration.
  • Ability to read mechanical drawings, interpret GD&T, and work from 3D models – and the judgment to know when something in the model won't work on the shop floor.
  • Experience writing work instructions, assembly procedures, or process documentation – you've captured a build process well enough that someone else could repeat it.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to give direct, specific design feedback to design engineers. You are not just flagging problems – you are proposing solutions.
  • Comfort working across multiple programs simultaneously, shifting between products as first-build needs arise.
  • A genuine interest in building things and a drive to figure out how hardware goes together. Personal experience in a machine shop, fabrication shop, or working on hardware (machining, welding, assembly, personal projects) is a strong plus.
  • Self-directed and resourceful – you don't wait for complete inputs or perfect information. You find what you need, make reasonable assumptions, and close the loop.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in aerospace or defense prototype/development manufacturing, particularly with structural, thermal, or fluid system hardware.
  • Exposure to Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) builds, integration test articles, or similar one-off/low-volume integration hardware.
  • Familiarity with AS9100 or similar quality management systems – enough to understand how prototype builds connect to production quality requirements.
  • Proficiency in CAD software (NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or similar) sufficient to navigate models and identify manufacturing concerns independently.
  • Experience with composite manufacturing processes (layup, cure, bonding, machining) in a prototype or development context.
  • Experience with fluid system assembly – tube routing, fitting installation, leak testing, cleanliness requirements.
  • Familiarity with BOM management, ERP systems, or PLM tools used to structure manufacturing data.
  • Experience developing or sourcing prototype tooling and fixtures.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
