ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maritime Manufacturing Technology team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Quality Technician to join our rapidly growing team in Santa Ana, CA. The Quality Technician for our Maritime team is a critical role responsible for ensuring our autonomous surface and undersea systems are built to the most stringent standards, blending the speed and innovation of a technology company with the discipline and rigor required for national security.

You will be the authority on quality for programs that operate in the harshest environments on Earth. This role requires a hands-on, first-principles approach to developing and enforcing quality systems that meet and exceed AS9100 and specific Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) standards. You will not just be checking boxes; you will be building the quality foundation for the next generation of naval technology.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support the Quality team to develop, implement, and sustain a robust Quality Management System (QMS) that is compliant with AS9100 and tailored to include specific NAVSEA requirements for maritime hardware.
  • Champion quality on the manufacturing floor. Support statistical process controls (SPC), conduct Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and continuous improvement initiatives to increase first-pass yield and reduce scrap.
  • Interpret and flow down NAVSEA standards and technical publications (e.g., material traceability, welding certifications, testing protocols) into actionable manufacturing and inspection processes.
  • Support the Material Review Board (MRB) to disposition non-conforming product. Help drive the Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) process using methodologies like 8D and 5 Whys to prevent recurrence.
  • Partner with the supply chain team to qualify, audit, and manage suppliers of critical components and special processes (e.g., welding, coatings, pressure testing), ensuring compliance with all prime contract and regulatory requirements.
  • Support the development of comprehensive inspection plans, work instructions, and criteria for receiving, in-process, and final inspection. Aid with First Article Inspections (FAIs) in accordance with AS9102.
  • Support internal and supplier audits to ensure system-wide compliance and identify opportunities for improvement. Support customer and third-party audits.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of experience in a Quality Engineering role within a manufacturing environment for aerospace, defense, or other regulated industries.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience implementing, maintaining, and being audited against an AS9100 certified Quality Management System.
  • Proficiency in root cause analysis methodologies (8D, 5 Whys, Fishbone, etc.) and implementing effective corrective actions.
  • Experience aiding First Article Inspections (FAIs) per AS9102.
  • Understanding of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) and the ability to interpret complex engineering drawings.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience with NAVSEA standards and requirements (e.g., SUBSAFE, NAVSEA S9074-AQ-GIB-010/248 for welding, material control specifications, technical publication adherence).
  • Experience in the production of maritime systems, including unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), or related pressure vessel and submersible hardware.
  • Experience with quality control for special processes such as composite fabrication, welding, complex electro-mechanical assembly, and environmental/pressure testing.
  • ASQ certification (Certified Quality Engineer - CQE, Certified Quality Auditor - CQA) or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt certification.
  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-mix, rapid development environment where speed and rigor must coexist.
  • Familiarity with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Manufacturing Execution System (MES) software.
  • Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

Anduril is seeking a Senior Finance Manager to join the Maritime finance team. Reporting to the Head of Maritime Finance, this role owns division-level FP&A consolidation, one reconciled, audit-ready view of Maritime's financials across business lines, products, and programs, and leads the high-value strategic initiatives that fall outside recurring business-line finance responsibilities as Maritime continues to rapidly scale, recommending and executing the strategies that drive both top- and bottom-line impact.

You will own the division’s consolidated financial picture, create dedicated ownership for high-impact initiatives that extend beyond recurring FP&A and business-line finance work, and present findings and recommendations directly to senior leadership. The work runs cross-functionally across Division Operations, Production Finance, Production, Supply and Demand Planning, Program Management, Inventory Management, Data, Product, and Engineering. The role is weighted approximately 60% consolidated FP&A, close, and division reporting and 40% strategic initiatives: the consolidation is the non-negotiable, and the strategic work follows a clean close.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Daily partnership with Business Line Leaders within Maritime to bring first class financial expertise and decision support to the business.
  • Own consolidated division FP&A end to end: set and enforce the close and forecast calendar, standardize business-line and program submissions and challenge them against materiality and variance thresholds before consolidation, reconcile the consolidated P&L and backlog to the general ledger, and publish division, business line, product and program reporting from a single source of truth. Unresolved gaps escalate to the Head of Finance before the division number is published.
  • Evaluate financial performance by comparing and analyzing actual results with forecasts, highlighting trends and analyzing causes of unexpected variances.
  • Partner with corporate FP&A and controllership to align the division's consolidation with corporate reporting requirements, calendars, and accounting policy, and serve as Maritime's single point of accountability for the numbers that roll up to corporate.
  • Lead executive-level reporting: own the division's performance dashboards, alerting, and KPI investigation, and present the resulting insights and recommendations to senior management.
  • Serve as a force multiplier to the Head of Finance and business-line finance leaders, providing leadership where division-level priorities require coordination across multiple businesses or functions, guiding junior analysts on consolidation and IRAD work without formal management responsibility, and implementing best practices and tools to ensure a well-controlled yet flexible finance organization.
  • Develop deep relationships with our customers (both internal and external) and oversee customer program reporting and monthly financial status reporting, partnering with billing on invoicing accuracy.
  • Own financial analysis and decision support for emerging Maritime priorities, including new product development, business formation, investment decisions, and international expansion, and lead the high-value projects where ownership crosses functional boundaries or recurring issues point to a structural problem. Build the frameworks and models that turn ambiguous opportunities into decisions, diagnose root causes across finance, systems, manufacturing, supply chain, and program operations, implement the fixes, and establish ownership that outlasts the project.
  • Provide guidance and financial oversight to a junior analyst who manages IRAD day to day, reviewing the roadmap that carries IRAD concepts from ideation through contract award and confirming financial viability at each stage.
  • Stand up program management office standardization: a common link and guide from proposal to award, kick off, active program management, execution reporting, and contract close-out.
  • Improve the systems, processes, data, and operating mechanisms supporting the division, including self-serve reporting that lets General Managers test delivery and schedule scenarios, and comprehensive program dashboards that give Program Managers system-based program financials. Focus on eliminating recurring work and failure modes rather than permanently adding resources to service them.

  • 5-10 years of finance experience in Defense, Large Manufacturing, or Government contracting, including at least 3 years owning a multi-business-line or multi-entity consolidation and close cycle.
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel, financial modeling and data analysis tools, and experience with financial reporting tools and ERP and consolidation systems (i.e. Oracle Fusion, Oracle EPM, Oracle ERP, Foundry).
  • Working fluency in program revenue recognition and estimates at completion in a government contracting environment (percentage-of-completion, CAS/DCAA), including how program-level judgments roll into a division consolidation.
  • Demonstrated track record of owning problems end-to-end in a finance function.
  • Experience consolidating FP&A across multiple business lines, products, or programs, and building the models and reporting that hold the consolidation together.
  • Intellectually curious: you seek to understand the why behind the numbers.
  • Highly technical: you value precision and accuracy when it comes to your work, and you can rapidly dissect complex quantitative problems.
  • Critical thinker: you consider problems from all angles to remove bias.
  • Results-oriented: you will do whatever it takes to get the job done.
  • Exceptional written and oral communication skills. You drive consensus through grounded arguments, interpersonal skills, and negotiation skills.
  • Creative problem-solver: able to identify obstacles and present viable solutions.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
  • Excited by large breadth of problems.
  • Confidence to execute in highly visible and accountable positions.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

ABOUT THE SITE

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed at which autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America's defense industrial base, strengthening America's warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril's Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air-breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVs) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family consists of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range, and payload capacity, but all Barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Barracuda Launch Team (BLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. As Barracuda transitions from low-rate initial production at Anduril HQ to high-rate manufacturing at Arsenal-1, this team will own the technology transfer, stand up production lines, and sustain the floor operations that make that ramp possible. You will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for up to 2 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Senior Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a key role in scaling Barracuda production from early builds at Anduril HQ to full-rate output at Arsenal-1. Your core responsibility is owning the manufacturing process on the floor — ensuring production quality, resolving issues in real time, and driving the continuous improvement that high-rate manufacturing demands. This role requires deep hands-on experience with complex electromechanical integration and full ownership of the manufacturing process ecosystem: work instructions, MBOMs, RCCA, line optimization, takt time management, yield improvement, scaling operations, and MES management. The role spans the full manufacturing value chain — Design for Manufacturability, tooling and fixture design, process creation and optimization, vendor collaboration, quality planning, and production documentation — with the added responsibility of leading the technology transfer from HQ and standing up production capability at Arsenal-1.

** This role requires relocation to Costa Mesa, CA for an initial training program of up to 2 months. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead the manufacturing of Barracuda products and sub-assemblies involving complex electromechanical integration from prototype through full-rate production, owning the build package end-to-end.
  • Drive the technology transfer of production processes from Anduril HQ to Arsenal-1 — validating process readiness, tooling, quality systems, and training the floor team to execute at rate.
  • Own and optimize the full manufacturing process ecosystem for your area: work instructions, MBOMs, process specs, RCCA, line layout, takt time targets, yield metrics, and MES configuration.
  • Lead line optimization initiatives — analyze production flow, balance workstations, reduce cycle times, and implement process changes that increase capacity by 15–25%+.
  • Root-cause and resolve complex floor issues using RCCA and 5-Why methodologies; lead failure analysis investigations and drive systemic corrective actions that prevent recurrence.
  • Manage and improve yield performance through statistical process control, defect trend analysis, and targeted process improvements that reduce scrap and rework.
  • Own MES management for your production area — configure workflows, ensure data integrity, drive real-time production visibility, and use MES data to inform process decisions.
  • Partner with design engineers early in the development process to drive DFM and producibility into the design, and help move products from design to prototype to rate.
  • Develop technical roadmaps for manufacturing technology advancement; independently evaluate and recommend capital equipment investments with ROI analysis.
  • Champion Lean and Six Sigma methodologies across production areas; lead cross-functional kaizen events that deliver substantial cost savings (>$100K annually).
  • Establish engineering standards and best practices that become benchmarks for the Barracuda production line and broader Arsenal-1 operations.
  • Mentor and develop junior and mid-level manufacturing engineers; create and deliver technical training programs for engineering and production teams.
  • Scale operations by developing production and test methodologies that enable ramp from low-rate to high-rate production of increasingly complex products.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 7+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware production environment.
  • Degree in an engineering or technical field preferred, or equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience.

Standards Development & Implementation 

  • Maintain material and process standards, including banned/approved materials lists, common material coatings, common procedures, and corrosion prevention and control requirements

Testing & Characterization

  • U.S. citizenship required

  • Experience with contamination control for precision optics or infrared sensor systems 
  • Experience with statistical analysis tools and design of experiments (DOE)

Anduril is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer specializing in electromechanical packaging and sensor integration to design, test, and scale mission-critical hardware across our autonomous air, sea, ground, and strike platforms. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Own enclosures, sensor integration, and electromechanical assemblies from requirements definition, hand calculations, and conceptual design through prototyping, testing, and volume manufacturing. 
  • Create high-fidelity 3D models and fully defined 2D drawing packages 
  • Design parts across diverse fabrication processes including designs for injection/other molding, precision 3/5-axis CNC machining, complex weldments, sheet metal, composite layups, and structural adhesive bonding. 
  • Apply first-principles engineering and FEA/hand calculations to validate structural, thermal, and vibrational performance under harsh operational and environmental conditions. 
  • Perform 1D/3D tolerance stacks, DFMEAs, and tool-access assessments early in development to de-risk production bottlenecks and scale throughput. 
  • Build physical prototypes, author detailed test plans, and run functional testing (environmental, dynamic, bench-top, or live arena/range tests depending on track). 
  • Collaborate with Electrical, Systems, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Quality, Safety, and Test teams, as well as external suppliers, to solve urgent hardware bottlenecks. 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor's, Master’s, or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related discipline. 
  • 4+ years of professional mechanical design experience taking physical hardware from initial concept through fabrication and functional test or LRIP. 
  • Proficiency in parametric 3D CAD (NX preferred, SolidWorks, or Creo) and modern PLM/PDM environments (e.g., Teamcenter). 
  • Working knowledge of engineering drawings and practical application of ASME Y14.5 GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis. 
  • Hands-on prototyping and fabrication experience, including root-cause analysis of manufacturing and hardware defects. 
  • Professional experience applying statics, dynamics, material selection, heat transfer, and structural mechanics to hardware design problems. 
  • Experience designing hardware with Design for Manufacturability and Assembly (DFM/DFA) in mind for future volume production (e.g., fast-paced automotive, robotics, aerospace, or marine environments). 
  • Experience designing tightly integrated electromechanical systems (dense PCBA packaging, active/passive thermal management, RF/EMI shielding, harness routing, and environmental sealing / IP ratings). 
  • Prior experience in defense, maritime, optics, automotive, or other highly regulated hardware development environments. 
  • Eligible for U.S. Security Clearance (DoD Secret, Top Secret, or DOE Q) 
  • Up to 15% travel 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Proficiency with FEA tools (Abaqus, ANSYS, or equivalent) for structural, thermal, or dynamic analysis. 
  • Deep expertise in tooling design, high-volume injection molding, robotic/manual weldment design, structural bonding, or building visual standard operating procedures (SOPs). 
  • Familiarity with ECAD tools (e.g., Altium Designer) or basic PCB design / schematic review.

Working under the guidance of Staff-level Project Engineers, you will be directly involved in the preparation, coordination, and delivery of stage gate review materials. You are a manufacturing engineer first — your understanding of how products are built gives you the credibility to assess whether gate deliverables accurately reflect manufacturing readiness. You will work with Product Program Managers, Program Managers, Chief Engineers, and Manufacturing Engineering managers and their teams to assemble review decks, track action items, and help drive gate content to completion.

Beyond stage gate support, you will take on ad-hoc, cross-functional projects as the Manufacturing Engineering representative — stepping in to support design, quality, supply chain, or operations when an experienced ME perspective is needed. This role is built for someone who thrives on cross-functional collaboration, stays organized across multiple workstreams, and is growing toward the kind of senior technical leadership that defines how an organization executes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support the execution of MDP and PDP stage gate deliverables for manufacturing engineering across AD&S programs, working under the guidance of Staff Project Engineers to ensure completeness, technical accuracy, and on-time delivery.
  • Coordinate with PPMs, PMs, Chief Engineers, and ME managers to gather, organize, and prepare stage gate review decks and presentations.
  • Track stage gate action items, open risks, and manufacturing readiness gaps — following up with owners to drive closure ahead of gate reviews.
  • Review ME stage gate content for quality and completeness, flagging gaps and working with program teams to address them before reviews.
  • Coordinate across multiple programs running on different timelines, helping ensure each team has the information and structure needed to hit their gates.
  • Represent Manufacturing Engineering on ad-hoc, cross-functional projects as assigned — providing an experienced ME perspective in design trades, quality investigations, supply chain decisions, and operational problem-solving.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with design engineering, quality, supply chain, operations, and program management on a daily basis — cross-functional collaboration is the core of this job.
  • Drive assigned projects to completion, taking ownership from problem definition through resolution.
  • Help identify gaps and inconsistencies in stage gate processes and contribute to improvements that make the system more effective as programs scale.
  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of stage gate templates, checklists, and standards.
  • Travel to production sites and partner facilities as needed (<10%).

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, with exposure to product development processes, stage gate reviews, or manufacturing readiness activities.
  • Solid understanding of manufacturing processes and what manufacturing maturity looks like at different phases of product development — you have supported hardware from prototype through production.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with program management, design engineering, quality, supply chain, and operations.
  • Strong ability to build relationships across functions and drive projects to completion through collaboration, not authority.
  • Experience contributing to or preparing technical review presentations for engineering and program leadership.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills — ability to track deliverables across multiple concurrent programs and keep things moving.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate manufacturing topics into clear content for stage gate reviews.
  • Self-motivated and proactive — you follow through on commitments and close the loop without being chased.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where processes are still being built and refined.
  • Personal experience on the production floor — you have built, tested, or directly supported the manufacturing of hardware.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

  • Experience in aerospace or defense manufacturing, particularly with qualified or flight-critical hardware programs.
  • Familiarity with AS9100/AS9102 quality management systems and their intersection with stage gate processes.
  • Exposure to manufacturing readiness level (MRL) assessments or similar maturity frameworks.
  • Background in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other process improvement methodologies applied in a production environment.
  • Proficiency in CAD software and familiarity with manufacturing technologies across multiple disciplines (machining, composites, electronics, assembly).
  • Appropriate clearance classification.

As a Senior Supply Quality Engineer, you will work inside & outside the organization to define, develop, and execute processes that deliver high quality & reliable composite structures and components used across Anduril’s autonomous systems and weapons programs. This role focuses on collaborating and driving early engagement with our design teams and suppliers to meet our quality requirements the first time. Everything comes down to clarity and action with our suppliers and partnering with them for world class results across the supply chain. The right person for this role has knowledge of composite manufacturing, supply management, supplier development, part performance criteria, metrology, and continuous improvement. If you are someone who loves to build world-class quality processes with suppliers, work hands-on with engineering, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Partner with our design teams to support the design development process, provide design for manufacturability feedback, and help generate product data (drawings details, BOM information, and part requirements) for composite assemblies that lead to supplier quality success.
  • Use your knowledge and expertise of composites, additive manufacturing, fabrication, special processes, mechanical sub-assembly, and inspection/measurement to support the internal Anduril design process and ideation. Provide leadership to manage technical risks, proof of concepts, prototyping, and scaling designs for production.
  • Drive the supplier quality development processes throughout the product development stages with the product engineering team through design reviews, supplier process development, testing, and qualification for components and sub-assemblies for precision mechanical parts.   • Own the elimination of supplier risk to improve quality & reliability across the product lifecycle. Utilize audits, readiness reviews, and training & documentation to ensure compliance.

  • Prepare, support, and lead supplier onsite audits and reviews for contract deliverables for quality management and compliance.

The Senior Supply Chain Manufacturing Engineer, Casting (internally known at Anduril as Senior Supplier Industrialization Engineer) is a high-profile, cross functional position that plays an integral role in enabling development and production flow of Anduril’s critical supply base. WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own and manage the mechanical casting commodities/subcategories to execute supplier production (NPI to full production) strategies across Anduril’s business lines

  • 6+ years of experience in supplier quality and industrialization within a manufacturing environment
  • Experience with specific category technical expertise, as applicable, mechanical casting manufacturing, IPC standards, CAD, GD&T
  • Ability to travel at least 50% of the time

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Previous experience in defense, aerospace, automotive, high tech, or another related industry
  • Strong understanding of quality systems, standards, and certifications
  • Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment
  • Exposure to working in a fast-pace, start-up environment
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance

WHY WE'RE HERE:

The systems engineering team is looking for an experienced system engineer to lead systems engineering for a Group 5 aircraft program at Anduril. The ideal candidate will have experience working with complex unmanned aerial systems (UAS), and ideally will have a strong background in at least one area of expertise (e.g. avionics, software, propulsion, communications, etc.). In addition to a strong technical background, the ideal candidate will also have experience using Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) tools to develop design artifacts for unmanned systems.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Shape customer needs into air vehicle and subsystem requirements in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams.
  • Develop System Engineering artifacts, including system model, to trace from stakeholder inputs through design in a digital thread. Incorporate input from system safety, software engineering, and other disciplines to shape system architecture.
  • Lead program team through systems engineering reviews including System Requirements Review, Preliminary Design review, and Critical Design Review.
  • Communicate and manage program risks in conjunction with Chief Engineer and Program Management.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • B.S. in aerospace, mechanical, computer science or similar engineering or technical field
  • 7+ years Systems Engineering Experience across the life cycle for an UAS with specific focus on aircraft systems
  • Familiarity and experience with the following standards and handbooks: MIL-HDBK-516C, MIL-STD-882E, ARP-4761, ARP-4754A, DO-178C, DO-254, MIL-STD-881
  • Experience developing subsystem and component requirements and interfaces
  • Experience with Systems Engineering, Requirements Elicitation and Management, Integration, and Test Activities on complex systems - DoD Weapon Systems, Space Systems, etc...
  • Experience with SysML, DoDAF, UAFP, or similar
  • Experience developing various model based system engineering artifacts - Operational Viewpoints, System Viewpoints, activity diagrams, use case diagrams, BDDs, IBDs, parametric diagrams, etc...
  • Outstanding communication skills to include presentation of developed artifacts
  • Experience leading systems engineering efforts on developmental programs.
  • Must hold an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

ABOUT THE TEAM

Discovery is Anduril's team for taking the newest problems across domains- space, missile systems, air, sensor capability, autonomy, and cyber- and proving out what is worth solving. We build the models, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. Discovery works alongside Air Defense, Space, Intelligence, Cyber, GNC, Hardware, and every other group at Anduril to incubate the solutions to the hardest problems.

ABOUT THE JOB

Discovery is building an expeditionary force: a team of engineers who want to solve difficult problems and who navigate unfamiliar territory as an operating standard. As a Discovery engineer, you pick up a concept nobody has proven and build the analysis or prototype that tests it to get to an answer. Whether you spend your time working on hard problems on our autonomy stack, acoustic sensor analysis, or battle space management, we tackle every challenge the same way: by questioning assumptions and building our way to the answer.

We are focused on taking AI models from research into production—onto classified platforms and edge hardware where they have to perform reliably in the real world. As our model portfolio and classified work grow, rigorous, repeatable evaluation of how these models actually perform has become mission-critical.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop Test Scenarios Simulation Environments: Develop comprehensive test scenarios, and simulation environments to assess agentic AI performance in classified simulations.
  • Validate AI on Classified & Edge Platforms: Lead the integration and validation of agentic AI systems onto classified platforms and edge hardware.
  • Build Reusable Evaluation Pipelines: Build reusable evaluation pipelines, automated test harnesses, and monitoring dashboards for continuous validation.
  • Define Actionable Metrics: Figure out what good metrics look like for AI models and traditional models—establishing systematic, historic capture of performance rather than one-shot, deployment-specific measurement.
  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Partner with cross-functional teams to define requirements, document test results, and contribute to AI model cards and deployment readiness reviews.
  • Own End-to-End Evaluation: Architect, build, and maintain the evaluation and validation infrastructure for our agentic AI and ML models, from unit-level model checks through full-system, scenario-based assessment.
  • Troubleshoot and Debug: Analyze and resolve issues uncovered in evaluation and in deployment, ensuring reliability and operational success across every release.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Technical Expertise: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Programming Proficiency: At least 12+ years of hands-on experience writing production-grade code, with strong Python skills for building evaluation pipelines, test harnesses, and tooling.
  • Evaluation Ownership Mindset: Demonstrated experience owning evaluation or automated testing for production ML or software systems—test scenarios, metrics, regression suites, and CI infrastructure.
  • AI/ML Evaluation Experience: Hands-on experience designing evaluation methodologies for AI or machine learning models—defining metrics, building benchmarks, and assessing model behavior against real-world scenarios.
  • Simulation Experience: Experience designing or working extensively with simulation environments to exercise model and system behavior.
  • Metrics Discipline: Working knowledge of how to define, capture, and reason about performance metrics for AI models and traditional models, including systematic historic capture over time.
  • Systems-Level Thinking: Ability to navigate and contribute to complex systems and established codebases.
  • Program Ownership: Comfort operating between technical program management and software engineering—defining requirements, coordinating across teams, and documenting results.
  • Real-World Impact: Passion for building the evaluation infrastructure that proves AI works—directly influencing mission-critical outcomes.
  • Security Clearance: Must be eligible for a US security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior Title Background: Experience as an ML Test & Evaluation Engineer, SDET for ML systems, ML/Evaluation Engineer, Simulation Engineer, or Technical Program Manager for AI/ML.
  • Agentic AI Evaluation: Experience designing test methodologies for agentic AI systems—tasking, decision-making, and scenario-based behavior validation.
  • Classified / Edge Deployment: Familiarity with validating and deploying AI models onto classified platforms, edge hardware, or resource-constrained environments.
  • Model Cards & Readiness Reviews: Experience contributing to AI model cards, deployment readiness reviews, or similar model-governance and release-gating practices.
  • Aerospace/Defense T&E: Familiarity with test and evaluation practices in aerospace or defense, including qualification testing, range operations, or operational assessment.
  • MLOps & Monitoring: Experience with MLOps tooling, monitoring dashboards, and continuous validation pipelines for ML models in production.
  • Programming Skills: Additional experience with Go, C++, or scripting for test automation and tooling.
  • Growth into Broader Ownership: Interest in growing from T&E ownership into deeper ownership of the AI evaluation and deployment stack over time.

ABOUT THE SITE

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed at which autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America's defense industrial base, strengthening America's warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril's Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air-breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVs) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family consists of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range, and payload capacity, but all Barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Barracuda Launch Team (BLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. As Barracuda transitions from low-rate initial production at Anduril HQ to high-rate manufacturing at Arsenal-1, this team will own the technology transfer, stand up production lines, and sustain the floor operations that make that ramp possible. You will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for up to 2 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Staff Manufacturing Engineer, you will drive the enterprise-wide manufacturing strategy for Barracuda at Arsenal-1 and architect how Anduril builds autonomous air vehicles at hyper-scale. You'll lead the end-to-end technology transfer from HQ, design the production systems and line architecture for high-rate output, and establish the manufacturing process frameworks — RCCA systems, MES strategy, yield management programs, takt time structures, and scaling playbooks — that become organizational standards. This role sits at the intersection of deep hands-on electromechanical manufacturing expertise and strategic program leadership. You'll balance short-term production demands with long-term capability development, pioneering manufacturing approaches that create lasting competitive advantage.

** This role requires relocation to Costa Mesa, CA for an initial training program of up to 2 months. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Drive the enterprise-wide manufacturing strategy for Barracuda, aligning production systems, processes, and capacity plans with Anduril's long-term business objectives and Arsenal-1's ramp targets.
  • Architect and lead the technology transfer of Barracuda production from Anduril HQ to Arsenal-1 — designing the production line layout, process flow, MES architecture, and quality systems for high-rate output.
  • Establish the manufacturing process frameworks that become organizational standards: RCCA systems, yield management programs, takt time structures, line balancing methodologies, and scaling playbooks.
  • Lead transformational line optimization initiatives that fundamentally redefine production capability — targeting step-change improvements in throughput, cost, and quality across the Barracuda program.
  • Define and own the MES strategy for Barracuda production at Arsenal-1: system selection, workflow architecture, data models, and integration with quality and supply chain systems.
  • Pioneer novel manufacturing approaches for complex electromechanical integration at scale; develop proprietary methods with potential for patent protection.
  • Direct large-scale capital improvement programs with enterprise-wide impact; manage multi-million dollar portfolios of interdependent projects from justification through validation.
  • Develop comprehensive manufacturing technology roadmaps, evaluate emerging technologies and create adoption strategies with quantified business impact.
  • Establish manufacturing excellence models that balance efficiency, quality, and flexibility; lead breakthrough cost reduction programs delivering 7-figure annual savings.
  • Serve as the company's foremost authority in electromechanical manufacturing processes for Barracuda; resolve the most complex technical challenges that impact critical business outcomes.
  • Develop comprehensive technical career paths and competency models for the manufacturing engineering organization; design mentorship programs that accelerate development of high-potential engineers.
  • Represent Anduril's manufacturing capabilities to key customers, partners, and industry bodies; establish strategic relationships with equipment suppliers and technology providers.
  • Translate executive-level business strategies into manufacturing capability requirements; develop cost models that inform product strategy and pricing decisions.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 12+ years in manufacturing of electromechanical hardware, with progressive leadership of complex production programs and scaling operations.
  • Degree in an engineering or technical field preferred, or equivalent depth of hands-on manufacturing experience.
  • Deep, demonstrated expertise in complex electromechanical integration at production scale — you've built it, optimized it, and scaled it.
  • Track record of standing up or transforming production lines: technology transfer, line design, process architecture, and ramp to rate.
  • Mastery of the manufacturing process ecosystem: work instructions, MBOMs, RCCA, line optimization, takt time management, yield programs, MES strategy, and scaling operations.
  • Experience leading transformational manufacturing initiatives with enterprise-wide impact and multi-million dollar scope.
  • Proven ability to resolve the most complex technical challenges where no established solution paths exist.
  • A world-class quality and mission-assurance mindset with the judgment to balance competing priorities across quality, cost, schedule, and manufacturability.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • High-rate manufacturing background in aerospace, defense, automotive/EV, or similar high-volume precision environment.
  • Experience architecting production systems for a new facility or major production line standup from the ground up.
  • Exposure to aircraft, aerospace, and defense programs at a strategic or program leadership level.
  • Harness and PCBA fabrication experience, including SMT process expertise at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with autonomous systems, flight vehicles, or related control systems.
  • Lean Six Sigma (Black Belt or higher); deep familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620.
  • Experience selecting, deploying, or architecting MES platforms for high-rate production environments.
  • Published work, patents, or recognized contributions to manufacturing technology advancement.
  • Software scripting ability in any language.
  • Current active U.S. Secret security clearance.

  • Experience with OEM turbine package installation, interconnection, and commissioning support.
  • Previous experience on power plants serving data centers, hyperscale, or other high-reliability industrial loads.

Head of Financial Crime

SpaceXAI  ·  X Money

Soho, London  ·  Full-time  ·  On-site 5 days  ·  Competitive base + equity

X Money is live in the US. The UK financial crime programme is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA. This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end — AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm. You will still work the hard cases. It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with “strategy” in the title.

If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat.

Why this seat is interesting

  • You write the UK programme while it is still being built. The standards you put in place are the ones the team — and the FCA — will actually use.
  • Payments financial crime at consumer scale, not a private-banking book of 400 names. You sit with Product and Engineering, not three layers from the customer journey.
  • Small team. Direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer. Scope is large; process theatre is not.
  • The measure of the job is a programme that still works a year later. The role sits next to MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity. If you want to be the named specialist in the room, this is how you get there.

  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or equivalent preferred.
  • Prior experience working with or within JFSA-supervised financial institutions, banking or payments providers, or supervised fintechs in Japan is a plus.
  • Based in Japan; fluency in English required; Japanese language proficiency a plus.

Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About the Role

We're looking for a design engineer to help build and maintain Waypoint, our design system, across both the Figma library and the production codebase. This is not a "designer who codes a little" or an "engineer who dabbles in Figma" role. You should be genuinely fluent on both sides, comfortable defining a component's behavior and states in Figma one hour and shipping the same component to npm the next.

You'll take direct ownership of the Figma side of our library (structure, variants, tokens, documentation) while also contributing to the core Waypoint system: our component packages, our token pipeline, and the tooling that keeps design and code in sync. If the idea of being the single point of continuity between a Figma frame and a production component sounds exciting rather than exhausting, this is your role.

We're also thinking beyond the system we have today. Waypoint isn't just meant to serve designers and engineers, it's meant to become something a model can read, reason about, and build with directly. We want someone who can help us get there: grounded enough to do the unglamorous work of making today's system solid, and forward looking enough to help define what an intelligent design system looks like next.



Why this role

Waypoint is still early enough that the decisions you make now will shape how the system scales. You'll have real ownership, not just a queue of component tickets, and you'll be working alongside a team that treats design and engineering as one discipline rather than two departments that hand work back and forth. And you'll be helping define what a design system becomes when it has to serve a third audience: the models that will increasingly build with it.

  • Exposure to multi-platform design systems work (iOS/SwiftUI, Android/Jetpack Compose, or token build tools like Style Dictionary).

  • Experience in an AI native product environment or genuine interest in how AI changes the way design systems get built and used.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

Shield AI builds intelligent systems that protect service members and civilians. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software and V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and our teams support customers and operations across the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. 

Shield AI is hiring a Senior Customer Sustainment Engineer to support Hivemind systems after they reach customers and operational teams. This role sits at the intersection of customer support, systems troubleshooting, and engineering. 

Customers and forward deployed employees bring valuable operational context when they report a mission interruption, update concern, or unexpected system behavior. You will work with them to translate that context into a clear technical problem by gathering the right evidence, understanding the operating environment, narrowing the likely causes, and identifying the best path to resolution. 

Some issues will be resolved through configuration changes, deployment corrections, known workarounds, or better guidance. Others will require a product or engineering change. In either case, you will stay with the issue through resolution, keep the customer informed, and make sure the outcome is captured for future use. 

The role is the primary owner for Tier 1 support, handles a meaningful portion of Tier 2 troubleshooting, and can contribute to limited Tier 3 investigation when deeper technical experience is useful. Using DoD sustainment language, this is roughly the software equivalent of intermediate-level maintenance: resolve what can be addressed at that level, identify what needs depot-level repair, and provide engineering with a complete technical handoff. Product Support and core engineering teams provide the depot-level repair capability, while this role stays engaged to validate the result and close the loop with the customer. 

You will work closely with Forward Deployment Engineering, Product Support Engineering, Operations & Sustainment, Product, Program, Licensing, and the core Hivemind engineering teams. The goal is straightforward: help customers return to mission-ready operation while making Hivemind easier to support over time. 

What you'll do:

    • Own Tier 1 customer support and incident coordination from initial report through confirmed resolution. 

    • Gather the information needed to understand an issue, including mission impact, software version, configuration, deployment state, logs, telemetry, screenshots, network context, and reproduction steps. 

    • Troubleshoot Hivemind software, APIs, licensing and provisioning, deployments, configurations, networks, operator workflows, and partner or OEM integrations. 

    • Separate product defects from configuration problems, environmental differences, integration issues, training needs, and feature requests. 

    • Resolve common technical problems, handle appropriate Tier 2 investigations, and reproduce more complex failures in lab, simulation, or representative test environments. 

    • Recognize issues that require Tier 3 or depot-level product repair and give engineering teams concise escalation packages that explain the impact, evidence, likely causes, work already attempted, and expected result. 

    • Provide customers with clear updates, practical next steps, and technically sound workarounds while investigations are in progress. 

    • Support software releases, upgrades, onboarding, licensing and provisioning workflows, and the transition from deployment into ongoing sustainment. 

    • Turn recurring issues into troubleshooting guides, known-issue records, diagnostic tools, training material, and product feedback. 

    • Use incident patterns to identify improvements to product reliability, diagnostics, documentation, and release readiness. 

Projects you may work on:

    • Investigate a mission failure after a software update by comparing logs, configurations, versions, network behavior, telemetry, and release notes. 

    • Reproduce an autonomy, API, or integration issue and provide engineering with the evidence needed to correct it. 

    • Restore an offline customer environment affected by licensing, provisioning, time synchronization, or version compatibility. 

    • Coordinate the technical response to a high-impact customer issue and validate the workaround or fix before closure. 

    • Build a diagnostic playbook for recurring deployment, configuration, networking, or operator-workflow problems. 

Required qualifications:

    • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical, military, field-engineering, or technical experience. 

    • 7+ years of hands-on experience supporting fielded, software-enabled systems in customer, operational, test, deployment, or sustainment environments. 

    • Experience with cyber-physical, edge, mission, robotics, autonomy, aviation, defense, industrial-control, or similarly complex deployed systems. 

    • Strong troubleshooting skills across software, Linux, configuration, networking, logs, telemetry, software versions, and hardware-adjacent interfaces. 

    • A record of owning technical issues from an incomplete initial report through diagnosis and resolution. 

    • Ability to read and reason about modern C++ and use existing Python, Bash, or similar scripts during troubleshooting and log analysis. 

    • Clear written and verbal communication with customers, operators, and engineering teams, including during time-sensitive situations. 

    • Ability to write useful incident records, troubleshooting guidance, engineering escalations, and customer-facing updates. 

    • Sound judgment when working within security, export-control, safety, customer-site, contractual, and data-handling requirements. 

    • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance when required by customers. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with autonomy software, robotics, unmanned systems, aviation, defense or mission software, ground-control software, SDKs, APIs, or edge-deployed systems.
  • Experience supporting fleet operations, operational-readiness events, flight or ground test campaigns, or customer-site deployments.
  • Familiarity with DoD sustainment, intermediate- and depot-level maintenance concepts, or comparable field-to-engineering support models.
  • Hands-on software engineering experience writing and debugging C++ and developing Python scripts or tools for diagnostics, automation, or data analysis.
  • Familiarity with software releases, configuration baselines, upgrade validation, rollback, and version compatibility.
  • Experience with licensing, provisioning, offline or air-gapped environments, edge compute, time synchronization, networking, or telemetry analysis.
  • Experience with Jira, Azure DevOps, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Confluence, or similar engineering and support tools.
  • Military, operator, maintainer, field-service, mission-support, or customer-engineering experience.
  • Active or prior security clearance. 
    •  

Success looks like:

    After 90 days,
  • You can independently manage Tier 1 Hivemind support, resolve appropriate Tier 2 problems, and bring well-supported Tier 3 or depot-level cases to the appropriate engineering team. 
  • Customers and internal teams receive clear updates, practical next steps, and consistent follow-through. 
  • Your escalation packages allow engineering teams to begin useful work without repeating basic discovery. 
  • After 6 months 
  • Common field issues have repeatable diagnostics, workarounds, and support guidance. 
  • Forward Deployment Engineers and core engineers spend less time reconstructing customer problems because the evidence and technical qualification are already in place. 
  • Incident trends are leading to improvements in Hivemind reliability, supportability, documentation, and release readiness.

Your work is hands-on and focused on engineering maximum velocity, reproducibility, and security into our distributed developer tooling and cloud testing environments.

You will completely automate tool workflows by writing scripts and API integrations connecting GitLab, Jira, and Confluence. You will configure and optimize C++, Python, and Node.js compilation pipelines, scale auto-running GitLab runner fleets, manage secure Artifactory container registries, deploy Forge in Azure Gov Cloud, and write custom HMS extensions to our pi-gov GenAI routing harness.

  • Deploy, scale, and configure the Forge simulation and test orchestrator in Azure Gov Cloud, optimizing runner autoscaling and cloud compute consumption.
  • Maintain, configure, and secure Artifactory package registries, implementing secure container builds via BuildKit, secret injection, and Entra ID integration.
  • Partner with development teams to migrate legacy project build systems to reproducible Nix developer environments, writing default Nix derivations and flake configurations.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to help drive the design, development, and integration of a safety critical Run-Time Assurance (RTA) product. The Hivemind Foundations team is responsible for a suite of core products and capabilities that brings resilient autonomy and intelligence to aircraft and other platforms operating in complex environments. The RTA product that the Foundations team develops is a real-time safety capability that helps keep autonomy safe, predictable, and effective at the edge.  

As a member of the Foundations team, you will be responsible for driving C++ software development against rigorous coding standards and requirements, integration of reusable safety capabilities into production systems, defining clean interfaces and tests, and turn safety-critical designs into reliable software that can fly, including support for X-BAT, Shield AI's flagship Group 5 Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) UAV. 

What you'll do:

  • Drive architecture, development, integration and testing of an extensible, configurable Run-Time Assurance (RTA) module that ensures safe operation of autonomous systems in diverse, adversarial conditions. 
  • Work closely with other engineers in Foundations to design and integrate with the low-assurance mission-autonomy software and high-assurance middleware. 
  • Specialize, integrate and test the RTA capability on a diverse set of platforms in various conditions to ensure robust fail-safe behavior. 
  • Drive principled software development practices across Foundations including but not limited to code analysis, audit trail, principled review processes. 
  • Collaborate with the team to generate artifacts that enable certifiability of Foundations software, including but not limited to static & dynamic analysis reports, software documentation, architecture decision records (ADRs), interface control diagrams (ICDs), system models. 
  • Mentor and guide Foundations developers on practices of safe software development to enhance software quality and assurance.

  • Typically requires a minimum of 10 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 9 years with a Master’s degree; or 7 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience. 
  • Demonstrated excellence in designing and developing C++ based safety-critical software systems with Real-Time guarantees. 
  • Experience working as a mentor to other engineers in a role driving software best practices to enhance software quality. 
  • Experience integrating software on real-world physical systems and driving up performance and reliability. 
  • Deep expertise in C++ software architecture design patterns and their practical implementation. 
  • Strong knowledge of software assurance certifications such as DO-178C and MIL-HDBK-516. 
  • Strong Git and Linux development skills, along with modern software development practices (e.g., CI/CD, test-driven development). 
  • A track record of technical leadership, with the ability to set and maintain high standards, guide teams through complex technical challenges, and collaborate effectively. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with airworthiness certifications such as MIL-HDBK-516, DO-178C. 
  • Experience taking a solution through a certification process and achieving a certification.

{
  "dataset": "workflow-schedules",
  "asOf": "2026-10-10",
  "taxYear": null,
  "source": {
    "name": "GitHub Actions configuration",
    "url": "https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule",
    "licence": "n/a"
  },
  "exportedAt": "2026-10-10",
  "values": {
    ".github/workflows/snapshot.yml": "name: Snapshot job boards

# GitHub-hosted runners can reach the public job-board APIs. This workflow
# fetches every built-in board and uploads data/snapshots/*.json as a workflow
# ARTIFACT. It does not commit them: real snapshots are tens of MB per day
# (anduril alone is ~38 MB), which would bloat the git history. pages.yml
# restores the latest artifact as its fallback before fetching fresh data.
#
# Beta channel (docs/process/beta-deploy.md): the big-tech boards are crawled
# here, never in pages.yml (a full crawl takes over an hour: about 1 request/s per
# host, and Amazon alone has ~22k postings). Every 6 hours:
#   beta-companies  the beta slugs from server/companies.js (the matrix)
#   beta-crawl      one job per company, in parallel (each a different host, so the
#                   per-host politeness holds), capped; its snapshot is vetted (the
#                   per-company beta gate) and only a passing one is handed on
#   beta-merge      the previous job-board-snapshots-beta artifact + this run's
#                   results: a company whose crawl failed keeps its previous file;
#                   the beta ledger is updated; one artifact uploaded
#   beta-deploy     dispatches pages.yml, so fresh posts go live without a push (a
#                   dispatched deploy makes no branch build, so no holding page)
# The stable job (daily) is unchanged and never waits on or depends on these.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *" # stable boards, daily, 06:17 UTC
    - cron: "47 0,6,12,18 * * *" # beta (big-tech) boards, every 6 hours at :47 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      channel:
        description: Which boards to fetch
        type: choice
        options: [both, stable, beta]
        default: both

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # find the newest history-ledger / beta snapshots artifact

# Ledger artifacts are only restored from trusted runs (REVIEW.md V2).
env:
  TRUSTED_BRANCHES: claude/stoic-ride-54ddxp

concurrency:
  group: snapshot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  snapshot:
    if: ${{ github.event.schedule == '17 6 * * *' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.channel != 'beta') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      # F4 history ledger (data/history/*.json): restore it before the snapshot
      # step updates it. Store: HISTORY_STORE repo variable, `artifact` (default:
      # newest non-expired `history-ledger` artifact from either workflow) or
      # `branch` (orphan data-history branch). Missing = start fresh.
      # See .github/scripts/ledger.sh and README "History ledger".
      - name: Restore history ledger
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HISTORY_STORE: ${{ vars.HISTORY_STORE || 'artifact' }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh restore

      - name: Fetch snapshots
        id: fetch
        run: npm run snapshot # no args = every built-in in server/companies.js; also updates data/history/

      # Always upload the updated ledger (also the hand-off to persist-ledger in
      # branch mode), even if a later step such as the vetting gate fails.
      - name: Upload history ledger
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: history-ledger
          path: data/history/
          retention-days: 90
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # Salary vetting gate: same command as pages.yml. A critical anomaly fails
      # this job (red run + step summary). The raw artifact is still uploaded
      # (below, `if: !cancelled()`) for review and as pages.yml's fallback;
      # pages.yml re-runs this gate, so bad pay still can't be published.
      - name: Salary vetting gate (fails on critical anomalies)
        id: vet
        continue-on-error: false
        run: node scripts/vet-salaries.js --no-write-flags --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Upload snapshots artifact
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: job-board-snapshots
          path: data/snapshots/*.json
          retention-days: 90 # GitHub maximum; the permanent copy is the data-archive branch (docs/DATA_ARCHIVE.md)
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Branch store only (HISTORY_STORE=branch): commit the ledger to the orphan
  # data-history branch. The only job with contents: write, and it is skipped
  # entirely in the default artifact store (and on beta-only runs).
  persist-ledger:
    needs: snapshot
    if: ${{ vars.HISTORY_STORE == 'branch' && !cancelled() && needs.snapshot.result != 'skipped' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    concurrency:
      group: history-ledger-branch
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: history-ledger
          path: data/history
      - name: Commit ledger to the data-history branch
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh commit-branch

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- beta channel

  beta-companies:
    if: ${{ github.event.schedule == '47 0,6,12,18 * * *' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.channel != 'stable') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      slugs: ${{ steps.list.outputs.slugs }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Beta companies (server/companies.js)
        id: list
        run: |
          slugs=$(node .github/scripts/beta-snapshots.mjs slugs)
          echo "slugs=$slugs" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Beta companies to crawl: $slugs" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # One crawl per company, in parallel. A failed or timed-out crawl, or one the beta
  # gate rejects, uploads nothing, so the merge keeps that company's previous file.
  beta-crawl:
    name: beta crawl (${{ matrix.slug }})
    needs: beta-companies
    if: ${{ needs.beta-companies.outputs.slugs != '' && needs.beta-companies.outputs.slugs != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        slug: ${{ fromJSON(needs.beta-companies.outputs.slugs) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      # The ledger is recorded by beta-merge, against the previous one; this run's copy is scratch.
      - name: Crawl (polite, about 1 request/s; capped at 140 min)
        id: crawl
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          SLUG: ${{ matrix.slug }}
          MELON_SNAPSHOT_DIR: data/beta-fresh
          MELON_HISTORY_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/ledger-scratch
        run: timeout --kill-after=60s 140m node scripts/snapshot.js "$SLUG"

      - name: Crawl did not finish (the previous snapshot stays on /beta/)
        if: ${{ steps.crawl.outcome != 'success' }}
        env:
          SLUG: ${{ matrix.slug }}
        run: echo "::warning::beta crawl of $SLUG failed or timed out; the beta site keeps its previous $SLUG snapshot"

      # Beta gate (per company): a snapshot with an unquarantined critical salary is moved aside.
      - name: Beta salary vetting gate
        env:
          BETA_GATE_TIMEOUT: "300"
        run: bash .github/scripts/beta-gate.sh data/beta-fresh "$RUNNER_TEMP/beta-rejected"

      - name: Hand the snapshot to the merge
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: beta-crawl-${{ matrix.slug }}
          path: data/beta-fresh/*.json
          retention-days: 90 # GitHub maximum; the permanent copy is the data-archive branch (docs/DATA_ARCHIVE.md)
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  beta-merge:
    needs: [beta-companies, beta-crawl]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.beta-companies.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      fresh: ${{ steps.merge.outputs.fresh }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      # data/beta/snapshots/ + data/beta/history/ as the last run left them (trusted runs only).
      - name: Restore last beta snapshots artifact (trusted runs only)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          LEDGER_ARTIFACT: job-board-snapshots-beta
          LEDGER_DIR: data/beta
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh restore-artifact

      - name: Download this run's crawls
        continue-on-error: true # no company produced a snapshot
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: beta-crawl-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: data/beta-fresh

      - name: Merge (fresh replaces previous; a failed company keeps its previous file)
        id: merge

  # runs make no branch-based Pages build, so the holding page never shows.

    needs: beta-merge
    if: ${{ needs.beta-merge.result == 'success' && fromJSON(needs.beta-merge.outputs.fresh || '0') > 0 }}

",
    ".github/workflows/pages.yml": "name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

# https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/ . Every run fetches fresh snapshots
# from the live boards (GitHub runners can reach them). Snapshots are not
# committed to git; the latest snapshot.yml artifact is restored first, so a
# board that fails during this run keeps its last good data instead of
# falling back to demo.
#

# same deploy also publishes https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/beta/, a full
# copy of the app with the stable companies plus the big-tech boards. This
# workflow never crawls the big-tech boards (a full crawl takes over an hour):
# it restores the latest trusted job-board-snapshots-beta artifact, which
# snapshot.yml crawls every 6 hours and then deploys by dispatching this

  actions: read # look up and download trusted snapshot/ledger artifacts

env:

concurrency:

jobs:

      # crawl left them. Same trust rules. Nothing here crawls a big-tech board.
      - name: Restore last beta snapshots artifact (trusted runs only; best effort)

          LEDGER_ARTIFACT: job-board-snapshots-beta

      # F4 history ledger (data/history/*.json): restore it before the snapshot

      - name: Upload history ledger

      - name: Build static site

      # or hold up the stable deploy.
      - name: Build beta site (best effort; dist/beta/)

        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 10

          SITE_URL: ${{ vars.SITE_URL || 'https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/' }}

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          grep -oE '<meta (property|name)="(og|twitter):[a-z:_]+" content="[^"]*"' dist/index.html
          img=$(sed -n 's/.*property="og:image" content="\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' dist/index.html | head -1)
          case "$img" in
            "${SITE_URL%/}"/*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::og:image '$img' is not an absolute URL under SITE_URL ($SITE_URL)"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          for k in 'property="og:url" content="https://' 'name="twitter:image" content="https://' 'name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image"'; do

      - name: Check live link preview

        env:

        run: |
          img=''; type=''

            if [ "$type" = "image/png" ]; then echo "og:image $img is live ($type)"; exit 0; fi
            echo "attempt $i: og:image='$img' content-type='$type'; retrying in 20s"; sleep 20
          done
          echo "::warning::Live link preview check failed: og:image='$img' content-type='$type' (docs/process/social.md)"
          exit 1

      # content="beta">). A beta outage is a warning annotation, never a failed deploy.
      - name: Verify the beta site (warning only)
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          EXPECT_CHANNEL: beta
          CHECK_LEVEL: warning
          CHECK_TIMEOUT: "120"
        run: |
          if ! bash .github/scripts/check-site.sh "${SITE%/}/beta/" "$GITHUB_SHA"; then

          fi
