    ".github/workflows/site-watchdog.yml": "name: Site watchdog

# Every 30 min (and on demand): is https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/ the
# melon-seek APP from the latest successful pages.yml deploy? If GitHub's
# README page (branch-based Pages build) or a wrong build is being served, it
# re-runs pages.yml and reports the problem in the job summary.
# Root cause it guards against: Settings -> Pages -> Source = "Deploy from a
# branch" (fix: Source = "GitHub Actions"; needs an admin, so this can't do it).
# It also checks the beta copy at <site>/beta/ (docs/process/beta-deploy.md):
# a beta problem is a warning annotation only (no re-deploy, no failed run).
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "11,41 * * * *" # every 30 min, off the hour
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write   # dispatch pages.yml
  contents: read   # sparse checkout of .github/scripts

concurrency:
  group: site-watchdog
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      SITE: ${{ vars.SITE_URL || 'https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: .github/scripts
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Expected build (latest successful pages.yml deploy)
        id: expect
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          busy=$(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow pages.yml --limit 20 --json status \
                   --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length')
          echo "busy=$busy" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          read -r sha branch < <(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow pages.yml --status success --limit 1 \
                                   --json headSha,headBranch --jq '.[0] | "\(.headSha // "") \(.headBranch // "")"')
          echo "sha=${sha:-}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "branch=${branch:-}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Latest successful deploy: ${sha:-none} on ${branch:-?}; pages.yml runs in flight: $busy"

      - name: Check the live site
        id: check
        if: steps.expect.outputs.busy == '0'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          CHECK_TIMEOUT: "60"
        run: bash .github/scripts/check-site.sh "$SITE" "${{ steps.expect.outputs.sha }}"

      - name: Check the beta site (warning only)
        if: steps.expect.outputs.busy == '0'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          CHECK_TIMEOUT: "60"
          EXPECT_CHANNEL: beta
          CHECK_LEVEL: warning
          EXPECTED: ${{ steps.expect.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          if ! bash .github/scripts/check-site.sh "${SITE%/}/beta/" "$EXPECTED"; then
            { echo "### Beta site check (warning)"; echo ""; echo "- URL: ${SITE%/}/beta/"; echo "- The main site is checked separately; a beta outage never re-deploys or fails this run."; echo ""; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Deploy in progress
        if: steps.expect.outputs.busy != '0'
        run: echo "A pages.yml run is in flight; skipping this check (it verifies the site itself)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Re-deploy and report
        if: steps.check.outcome == 'failure'
        env:
          RESULT: ${{ steps.check.outputs.result }}
          DETAIL: ${{ steps.check.outputs.detail }}
          BRANCH: ${{ steps.expect.outputs.branch }}
        run: |
          ref="${BRANCH:-${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}}"
          dispatched="no"
          if gh workflow run pages.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$ref"; then dispatched="yes (ref $ref)"; fi
          {
            echo "### Live site is NOT the app"
            echo ""
            echo "- URL: $SITE"
            echo "- Problem: ${RESULT:-unknown}, ${DETAIL:-no detail}"
            echo "- Re-ran pages.yml: $dispatched"
            echo ""
            if [ "$RESULT" = "readme" ]; then
              echo "GitHub is publishing the README from a branch. Permanent fix: **Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> Source: GitHub Actions**."
            fi
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "::error::Live site is not the app ($RESULT: $DETAIL); re-ran pages.yml: $dispatched"
          exit 1
",
    ".github/workflows/monthly-refresh.yml": "name: Monthly data refresh

# Monthly refresh of every reference number the product shows, cites or computes
# from: FX, Big Mac prices, rents, cost index, the NYC living-cost baseline, tax
# rules, and the models built on job data (market comps, Compstimate backtest,
# vetting health, lexicon coverage). The registry is data/freshness.json; the
# runbook is docs/DATA_FRESHNESS.md. Job postings themselves are refreshed daily
# by snapshot.yml / pages.yml and are only health-checked here.
#
# scripts/refresh/run.js runs one updater per data family (scripts/refresh/*.js):
#   auto    fetch + validate + diff; validated changes become a REVIEW PR
#   detect  compare the official source with the encoded values; a mismatch or a
#           newly published tax/data year becomes a GitHub ISSUE with the evidence
#   manual  past-due entries are listed in the same issue with their checklist
# Safety model (REVIEW.md V12, as col-refresh.yml before it): nothing is ever
# pushed to the default/deploy branch. Changes go to the bot/monthly-refresh
# branch and a pull request for a human to review; merging it deploys.
#
# Repo settings this needs (the workflow degrades gracefully without them):
#   - Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions ->
#     "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" (to open the PR;
#     without it the branch is pushed and the run says to open the PR by hand).
#   - Optional secrets: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (advisory LLM read of tax pages),
#     HUD_API_TOKEN (HUD USER API for US rents), BLS_API_KEY (BLS API v2 limits).
# PRs opened with GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger CI; re-run CI from the PR (or push to it).
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 5 3 * *" # monthly, 05:17 UTC on the 3rd (after ECB/Fed monthly averages are out)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      only:
        description: "Comma-separated updater modules or registry ids (empty = everything)"
        required: false
        default: ""
        type: string
      dry_run:
        description: "Report only: no branch, PR or issue"
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: monthly-refresh
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  TRUSTED_BRANCHES: claude/stoic-ride-54ddxp
  REVIEW_BRANCH: bot/monthly-refresh
  ISSUE_LABEL: data-freshness

jobs:
  refresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: write      # push the bot/monthly-refresh review branch (never the default branch)
      pull-requests: write # open / update the review PR
      issues: write        # open / update the data-freshness issue
      actions: read        # restore the latest trusted job-board snapshot artifact
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install pdftotext (official tax schedules are often PDFs)
        run: command -v pdftotext || (sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils > /dev/null)

      # The job-data checks (market comps, Compstimate backtest, vetting health)
      # read the newest snapshots. Trusted runs only (REVIEW.md V2). Best effort:
      # without them those checks report 'skipped'.
      - name: Restore last snapshots artifact (trusted runs only)
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          LEDGER_ARTIFACT: job-board-snapshots
          LEDGER_DIR: data/snapshots
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh restore-artifact

      - name: Restore history ledger (best effort)
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HISTORY_STORE: ${{ vars.HISTORY_STORE || 'artifact' }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh restore

      - name: Restore last beta snapshots artifact (trusted runs only; best effort)
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 5
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          LEDGER_ARTIFACT: job-board-snapshots-beta
          LEDGER_DIR: data/beta
        run: bash .github/scripts/ledger.sh restore-artifact

      # Last month's archived aggregates are the baseline for the month-over-month
      # checks (docs/DATA_ARCHIVE.md). Read-only worktree; without it the checks
      # fall back to absolute bounds and say so.
      - name: Check out the data archive (read-only baseline; best effort)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          if git fetch --depth=1 origin data-archive 2>/dev/null; then
            git worktree add --detach tmp/archive FETCH_HEAD
          else
            echo "No data-archive branch yet; month-over-month checks use absolute bounds."
          fi

      # The archive (docs/DATA_ARCHIVE.md) keeps every version of every dataset forever.
      # BEFORE the refresh touches anything, export the current (live, merged) value of each
      # registry dataset; archive.yml imports tmp/refresh/ (report, archive/ and reference/
      # manifests) from the uploaded artifact into the data-archive branch. Proposed changes
      # in the review PR are archived once merged (the archive's capture of the code branch).
      - name: Export the current reference datasets for the archive
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/refresh/run.js --export-reference tmp/refresh/reference

      - name: Refresh (fetch, validate, diff)
        id: refresh
        env:
          MELON_ARCHIVE_DIR: tmp/archive
          MELON_BETA_SNAPSHOT_DIR: data/beta/snapshots
          MELON_BETA_HISTORY_DIR: data/beta/history
          ONLY: ${{ inputs.only }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          HUD_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HUD_API_TOKEN }}
          BLS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.BLS_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out tmp/refresh)
          if [ -n "${ONLY:-}" ]; then args+=(--only "$ONLY"); fi
          if [ "${DRY_RUN:-false}" = "true" ]; then args+=(--dry-run); fi
          node scripts/refresh/run.js "${args[@]}" > tmp-refresh.log 2>&1 || { cat tmp-refresh.log; exit 1; }
          tail -n 40 tmp-refresh.log
          node -e '
            const o = require("./tmp/refresh/outcome.json");
            const out = require("fs").createWriteStream(process.env.GITHUB_OUTPUT, { flags: "a" });
            out.write(`files=${o.files.length}\nalerts=${o.alerts + o.problems}\n`);
            out.end();
            console.log(`files changed: ${o.files.length}, alerts: ${o.alerts}, problems: ${o.problems}`);
          '

      # The suite runs against the refreshed data, so a PR shows which tests a
      # data change breaks (e.g. worked examples pinned to old FX). Never blocks
      # the PR: a human decides.
      - name: Tests against the refreshed data (advisory)
        id: tests
        if: steps.refresh.outputs.files != '0' && inputs.dry_run != true
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          npm test 2>&1 | tee tmp/refresh/npm-test.log | tail -n 25
          echo "Tests passed against the refreshed data." > tmp/refresh/tests.md

      - name: Note failing tests
        if: steps.refresh.outputs.files != '0' && inputs.dry_run != true && steps.tests.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          {
            echo "**Tests FAILED against the refreshed data.** Review before merging; failing tests may pin old values (see docs/DATA_FRESHNESS.md, 'Pinned values')."
            echo
            echo '```'
            grep -E '^not ok|^# (pass|fail)' tmp/refresh/npm-test.log | head -n 40 || true
            echo '```'
          } > tmp/refresh/tests.md

      - name: Upload the report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: monthly-refresh-report
          path: tmp/refresh/
          retention-days: 90
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Push the review branch and open a PR (never the default branch)
        if: steps.refresh.outputs.files != '0' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          branch="$REVIEW_BRANCH"
          day=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
          # Stage exactly the files the orchestrator reported (never `git add -A`).
          node -e 'for (const f of require("./tmp/refresh/outcome.json").files) console.log(f)' > tmp/refresh/files.txt
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git switch -c "$branch"
          xargs -a tmp/refresh/files.txt -d '\n' git add --
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "No changes to commit."; exit 0; fi
          git commit -m "chore(data): monthly refresh of reference data ($day)" -m "Generated by .github/workflows/monthly-refresh.yml (scripts/refresh/run.js). See the PR body for the report."
          git push --force origin "$branch"
          { cat tmp/refresh/tests.md 2>/dev/null || true; echo; cat tmp/refresh/summary.md; } | head -c 64000 > tmp/refresh/pr-body.md
          base="${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}"
          if gh pr view "$branch" --json state --jq .state 2>/dev/null | grep -q OPEN; then
            gh pr edit "$branch" --title "chore(data): monthly data refresh ($day)" --body-file tmp/refresh/pr-body.md
            echo "Updated the open PR for $branch."
          elif gh pr create --base "$base" --head "$branch" --title "chore(data): monthly data refresh ($day)" --body-file tmp/refresh/pr-body.md; then
            echo "Opened a PR for $branch."
          else
            echo "::warning::Pushed $branch but could not open a PR (enable Settings -> Actions -> General -> 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests', or open it by hand)."
          fi

      - name: Open or update the data-freshness issue (drift, flags, stale entries, errors)
        if: inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ALERTS: ${{ steps.refresh.outputs.alerts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          day=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
          head -c 64000 tmp/refresh/summary.md > tmp/refresh/issue-body.md
          open=$(gh issue list --label "$ISSUE_LABEL" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "${ALERTS:-0}" = "0" ]; then
            if [ -n "$open" ]; then
              gh issue comment "$open" --body "Monthly refresh $day: no drift, flags, stale entries or errors. Closing." && gh issue close "$open" --reason completed || true
            fi
            echo "No alerts."
            exit 0
          fi
          gh label create "$ISSUE_LABEL" --color FBCA04 --description "Reference data needs a human (docs/DATA_FRESHNESS.md)" 2>/dev/null || true
          title="Data freshness: $ALERTS item(s) need review ($day)"
          if [ -n "$open" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$open" --title "$title" --body-file tmp/refresh/issue-body.md
            gh issue comment "$open" --body "Monthly refresh $day updated this issue: $ALERTS item(s). Run: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --label "$ISSUE_LABEL" --body-file tmp/refresh/issue-body.md
          fi
",
    ".github/workflows/archive.yml": "name: Archive (daily ingest into the data branch)

# The permanent historical database (docs/DATA_ARCHIVE.md). After every run of
# "Snapshot job boards", "Deploy to GitHub Pages" and "Monthly data refresh" (and
# daily as a safety net) it:
#   1. sweeps every trusted artifact that is not in the archive yet (job-board
#      snapshots, the F4 ledger, salary-vetting reports, reference-data hand-offs) and
#      folds each into the append-only archive;
#   2. records a new dated version of every reference dataset the code branch defines
#      (FX, cities.json rents and cost index, the Juice/tax model, policy constants)
#      when it changed;
#   3. freezes the monthly cross-company comparisons of every month that is complete;
#   4. writes the monthly report of each complete month, the annual review of the year
#      (year to date), and in January the final review of the year before;
#   5. verifies the result against the previous commit and commits it to the orphan
#      data-archive branch.
# It never pushes to the code branch and never force-pushes; artifacts from
# pull_request, fork or untrusted-branch runs are never read (same rules as
# .github/scripts/ledger.sh). The sweep also covers runs whose archive job was replaced
# while queued (the concurrency group keeps one pending run), so nothing is missed when
# many deploys finish close together.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Snapshot job boards", "Deploy to GitHub Pages", "Monthly data refresh"]
    types: [completed]
  schedule:
    - cron: "37 9 * * *" # daily safety net, after snapshot.yml (06:17) and pages.yml (07:41)
    - cron: "23 4 1 * *" # monthly: freeze last month's comparisons and write its report (January: the annual review)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      verify_history:
        description: "Also re-verify this many past data-branch commits (0 = skip)"
        required: false
        default: "0"

permissions:
  contents: read

# Artifacts are only read from trusted runs (REVIEW.md V2; scripts/archive/sweep.js).
env:
  TRUSTED_BRANCHES: claude/stoic-ride-54ddxp

# Shared with archive-backfill.yml: two archive runs never interleave on the data branch.
concurrency:
  group: archive
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # contents: write is allowed for this job by name in test/workflows.test.js (it pushes only
  # the orphan data-archive branch; scripts/archive/branch.sh refuses main and claude/*).
  archive-ingest:
    name: Ingest into the data-archive branch
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the orphan data-archive branch (never the code branch)
      actions: read   # list and download workflow artifacts
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      VERIFY_HISTORY: ${{ inputs.verify_history || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Open the data-archive branch
        env:
          ARCHIVE_DEPTH: ${{ (inputs.verify_history && inputs.verify_history != '0') && '400' || '1' }}
        run: |
          echo "ARCHIVE=$RUNNER_TEMP/archive" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          bash scripts/archive/branch.sh open "$RUNNER_TEMP/archive"

      - name: Migrate the schema if the code is newer, then verify before ingesting
        run: |
          node scripts/archive/migrate.js --archive "$ARCHIVE"
          node scripts/archive/verify.js --archive "$ARCHIVE"
          case "$VERIFY_HISTORY" in ''|0|*[!0-9]*) ;; *) node scripts/archive/verify.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --history "$VERIFY_HISTORY" ;; esac

      - name: Sweep artifacts, verify and commit
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          for i in $(seq 1 20); do
            if [ "$SECONDS" -gt 3600 ]; then echo "::warning::time budget used; the next run continues"; break; fi
            node scripts/archive/sweep.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --max 3 --run-cache "$RUNNER_TEMP/runs.json"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$rc" -ne 10 ]; then echo "::error::sweep failed (exit $rc)"; exit "$rc"; fi
            node scripts/archive/verify.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --prev-rev HEAD || { echo "::error::archive verify failed; nothing from this batch is committed"; exit 1; }
            bash scripts/archive/branch.sh commit "$ARCHIVE" "archive: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ) ($(node scripts/archive/status.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --oneline))" || exit 1
            [ "$rc" -eq 10 ] || break
          done

      - name: Reference data, monthly comparisons and reports
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/archive/record.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --from-repo
          node scripts/archive/monthly.js --archive "$ARCHIVE"
          node scripts/archive/report.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --auto
          node scripts/archive/reconstruct.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --check-all
          node scripts/archive/verify.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --prev-rev HEAD
          bash scripts/archive/branch.sh commit "$ARCHIVE" "archive: reference data, monthly comparisons and reports ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"

      - name: Summary
        if: ${{ always() }}
        run: |
          if [ -f "$ARCHIVE/MANIFEST.json" ]; then
            node scripts/archive/status.js --archive "$ARCHIVE" --markdown | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
",
    ".github/workflows/ci.yml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test (Node ${{ matrix.node }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: [20, 22]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test

      # Warn-only staleness gate (docs/DATA_FRESHNESS.md): a step-summary table of every
      # dataset's age plus a warning per entry past its cadence + grace. Never fails CI.
      - name: Data freshness (warn only)
        if: matrix.node == 22
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/refresh/run.js --staleness

      - name: Static build (GitHub Pages bundle)
        run: |
          npm run build
          jq -e 'type == "array" and length >= 3' dist/api/companies.json
          for f in dist/api/jobs/*.json; do jq -e '.jobs | type == "array"' "$f" > /dev/null; done
          test -f dist/config.js && test -f dist/.nojekyll && test -f dist/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.js
          # Lazy descriptions: lists carry no HTML, each job has a desc file.
          jq -e '[.jobs[] | select(has("descriptionHtml") and .descriptionHtml != "")] | length == 0' dist/api/jobs/anthropic.json
          test -n "$(find dist/api/desc -name '*.json' -print -quit)"
          # Juice Score: inputs and module are bundled; juice itself is never stored in lists.
          test -f dist/lib/juice.js
          jq -e '(.cities | type == "array") and (.cities | length > 0)' dist/api/cities.json > /dev/null
          for f in dist/api/jobs/*.json; do jq -e '[.jobs[] | select(has("juice"))] | length == 0' "$f" > /dev/null; done
          # v2 (1-up): packed-2 lists with meta, plus per-company history and meta files.
          for f in dist/api/jobs/*.json; do
            slug=$(basename "$f" .json)
            jq -e '.format == "melon-packed-2" and (.meta | has("compstimate") and has("history"))' "$f" > /dev/null
            jq -e 'type == "object"' "dist/api/history/$slug.json" > /dev/null
            jq -e 'has("compstimate") and has("history")' "dist/api/meta/$slug.json" > /dev/null
          done

      - name: Smoke test (start server, hit API)
        env:
          PORT: 5173
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npm start > server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

          # Wait up to ~30s for the server to come up.
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/companies" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done

          echo "::group::GET /api/companies"
          curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/companies" | tee companies.json | jq .
          echo "::endgroup::"
          jq -e 'type == "array" and length >= 3 and (map(.slug) | index("anthropic") != null)' companies.json

          echo "::group::GET /api/jobs?company=anthropic"
          curl -fsS --max-time 90 "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/jobs?company=anthropic" > jobs.json
          jq '{mode, fetchedAt, error, company: .company.slug, count: (.jobs | length)}' jobs.json
          echo "::endgroup::"
          jq -e '(.jobs | type == "array") and (.mode | IN("live","cache","snapshot","demo"))' jobs.json

      - name: Server log
        if: always()
        run: cat server.log || true

  # External links (scripts/external-links.js; docs/process/devops.md decision
  # 66). GitHub's runners can reach the internet; the dev sandbox can't. One run
  # per push/PR, outside the Node matrix. Broken links are listed in the step
  # summary. Job postings close daily, so the job-URL and doc-URL steps are
  # advisory; the site's own pages must answer, or CI fails.
  links:
    name: External links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      SITE_URL: ${{ vars.SITE_URL || 'https://alvations.github.io/melon-seek/' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # 20 Apply URLs per built-in company, seeded by the UTC date (reruns on
      # the same day pick the same jobs; the seed is in the summary). Source:
      # the deployed site's built lists (a CI build has no snapshots, so its
      # lists are demo data with synthetic URLs).
      - name: Job Apply URLs (advisory)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/external-links.js --jobs "$SITE_URL" --per-company 20 --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Doc URLs in README.md and docs/**/*.md (advisory)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/external-links.js --docs --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Advisory here: CI starts on the same push as the Pages deploy, so it races it and can
      # catch the old site, or the branch build's holding page (repo-root index.html), mid-deploy.
      # The hard live-site gate is pages.yml's post-deploy check (check-site.sh) after the deploy.
      - name: Site pages (advisory; pages.yml's post-deploy check is the gate)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: node scripts/external-links.js --site --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
"
  }
}

ABOUT THE JOB

Discovery is building an expeditionary force: a team of engineers who want to solve difficult problems and who navigate unfamiliar territory as an operating standard. As a Discovery engineer, you pick up a concept nobody has proven and build the analysis or prototype that tests it to get to an answer. Whether you spend your time working on hard problems on our autonomy stack, acoustic sensor analysis, or battle space management, we tackle every challenge the same way: by questioning assumptions and building our way to the answer.

We are focused on taking AI models from research into production—onto classified platforms and edge hardware where they have to perform reliably in the real world. As our model portfolio and classified work grow, rigorous, repeatable evaluation of how these models actually perform has become mission-critical.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop Test Scenarios Simulation Environments: Develop comprehensive test scenarios, and simulation environments to assess agentic AI performance in classified simulations.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a DFx Engineer to support design for manufacturability, assembly, and cost analysis across our avionics, electronics, wiring,and harnessing subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — and is an excellent opportunity for an early-career engineer to develop deep expertise in how design decisions impact producibility, supplier selection, and unit cost.

Working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, you will learn to evaluate designs through the lenses of manufacturability, assembly, and cost — the three factors that determine whether hardware can be produced at rate, by a qualified supplier, at an affordable price point. You will work alongside subject matter expert (SME) manufacturing engineers and design engineers, building the technical judgment and cross-functional relationships that make DFx effective.

You will also gain hands-on exposure to contract manufacturer evaluation and qualification — visiting supplier facilities, participating in process assessments, and learning how to match supplier capabilities to production requirements. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, and program teams in addition to ME and DE. You will grow quickly here — our programs move fast, the hardware is real, and the impact of your work shows up on the production floor and in the cost model.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Support DFx analysis across avionics, electronics, wiring, and harnessing subsystems for AD&S programs, working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, with a focus on manufacturability, assembly, and cost.
  • Participate in structured DFM/DFA/DFC reviews at key design milestones, learning and applying the scoring methodology to identify producibility and cost risks and recommend design changes.
  • Work with SME manufacturing engineers and design engineers to provide manufacturing and cost feedback on designs, learning to translate constraints into actionable recommendations.
  • Support the evaluation and qualification of contract manufacturers — participating in facility reviews, process audits, and capability assessments under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Help build and maintain should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for electronics and harnessing assemblies.
  • Help develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to electronics manufacturing processes including SMT, wave/selective solder, conformal coating, potting, wire harness fabrication, and box-build assembly.
  • Analyze designs across key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, cost structure, adherence to specification, process capability, and technology maturity — contributing to risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Work with supply chain to understand how DFx requirements connect to sourcing strategy and supplier selection.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to understand how DFx findings translate into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.
  • Spend time on the production floor and at supplier sites to build firsthand understanding of how electronics and harnesses are manufactured.
  • Contribute to the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials.
  • Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5 years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, or a related role with exposure to electronics, avionics, wiring, or harnessing. Co-op, internship, or capstone project experience in a manufacturing environment counts.
  • Foundational knowledge of electronics and/or harnessing manufacturing processes: SMT, soldering, conformal coating, wire harness fabrication, or electromechanical assembly.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics, PCB layouts, and harness drawings with an eye toward producibility.
  • Interest in understanding manufacturing cost drivers and how design decisions impact unit cost.
  • Familiarity with IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620) or a willingness to learn and apply them quickly.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to engage directly with design engineers, manufacturing engineers, quality, supply chain, and operations — cross-functional collaboration is the core of this job, not a side task.
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced environment across multiple programs simultaneously.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and a drive to understand how things are actually built and what they cost to produce. Personal experience physically building or working on hardware (soldering, harness build, assembly, personal projects) is a strong plus.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • Self-motivated and proactive — you take initiative, ask good questions, and close the loop on what you commit to.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Master's degree in Engineering or a related field.
  • Internship or co-op experience in aerospace or defense electronics manufacturing.
  • Exposure to DFM/DFA review processes, producibility engineering, or cost analysis.
  • Familiarity with AS9100 or similar quality management systems.
  • Experience visiting or evaluating manufacturing suppliers in any capacity.
  • Proficiency in ECAD tools (Altium, KiCad, or similar) sufficient to navigate and review designs.
  • Experience with data analysis, cost modeling, or presentation development.
  • Appropriate clearance classification & eligibility.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Industrial Security team is a highly specialized security team responsible for managing Anduril’s cleared personnel, classified programs, and secure facilities. We operate at the intersection of cutting-edge defense technology and stringent security requirements, ensuring the integrity and protection of national security. Our team is composed of experts in security management, compliance, risk assessment, and physical security, dedicated to upholding the highest standards of security in support of national and international defense initiatives while providing the best customer service, both within Anduril and externally.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Facility Security Officer to join our rapidly growing team at our McHenry, MS location. The Facility Security Officer (FSO) is responsible for implementing and directing the industrial security program and ensuring company and customer security requirements are met. Candidates will interface with all levels of personnel and government management personnel to ensure contract security compliance with 32 CFR Part 117, the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), Contract Security Classification Specification (DD Form 254), DoD Manual 5100.76- Physical Security of Sensitive Arms, Ammunitions, and Explosives (AA&E), and Security Classification Guides (SCGs). The position requires a self-motivated candidate that can work in an independent or team environment. The candidate will be required to work with the Anduril FSO team in developing and implementing processes and procedures for the department and site, conduct security self-inspections, expand our classified footprint, apply risk mitigation methodologies, support customer assessments, and implement security measures to meet requirements.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Administer day-to-day security programs in compliance with 32 CFR Part 117, Security Classification Guides, and program guidance: personnel processing, program reviews, document control system, inventories, audits & self-inspections, violation investigations & reports, receipt/dispatch/destruction/mail logs, visit certs, and other requirements at the McHenry location.
  • Administer contract requirements and policy requirements of the DoD Manual 5100.76, Physical Security of Sensitive Conventional Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E).
  • Act as a liaison to the Special Programs Security team.
  • Provide guidance to employees and recommend modifications to operations policies or procedures
  • Work with a variety of stakeholders and collaborators including but not limited to: Program Management, Classified IT, Classified Networks/Mission Assurance, Insider Threat and Counterintelligence, Physical Security, Legal
  • Act as security point person for Open Storage Area (OSA) buildout coordination from proposal through accreditation.
  • Maintain and update NISS for your Operating Location
  • Coordinate, conduct, and prepare for Security Vulnerability Assessments (SVA), annual self-inspections, and other local inspections as required. Prepare and present reports with appropriate corrective actions delineated.
  • Send and receive collateral visit requests; oversee and provide facility badge access.

This position is looking for a highly motivated flight test engineer with emphasis in developmental test of new aircraft weapon and missile systems. You will work closely with the program test leadership, and a wide spectrum of cross-departments team members, solving hard problems and changing the industry forever. The role will be responsible for planning, coordination, execution and reporting on all facets of the test program.

The Test and Evaluation team at Anduril works across the entire spectrum of products and business lines, as well as all flight operations and test range management. Our team conducts full system level development testing, new production acceptance testing, sub-component qualification testing and much more. In short, if it involves test, we support it. If you are interested in working in an extremely innovative and fast paced environment, where your work directly makes an impact and difference in the products that are fielded, this a fantastic opportunity.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Plan and execute system level T&E of hardware and software with emphasis placed on resource planning, conducting ground and flight test, initial issue investigation, and process improvement/development.
  • Act as lead or supporting test engineer for missile or weapon systems to include development, certification and integration test of subsystems to the AUR configuration.
  • Collect test data and perform initial data analysis for the system under test.
  • Work closely with program management and other engineering departments to develop requirements, and discuss test results to include collected data and observations.
  • Assist in the creation of developmental test plans, test cards, technical updates and test reports.
  • Conduct ground and flight testing at private and government-owned test ranges.
  • Work in a safe manner in accordance with established operating procedures and standard practices.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • A bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution. May substitute equivalent engineering experience in lieu of education.
  • 3+ years of experience as test conductor/director for developmental aircraft, weapons, or missile systems.
  • Must have a good understanding of engineering concepts, principles, codes, and theory; experience demonstrating a broad application of those concepts; and expanding knowledge of principles, concepts, theory, and practices in related technical specialties.
  • Test engineering experience working with developmental weapon or missile systems on manned and/or unmanned aircraft to include requirements development, planning, execution, and reporting.
  • Previous experience with and/or current working knowledge of MIL-STD-8591, MIL-STD-2088, MIL-STD-1553, MIL-STD-1760, AS8775, AS5653, etc.
  • Experience integrating and conducting test with suspension, arming, and release equipment.
  • Previous expertise and working knowledge of the National Airspace System and UAS operating rules and regulations thereof.
  • Must possess the ability to understand new concepts quickly; apply them accurately; organize, schedule, and coordinate work phases; and, determine the appropriate approach at the task level or, with assistance, at the project level to provide solutions to a range of complex problems.
  • Strong computer and documentation experience.
  • Must have strong communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team; able to perform complex tasks in one or more engineering areas.
  • Able to work extended hours as required.
  • Ability to travel as required for test planning and execution.
  • Bias for action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret-Level security clearance.
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience working with the Department of Defense (DoD).
  • Prior experience with software code/script building using programming languages such as Go, Java, C++, Python, JavaScript, etc.
  • Prior experience with Linux based systems and command line.
  • Working Knowledge with COTs Small UAS autopilot and mission planning software.
  • Experience working with manned aircraft personnel and familiar with aviation terminology.
  • Experience with weapon or tactical datalinks.
  • Experience with multiple different propulsion systems to include air and non-air breathing.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, Fuel Systems to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to own integration and test of the fuel system for Omen, an advanced Group 3 VTOL tail-sitting aircraft. This individual will own fuel system integration testing across increasingly mature environments, from component bench tests through full vehicle ground test, and will support the vehicle-level mass properties test program by defining and planning the fuel-system-specific inputs needed to account for the effects of fuel state and vehicle orientation on weight, center of gravity, and moments of inertia. This is a hands-on, build-and-run role suited to someone who wants to own a test campaign end to end: requirements, fixturing, execution, and reporting.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own all fuel system integration and test activities from component bench tests through full vehicle ground test, including tanks, pumps, valves, fluid lines, sensors, and dispense sequencing, developing right-sized test plans and efficiently capturing and reporting learnings as inputs to design
  • Define and plan the fuel-system-specific requirements, measurement approach, and instrumentation needed to characterize vehicle weight, center of gravity, and moments of inertia, supporting the vehicle mass properties test program across fuel states and vehicle orientations
  • Develop and execute a fuel system orientation test program capturing fuel flow behavior, pump performance, and tank dispense sequencing across multiple vehicle orientations
  • Define fixturing, tooling, and test setup requirements for fuel system bench and vehicle-level orientation testing, partnering with fabrication and ground support teams on buildup of long-lead hardware
  • Coordinate with structures/loads and systems engineering teams to define the load cases and vehicle configurations required to support orientation and mass properties testing
  • Feed mass properties test results into vehicle models and hand off clean data to support downstream ground vibration testing (GVT) and flight dynamics work
  • Focus on the safety of integration environments, ensuring that potential harm to team members is eliminated by design, with particular attention to fuel/hazardous fluid handling and heavy-lift or orientation-change operations
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of fuel system integration environments and test fixtures
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test of prototype and production representative systems

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical, Aerospace, Systems, or related engineering discipline
  • 5+ years experience in integration and test of fluid/fuel systems, and/or aircraft mass properties (weight and balance) test programs
  • Experience with aircraft or vehicle mass properties measurement techniques (e.g., weight and balance, moment of inertia measurement via pendulum/swing or similar methods) and associated instrumentation
  • Experience with fuel or fluid system components (tanks, pumps, valves, fluid lines, and associated sensors) and fluid system test setups
  • Experience defining fixturing and test setup requirements for fluid system rigs or multi-orientation ground testing
  • Adept at working safely with fuel, hazardous fluids, and pressurized systems
  • Strong test engineering foundation — DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, and fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial)
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal and written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with tail-sitter, VTOL, or unconventional aircraft configurations where fuel state and vehicle orientation significantly impact performance and mass properties.
  • Familiarity with autonomous air vehicle (AAV) or UAS integration environments, particularly Group 3 platforms operating in runway-independent or shipboard contexts.
  • Experience feeding test data into vehicle-level models for downstream analysis such as ground vibration testing (GVT) or flight dynamics characterization.
  • Exposure to production-representative test campaigns, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) processes and configuration control in a rapid-iteration hardware development environment.

Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. You will lead the planning, integration, and execution of flight test activities using surrogate platforms, including crewed test-beds with representative payload pods, full-size mock-ups, and powertrain rigs to characterize and demonstrate subsystem performance in representative environments before integration into air vehicles.   • Own surrogate platform test activities including crewed carry/representative pod configurations, full-size mock-ups (with partial or full system integration) and powertrain rigs

  • Lead integration of Vehicle and Mission System components onto surrogate platforms for characterization in representative flight envelopes (altitude, airspeed, temperature, vibration)
  • Evolve and demonstrate Support System design with full-size mock-ups
  • Coordinate crewed surrogate operations including pod integration, instrumentation, pre-flight checks, and mission planning
  • Support subscale UAS flight operations for software and subsystem development teams
  • Plan and execute powertrain rig operations for powertrain and control system integration testing
  • Ensure safety of airborne test environments through structured hazard identification and risk management
  • Coordinate test range access, airspace approvals, spectrum approvals, and operational permissions across CONUS and UAE locations
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of surrogate test assets and installed instrumentation

  • 5+ years experience in flight test operations, preferably with uncrewed or autonomous air systems (Group 3 or larger)
  • Experience integrating subsystems, payloads, and flight test instrumentation (FTI) onto flight platforms, including telemetry and real-time monitoring
  • Knowledge of airspace management, flight test safety and test range operations
  • Adept at working safely with high voltage systems, including integration, checkout and test
  • Strong test engineering foundation — DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial), and command line interface (CLI)

  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

  • Experience with surrogate or test-bed aircraft operations, including crewed platforms carrying representative payload pods or instrumented mock-ups for subsystem characterization prior to integration onto target vehicles.

  • Experience coordinating test range access, airspace approvals, and spectrum authorizations across multiple sites, including OCONUS locations.
  • Background in subscale UAS flight operations supporting rapid software and subsystem development cycles, with an emphasis on feeding test results directly back into design iteration

ABOUT THE TEAM

Omen is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that packs the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger airplanes into a novel runway-independent Group 3 platform. Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. Omen is the first tail-sitter aircraft with a mass-production contract, with an order of 50 systems representing a decisive investment that anchors production and accelerates the development of future systems.


ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, Electrical Systems to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to own integration and test of electrical systems for Omen, an advanced Group 3 VTOL tail-sitting aircraft. This individual will own integration and test activities across electrical systems including avionics, power systems, actuator and motor controls, mission systems, networking, sensors, and harnessing. This is a hands-on, build-and-run role suited to someone who wants to own a test campaign end to end: requirements, tooling, execution, and reporting.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support bring-up, functional checkout, and troubleshooting of electrical hardware across multiple vehicle systems
  • Develop and execute right-sized test plans and procedures for electrical component and subsystem integration
  • Coordinate with design engineers across disciplines (electrical, GNC, mission systems, flight software) to burn-down design risks and demonstrate system maturity
  • Use standard electrical test instrumentation (multimeter, oscilloscope, logic analyzer, spectrum and network analyzer) to characterize hardware and diagnose failures
  • Write and maintain test scripts and tooling (Python or similar) to automate data capture, sequencing, and reporting
  • Follow and maintain safety protocols for high voltage and stored energy hazards during integration and test activities
  • Maintain configuration control records for test hardware, tooling, and firmware/software versions
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test activities for prototype and production representative system

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or related engineering discipline
  • 1+ years of experience in integration and test, electrical hardware bring-up, or embedded systems/firmware work with hands-on hardware validation
  • Demonstrated hands-on proficiency with multimeters, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers
  • Working software/firmware literacy (C, Python, or similar) sufficient to read embedded code, write test scripts, and reason through firmware behavior during hardware debug
  • Comfort working across more than one electrical domain (power electronics, controls, communications)
  • Fluency in at least one common communication protocol (CAN, Ethernet, or Serial)
  • Willingness and demonstrated aptitude to work safely with high voltage systems (400V+) under supervision
  • Basic EMI/EMC fluency (conducted/radiated susceptibility or emissions)
  • Wiring harness design, sizing, or fabrication experience
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, with clear verbal and written communication skills
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense industry background not required, but genuine interest in the mission is
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with electrical system integration on aerospace or UAS platforms, particularly involving avionics, actuator controls, and power distribution in space-constrained, weight-sensitive environments.
  • Familiarity with EMI/EMC testing and mitigation techniques in integrated vehicle environments, including conducted and radiated emissions troubleshooting on densely packaged systems.
  • Experience automating test workflows end to end — from data acquisition and sequencing through automated report generation — using Python or similar scripting languages.
  • Exposure to VTOL, tail-sitter, or unconventional aircraft architectures where electrical system behavior varies significantly across flight modes and vehicle orientations

$112,000—$149,000 USD

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, specializing in Powertrain, to join the Omen team at our Costa Mesa HQ. Omen is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that packs the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger airplanes into a novel runway-independent Group 3 platform. Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. Omen is the first tail-sitter aircraft with a mass-production contract, with an order of 50 systems representing a decisive investment that anchors production and accelerates the development of future systems.

You will plan and execute Powertrain integration and test activities across increasingly mature environments, from discrete bench tests through Hardware In Lab (HIL), Hardware In The Loop (HITL), surrogate platforms, and flight test. The Powertrain scope encompasses electric machines, inverters, gearboxes, battery modules, battery management systems (BMS), high voltage distribution, powertrain controllers, power conditioning, and associated thermal management systems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will own component and subsystem test campaigns end to end and contribute to vehicle-level campaigns led by senior engineering. All of this in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Plan and execute powertrain (propulsion drive, battery, hybrid management) test activities across increasingly mature integration environments, owning individual test campaigns end to end
  • Develop, review, and execute right-sized test plans for Powertrain component and subsystem integration, efficiently capturing and reporting learnings, and making recommendations as inputs to design
  • Perform integration, bring-up, and characterization of electric machines, inverters, gearboxes, battery modules, BMS, high voltage distribution, powertrain controllers, and power conditioning components
  • Support development and operation of the Powertrain surrogate for integrated powertrain characterization and control tuning
  • Focus on the safety of integration environments, ensuring that potential harm to team members is eliminated by design, with particular attention to high voltage and stored energy hazards
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of Powertrain integration environments
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test of prototype and production representative systems

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor degree or higher in Electrical, Mechatronics, Mechanical, Aerospace, Systems or aviation related technical engineering discipline
  • 3-5 years experience in integration and test of hybrid powertrain or high voltage electric drive systems
  • Working knowledge of high voltage electric drive systems including motors/generators, inverters, and power electronics
  • Hands-on experience with powertrain dynamometer testing, motor characterization, or gearbox acceptance testing
  • Adept at working safely with high voltage systems (400V+), including integration, checkout, test, and safe discharge procedures
  • Strong test engineering foundation - DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial), and command line interface (CLI)
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal and written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australi

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with hybrid-electric or full-electric propulsion systems in aerospace or UAS applications, particularly platforms where power-to-weight ratio and thermal constraints are critical design drivers.
  • Familiarity with battery management system (BMS) integration, battery module characterization, and safe handling of lithium-based energy storage systems in test environments.
  • Experience developing or operating Hardware In the Loop (HITL) or surrogate test platforms for powertrain control tuning and integrated system validation.
  • Exposure to rapid-iteration hardware development environments with short design-to-flight timelines, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and flight test support for prototype systems.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Lead Electrical Engineer to join our team in Costa Mesa, California. You will work closely with the program leadership and a wide spectrum of cross-departments as part of a team focused on solving hard problems and changing the industry forever. In this role you will be responsible for designing and supporting the integration of various subsystems, supporting testing efforts, and ensuring overall system performance meets the required specifications and standards. Join our dynamic team and help us build the next generation of autonomous flight systems.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Full cycle PCB design including collecting requirements, schematic design, component selection, supervision or completion of layout, bring-up, test, debug and system integration
  • Troubleshoot issues that span the electrical and software boundaries, with solid skills using both lab equipment (Oscilloscopes, DMM, etc.) and basic software debugging tools
  • Development of payloads and subsystems (sensors, payload interfaces, power management, and networking)
  • Develop system interconnect diagrams and define wire harnesses that connect electronic equipment within a subsystem
  • Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products
  • Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments and customer operated hardware
  • Conduct peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews
  • Design and support the integration & testing of an rotorcraft system through TRLs 3-8.
  • Conduct vehicle platform system design & analysis as required by your supported program or effort
  • Conduct design reviews, perform requirements analysis, and plan system verification to ensure compliance with project goals and industry standards
  • Work within a dynamic team of multidisciplinary engineers and specialists throughout the life of product design, integration, and test effort

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 5+ years of experience designing, testing, and troubleshooting complex board designs
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits.
  • Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, thermal chambers, current-probes, and automation of tests.
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, etc.
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies.
  • Familiarity with software development processes and tools such as git, Github, JIRA, etc
  • Comfortable with a variety of electronic CAD tools (Altium preferred, Eagle and others acceptable)
  • Experience in design for signal integrity / power integrity
  • Experience with battery systems and ability to support alternate battery systems design
  • Experience with high reliability systems
  • Experience with radio frequency-based systems
  • Experience with rapid payload/sensor integration
  • Experience in designing and integrating high power electronics
  • Experience in fieldable system design
  • Comfortable in conducting worst case circuit or uncertainty analysis
  • High-ownership and a bias toward action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel 25% with potential surges above 25%

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience designing electrical and power systems for autonomous rotorcraft.
  • Experience with battery systems both primary and secondary chemistries.
  • Experience with High Voltage Power Electronics.
  • Experience with inverters and high power electric motors.
  • Understanding of MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-810G
  • Outstanding leadership and interpersonal skills
  • Familiarity with running a qualification campaign for flight hardware
  • Familiarity with designing for rugged environments
  • Experience with electro-mechanical and electrical design concepts
  • Experience with Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly, etc.

$146,000—$194,000 USD

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Legal Counsel to join our rapidly growing team in Washington, DC |Costa Mesa, CA | Ashville, OH to support Anduril’s Frontier Systems Division, Air Defense and Counter-Intrusion Business Lines, with a focus on the full spectrum of United States government contracts. This includes: providing legal oversight to proposals, procurement, advising on data rights and contract structures, giving legal guidance to existing business areas, and crafting legal and business strategies. This role will partner closely with customers, outside counsel, and business partners across the organization to support business development and legal operations.

Anduril is a fast-growing company at the early stages of growth. Consistent with this fast growth, members of Anduril’s Legal Team must be resourceful, creative, and eager to take ownership of complex matters. The Legal Counsel-Government Contracts role will require creativity and resourcefulness to navigate the US Government’s complex procurement and compliance rules, with a singular focus on helping Anduril deploy its path-making technology into operational settings for the United States and its allies. In addition to helping capture and execute new government deals, you will work on all other aspects of Anduril’s business, from negotiating license and services agreements, to bid protests and litigation, to handling intellectual property, compliance, and employment matters. Experience across all of these areas is not expected, but a willingness to learn and adapt is.

Our team is passionate about the law and policy of defense technology and you should have an independent interest in the key issues in this field. Anduril fosters a diverse, collaborative, culture with tremendous opportunities for ownership and professional growth.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Be a key member of Anduril’s small, dynamic Legal Team.
  • Drive customer growth by executing new government contracts and growing existing ones. Use your expertise in federal procurement law to help the Business Development, Proposal, and Engineering Teams efficiently capture new contracts, grow existing contracts, and set up follow-on opportunities for future contracts. Assist in the strategy development for new business.
  • Manage relationships with procurement office representatives at Government agencies. High-trust professional relationships with Government contracting and procurement offices are critical to Anduril’s continued success, and you will be called upon to develop and foster these relationships throughout your tenure.
  • Provide legal counsel and day-to-day management of the entire acquisitions lifecycle. Oversee and evaluate major proposals, monitor large contracts, lead or assist in key negotiations, resolve performance issues, identify risks and mitigations, and ensure compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
  • Work on all legal aspects of Anduril’s business, from negotiating license and services agreements, to bid protests and litigation, to handling deal-related intellectual property, compliance, and employment matters. You will represent the legal team in relationships with outside counsel, vendors, engineers, executives, customers, and regulators.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of work on US Government contracts matters, preferably with a law firm or in-house at a government contractor 
  • A solid understanding of the government procurement process; particularly contract vehicles and types, including non-traditional and CAS coverage, software acquisition approaches, and data rights issues
  • The judgment and initiative required to own multiple projects from end-to-end, whether guiding the Business Development Team through the lifecycle of a deal or handling unexpected legal issues that may arise in defense or start-up companies
  • Strong communication, writing, and interpersonal skills.

Anduril’s Manufacturing Operations Team is seeking an Asset Reliability Manufacturing Manager to join our team. The Production Maintenance team is responsible for helping scale production at Anduril and ensuring maximum equipment uptime, a world class preventative maintenance program, and supporting line commissioning of our growing production landscape.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Asset Reliability Manufacturing Manager is responsible for leading, managing, and developing the maintenance team to ensure the reliable operation of all production equipment and facilities. This role is critical in maximizing equipment uptime, optimizing maintenance costs, ensuring a safe working environment, and driving continuous improvement initiatives within the manufacturing facility. The manager will develop and implement robust preventive and predictive maintenance programs, manage spare parts inventory, and work collaboratively with production, engineering, and quality teams to achieve operational excellence.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Team Leadership & Development:
    • Recruit, train, mentor, and supervise a team of maintenance specialists (electrical, mechanical, PLC, etc.).
    • Conduct performance reviews, provide constructive feedback, and identify professional development opportunities for team members.
    • Develop and manage work schedules, assignments, and priorities for the maintenance team to ensure adequate coverage and efficient workflow.
    • Foster a strong safety culture within the maintenance department, ensuring adherence to all safety policies and procedures (e.g., LOTO, confined space, hot work).
  • Maintenance Operations Management:
    • Develop, implement, and continuously improve comprehensive Preventive Maintenance (PM) and Predictive Maintenance (PdM) programs to minimize downtime and extend equipment life.
    • Oversee all reactive maintenance activities, ensuring prompt and effective troubleshooting and repair of production equipment breakdowns.
    • Utilize and optimize the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) for work order generation, tracking, scheduling, and historical data analysis.
    • Manage spare parts inventory, ensuring critical spares are available while optimizing inventory levels and costs.
    • Troubleshoot complex mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic issues on various production machinery.
  • Strategic Planning & Continuous Improvement:
    • Analyze maintenance data (e.g., downtime, MTBF, MTTR, OEE) to identify root causes of equipment failures and implement corrective actions.
    • Drive continuous improvement initiatives (e.g., Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma principles) within maintenance to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and improve equipment reliability.
    • Participate in the planning and execution of capital projects related to new equipment installations, upgrades, and facility improvements.
    • Stay abreast of new maintenance technologies and best practices to continually improve departmental performance.
  • Collaboration & Communication:
    • Collaborate closely with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Safety departments to align maintenance activities with production schedules and overall plant objectives.
    • Communicate maintenance status, schedules, and issues effectively to all relevant stakeholders.
    • Manage relationships with external vendors, contractors, and service providers for specialized maintenance tasks or equipment support.
  • Budget & Resource Management:
    • Develop and manage the annual maintenance budget, including expenditures for labor, parts, external services, and capital improvements.
    • Monitor and control maintenance costs, seeking opportunities for cost reduction without compromising quality or reliability.
    • Ensure proper allocation and utilization of maintenance resources.
  • Compliance & Safety:
    • Ensure all maintenance activities comply with company policies, local, state, and federal regulations (e.g., OSHA, EPA).
    • Participate in safety audits and incident investigations, implementing corrective actions as needed.
    • Maintain accurate records of all maintenance activities, inspections, and safety compliance.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in a manufacturing maintenance role.
  • At least 3-5 years of experience in a maintenance leadership or supervisory position, preferably in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Proven experience implementing and managing PM/PdM programs.
  • Strong track record of improving equipment reliability and reducing downtime.
  • Proficiency with CMMS software.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and P&IDs.
  • Knowledge of instrumentation and calibration techniques.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, climb, and lift up to 50 pounds regularly.
  • Ability to work in various environmental conditions common in a manufacturing plant (e.g., noise, varying temperatures, dust).
  • Ability to work extended hours, including occasional nights, weekends, or holidays, as needed.
  • Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses, hearing protection, safety shoes, etc.
  • Strong knowledge of industrial electrical systems (up to 480V), PLCs (e.g., Allen-Bradley, Siemens), VFDs, and motor controls.
  • Expertise in mechanical systems, including hydraulics, pneumatics, pumps, conveyors, gearboxes, and power transmission.

ABOUT THE JOB

In this role, you will own the end-to-end mechanical development of novel, first-of-type Support Systems and Ground Servicing Equipment (GSE). You will take hardware from blank-sheet concept through detailed CAD, rapid prototyping, dynamic mechanism design, and production. Your scope spans launch and recovery systems, ruggedized expeditionary transport equipment, automated fueling and charging interfaces, and precision payload handling devices. We operate in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly architect the physical product and move at the velocity required to field clean-sheet mechanical designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Architect, model, and build novel Support Systems and Ground Servicing Equipment (GSE)—driving hardware from blank-sheet concept down-selection through CAD, physical prototyping, and fielded customer demonstrations.
  • Rapidly develop full-scale mechanical mock-ups, functional prototypes, and vehicle interface elements to iteratively de-risk mechanical handling, launch, and recovery concepts.
  • Design and execute lean, right-sized test plans to validate new mechanisms, efficiently capturing empirical learnings to drive immediate CAD and hardware design revisions.
  • Design ruggedized systems tailored for austere land and dynamic maritime conditions, ensuring field survivability, high reliability, and intuitive human factors.
  • Apply rigorous engineering practices to design out physical hazards at the component level (leveraging MIL-STD-882E principles), establishing both built-in mechanical safeguards and streamlined Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Partner closely with Airframe, Powertrain, and Mission Systems teams to ensure vehicle-to-ground mechanical, electrical, and fluid interfaces are seamlessly integrated.
  • Establish and maintain baseline configuration control across fast-evolving prototype builds, test fixtures, and field-trial assets.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 3+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience owning the design, analysis, build, and functional test of complex physical hardware or mechanisms.
  • Strong foundation in first-principles mechanical design, structural packaging, material selection (metals, composites, hardware), and 3D CAD modeling.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with system safety practices, hazard assessments, and risk mitigation methodologies (e.g., MIL-STD-882E or equivalent industrial standards).
  • Hands-on mechanical aptitude with an iterative, prototype-to-learn mindset and a high bias for action in fast-paced environments.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience developing Ground Support Equipment (GSE), launch/recovery mechanisms, mobile heavy equipment, or transport and packaging solutions for aerospace or defense systems.
  • Operational experience in land or maritime expeditionary environments—supporting flight line operations, field maintenance, or complex tactical deployments.
  • Familiarity with high-voltage battery systems, electric powertrains, or fluid/fueling delivery systems.
  • Hands-on fabrication, trade, machining, or aircraft mechanic experience (A&P license or military maintenance MOS/AFSC).
  • Prior military service or defense contracting background with unmanned aerial systems (UAS).

The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines. The team in London builds the Mission System and the autonomy that makes aircraft like Thunder work.

Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to join the Thunder team in our Costa Mesa office. The Maneuver Dominance (MD) Team at Anduril develops aerial robotic systems designed to operate in large coordinated teams in concert with ground maneuver forces.

Here you will work on core product development for unmanned rotorcraft and complex systems, including but not limited to design and development of a novel payload carriage and release system, analysis and testing of the system and it’s tooling design. The ideal candidate would be practical, hands-on and a self starter with high growth potential.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own and drive the physical design of the payload carriage and release for a novel aircraft type, overseeing the process from initial concept to low rate production.
  • Define requirements, propose possible solutions, and establish a methodology for evaluating and verifying mechanical systems. This will involve close collaboration with partner organizations, in both the UK and US.
  • Work in close partnership with other disciplines internal to Anduril to ensure the electrical, actuation, and mechanical systems collectively form a reliable, flexible, cost-effective system.
  • Spearhead design reviews, conduct analysis, build prototypes and design and implement hardware test plans.
  • Lead the enhancement of team tools, templates, processes, and standards.
  • Cultivate a vibrant, positive, dedicated and educational collaborative work environment.
  • Travel to test sites and vendors to support critical hardware demonstrations and development test activities as needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BEng, BSc, MEng, MSc or higher in mechanical or aerospace engineering, or equivalent work experience.
  • 4+ years in a technical engineering role in a professional aerospace setting, with demonstrated track record of successful stakeholder management, consensus building and successful project delivery.
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter and strong proficiency in CAD software with specific emphasis on rapid concepting and iteration of novel designs.
  • Strong technical knowledge in core engineering principles, including fundamental mechanics of composite and metallic materials, design, analysis, testing, and fabrication.
  • Deep understanding of load paths, design practices, and hand calculations to design robust structurally efficient assemblies.
  • An excellent communicator, experienced in report writing and the development and delivery of presentations across a range of settings.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with design and development of payload carriage and release systems.
  • Experience in systems integration during airframe assembly, particularly focusing on mechanical systems.
  • Experience in metrology verification methods and equipment used for aircraft assembly fixturing and part fabrication.
