Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. Anduril is seeking an experienced Power Controls Engineer to develop and implement advanced control algorithms for high-performance power electronic systems. We're looking for someone with deep expertise in control system modeling and simulation — particularly in Simulink and PLECS — who can take a controls concept from simulation through hardware validation. This individual will own the control architecture for DC/DC converters, inverters, and motor drives built around discrete SiC and GaN power stages, and will work closely with power hardware and firmware engineers to deliver tightly integrated, high-reliability systems for defense and aerospace applications.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Design, simulate, and validate closed-loop control algorithms for switch-mode power converters and inverters using Simulink and/or PLECS.
  • Controls for 3-phase AC systems, with and without a switched Neutral
  • Develop plant models and controller architectures (voltage-mode, current-mode, sensorless FOC, etc.) for multi-kW power stages utilizing discrete SiC and GaN FETs.
  • Perform stability analysis, loop shaping, and compensator design to meet transient response, efficiency, and EMI targets.
  • Collaborate with power hardware engineers on gate drive tuning, dead-time optimization, and switching-loss characterization of wide-bandgap devices.
  • Support model-based code generation workflows and work with firmware engineers to translate control designs into embedded implementations.
  • Define and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and power-hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) test plans to validate control performance against system requirements.
  • Contribute to trade studies on converter topology, modulation strategy, and control bandwidth as they relate to size, weight, power, and thermal constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience designing and tuning digital control loops for power electronic converters (DC/DC, DC/AC, or motor drives).
  • Proficiency in Simulink and/or PLECS for control system modeling, simulation, and analysis.
  • Strong foundation in control theory — z-domain and s-domain design, bode analysis, state-space methods, and discrete-time implementation considerations.
  • Hands-on experience with discrete SiC and/or GaN FET-based power stages in the multi-kW range.
  • Familiarity with military or aerospace environments and standards such as MIL-STD-461, 464, 810, or DO-160.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MS/PhD with a focus in power electronics controls or control systems.
  • Experience writing embedded firmware (C/C++) for microcontrollers or DSPs used in power converter control (e.g., TI C2000, STM32).
  • Familiarity with auto-code generation from Simulink (Embedded Coder) or similar model-based design toolchains.
  • Experience with real-time HIL platforms (e.g., Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT).
  • Knowledge of advanced modulation techniques (SVM, DPWM) and their impact on switching losses in wide-bandgap devices.
  • Design-for-Reliability practices including DFMEA.
  • Experience with EMI mitigation strategies at the controls and layout level.

About the Role

Anduril Industries is building next-generation defense technology to protect the United States and its allies. We are looking for Production Technicians to join our Rocket Motor Systems manufacturing team. In this role, you will perform hands-on final assembly operations on solid rocket motors and their subassemblies, working in a fast-paced production environment where precision, safety, and teamwork are paramount.

You do not need prior experience with solid rocket motors or energetic materials to be successful here — we will train you. What matters most is that you bring a strong safety mindset, a willingness to learn, the technical aptitude to master detailed procedures, and the ability to work collaboratively with your team.

Core Responsibilities

  • Perform solid rocket motor final assembly operations including mandrel extraction, nozzle installation, and igniter assembly integration per detailed work instructions
  • Execute igniter subassembly build-up, including component preparation, epoxy application, and curing processes
  • Conduct motor marking, labeling, and serialization in accordance with configuration control requirements
  • Perform leak check and pressure testing of completed motor assemblies using calibrated test equipment
  • Complete pack-out and preparation of finished motors for storage or shipment, ensuring compliance with packaging and handling specifications
  • Maintain accurate and thorough records of all assembly operations, inspections, and test results in the production tracking system
  • Participate in daily production stand-ups, communicate status and blockers, and coordinate handoffs between shifts or stations

Safety & Compliance

  • Solid propellant and other energetic materials are exceptionally dangerous if mishandled — adhere strictly to all safety protocols, standard operating procedures, and explosive safety requirements at all times with zero tolerance for deviation
  • Maintain housekeeping and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) control standards in all work areas
  • Identify and escalate safety concerns, near-misses, and hazards immediately through established reporting channels
  • Use required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) correctly and consistently
  • Support and participate in safety audits, process hazard analyses, and continuous improvement initiatives

What We're Looking For

We hire for mindset and aptitude. If you've built things with your hands — whether in a factory, a shop, the military, or your own garage — and you take pride in doing precise, careful work, we want to hear from you.

Required

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Demonstrated safety-first mindset — you stop the line when something doesn't look right
  • Ability to follow detailed written and visual work instructions with precision and consistency
  • Moderate to high mechanical aptitude: comfortable working with hand tools, torque wrenches, fixtures, and small components
  • Strong attention to detail and quality — you catch your own mistakes before they move downstream
  • Team-oriented attitude with clear, direct communication skills
  • Coachable and self-aware — you seek feedback, absorb it, and apply it
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs and stand for extended periods
  • Willingness to work in environments with energetic materials after completing required training and certification
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance (U.S. citizenship required)
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an ATF Explosives "Employee Possessor" license

Preferred

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, automotive, or other precision manufacturing environments
  • Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, or equivalent aerospace quality management systems
  • Experience working with adhesives, sealants, epoxies, or potting compounds
  • Military service or experience in an environment with strict procedural discipline
  • Experience with calibrated measurement tools (micrometers, calipers, pin gauges, etc.)
  • Lean manufacturing, 5S, or continuous improvement experience

  • Mission-driven work — what you build matters for national security
  • A team culture that values safety, ownership, and getting better every day
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and benefits
  • Hands-on training and career growth pathways into senior technician, lead, and supervisory roles
  • The opportunity to build a production operation from the ground up alongside a tight-knit team

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maritime team at Anduril builds world-class autonomous maritime platforms - undersea and surface vehicles and systems and seabed sensors. The team is responsible for taking products like Dive-LD, Dive-XL, Copperhead, and Seabed Sentry from concept to operational systems. As part of this team, your role will involve building the Product Operations function within a larger deployment and sustainment group. We work in close coordination with specialist teams including engineering, program management, and field operations to ensure successful employment of these products and to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Operations Technical Specialist for Maritime, you will play an important role in ensuring the reliability and readiness of Anduril’s Maritime products. This family of intelligent, autonomous undersea systems work together to develop unmatched situational awareness, precision engagement, and scalable maritime dominance. You will be an integral piece to ensuring that Anduril meets this mission for our customers. In this role you will help support end users by following and improving field failure discovery, mitigation, and resolution processes. You will help identify failure modes that contribute to root cause analysis, and you will help deploy fixes and manage the incident lifecycle across the Maritime fleet. This position requires a strong problem-solving mindset and hands-on expertise in debugging and resolving complex electromechanical issues. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own Incident Triage and Resolution: Be the first technical responder for issues across our global Maritime fleet. Dig into logs, telemetry, and system state to isolate faults across software, hardware, and network boundaries, and drive incidents to resolution.
  • Keep Customers Operational: When a full engineering fix will take time, identify and deploy interim mitigations and workarounds so customers can keep operating, while you manage the permanent fix in parallel.
  • Analyze Fleet Telemetry: Pull, query, and analyze fleet health data and logs yourself to spot trends, predict failures, and prevent issues before they reach the customer.
  • Drive Fleet Reliability: Partner directly with software and hardware engineering teams to turn real-world field data and failure analysis into permanent system upgrades and design improvements.
  • Bridge the Gap: Act as the critical translator between deeply technical engineering teams, business development stakeholders, and military operators in the field, explaining complex issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Help Build the Playbook: Turn what you learn on real incidents into repeatable triage procedures, diagnostic tooling, and runbooks that scale as the Maritime fleet grows worldwide.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, maritime, industrial, or field support).
  • Systems Troubleshooting: Hands-on experience troubleshooting software-intensive or networked systems in a production, field, or customer-facing environment (for example: reading logs, isolating faults across software and hardware boundaries, reproducing issues).
  • Command Line and Data Skills: Working proficiency with the Linux command line, and comfort analyzing data beyond spreadsheets (SQL, Python, bash, or similar).
  • Problem-Solving Mindset: A proven ability to work through ambiguous, unstructured technical problems from first principles, including the instinct to deploy interim mitigations and workarounds that keep customers operational while permanent fixes are engineered.
  • Self-Driven: Self-starter with a record of high achievement in multiple domains, who learns new systems by getting hands-on with them.
  • Technical Communication and Collaboration: Ability to communicate and coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across business, engineering, and sustainment functions, influencing decision-making, resource allocation, and operational planning.
  • Clearance and Location: Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance, and based in (or willing to relocate to) Quincy, MA.
  • Travel and Schedule: Ability to travel as needed to support customer operations and test events. Willingness to work non-standard hours and weekends as needed.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

  • Prior experience in a technical support escalation, field service engineering, site reliability (SRE), or customer-facing technical operations role.
  • Scripting experience (Python or bash) used to automate diagnostics, parse logs, or build internal tooling.
  • Familiarity with modern observability and ticketing tools (such as Grafana, Jira, or Git).
  • Experience with data platforms (such as Palantir Foundry) to conduct trend analysis and drive decisions.
  • Experience supporting and/or deploying undersea munitions, vehicles, or unmanned undersea systems (UUVs) as a DoD contractor or military end-user.
  • Familiarity with naval systems or operations, or prior military, DoD civilian, or government agency experience.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Quality Specialist to join our Product Quality Team in Ashville, Ohio. This Quality Specialist is a professional who is responsible for monitoring, inspecting and proposing measures to correct or improve the incoming inspection process to meet quality standards. They are a highly motivated team player who is willing to support a fast paced team environment. They will partner across the organization and help prioritize process and product quality issues that impact the effectiveness of the incoming materials inspection process as well as provide support for end of line supplier inspection. Also, as a quality specialist, they are responsible for monitoring, inspecting and proposing measures to correct or improve the final product quality standard. This role will focus on both product quality issues as well as process issues that impact efficiencies and completeness of of the inspection operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Manages the site Materials Review Board (MRB) process
  • Inspect to verify non-conforming parts at Santa Ana  Site and at Supplier Sites as assigned
  • Partner with Site Supplier Quality Engineering Organization  to support Supplier Quality Control
  • Assist in the root cause analysis
  • Assist in the dispositioning of non-conforming material and ensure the tasks are completed in a timely manner
  • Manage internal re-work to support dispositions
  • Ensure data collection and entry is accurate and complete for the MRB process
  • Communicate the process performance and quality issues to key stakeholders to drive improvements
  • Execute vendor return material authorization (RMA) with partnership between Warehouse and Buyers to ensure material leaves the MRB area for suppliers
  • Perform Verification of First Article Inspection (FAI) on incoming material and coordinate acceptance of FAI data submitted by suppliers
  • Manage quality containment process for material, tooling, and inspection equipment that are involved in non-conformances impacting production capacity and capability
  • Create inspection plans for incoming material, in-process inspection steps, and end of line inspection, as per direction from product quality engineers.  Execute inspection as needed
  • Train technicians and inspectors to execute inspection plans and data capture in the process
  • Propose, develop and implement quality assurance policies and procedures and review with the product quality engineers
  • Review and propose continuous improvement projects for productivity gains, quality improvements, and benefits to Anduril's quality policy
  • Deep dive into data and traceability investigations to identify trends, oddities, inconsistencies, and variation that impacts the effectiveness of processes, procedures, and product quality

This position is permanently based in Ashville, OH, and requires candidates to temporarily relocate for a comprehensive 2-month training program in Santa Ana, CA. To support your transition, Anduril will fully provide and cover all corporate housing, transportation, and travel accommodations during this training period. Your recruiter will discuss the logistics of this program with you in detail during the hiring process

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Associate degree or equivalent in a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years of experience in metrology inspection or quality role
  • Experience with production support and quality management
  • Proficiency with ERP/MES software and inspection data management software
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
  • Experience with Calibrated equipment (calipers, micrometers, CMM, Faro arm, OMM, etc.)

The Maritime Manufacturing Technology team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Quality Technician to join our rapidly growing team in Santa Ana, CA. The Quality Technician for our Maritime team is a critical role responsible for ensuring our autonomous surface and undersea systems are built to the most stringent standards, blending the speed and innovation of a technology company with the discipline and rigor required for national security.

You will be the authority on quality for programs that operate in the harshest environments on Earth. This role requires a hands-on, first-principles approach to developing and enforcing quality systems that meet and exceed AS9100 and specific Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) standards. You will not just be checking boxes; you will be building the quality foundation for the next generation of naval technology.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support the Quality team to develop, implement, and sustain a robust Quality Management System (QMS) that is compliant with AS9100 and tailored to include specific NAVSEA requirements for maritime hardware.
  • Champion quality on the manufacturing floor. Support statistical process controls (SPC), conduct Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and continuous improvement initiatives to increase first-pass yield and reduce scrap.
  • Interpret and flow down NAVSEA standards and technical publications (e.g., material traceability, welding certifications, testing protocols) into actionable manufacturing and inspection processes.
  • Support the Material Review Board (MRB) to disposition non-conforming product. Help drive the Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) process using methodologies like 8D and 5 Whys to prevent recurrence.
  • Partner with the supply chain team to qualify, audit, and manage suppliers of critical components and special processes (e.g., welding, coatings, pressure testing), ensuring compliance with all prime contract and regulatory requirements.
  • Support the development of comprehensive inspection plans, work instructions, and criteria for receiving, in-process, and final inspection. Aid with First Article Inspections (FAIs) in accordance with AS9102.
  • Support internal and supplier audits to ensure system-wide compliance and identify opportunities for improvement. Support customer and third-party audits.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of experience in a Quality Engineering role within a manufacturing environment for aerospace, defense, or other regulated industries.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience implementing, maintaining, and being audited against an AS9100 certified Quality Management System.
  • Proficiency in root cause analysis methodologies (8D, 5 Whys, Fishbone, etc.) and implementing effective corrective actions.
  • Experience aiding First Article Inspections (FAIs) per AS9102.
  • Understanding of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) and the ability to interpret complex engineering drawings.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience with NAVSEA standards and requirements (e.g., SUBSAFE, NAVSEA S9074-AQ-GIB-010/248 for welding, material control specifications, technical publication adherence).
  • Experience in the production of maritime systems, including unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), or related pressure vessel and submersible hardware.
  • Experience with quality control for special processes such as composite fabrication, welding, complex electro-mechanical assembly, and environmental/pressure testing.
  • ASQ certification (Certified Quality Engineer - CQE, Certified Quality Auditor - CQA) or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt certification.
  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-mix, rapid development environment where speed and rigor must coexist.
  • Familiarity with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Manufacturing Execution System (MES) software.
  • Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

The team in London builds the Mission System and the autonomy that makes aircraft like Thunder work. Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own.


ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Systems Engineering, Integration and Test (SEIT) Lead to join the Thunder team at our Costa Mesa HQ. You will work on new aircraft and mission system development, including propulsion systems, avionics, batteries, mechanisms, structures, sensors and payloads, in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Deploy right-sized, Agile Systems Engineering governance approaches for rapid capability development efforts - with the right amount of process discipline and artifacts and support System Design Reviews (SDRs)
  • Lead the use of ‘Test’ as a design tool to support component, system and subsystem maturation from discrete bench tests to production representative Vehicle, Mission and Support Systems
  • Work with customers and end-users to evolve Concept of Operations (CONOPS) and the Product Life Cycle, developing inputs to high-level requirements informing key design decisions
  • Develop and sustain highly representative Hardware In Lab (HIL) and Hardware In The Loop (HITL) physical integration environments – capable of ‘flying’ missions, as well as full-size geometry representative section demonstrators for payload development
  • Focus on the safety of integration environments, ensuring that potential harm of team members can be eliminated by design
  • Leverage crewed and uncrewed flying assets as surrogates for subsystem development in the representative environment
  • Develop, review, and execute right-sized test plans across integration environments, efficiently capturing and reporting learnings, and making recommendations as inputs to design
  • Conduct Test Readiness Reviews (TRR), and assess and mitigate hazards to ensure that testing can be safely and efficiently executed
  • Support factory acceptance, ground and flight test of prototype and production representative Systems
  • Liaise with partner organizations and local authorities to secure operational approvals (airspace, frequency, physical deconfliction, safety, and appropriate test range facilities)
  • Conduct safety assessments with a pragmatic understanding of hazards and mitigations - holding the safety of team members above all else

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor degree or higher in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering or aviation related technical discipline
  • 10+ years experience in Systems Engineering, integration and test
  • Experience in developing and operating HIL/HITL/IRON BIRD integration environments for flight vehicles
  • Vehicle/System level integration and test experience, preferably with Group 4/5 uncrewed and autonomous platforms, including ground and flight test
  • Experience in all facets of the test process including writing test plans and procedures, conducting risk assessments, mitigating hazards, running test readiness reviews, directing test events, and responding to unplanned occurrences
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal & written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Proven track record of leading SEIT efforts for a clean-sheet aircraft program from early architecture and bench testing through IRON BIRD commissioning, first flight, and envelope expansion
  • Specific experience integrating and testing complex rotorcraft dynamic systems, hybrid/electric powertrains, or high-performance Group 4/5 tactical UAS.
  • Hands-on experience architecting full-vehicle IRON BIRD or system integration labs (SIL) featuring closed-loop dynamic models, real-time sensor injection, and automated regression testing
  • Demonstrated background planning and executing risk-reduction flight tests utilizing airborne surrogate platforms (crewed or uncrewed testbeds)
  • Experience establishing formal ground/flight test safety protocols, hazard analyses (MIL-STD-882), and supporting military or civil flight clearance releases (e.g., MIL-STD-516C, NAVAIR, or US Army Airworthiness).

Our teams set engineering standards, run development manufacturing and test sites, and develop core technology products that ship across multiple product lines.

WHAT YOU'LL DO


Motor Control Algorithm Development
•       Design and implement field-oriented control (FOC), six-step commutation, and direct torque control algorithms for BLDC and PMSM motors
•       Develop sensorless rotor position estimation techniques (back-EMF observer, sliding-mode observer, high-frequency injection) for applications where Hall sensors or encoders are not viable
•       Design current, speed, and position control loops with rigorous bandwidth, stability margins, and disturbance rejection specifications
Modelling & Simulation (MIL / SIL / HIL)
•       Build high-fidelity motor and inverter plant models in MATLAB / Simulink, including magnetic saturation, iron losses, and thermal coupling
•       Develop controller models and validate performance through Model-in-the-Loop (MIL) simulation against requirements
•       Execute Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) testing using Embedded Coder auto-generated C code to verify fixed-point scaling, quantisation effects, and code-generation fidelity
•       Support Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) integration with real-time simulators (dSPACE, Typhoon HIL, or equivalent) for full controller board validation
•       Integrate Simulink auto-coded algorithm modules with the microcontroller RTOS, peripheral drivers, and application framework
Firmware & Embedded Systems
•       Implement motor control firmware in C on microcontrollers (e.g., STM32, TI C2000, NXP S32K) with hard real-time constraints
•       Configure and optimise motor control peripherals: PWM timers, ADC synchronization, encoder/Hall interfaces, comparator-based overcurrent protection
•       Architect firmware for deterministic control loop execution — interrupt prioritization, DMA pipelines, and minimal-jitter scheduling
•       Implement fault detection, diagnosis, and safe-state management in firmware (overcurrent, over-voltage, over-temperature, sensor loss, stall, phase loss)
•       Develop communication interfaces (CAN, SPI, UART, RS-485) for command, telemetry, and diagnostics

•       Strong foundation in classical and modern control theory — PID tuning, frequency-domain analysis, state estimation, observer design

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Senior DFx Engineer to drive design for manufacturability, assembly, and cost across our avionics, electronics, wiring, and harnessing subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — ensuring that design decisions account for how hardware will be built, by whom, and at what cost.

You will bring specialty expertise in at least one of the following domains: avionics, wire harnessing, electronics (PCBA), or electrical systems. Your primary focus areas are manufacturability, assembly, and cost — the three lenses that determine whether a design can be produced at rate, by a qualified supplier, at an affordable price point. You will work directly with subject matter expert (SME) manufacturing engineers and design engineers to evaluate producibility, negotiate design trades, and drive improvements that make hardware buildable and cost-effective.

A key part of this role is supporting the selection and qualification of contract manufacturers — assessing supplier capabilities against DFx requirements and helping ensure that external production partners can deliver to the quality, rate, and cost targets our programs demand. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, and program teams in addition to ME and DE.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Execute DFx analysis across avionics, electronics, wiring, and harnessing subsystems for AD&S programs, with a primary focus on manufacturability, assembly, and cost.
  • Participate in and help lead structured DFM/DFA/DFC reviews at key design milestones, applying rigorous scoring to identify producibility and cost risks and drive design changes before they reach production.
  • Work directly with SME manufacturing engineers and design engineers to evaluate designs, translate manufacturing constraints into actionable feedback, and support design trades that balance performance, producibility, and cost.
  • Support the selection and qualification of contract manufacturers for avionics, electronics, and harnessing production — assessing supplier manufacturing capability, process maturity, and cost competitiveness against DFx requirements.
  • Participate in supplier manufacturing assessments including facility reviews, process audits, and capability evaluations.
  • Contribute to should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for electronics and harnessing assemblies, identifying design changes that reduce unit cost without compromising quality or performance.
  • Develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to electronics manufacturing processes including SMT, wave/selective solder, conformal coating, potting, wire harness fabrication, and box-build assembly.
  • Analyze designs across key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, cost structure, adherence to specification, process capability, and technology maturity — to contribute to quantified risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Partner with supply chain to align DFx requirements with sourcing strategy, ensuring that designs are producible by the suppliers we intend to use.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to ensure DFx findings flow into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.
  • Close the loop between production floor feedback, supplier performance data, and upstream design improvements.
  • Contribute to the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials — so that DFx knowledge scales across the organization.
  • Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, producibility engineering, or DFx with a significant focus on electronics, avionics, wiring, or harnessing — with specialty expertise in at least one of these domains.
  • Strong working knowledge of electronics and/or harnessing manufacturing processes: SMT placement and reflow, wave and selective soldering, conformal coating, potting and encapsulation, wire harness fabrication (cut/strip/crimp/solder/mold), and electromechanical box-build.
  • Experience participating in or leading DFM/DFA reviews and translating findings into measurable design improvements that reduce cost and improve producibility.
  • Experience supporting contract manufacturer evaluations — including facility assessments, process capability reviews, or production readiness evaluations.
  • Understanding of cost drivers in electronics and harnessing production, with exposure to should-cost modeling or cost analysis.
  • Ability to read and critically evaluate electrical schematics, PCB layouts, harness drawings, and mechanical packaging for producibility and cost impact.
  • Working knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620, IPC-6012) and their application to design, process, and supplier qualification decisions.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, manufacturing engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present DFx and cost findings to engineering teams and drive alignment on design changes.
  • Comfortable working across multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Personal experience physically building or reworking electronic assemblies or harnesses. Hands-on credibility matters.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Master's degree in Engineering or a related field.
  • Specialty expertise in two or more of: avionics, PCBA/electronics, wire harnessing, electrical systems.
  • Experience in aerospace or defense electronics production, particularly with qualified or flight-critical hardware.
  • Familiarity with AS9100/AS9102 quality management systems and First Article Inspection processes.
  • Experience with PCBA insourcing or standing up electronics manufacturing lines (SMT, test, integration).
  • Proficiency in ECAD tools (Altium, KiCad, or similar) sufficient to review designs independently.
  • Background in Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical process control, or Six Sigma applied to electronics manufacturing.
  • Experience with value engineering or formal cost reduction programs in a production environment.
  • Appropriate clearance classification & eligility.

  • A solid understanding of hardware manufacturability and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing.
  • Strong communication skills.

  • Technical leadership experience.
  • Exhibits strong initiative and ownership of tasks.
  • Experience with NX CAD software and/or Abaqus FEA software.
  • Certification in Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing.
  • Expertise in engineering tool development in Microsoft Excel, MATLAB, and/or Python.
  • Experience with propulsion systems.

This team is the nexus of premier Anduril-built products such as Roadrunner, Sentry, Anvil, Pulsar, and Wisp integrated into a software-enabled Air Defense family of systems tailored to the modern battlespace. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, we provide critical force protection capabilities to support the warfighter. Our autonomous family of networked sensors and effectors enables our users to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats that continue to evolve at a rapid pace. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

  • The Air Defense team needs a Senior Network Engineer to own the networks that connect sensors, compute, and effectors from detection to engagement. You’ll be responsible for owning the networking components across deployed Anduril Systems, designing the physical infrastructure behind fielded networks, and troubleshooting failures from routing configuration down to physical interconnect of the system. This role requires deep Linux networking expertise and the ability to work hands-on in the field. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Configure and troubleshoot Linux networking across deployed Anduril hardware as well as network appliances, including interfaces, bonding, VLAN tagging, routing tables, and host firewall rules 
  • Own networking for the Air Defense family of systems. Work with sensor, effector, autonomy, and Lattice teams to move each detection to the effector that acts on it 
  • Diagnose network behavior end to end, from host-level packet captures and system troubleshooting to the switch, link, and cable underneath it 
  • Design, deploy, and maintain the networks that support Air Defense development, integration, and test, including lab networks, integration facilities, and their physical infrastructure 
  • Design and implement secure, segmented network architectures using ACLs, firewalls, and intrusion detection or prevention 
  • Maintain accurate documentation for network topology, cabling, VLAN and IP assignments, and inter-zone communication flows. Support field integration and test events

Anduril is seeking an experienced Power Controls Engineer to develop and implement advanced control algorithms for high-performance power electronic systems. We're looking for someone with deep expertise in control system modeling and simulation — particularly in Simulink and PLECS — who can take a controls concept from simulation through hardware validation. This individual will own the control architecture for DC/DC converters, inverters, and motor drives built around discrete SiC and GaN power stages, and will work closely with power hardware and firmware engineers to deliver tightly integrated, high-reliability systems for defense and aerospace applications.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Design, simulate, and validate closed-loop control algorithms for switch-mode power converters and inverters using Simulink and/or PLECS.
  • Controls for 3-phase AC systems, with and without a switched Neutral
  • Develop plant models and controller architectures (voltage-mode, current-mode, sensorless FOC, etc.) for multi-kW power stages utilizing discrete SiC and GaN FETs.
  • Perform stability analysis, loop shaping, and compensator design to meet transient response, efficiency, and EMI targets.
  • Collaborate with power hardware engineers on gate drive tuning, dead-time optimization, and switching-loss characterization of wide-bandgap devices.
  • Support model-based code generation workflows and work with firmware engineers to translate control designs into embedded implementations.
  • Define and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and power-hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) test plans to validate control performance against system requirements.
  • Contribute to trade studies on converter topology, modulation strategy, and control bandwidth as they relate to size, weight, power, and thermal constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related discipline.
  • 8+ years of experience designing and tuning digital control loops for power electronic converters (DC/DC, DC/AC, or motor drives).
  • Proficiency in Simulink and/or PLECS for control system modeling, simulation, and analysis.
  • Strong foundation in control theory — z-domain and s-domain design, bode analysis, state-space methods, and discrete-time implementation considerations.
  • Hands-on experience with discrete SiC and/or GaN FET-based power stages in the multi-kW range.
  • Familiarity with military or aerospace environments and standards such as MIL-STD-461, 464, 810, or DO-160.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MS/PhD with a focus in power electronics controls or control systems.
  • Experience writing embedded firmware (C/C++) for microcontrollers or DSPs used in power converter control (e.g., TI C2000, STM32).
  • Familiarity with auto-code generation from Simulink (Embedded Coder) or similar model-based design toolchains.
  • Experience with real-time HIL platforms (e.g., Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT).
  • Knowledge of advanced modulation techniques (SVM, DPWM) and their impact on switching losses in wide-bandgap devices.
  • Design-for-Reliability practices including DFMEA.
  • Experience with EMI mitigation strategies at the controls and layout level.

About the Role

Anduril's Rocket Motor Systems group is seeking a Senior Quality Engineer, Quality Systems & Quality Intelligence to join our team supporting operations across McHenry, Mississippi; West Lafayette, Indiana; and Huntsville, Alabama. The Rocket Motor Systems team designs, develops, and manufactures next-generation solid rocket motors for defense and space applications at Anduril.

As a Senior Quality Engineer focused on Quality Systems and Quality Intelligence, you will own the quality management system infrastructure that enables RMS to scale across multiple sites, programs, and customers. You are the person who ensures our QMS is not just compliant but intelligent - leveraging AI tools, data-driven insights, and scalable compliance frameworks to stay ahead of program requirements rather than chasing them. From maintaining our AS9100/IAQG certification posture to architecting modular data packages that flex across customer deliverable requirements, you will build the quality systems backbone that the rest of the RMS quality team operates within. If you are someone who thinks in systems, thrives on bringing order to complexity, and sees AI as a force multiplier for quality rather than a buzzword, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Create, maintain, and own the RMS compliance matrix across all programs, mapping customer contract quality requirements, regulatory obligations, and internal standards to specific QMS processes, procedures, and objective evidence ensuring nothing falls through the cracks as programs scale.
  • Serve as the RMS subject matter expert for AS9100 and IAQG 9100-series standards, providing interpretation guidance, leading internal readiness assessments, and ensuring RMS operations across McHenry, West Lafayette, and Huntsville maintain consistent compliance with the quality management system.
  • Evaluate and integrate quality management software, digital tools, and data platforms that enhance RMS quality system efficiency, traceability, and reporting - ensuring the QMS infrastructure scales with the growth of RMS operations.
  • Evaluating, piloting, and deploying AI and automation tools across quality workflows including nonconformance trending, document generation, compliance monitoring, and predictive quality analytics - and training the RMS quality team on effective, responsible usage.
  • Provide QMS oversight across all RMS locations (McHenry, MS; West Lafayette, IN; Huntsville, AL), ensuring that site-specific procedures, work instructions, and quality records are aligned to the RMS quality system and that multi-site operations do not create compliance gaps or inconsistencies.
  • Support the expansion of production, development, and testing laboratory facilities by ensuring new operations, equipment, and processes are integrated into the QMS from the outset - including procedure development, training requirements, calibration programs, and document control infrastructure.
  • Lead the RMS internal audit program, ensuring audit coverage meets AS9100 requirements and organizational risk priorities, and that audit findings drive meaningful corrective actions rather than paperwork exercises.
  • Develop and deliver quality system training for RMS personnel - from new hire orientation on QMS fundamentals to advanced training on AI tools, compliance requirements, audit techniques, and customer-specific quality expectations building quality literacy across all functions and sites.
  • Interface with external auditors (registrar, customer, and government) during AS9100 surveillance and certification audits, DCMA oversight activities, and customer quality system reviews - serving as the primary RMS point of contact for quality system inquiries and findings.
  • Monitor and analyze quality system performance metrics - including audit findings, corrective action effectiveness, document control compliance, training completion rates, and customer quality escapes - translating data into management review inputs and continuous improvement priorities.
  • Support Program Quality team with customer contract reviews and proposal activities by interpreting quality requirements from SOWs, CDRLs, and contract quality clauses, and translating them into actionable RMS data package configurations.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Industrial, or Manufacturing), Quality Management, or a related technical field.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in quality systems or quality engineering, with significant experience in QMS development, maintenance, and multi-site compliance in aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated industries.
  • Deep working knowledge of AS9100 (current revision) and IAQG 9100-series standards, including demonstrated experience leading or supporting AS9100 certification and surveillance audits.
  • Experience building or managing compliance matrices that map customer, regulatory, and internal requirements to QMS processes and objective evidence across multiple programs.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and train others on AI and automation tools applied to quality workflows with a vision for how these technologies transform quality operations beyond simple efficiency gains.
  • Experience with quality data package assembly and delivery for defense contracts, including familiarity with CDRL structures, customer-specific data requirements, and the challenge of scaling documentation across programs with different deliverable expectations.
  • Proven experience managing internal audit programs, including audit planning, auditor qualification, finding classification, and corrective action tracking through to verified closure.
  • Excellent communication and training skills, with the ability to make quality system requirements understandable and actionable for engineers, operators, and leadership across multiple sites.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • AS9100 Certified Lead Auditor certification (or equivalent IAQG-recognized auditor qualification).
  • ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQMgr), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA).
  • Familiarity with solid rocket motor systems, propulsion manufacturing, or energetic materials operations - including prior experience safely working in proximity to energetic materials.
  • Experience with testing and qualification processes for aerospace or defense hardware, including knowledge of qualification test planning, data documentation requirements, and acceptance criteria development.
  • Experience with DCMA interface, government source inspection (GSI), and the quality requirements that flow from DoD contracts including MIL-STD and DFARS clauses.
  • Proficiency with quality management software platforms, ERP systems (e.g., Oracle), PLM tools, and document control systems used in regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Experience supporting facility expansions, new site stand-ups, or production scaling where QMS infrastructure had to be built or extended to cover new operations.
  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification, or demonstrated experience applying continuous improvement methodologies to quality system processes.

Anduril is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead cross-functional execution across a portfolio of warhead-development programs. Motor Control Algorithm Development

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Staff DFx Manufacturing Engineer to drive design-for-manufacturability, assembly, and testability across our avionics, electronics, and harnessing subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — ensuring that electronics hardware is designed to be produced at scale from the earliest stages of development.

As a Staff-level individual contributor, you will be the technical authority on DFx for electronics and avionics across AD&S. You will embed with design engineering teams during concept and detailed design, lead structured DFx reviews, and translate manufacturing constraints into actionable design guidance. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily alongside supply chain, design engineering, quality, and operations teams to ensure producibility is built into every decision, from component selection through final acceptance. Your work directly shapes whether our products can be built reliably, affordably, and at the rate our programs demand.

You will also mentor manufacturing engineers across programs and build the DFx methodology and toolset that scales with the organization.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own and drive the DFx process for avionics, electronics, and harnessing subsystems across AD&S programs, from concept through rate production.
  • Lead structured DFM/DFA/DFT reviews at key design milestones, applying a rigorous scoring methodology to identify producibility risks and drive design changes before they become production problems.
  • Embed with electrical and avionics design engineering teams to provide real-time manufacturing feedback on PCBA layout, component selection, connector and harnessing architecture, and test access.
  • Work cross-functionally with supply chain, quality, operations, and design engineering on a daily basis — this role is the connective tissue between what gets designed and what gets built.
  • Develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to electronics manufacturing processes including SMT, wave/selective solder, conformal coating, potting, wire harness fabrication, and box-build assembly.
  • Analyze designs across five key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, quality, adherence to
  • specification, process capability, and technology maturity — to produce quantified risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Champion testability early in the design cycle: define test point access, boundary scan requirements, functional test strategies, and fixtures needed for production-rate acceptance testing.
  • Partner with quality engineering to ensure DFx findings flow into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and process control strategies.
  • Collaborate with supply chain and sourcing teams to assess supplier manufacturing capability, support make-vs-buy decisions, and ensure external production meets DFx requirements.
  • Close the loop between production floor feedback and upstream design improvements by working directly with operations and production engineering teams.
  • Build and evolve the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, lessons-learned databases, and training materials — so that DFx knowledge scales beyond any single person.
  • Mentor and develop junior and mid-level manufacturing engineers on DFx principles and review techniques.
  • Travel to production sites, suppliers, and partner facilities as needed (<10%).


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, or producibility engineering with a significant focus on electronics, avionics, or electromechanical assemblies. A
  • Master’s Degree can replace 2 years of work experience.
  • Deep working knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes: SMT placement and reflow, wave and selective soldering, conformal coating, potting and encapsulation, cable and harness fabrication, and electromechanical box-build.
  • Demonstrated experience leading DFM/DFA/DFT reviews and translating findings into measurable design improvements.
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations — and to be effective without positional authority.
  • Ability to read and critically evaluate electrical schematics, PCB layouts, harness drawings, and mechanical packaging for producibility.
  • Strong command of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620, IPC-6012) and their application to design and process decisions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present DFx findings to engineering leadership and drive alignment on design changes.
  • Comfortable working across multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Personal experience physically building or reworking electronic assemblies (soldering, harness build, test, debug). Hands-on credibility matters.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Support Systems Engineering Lead to join the Thunder team at our Costa Mesa HQ. Thunder is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that combines vertical takeoff and landing with the range, speed, and heavy strike power of advanced attack platforms in a novel Group 5 tiltrotor airframe. Powered by a hybrid-electric powertrain and Lattice for Mission Autonomy, Thunder operates as a loyal wingman alongside crewed platforms like the AH-64 Apache in highly contested environments.

You will work on new aircraft development, bringing pragmatic Support Systems thinking to complement and enhance the overall capability, ensuring that end-user needs are met in challenging operational environments. You will be part of a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Architect, plan, and lead the design and development of a broad Support System (including deployment, supply, operations and maintenance; and everything in between)
  • Hire, develop, and grow a hands-on Engineering team focused on practical Support System solutions
  • Collaborate with customer stakeholders on a comprehensive concept of employment to ensure operational needs are understood
  • Own ‘Day In The Life Of’ decomposition activities to influence functional decomposition shaping the design of the Air Vehicle and Mission Systems
  • Design, fabricate and test Mission System transport and handling equipment (GSE) to enable rapid deployment in a range of challenging operational environments
  • Identify appropriate standards and associated interfaces for supply systems (such as fueling and charging) as inputs to design
  • Leverage emerging technologies to develop maintenance systems, operational processes, and training approaches that set new standards for what good looks like

Software is eating the world, but AI is eating software. We live in unprecedented times – AI has the potential to exponentially augment human intelligence. Every person will have a personal tutor, coach, assistant, personal shopper, travel guide, and therapist throughout life. As the world adjusts to this new reality, leading platform companies are scrambling to build LLMs at billion scale, while large enterprises figure out how to add it to their products. To make them safe, aligned and actually useful, these models need human eval and reinforcement learning through human feedback (RLHF) during pre-training, fine-tuning, and production evaluations. This is the main innovation that’s enabled ChatGPT to get such a large headstart among competition.

At Scale, our products include the Generative AI Data Engine, SGP, Donovan, and others that power the most advanced LLMs and generative models in the world through world-class RLHF, human data generation, model evaluation, safety, and alignment. The data we are producing is some of the most important work for how humanity will interact with AI.

At the foundation of these products is the Identity  Engineering team.  In this role, you will help support the design and development of core software systems specifically focused on identity, access management, authorization, and authentication.  You’ll also get widespread exposure to the forefront of the AI race as Scale sees it in enterprises, startups, governments, and large tech companies.

You will:

  • Drive the design, and implementation of our identity infrastructure to ensure secure authentication and authorization across enterprise systems.
  • Build software for authentication mechanisms such as Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and federated identity solutions (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect).
  • Build software for authorization mechanisms such as Relation-based access control (ReBAC), Attribute-based access control (ABAC), Role-based access control (RBAC).
  • Build software-defined identity governance policies to ensure compliance with security policies, industry regulations (e.g., NIST, SOC2, ISO 27001), and organizational standards.
  • Present technical information to teams and stakeholders, providing guidance and insight on identity management and best practices.

Ideally you’d have:

  • 5+ years of full-time engineering experience, post-graduation with specialities in infrastructure and identity systems.
  • Infrastructure expertise – IAM controls, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Pulumi), microservice deployment best practices.
  • Hands-on experience working with OpenFGA, Authzed, Cedar, Topaz, or similar authorization frameworks at scale.
  • Strong understanding of Zanzibar-based ReBAC models, relationship tuples, and access control evaluation.
  • Strong knowledge of authentication standards such as OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and JWT, as well as industry standard IdP solutions like EntraID, Okta, etc.
  • Extensive experience in software development and a deep understanding of distributed systems and public cloud platforms (AWS preferred).
  • Show a track record of independent ownership of successful engineering projects.
  • Possess excellent communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to translate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to haves:

  • Experience securing API access and implementing access control mechanisms at the application level.
  • Multi-cloud infrastructure experience – AWS, Azure, GCP, and more.
  • Proficiency in integrating IAM solutions with applications built using frameworks such as Java, Python, Node.js, or .NET.
  • Mentorship/leadership experience supporting junior engineers

Job Description:

Bring promising AI research into autonomous systems that operate in the real world.  Shield AI’s Perception team is looking for an engineer who enjoys exploring new ideas and making them work on real hardware. You’ll help turn advances in multimodal computer vision, visual foundation models, and embodied AI into useful capabilities for autonomous aircraft and vehicles. 

Working alongside researchers and autonomy engineers, you’ll evaluate promising approaches, build prototypes, and carry successful ideas into the Hivemind product. You’ll combine learned methods with established perception techniques, working through the sensor, software, and compute challenges that make edge robotics different from a benchmark. 

What you'll do:

    • Evaluate emerging models and methods against representative sensor data and autonomy needs. 

    • Build prototypes and experiments that reveal strengths, limitations, and practical deployment opportunities. 

    • Combine learned and classical approaches to improve detection, tracking, geometric vision, or sensor fusion. 

    • Optimize and integrate capabilities for edge deployment, contributing Python and C++ software with support from experienced product engineers. 

    • Help deliver tested, documented capabilities and stay involved as other teams adopt them. 

Required qualifications:

    • A PhD in computer vision, machine learning (ML/DL), robotics, or a related field, or an equivalent record of advanced research and hands-on engineering. 

    • Research depth in an area such as multimodal vision, visual foundation models, video understanding, open-vocabulary perception, or embodied learning. 

    • Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or a comparable ML framework. 

    • A thoughtful approach to experiments, evaluation data, and understanding why models fail. 

    • Experience building substantial research software, an interest in developing production-quality C++, and a collaborative approach to solving problems. 

Preferred qualifications:

    • Experience bringing a research prototype into sustained use. 

    • Experience with robotics, real sensors, temporal data, or multi-sensor perception. 

    • Familiarity with vision-language models, vision-language-action models, or embodied AI. 

    • Experience with C++, edge inference, or model optimization using tools such as ONNX, TensorRT, or CUDA. 

    You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification or arrive as an expert C++ engineer. We welcome recent PhD graduates and early-career researchers, and we value technical depth, curiosity, and enthusiasm to transfer research to business value more than publication count alone.

Job Description:

The Range Operations Officer supports the daily operation, readiness, and sustainment of Shield AI’s flight-test ranges . The role ensures that range, facilities, equipment, consumables, access controls, required notifications, and operational records are prepared and maintained for safe range operations.

Reporting to the Range Operations Manager, the Officer performs day-to-day range support and site-readiness activities. The role does not hold flight-release, airworthiness, test-director, or airport-authority responsibility. It escalates operational issues, safety concerns, resource constraints, and external coordination needs to the Range Operations Manager.

What you'll do:

  • Open, inspect, configure, and close the range for scheduled test activity; maintain daily readiness, operating, and closeout logs.
  • ·Verify that required NOTAMs, airport coordination, site access, weather information, safety equipment, emergency contacts, exclusion-zone controls, and operational signage are in place before testing.
  • Coordinate routine daily requirements with Airport Operations, the Flight Test Director, Maintenance, Engineering, FTI, Security, suppliers, contractors, and visitors.
  • Maintain the NOTAM tracker, verify active NOTAM status, retain NOTAM records, and alert the Range Operations Manager of upcoming, missing, conflicting, or expired NOTAMs.
  • Monitor and maintain readiness of range vehicles, fuel , POL, consumables, towing/recovery equipment, radios, and assigned ground-support equipment; identify shortfalls and coordinate replenishment or repair before they affect planned operations.
  • Coordinate fuel deliveries, vehicle servicing, range-equipment rentals, operational vendors, and contractor support required for scheduled flight-test activity; maintain status of orders, deliveries, and open operational issues.
  • Conduct routine inspections of the test areas/facilities, hangar, access roads, fencing, gates, signage, lighting, storage areas, utilities, GSE, and operational support equipment; document discrepancies and track corrective actions.
  • Support test-day briefs by confirming range status, weather, personnel access, emergency readiness, communications, and changes affecting the planned operation.
  • Maintain range maps, emergency contact lists, site layouts, equipment inventories, supplier lists, service records, inspection records, and controlled operational templates.
  • Serve as Range Safety Officer (RSO) under delegated authority from the Range Operations Manager when required.
  • ·upport emergency-response readiness through equipment checks, contact-list verification, responder access coordination, and maintenance of recovery/spill-response resources.
  • During an event, support the Range Operations Manager, Flight Test Director, and responding agencies with access control, personnel accountability, event logging, documentation, and resource coordination.
  • Identify recurring operational issues and recommend practical improvements to site readiness, facilities, inventory levels, procedures, vendor support, and test-day efficiency.
  • Daily range-operations positions commonly include readiness inspections, safety/access control, operational documentation, equipment issue and tracking, weather communication, range opening/closing, and emergency-response support; aviation operations Officers similarly coordinate the services, resources, documentation, and external stakeholders needed for safe operations.

Required qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in aviation operations, airport operations, flight test, UAS operations, military range operations, maintenance operations, logistics, or a comparable high-tempo technical environment.
  • Working knowledge of aviation safety, airfield operations, weather, NOTAM coordination, aircraft ground operations, hazardous-material awareness, and operational documentation.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize competing test-day requirements, communicate clearly by radio and phone, and maintain disciplined records.
  • Comfortable working outdoors around aircraft, fuel, GSE, high-noise operations, contractors, and changing weather conditions.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to operate site vehicles, trailers, and approved GSE after training.
  • Ability to obtain airport access credentials and pass applicable background/security requirements.
  • Willingness to support nonstandard hours, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and time-sensitive test operations.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting flight-test, UAS, VTOL, military, aerospace, or airport operations.
  • Familiarity with FAA NOTAM processes, airport operating procedures, and airside vehicle/access controls.
  • Experience with fuel and hazardous-material handling, spill-response readiness, inventory control, vendor management, and contractor coordination.
  • Current or prior training in OSHA 10/30, HAZWOPER awareness, first aid/CPR/AED, fire-extinguisher use, incident command system, or airfield-driver safety.
  • Experience with Excel-based trackers, asset/inventory systems, maintenance/work-order tools, document control, and operational readiness checklists.

Success measures:

  • All planned tests begin with completed range-readiness checks, current required notifications, required access controls, and no preventable site-readiness delay.
  • Fuel, consumables, safety equipment, emergency supplies, and operational equipment remain available, inspected, and within defined reorder limits.
  • NOTAMs, range logs, inspections, visitor records, and corrective-action trackers are current and audit-ready.
  • Safety, facility, access, and vendor issues are identified early, communicated clearly, and closed on schedule.
  • The Range Operations Manager receives a concise daily status update covering test readiness, open actions, upcoming coordination needs, inventory concerns, and escalations.
  • The Flight Test Range Operations Officer is a hands-on, highly organized role for someone who enjoys turning complex flight-test requirements into an orderly, safe, and ready-to-operate test environment. The successful candidate will be the day-to-day operational backbone of the Newton range, enabling the Range Operations Manager and flight-test team to focus on safe, disciplined execution of advanced aviation programs.

Job Description:

As a Environmental Test Technician at Shield AI, you'll prepare, execute, and manage environmental tests on electronic flight hardware across the VBAT and XBAT aircraft, ensuring it meets performance requirements through rigorous thermal, vibration, shock, humidity, and altitude testing. This is a highly hands-on role. Working with design and reliability stakeholders, you'll help define test plans — stress profiles, setup, and instrumentation — then bring them to the bench: designing and modeling test fixtures in CAD, instrumenting hardware with thermocouples, accelerometers, strain gauges, and humidity sensors, configuring data acquisition, and programming and loading chambers. You'll frequently run several campaigns at once, owning the equipment scheduling needed to keep them moving without compromising data quality.

Once tests are running, you'll operate the equipment, monitor for and investigate failures, and reduce and document results in clear reports — including the plots and visualizations stakeholders rely on to make disposition and qualification decisions. You'll work with cutting-edge deep-tech hardware, collaborate across disciplines, and directly influence product quality and long-term reliability over the vehicles’ lifecycles.

What you'll do:

  • Operate and continuously improve a world-class environmental test lab for electronics that includes HALT/HASS chambers, thermal-humidity chambers, vibration/shock equipment, and data acquisition equipment.
  • Develop and implement lab procedures for use of environmental test equipment, test setup and tear down, data acquision, and test reporting.
  • Perform reliability tests on electronic products, including thermal cycling, temperature-humidity soaks, HALT, HASS, vibration, and shock testing.
  • Develop lab best-practices, including automation of data acquisition, defining test plans, documenting test results, and management of tests.
  • Manage procurement and maintenance of lab consumables, including instrumentation, adhesives, fasteners, and fixtures.
  • Oversee the maintenance, organization, and safety of all laboratory equipment and work areas.
  • Work with external laboratories to perform environmental tests as necessary.
  • Educate stakeholders on environmental test best-practices to improve test plans and design-for-test practices.
  • Stay current with industry trends, advancements, and best practices in all aspects of environmental testing and equipment.

Required qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience with environmental testing, including temperature cycling, vibration, highly accelerated limit testing (HALT), and highly-accelerated stress screening (HASS).
  • Candidate must be self-starting and come with a growth mindset, with excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Knowledgeable in data acquisition equipment and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, humidity sensors, and strain gauges.
  • Familiarity with electronics (PCBs, PCBAs, electronic components) and moving mechanical assemblies. Knowledgeable in failure mechanisms including solder fatigue, intermetallic growth, conductive anodic filaments, tin whiskers, electromigration, and corrosion.
  • Team-player with clear and concise written and oral communication skills.
  • Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production.
  • Experience with management of technical projects.
  • Familiarity with relevant industry test standards, including IPC, JEDEC, MIL, and ASTM standards.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in a reliability testing role, including temperature cycling, vibration, highly accelerated limit testing (HALT), and highly-accelerated stress screening (HASS).
  • Familiarity with reliability concepts, including Weibull statistics, accelerated life test design, highly-accelerated limit testing (HALT), and highly-accelerated stress screening (HASS).
  • Proficiency in CAD modelling software, including ANSYS SpaceClaim, NX, or Solidworks.
